implication_if_solved: Would show whether writing is an inevitable consequence of state complexity

phenomenon: Human music and its emotional power
observation_summary: Organized sound reliably produces strong emotion, physiological change and social bonding across all cultures with no clear survival function
why_it_resists_explanation: The reward mechanism is measurable but why abstract sound patterns engage it is not explained; no animal shows comparable responses to melody
leading_hypotheses: Auditory cheesecake byproduct of other adaptations (Pinker); social bonding and coalition signaling adaptation; sexual selection (Darwin); prediction-and-resolution reward in the dopaminergic system; vocal-emotion mimicry
mainstream_view: Neural reward mechanisms are mapped; evolutionary function is openly contested
testable_prediction: Cross-cultural and infant studies plus dopamine blockade studies constrain the hypotheses
key_evidence_or_cases: Salimpoor dopamine release during musical peaks 2011; naltrexone blunting musical pleasure; universal features across cultures
implication_if_solved: Would explain a universal human behavior with no obvious adaptive payoff

observation_summary: Yawning occurs across vertebrates, is contagious in some social species, and has no confirmed function
why_it_resists_explanation: Proposed functions are hard to isolate experimentally, and the contagious aspect involves a separate social mechanism
leading_hypotheses: Brain cooling via increased blood flow and cool air intake (best supported); arousal and state-transition signaling; social synchronization and empathy for contagion; oxygenation (disproven)
mainstream_view: Brain cooling has reasonable support; no settled consensus
testable_prediction: Yawn frequency should track ambient and brain temperature within a thermal window, which some studies support
key_evidence_or_cases: Gallup brain cooling studies; contagious yawning in chimpanzees and dogs; yawn duration correlating with brain size across species
implication_if_solved: Would resolve a trivial-seeming but genuinely open physiological question

observation_summary: Being tickled produces involuntary laughter but only by another person, and ticklishness has no established function
why_it_resists_explanation: Self-tickling fails, which implicates predictive cancelation, but the overall purpose and the neural basis of ticklish laughter remain unclear
leading_hypotheses: Social play and bonding signal predating language; reflexive defense of vulnerable body areas; a prediction-error phenomenon requiring unpredictability; rat ultrasonic vocalization homologue in somatosensory cortex
mainstream_view: Partially mapped; function still speculative
testable_prediction: Blocking somatosensory cortex regions in animals should abolish tickle responses, which has been shown in rats
key_evidence_or_cases: Rat tickle-responsive somatosensory cortex 2016; cerebellar prediction studies of self-tickling; Darwin on laughter
implication_if_solved: Would illuminate the neural basis of play and social bonding

observation_summary: Neural precursors of simple choices can be detected before reported awareness of deciding, raising unresolved questions about the role of conscious intention
why_it_resists_explanation: The experiments measure arbitrary timed movements rather than deliberated decisions, and the readiness potential may reflect background noise rather than a decision
leading_hypotheses: Conscious intention as a post hoc narrative; the readiness potential as stochastic drift crossing a threshold (Schurger); compatibilist agency unaffected by timing; genuine libertarian free will
mainstream_view: Libet-style results no longer support strong anti-free-will conclusions; the broader metaphysical question is unresolved
testable_prediction: Decoding deliberated value-based decisions rather than arbitrary movements changes the picture, as recent work suggests
key_evidence_or_cases: Libet 1983; Soon et al 2008 fMRI prediction; Schurger 2012 stochastic accumulator reinterpretation
implication_if_solved: Would reshape law, ethics and self-understanding

observation_summary: Historical crucible steel blades had distinctive patterns and reportedly superior properties, and the exact process was lost by the 1800s
why_it_resists_explanation: The original ore sources with specific trace impurities were exhausted, and the process was a craft tradition never written down
leading_hypotheses: Trace vanadium and molybdenum in specific Indian ores promoting carbide banding; cyclic forging and thermal cycling producing cementite sheets; carbon nanotube formation reported in 2006 (contested)
mainstream_view: Substantially reverse-engineered; the historical process has been plausibly reconstructed and reproduced
testable_prediction: Reproduction using ore with the same trace elements should yield the characteristic pattern, and has
key_evidence_or_cases: Verhoeven and Pendray reproduction; Reibold carbon nanotube report 2006; trace-element analyses of museum blades
implication_if_solved: Would recover a historical materials technology and inform modern steel design

observation_summary: Roman marine concrete has survived 2000 years in seawater while modern reinforced concrete degrades in decades
why_it_resists_explanation: The mechanism involves mineral growth over centuries, which cannot be observed in real time in modern samples
leading_hypotheses: Hot mixing with quicklime producing lime clasts that enable self-healing (2023 MIT work); pozzolanic volcanic ash forming aluminous tobermorite and phillipsite in seawater; absence of corroding steel reinforcement
mainstream_view: Largely solved in the last decade; engineering translation is ongoing
testable_prediction: Hot-mixed modern concrete should show self-healing of cracks, which lab tests demonstrate
key_evidence_or_cases: Jackson et al mineral analysis of Portus Cosanus samples; Seymour and Masic 2023 lime clast study
implication_if_solved: Would enable far more durable low-carbon infrastructure

observation_summary: A liquid incendiary that burned on water and could be pumped through siphons, whose recipe was a state secret and is lost
why_it_resists_explanation: The formula was restricted to a few families, no sample survives, and descriptions are deliberately vague
leading_hypotheses: Refined crude oil or naphtha with resin and sulfur thickeners under pressure; quicklime-based water-reactive mixture; saltpeter-containing mixture (anachronistic); a petroleum distillate heated and pressurized
mainstream_view: Accepted as a real petroleum-based weapon; exact composition unrecoverable
testable_prediction: Reproduction experiments with Black Sea petroleum fractions reproduce the described behavior
key_evidence_or_cases: Byzantine naval accounts; Haldon and Byrne reconstruction experiments; absence of surviving samples
implication_if_solved: Would complete the record of pre-modern military chemistry

observation_summary: Instruments by Stradivari and Guarneri are widely believed superior, and the reason has been sought for three centuries
why_it_resists_explanation: Blinded listening tests repeatedly fail to show that listeners or players prefer old Italian instruments, undercutting the premise
leading_hypotheses: Wood treatment with mineral salts and borax; dense Little Ice Age growth rings; varnish composition; superb but not unique craftsmanship; the perceived superiority is largely reputation and bias
mainstream_view: Double-blind studies suggest the premise itself is weak; material differences are real but their acoustic significance is unproven
testable_prediction: Double-blind preference tests, which have repeatedly favored modern instruments
key_evidence_or_cases: Fritz and Curtin double-blind studies 2012 and 2014; Nagyvary chemical analyses; dendrochronology of Cremonese wood
implication_if_solved: Would resolve whether a famous material mystery exists at all

observation_summary: Barium copper silicate pigment was synthesized in ancient China with no known glass or silicate industry precursor explanation, and loses dimensionality magnetically at low temperature
why_it_resists_explanation: The production route required precise temperature control and barium sources, and no texts describe the synthesis
leading_hypotheses: Byproduct of Taoist alchemical glass-making experiments with barite; deliberate synthesis route lost with the dynasty; independent development parallel to Egyptian blue
mainstream_view: Chemistry is fully characterized and reproducible; historical origin of the recipe remains open
testable_prediction: Experimental archaeology with period kilns and local barite should reproduce the pigment, and has
key_evidence_or_cases: Terracotta Army pigment analysis; 2006 quantum magnetic dimensional reduction in BaCuSi2O6
implication_if_solved: Would document an independent ancient chemical industry

observation_summary: Sand and grains behave as solid, liquid or gas depending on conditions, and jamming transitions lack a general theory
why_it_resists_explanation: Granular systems are athermal and history-dependent, so equilibrium statistical mechanics does not apply
leading_hypotheses: Jamming phase diagram with density stress and temperature axes; force chain networks; effective temperature formulations; no unifying theory yet
mainstream_view: Acknowledged open problem with major industrial importance
testable_prediction: A theory should predict silo clogging and avalanche statistics from grain properties
key_evidence_or_cases: Brazil nut effect; silo clogging statistics; force chain photoelastic imaging; Liu and Nagel jamming framework
implication_if_solved: Would improve handling of powders, which is a large fraction of industrial processing

observation_summary: Breaking certain crystals emits light, in some cases with spectra containing nitrogen emission lines implying electrical discharge
why_it_resists_explanation: The emission involves charge separation at crack tips over nanoseconds, which is difficult to observe in situ
leading_hypotheses: Charge separation on fracture surfaces producing microdischarges in surrounding gas; piezoelectric field generation in non-centrosymmetric crystals; excited-state formation at fresh surfaces
mainstream_view: Basic mechanism understood; why specific materials are efficient and the role of impurities remain open
testable_prediction: Fracture in different gas atmospheres should shift the emission spectrum accordingly, and does
key_evidence_or_cases: Wint-O-Green Lifesaver demonstrations; quartz and sucrose spectra; adhesive tape X-ray emission 2008
implication_if_solved: Would allow design of mechanoluminescent stress sensors

phenomenon: Radiometric and clock anomalies in the Pioneer and flyby data
observation_summary: Pioneer 10 and 11 showed a small unexplained sunward acceleration, and some Earth flybys showed unexplained velocity changes
why_it_resists_explanation: The effects are at the limit of radiometric precision and require modeling every thermal and radiative force on complex spacecraft
leading_hypotheses: Anisotropic thermal radiation from the spacecraft radioisotope generators and electronics (now accepted for Pioneer); modeling errors in Earth rotation and station delays for the flyby anomaly; modified gravity (effectively ruled out)
mainstream_view: The Pioneer anomaly is considered solved as thermal recoil; the flyby anomaly is less fully resolved but has no significant support for new physics
testable_prediction: Thermal modeling should account for the full magnitude, which 2012 analyses achieved for Pioneer
key_evidence_or_cases: Anderson et al 1998 Pioneer anomaly; Turyshev and Toth 2012 thermal resolution; Galileo and NEAR flyby residuals
implication_if_solved: Already a model case of an anomaly resolved by better engineering modeling

phenomenon: Cold fusion and low-energy nuclear reactions
observation_summary: Reports of excess heat and occasional nuclear products from deuterium-loaded palladium that mainstream nuclear physics says should be impossible at those energies
why_it_resists_explanation: The original claims failed to replicate under scrutiny, and positive reports are sporadic, poorly controlled, and lack the expected neutron and gamma signatures
leading_hypotheses: Calorimetry and measurement errors with unaccounted chemical heat; irreproducible material conditions in palladium loading; an unknown condensed-matter nuclear mechanism (not accepted); contamination accounting for nuclear products
mainstream_view: Rejected by mainstream physics; the 2015-2019 Google-funded program found no evidence of excess heat despite careful work
testable_prediction: Reproducible excess heat with commensurate nuclear products in blinded calorimetry
key_evidence_or_cases: Fleischmann and Pons 1989; 1989 DOE and 2004 DOE reviews; Berlinguette et al Nature 2019 null program
implication_if_solved: Would be transformative energy technology if real, but repeated careful tests say otherwise

observation_summary: Uranium ore bodies showed depleted U-235 because they sustained natural fission chain reactions about 1.7 billion years ago
why_it_resists_explanation: Not actually unexplained, but it was initially baffling and remains a remarkable natural occurrence requiring a specific coincidence of conditions
leading_hypotheses: Higher natural U-235 abundance in the Precambrian plus groundwater moderation producing self-regulating cyclic criticality
mainstream_view: Fully explained and now used as a natural laboratory for testing constancy of physical constants and long-term waste containment
testable_prediction: Fission product isotope ratios should match reactor physics predictions, and they do
key_evidence_or_cases: Oklo isotopic anomalies; xenon isotope analysis showing cyclic operation; constraints on variation of the fine-structure constant
implication_if_solved: Already resolved; provides unique data on nuclear waste behavior over geological time

observation_summary: Whether antimatter falls the same way as matter was unverified for 70 years and was only directly measured in 2023
why_it_resists_explanation: Producing and trapping neutral antimatter long enough to measure a gravitational effect is extremely difficult
leading_hypotheses: Antimatter falls down exactly like matter (now confirmed to ~20 percent precision); antigravity scenarios (now excluded)
mainstream_view: The 2023 ALPHA-g result confirms normal gravitational behavior; precision improvements continue
testable_prediction: Higher precision measurements should match g to better than one percent
key_evidence_or_cases: CERN ALPHA-g result 2023; AEgIS and GBAR experiments
implication_if_solved: Already confirms the weak equivalence principle for antimatter

observation_summary: Bottle and beam methods for measuring the free neutron lifetime disagree by about nine seconds, roughly four sigma apart
why_it_resists_explanation: The two methods have different systematic error sources, and extensive cross-checking has not resolved the gap
leading_hypotheses: Unaccounted systematic error in one method; a neutron dark decay channel into dark sector particles; neutron oscillation into a mirror neutron
mainstream_view: Taken seriously as either a systematics problem or a hint of new physics
testable_prediction: A dark decay channel would show a missing-energy branch detectable in dedicated searches, so far null
key_evidence_or_cases: UCNtau bottle measurements; NIST beam measurements; dark decay searches
implication_if_solved: Would either tighten nucleosynthesis predictions or reveal a dark sector

observation_summary: The CDF II experiment reported a W boson mass seven sigma above Standard Model prediction, conflicting with other measurements
why_it_resists_explanation: The CDF result disagrees with ATLAS, LHCb and the earlier world average, so one or more measurements must have an unidentified systematic
leading_hypotheses: Unidentified systematic in the CDF measurement; new physics affecting electroweak precision; underestimated parton distribution uncertainties
mainstream_view: The 2024 ATLAS and 2025 CMS measurements agree with the Standard Model, leaving CDF as the outlier
testable_prediction: Further high-precision W mass measurements should converge; they are converging away from CDF
key_evidence_or_cases: CDF II 2022 result; ATLAS 2024 and CMS 2024-2025 measurements
implication_if_solved: A confirmed deviation would be direct evidence of new electroweak physics

observation_summary: Pulsars occasionally speed up abruptly then relax, and magnetars emit giant flares, driven by interior physics we cannot model from first principles
why_it_resists_explanation: The interior involves superfluid neutrons and superconducting protons at densities beyond laboratory reach, with an unknown equation of state
leading_hypotheses: Vortex unpinning in the neutron superfluid crust; crustquakes from stress release; magnetic field reconfiguration for magnetar flares
mainstream_view: Established phenomena with partially understood mechanisms; the dense-matter equation of state is the limiting unknown
testable_prediction: Gravitational-wave observations of neutron star mergers constrain the equation of state and should discriminate models
key_evidence_or_cases: Vela pulsar glitches; SGR 1806-20 giant flare 2004; GW170817 tidal deformability constraints
implication_if_solved: Would reveal the behavior of matter at supranuclear density

observation_summary: The corona is over a million kelvin while the photosphere below is about 5800 K, violating naive thermodynamic expectation
why_it_resists_explanation: Energy transport through the chromosphere is difficult to observe at the required scales, and multiple mechanisms likely operate together
leading_hypotheses: Nanoflare magnetic reconnection heating; Alfven wave dissipation; braiding and tangling of magnetic field lines; a combination varying by region
mainstream_view: Long-standing open problem with major progress from Parker Solar Probe and Solar Orbiter; not fully resolved
testable_prediction: In situ measurements in the corona should reveal the dominant energy deposition channel
key_evidence_or_cases: Grotrian and Edlen identification of coronal ion lines; Parker Solar Probe switchbacks; IRIS and Solar Orbiter observations
implication_if_solved: Would allow prediction of space weather and solar wind acceleration

phenomenon: Coronal heating related solar wind acceleration
observation_summary: The solar wind is accelerated to hundreds of kilometers per second beyond what thermal expansion alone predicts
why_it_resists_explanation: The acceleration region is close to the Sun and was unreachable until recently
leading_hypotheses: Wave-driven acceleration by Alfven waves; interchange reconnection in coronal funnels (supported by Parker Solar Probe 2023); turbulent heating
mainstream_view: Active and progressing; interchange reconnection is gaining support
testable_prediction: Perihelion passes should show predicted magnetic switchback and energy flux signatures
key_evidence_or_cases: Parker 1958 prediction; Parker Solar Probe switchback observations; Ulysses fast and slow wind structure
implication_if_solved: Would complete space weather forecasting from source to Earth

observation_summary: A storm larger than Earth has persisted for at least 190 years and possibly 360, far longer than terrestrial storms, while shrinking in recent decades
why_it_resists_explanation: The vertical structure and energy supply were unknown until Juno, and the long-term stability mechanism is still not fully modeled
leading_hypotheses: Energy feeding from surrounding jets and vortex mergers; depth extending hundreds of kilometers providing stability (Juno gravity data); absence of a solid surface eliminating friction
mainstream_view: Partly explained by its depth and the absence of a dissipating surface; the detailed lifetime and shrinkage remain open
testable_prediction: Continued Juno monitoring should track depth and vorticity changes against models
key_evidence_or_cases: Cassini and Hooke early observations; Juno microwave and gravity depth sounding; measured shrinkage since 1870s
implication_if_solved: Would advance understanding of planetary atmospheric dynamics generally

phenomenon: Venus atmospheric anomalies and possible phosphine
observation_summary: A reported phosphine detection, unexplained ultraviolet absorbers, and atmospheric chemical disequilibrium in the Venus clouds
why_it_resists_explanation: The phosphine detection is contested on data-processing grounds, and in-situ measurements are decades old and sparse
leading_hypotheses: Unknown abiotic phosphorus chemistry; volcanic delivery of phosphides; microbial life in the cloud layer (speculative); the detection is a data artifact or sulfur dioxide misassignment
mainstream_view: Phosphine detection is not established; reanalyses dispute it. The unknown UV absorber remains a genuine open question
testable_prediction: Dedicated missions such as DAVINCI and Rocket Lab Venus Life Finder should measure cloud composition directly
key_evidence_or_cases: Greaves et al 2020 phosphine claim; Villanueva et al rebuttal; Pioneer Venus legacy data reanalysis
implication_if_solved: Would either find a biosignature or reveal unknown planetary chemistry

observation_summary: Titan shows an unexplained hydrogen and acetylene depletion gradient, and Enceladus plumes contain molecular hydrogen and complex organics indicating active chemistry
why_it_resists_explanation: Measurements come from flybys with limited instruments, and abiotic and biotic explanations are not yet distinguishable
leading_hypotheses: Serpentinization-driven hydrogen production in Enceladus; abiotic surface catalysis on Titan; methanogenic life (highly speculative); instrumental and modeling uncertainty in the Titan gradients
mainstream_view: Treated as interesting chemistry warranting investigation, not as evidence of life
testable_prediction: Dragonfly at Titan and a dedicated Enceladus plume mission should measure the relevant species precisely
key_evidence_or_cases: Cassini INMS plume composition; Strobel 2010 Titan hydrogen gradient analysis; detection of phosphates in Enceladus plume 2023
implication_if_solved: Would identify habitable or inhabited environments in the outer solar system

observation_summary: Large cylindrical craters appear suddenly in permafrost with ejecta rings, formed by explosive gas release
why_it_resists_explanation: The formation events are unwitnessed, remote and rapid, and the subsurface gas accumulation process is only partly characterized
leading_hypotheses: Methane and carbon dioxide accumulation in cryopegs and gas hydrates beneath thawing permafrost producing pneumatic explosion; gas migration along faults; cryovolcanism analogues
mainstream_view: Accepted as gas-driven permafrost explosions; the specific gas source and trigger threshold are debated
testable_prediction: Geophysical surveys should detect pressurized gas pockets before eruption, enabling prediction
key_evidence_or_cases: Yamal crater discovery 2014; subsequent craters mapped by satellite; 2024 modeling of osmotic pressure mechanism
implication_if_solved: Would quantify a permafrost carbon feedback and a hazard to infrastructure

phenomenon: Blue holes and underwater sinkhole depths
observation_summary: Vertical submarine shafts hundreds of meters deep with anoxic layers and unique chemistry, some with no measured bottom
why_it_resists_explanation: Access requires technical diving or ROVs, water chemistry prevents standard survey methods, and formation occurred during lower sea levels
leading_hypotheses: Karst dissolution during Pleistocene low sea level followed by flooding; collapse of cave systems; hydrothermal and mixing-zone dissolution
mainstream_view: Formation broadly understood; individual depths and interior structures remain unmapped
testable_prediction: ROV surveys should reveal the predicted karst morphology, and increasingly do
key_evidence_or_cases: Dean Blue Hole; Dragon Hole Sansha Yongle 300 m; Taam Ja Blue Hole measured over 420 m in 2024
implication_if_solved: Would map ancient sea-level records and extreme-environment ecosystems

observation_summary: Large soft-bodied organisms with quilted fractal body plans that cannot be confidently assigned to any living kingdom
why_it_resists_explanation: They have no close living relatives, preservation is as impressions, and internal anatomy is largely lost
leading_hypotheses: A failed experiment in multicellularity (Vendobionta, Seilacher); early animals including cnidarian and bilaterian grade forms (supported for Dickinsonia by cholesterol biomarkers); fungi or lichens; colonial protists
mainstream_view: At least some, notably Dickinsonia, are now identified as animals via biomarkers; many remain unclassifiable
testable_prediction: Biomarker analysis of additional taxa should resolve kingdom-level affinities one by one
key_evidence_or_cases: Mistaken Point and Ediacara Hills assemblages; Bobrovskiy 2018 cholesteroid biomarkers in Dickinsonia; Charnia
implication_if_solved: Would clarify the origin of animals and early multicellular experimentation

observation_summary: Atmospheric oxygen rose sharply hundreds of millions of years after oxygenic photosynthesis evolved, and the delay is unexplained
why_it_resists_explanation: The oxygen sinks and the timing of cyanobacterial origin are both poorly constrained by proxies
leading_hypotheses: Gradual saturation of reduced sinks such as iron and sulfide; decline in volcanic reductant delivery; nickel famine limiting methanogens; tectonic change in continental weathering; a delayed evolutionary innovation
mainstream_view: The event is well documented; its timing and the length of the delay remain contested
testable_prediction: Improved molecular clocks for cyanobacteria plus better redox proxies should close the gap
key_evidence_or_cases: Mass-independent sulfur isotope fractionation disappearance; banded iron formations; red bed appearance
implication_if_solved: Would explain the prerequisite for all complex life on Earth

observation_summary: Evidence suggests near-global glaciation possibly reaching the equator, and escaping a fully frozen state requires extreme conditions
why_it_resists_explanation: Ice-albedo feedback makes a full freeze very hard to exit, requiring enormous carbon dioxide buildup, and the evidence for full versus partial freezing is contested
leading_hypotheses: Carbon dioxide accumulation from volcanism over millions of years with weathering shut down; slushball Earth with an open tropical ocean; dust and organic darkening of ice; methane release
mainstream_view: Widely accepted that severe glaciations occurred; the full-freeze versus slushball debate and the exit mechanism are active
testable_prediction: Modeling plus cap-carbonate isotope records should constrain the required CO2 levels
key_evidence_or_cases: Low-latitude glacial deposits; cap carbonates; Harland and Kirschvink paleomagnetic work; Hoffman snowball synthesis
implication_if_solved: Would reveal how habitable a planet can remain through extreme climate states

observation_summary: About 81 percent of marine species died in the largest known extinction, with the detailed kill mechanism and sequence still debated
why_it_resists_explanation: Multiple stressors coincide within the resolution of the rock record, making causal ordering difficult
leading_hypotheses: Siberian Traps volcanism driving CO2 release, ocean anoxia, acidification and warming; methane clathrate release; hydrogen sulfide poisoning from euxinic oceans; coal combustion by intruded sills; a cascade of all of these
mainstream_view: Siberian Traps volcanism is the accepted trigger; the precise kill chain and timing resolution remain open
testable_prediction: High-precision zircon dating and proxy records should resolve the sequence to within thousands of years
key_evidence_or_cases: Siberian Traps dating; Meishan section geochemistry; carbon isotope excursion; ocean anoxia proxies
implication_if_solved: Would inform the consequences of rapid carbon release for modern climate

phenomenon: Ocean twilight zone biomass and migration
observation_summary: The largest animal migration on Earth occurs nightly, with biomass estimates uncertain by an order of magnitude
why_it_resists_explanation: Acoustic methods misestimate biomass due to avoidance behavior and swimbladder variability, and nets undersample
leading_hypotheses: Mesopelagic fish biomass between one and twenty billion tonnes; acoustic target strength uncertainty; gear avoidance biasing all historical estimates
mainstream_view: Recognized as a major gap; the uncertainty has direct climate and fisheries implications
testable_prediction: Combined acoustic, eDNA and optical surveys should converge on a biomass estimate
key_evidence_or_cases: Deep scattering layer discovery; Malaspina expedition estimates; Ocean Twilight Zone project data
implication_if_solved: Would resolve a large uncertainty in the ocean carbon pump

phenomenon: Dark oxygen production on the abyssal seafloor
observation_summary: Oxygen was reported to be produced in complete darkness at the seafloor, apparently by polymetallic nodules acting as natural batteries
why_it_resists_explanation: The measurement is new, methodologically contested, and deep-sea in situ oxygen measurement is prone to artifacts
leading_hypotheses: Electrochemical seawater splitting by nodule voltage differences; measurement artifacts from chamber incubation and sensor handling; microbial processes
mainstream_view: A striking new claim under active scrutiny; several groups have raised methodological objections
testable_prediction: Independent in situ replication with different sensor types is the decisive test
key_evidence_or_cases: Sweetman et al Nature Geoscience 2024; nodule voltage measurements; published critiques 2024-2025
implication_if_solved: Would revise deep-sea biogeochemistry and the environmental case around seabed mining

phenomenon: Microbial dark matter and unculturable majority
observation_summary: The vast majority of microbial species cannot be grown in the laboratory, and entire phyla are known only from DNA sequences
why_it_resists_explanation: Growth requirements are unknown and often depend on interspecies dependencies that are hard to reconstruct
leading_hypotheses: Obligate syntrophic dependencies requiring partner organisms; unknown growth factors; extremely slow growth rates; dormancy states; candidate phyla radiation with reduced genomes
mainstream_view: Accepted as a major gap; metagenomics has revealed the diversity without enabling culture
testable_prediction: Co-culture and reduced-genome analysis should identify the missing dependencies
key_evidence_or_cases: Great plate count anomaly; candidate phyla radiation genomes; Asgard archaea culturing success after 12 years
implication_if_solved: Would unlock a vast reservoir of unknown biology and biochemistry

observation_summary: Viruses larger than some bacteria with genomes up to 2.5 million base pairs and hundreds of genes of unknown origin
why_it_resists_explanation: Their phylogenetic position is ambiguous and the direction of genome evolution is disputed
leading_hypotheses: Reduction from an ancestral cellular lineage constituting a fourth domain; gene accretion from hosts by a smaller ancestral virus; a mixture of both
mainstream_view: Existence and importance accepted; origin genuinely contested
testable_prediction: Discovery of intermediate forms and better phylogenomic methods should resolve the direction of evolution
key_evidence_or_cases: Mimivirus 2003; Pandoravirus 2013; Pithovirus from permafrost 2014; Medusavirus
implication_if_solved: Would affect the definition of life and the structure of the tree of life

observation_summary: Animal genomes contain genes apparently acquired from bacteria, fungi and plants, which should be blocked by the germline barrier
why_it_resists_explanation: Contamination in sequencing data has caused several false claims, so each case requires careful verification
leading_hypotheses: Transfer via viral vectors and endosymbionts; transfer during early development before germline segregation; many claimed cases are contamination artifacts
mainstream_view: Some cases are solidly established (bdelloid rotifers, coffee berry borer, aphid carotenoid genes); the frequency and mechanism remain open
testable_prediction: Long-read sequencing of chromosomal context distinguishes real integration from contamination
key_evidence_or_cases: Bdelloid rotifer foreign genes; Tardigrade HGT claim largely retracted as contamination; aphid fungal carotenoid genes
implication_if_solved: Would revise models of how animal genomes acquire novelty

phenomenon: Sexual reproduction and the paradox of sex
observation_summary: Sex halves the genetic contribution of each parent and costs time and risk, yet is nearly universal in eukaryotes
why_it_resists_explanation: Theoretical advantages are demonstrable in models but hard to measure as sufficient in the field; asexual lineages do persist in some cases
leading_hypotheses: Red Queen coevolution with parasites; purging of deleterious mutations (Muller ratchet avoidance); faster adaptation through recombination; DNA repair origin with later co-option
mainstream_view: Multiple partial explanations with experimental support; no single sufficient account
testable_prediction: Experimental evolution under parasite pressure should favor sexual lineages, which it does in several systems
key_evidence_or_cases: Snail and nematode Red Queen experiments; bdelloid rotifer ancient asexuality as a counterexample; Lively Potamopyrgus work
notable_names: Weismann; Williams; Maynard Smith; Lively; Otto
implication_if_solved: Would explain why nearly all complex life reproduces this way

phenomenon: Dinosaur to bird and the origin of flight
observation_summary: Powered flight evolved from terrestrial dinosaurs, but the functional sequence of feather and wing evolution before flight is unresolved
why_it_resists_explanation: Intermediate function must be inferred from morphology, and feathers evolved long before flight for other reasons
leading_hypotheses: Wing-assisted incline running; trees-down gliding origin; flapping for prey pursuit or display then co-option; thermoregulatory and display origin of feathers followed by exaptation
mainstream_view: Avian origin from theropods is settled; the specific flight-origin pathway is debated
testable_prediction: Biomechanical modeling of fossil taxa plus studies of extant chick wing-assisted running constrain the options
key_evidence_or_cases: Archaeopteryx; feathered dinosaurs from Liaoning; Microraptor four-wing form; chukar wing-assisted incline running studies
implication_if_solved: Would explain the origin of the most successful vertebrate flight lineage

observation_summary: Habitual upright walking evolved before large brains and tools, and the selective driver is not established
why_it_resists_explanation: The fossil record of the critical period is sparse, and the proposed drivers are not mutually exclusive or easily tested
leading_hypotheses: Energy efficiency in open habitats; freeing hands for carrying food and infants; thermoregulation in open sun; arboreal bipedal ancestry on flexible branches; display and reach for feeding
mainstream_view: Timing is well constrained by fossils; the driver remains genuinely open
testable_prediction: New fossils from 8-6 million years ago plus energetics modeling should narrow the candidates
key_evidence_or_cases: Laetoli footprints; Ardipithecus and Orrorin postcrania; Sahelanthropus femur; energetics of human versus chimp walking
implication_if_solved: Would explain the defining anatomical shift of the human lineage

observation_summary: Neanderthals Denisovans and other archaic humans vanished after hundreds of thousands of years, overlapping with modern humans
why_it_resists_explanation: Dating resolution near the extinction window is coarse, and competition, interbreeding and climate all operated simultaneously
leading_hypotheses: Competitive exclusion by modern humans with better networks and technology; absorption through interbreeding into modern populations; small population sizes and inbreeding load; climate instability; disease exchange
mainstream_view: Multi-causal, with low population size and competitive replacement plus genetic absorption favored
testable_prediction: Improved radiocarbon dating and ancient DNA from the final millennia should order the causes
key_evidence_or_cases: Vindija and Mezmaiskaya dates; 1 to 4 percent Neanderthal ancestry in modern non-Africans; Denisovan ancestry in Oceania; hybrid individuals like Oase 1
implication_if_solved: Would explain why only one human species remains

observation_summary: Certain cohomology classes on algebraic varieties behave as though they come from subvarieties, and in every verified case they do, but no proof exists
why_it_resists_explanation: The conjecture relates topology to algebraic geometry across a gap no construction bridges; known cases rely on special structure that does not generalize
leading_hypotheses: Full conjecture is true; it fails in high codimension; it requires a motivic framework not yet built
mainstream_view: Clay Millennium Prize problem; believed true, proven only for divisors and some special varieties
testable_prediction: A counterexample Hodge class with no algebraic representative would settle it
key_evidence_or_cases: Lefschetz 1 1 theorem; verified cases for abelian varieties; Grothendieck standard conjectures
implication_if_solved: Would unify topology and algebraic geometry

observation_summary: The number of rational points on an elliptic curve appears encoded in the behavior of its L-function at a specific point, matching in every computation
why_it_resists_explanation: Connecting an analytic object to arithmetic rank requires machinery that exists only in low-rank cases
leading_hypotheses: The conjecture is true; Iwasawa theory and Euler systems will extend current partial results
mainstream_view: Clay Millennium Prize problem; proven for rank 0 and 1 under conditions, widely believed in general
testable_prediction: Computation of ranks for high-rank curves continues to match the prediction
key_evidence_or_cases: Coates-Wiles theorem; Gross-Zagier formula; Kolyvagin Euler systems; extensive numerical verification
implication_if_solved: Would give an effective method for finding rational solutions to cubic equations

observation_summary: All 51 known perfect numbers are even and no odd perfect number exists below 10 to the 1500, yet none is proven impossible
why_it_resists_explanation: Constraints accumulate without closing: an odd perfect number must satisfy dozens of incompatible-looking conditions simultaneously without a contradiction being derivable
leading_hypotheses: No odd perfect numbers exist; one exists above all computational bounds
mainstream_view: Open since antiquity; believed none exist
testable_prediction: Any proof must either construct one or derive a contradiction from the divisor conditions
key_evidence_or_cases: Euclid-Euler theorem for even perfect numbers; Ochem and Rao bound; at least 101 prime factors required
implication_if_solved: Would close one of the oldest questions in mathematics

observation_summary: The digits of pi pass every statistical randomness test over 100 trillion digits, yet it is unproven that each digit block occurs with expected frequency
why_it_resists_explanation: Proving normality requires controlling all digit blocks at once, and no technique handles any natural constant
leading_hypotheses: Pi is normal in every base; normality is provable only for artificially constructed numbers
mainstream_view: Universally believed; unproven for pi e and every other natural constant
testable_prediction: Statistical tests on computed digits continue to show normality, and they do
key_evidence_or_cases: Bailey-Crandall analysis; 100 trillion digits computed 2022; proven normality of the Champernowne constant
implication_if_solved: Would settle the randomness of fundamental constants

observation_summary: Gamma appears throughout analysis and has been computed to over a trillion digits with no pattern, yet it is not known to be irrational
why_it_resists_explanation: No series or continued fraction representation of gamma has yielded to the standard irrationality criteria that worked for e and pi
leading_hypotheses: Gamma is irrational and transcendental; a proof requires a new approach to its integral representations
mainstream_view: Believed irrational and transcendental; completely unproven
testable_prediction: The continued fraction shows no eventual periodicity, which is consistent with irrationality
key_evidence_or_cases: Computation to 10 to the 13 digits; if rational its denominator exceeds 10 to the 242080
implication_if_solved: Would resolve the status of a constant as fundamental as pi and e

observation_summary: The exact value is known only to lie between 43 and 48 after decades of work, and cannot be pinned down even with modern computing
why_it_resists_explanation: The search space grows faster than any feasible exhaustive method, and the known bounds come from arguments that do not tighten further
leading_hypotheses: The value is 43; it is 44 or 45; resolution needs a fundamentally new combinatorial method
mainstream_view: Famously hard; Erdos quipped that aliens demanding R(5 5) should be fought rather than computed for
testable_prediction: Narrowing the interval by exhaustive search or by structural argument
key_evidence_or_cases: R(4 4) equals 18 computed; 2023 exponential improvement on general Ramsey upper bounds
implication_if_solved: Would mark a breakthrough in extremal combinatorics

observation_summary: With n runners at distinct constant speeds each appears always to become lonely at some moment, verified for up to seven runners
why_it_resists_explanation: The problem resists induction because the cases interact, and simultaneous Diophantine approximation geometry is poorly controlled
leading_hypotheses: The conjecture holds for all n; counterexamples exist for large n
mainstream_view: Open; proven for up to seven runners
testable_prediction: Verification for eight runners would be strong evidence either way
key_evidence_or_cases: Wills 1967 formulation; Barajas and Serra proof for seven runners 2008
implication_if_solved: Would advance simultaneous Diophantine approximation

phenomenon: Kissing numbers in dimensions five six and seven
observation_summary: The maximum number of unit spheres touching a central sphere is known exactly in dimensions 1 2 3 4 8 and 24 but not in 5 6 or 7
why_it_resists_explanation: The solved dimensions have exceptional lattice structure; intermediate dimensions lack the symmetry that makes linear programming bounds tight
leading_hypotheses: The answer is 40 in dimension five; semidefinite programming bounds will eventually close the gap
mainstream_view: Open; bounded between 40 and 44 in dimension five
testable_prediction: Improved semidefinite programming relaxations should close the bounds
key_evidence_or_cases: Newton-Gregory dispute over dimension three; Musin dimension four proof 2003; Viazovska dimensions 8 and 24
implication_if_solved: Would complete the low-dimensional sphere packing picture

observation_summary: In any family closed under unions some element appears to belong to at least half the sets, verified widely but long unproven
why_it_resists_explanation: The statement is elementary yet every attempted induction fails; the 2022 breakthrough came from an unexpected information-theoretic angle
leading_hypotheses: The constant is one half; the entropy method will be pushed from roughly 0.38 to one half
mainstream_view: Nearly solved: Gilmer 2022 proved a constant bound, since improved to about 0.38
testable_prediction: Pushing the entropy argument to one half would complete it
key_evidence_or_cases: Frankl 1979 conjecture; Gilmer entropy breakthrough 2022; rapid follow-up improvements
implication_if_solved: Already a landmark case of a new proof technique appearing suddenly

observation_summary: Whether every bounded operator on a separable Hilbert space has a nontrivial closed invariant subspace was open for about 90 years
why_it_resists_explanation: Counterexamples were found in Banach spaces but Hilbert space rigidity blocked both construction and proof
leading_hypotheses: Enflo and separately Neville posted claimed counterexamples in 2023; verification is ongoing
mainstream_view: A claimed counterexample exists but the community has not finished verifying it
testable_prediction: Peer verification of the 2023 constructions
key_evidence_or_cases: Enflo Banach space counterexample 1976; Read 1984; Enflo 2023 Hilbert space preprint
implication_if_solved: Would complete the structure theory of Hilbert space operators

phenomenon: abc conjecture and the Mochizuki dispute
observation_summary: A deep relation between addition and multiplication of integers is strongly supported numerically, but a claimed 500-page proof is rejected by key experts
why_it_resists_explanation: The claimed proof uses a self-contained framework that almost nobody else can verify, and one specific inference is disputed
leading_hypotheses: The conjecture is true and the proof is valid; the proof has a gap at Corollary 3.12; the conjecture is true but needs different methods
mainstream_view: The conjecture is widely believed; the Mochizuki proof is accepted in Japan and rejected by Scholze Stix and most other experts
testable_prediction: Independent reconstruction of the disputed corollary either way
key_evidence_or_cases: Mochizuki IUT papers 2012 and 2021 publication; Scholze-Stix report 2018; numerical verification of abc triples
implication_if_solved: Would imply Fermat-type results and transform Diophantine geometry

observation_summary: Dimension four is uniquely resistant: the topological version is proven and all other dimensions are settled, but the smooth version remains open
why_it_resists_explanation: Four dimensions is too large for low-dimensional geometric methods and too small for surgery theory to apply
leading_hypotheses: Every smooth manifold homotopy equivalent to the 4-sphere is diffeomorphic to it; exotic 4-spheres exist
mainstream_view: Open; widely regarded as the last Poincare case and among the hardest problems in topology
testable_prediction: Construction of an exotic 4-sphere or a proof of uniqueness
key_evidence_or_cases: Freedman topological classification 1982; Donaldson invariants; exotic R4 existence; Gluck twists
implication_if_solved: Would complete the classification of manifolds in every dimension

locus: Polynomial vector fields in the plane
observation_summary: Whether polynomial differential equations of a given degree have a bounded number of limit cycles is unknown even for quadratic systems
why_it_resists_explanation: Limit cycles can accumulate in ways that resist all known finiteness arguments; the related Dulac problem took 90 years to resolve
leading_hypotheses: A uniform bound exists; the bound depends computably on degree; no uniform bound exists
mainstream_view: Open and considered among the hardest Hilbert problems still standing
testable_prediction: Determining the maximum number of limit cycles for quadratic systems, known to be at least four
key_evidence_or_cases: Dulac finiteness proven by Ilyashenko and Ecalle; quadratic examples with four limit cycles
implication_if_solved: Would ground the qualitative theory of differential equations

observation_summary: Trajectories in nearly integrable systems can drift arbitrarily far in action space over long times, observed numerically but only partly proven
why_it_resists_explanation: The mechanism requires chains of hyperbolic structures whose existence is hard to establish for generic systems
leading_hypotheses: Diffusion is generic with three or more degrees of freedom; variational and geometric methods now under development will complete the proof
mainstream_view: Partially proven for specific classes; the generic case is open
testable_prediction: Numerical experiments show diffusion rates matching predictions in a priori unstable systems
key_evidence_or_cases: Arnold 1964 example; Mather theory; Bernard-Kaloshin-Zhang results; solar system integrations
implication_if_solved: Would determine the long-term stability of planetary systems

phenomenon: Long-term stability of the solar system
observation_summary: Integrations show the inner solar system is marginally chaotic with a small chance of Mercury destabilizing within five billion years, and the true outcome cannot be computed
why_it_resists_explanation: The Lyapunov time is about five million years, so integrations lose predictive power long before the Sun dies, and results depend on tiny initial-condition differences
leading_hypotheses: The system is chaotic but statistically stable; Mercury has roughly a one percent destabilization chance; relativistic corrections matter at the margin
mainstream_view: The chaotic nature is established; specific outcomes are irreducibly probabilistic
testable_prediction: Ensemble integrations give a probability distribution rather than a prediction
key_evidence_or_cases: Laskar and Gastineau 2009 ensemble integrations; Sussman and Wisdom chaos detection; Mercury-Jupiter resonance
implication_if_solved: Would determine the ultimate fate of the planets

observation_summary: No closed-form general solution exists and the system is chaotic, yet new families of periodic orbits keep being discovered numerically
why_it_resists_explanation: The system is provably non-integrable, so solutions exist only as series or numerically, and the family space appears unbounded
leading_hypotheses: No closed form exists; the periodic families are infinite and still being catalogued
mainstream_view: Non-integrability is proven; orbit classification is an ongoing discovery process
testable_prediction: Numerical searches continue to find new periodic families, and they do
key_evidence_or_cases: Poincare non-integrability; Sundman series; figure-eight orbit 1993; thousands of families catalogued since 2017
implication_if_solved: Would complete the classification of a foundational dynamical system

phenomenon: Zeta zero spacing matching random matrices
locus: Zeros of the Riemann zeta function
observation_summary: Spacing statistics of zeta zeros match the eigenvalue statistics of random Hermitian matrices to extraordinary precision, with no proven reason
why_it_resists_explanation: No operator whose eigenvalues are the zeros has been identified, so the agreement is an unexplained empirical coincidence
leading_hypotheses: A self-adjoint operator exists whose spectrum gives the zeros; the quantum chaos analogy reflects deeper structure; it follows from unproven correlation conjectures
mainstream_view: The numerical agreement is accepted as remarkable; the explanation is entirely absent
testable_prediction: Higher-order correlation statistics should keep matching the Gaussian unitary ensemble, and they do
key_evidence_or_cases: Montgomery pair correlation 1973; Odlyzko computations near the 10 to the 20th zero; Keating-Snaith moment conjectures
implication_if_solved: Would likely prove the Riemann hypothesis via a spectral interpretation

observation_summary: Leading digits of many real-world datasets follow a logarithmic distribution with digit one appearing about 30 percent of the time
why_it_resists_explanation: The law holds across an enormous range of unrelated datasets with no single criterion predicting which datasets obey it
leading_hypotheses: Scale invariance and multiplicative processes; mixtures of distributions converging to the log law; base invariance; no universal criterion exists
mainstream_view: Explained for specific mechanisms; the universality across unrelated domains is still not fully accounted for
testable_prediction: Datasets generated by identified multiplicative processes should obey the law, and they generally do
key_evidence_or_cases: Newcomb 1881; Benford 1938 survey of 20 datasets; Hill 1995 random-mixture theorem; forensic accounting use
implication_if_solved: Already used in fraud detection; a full explanation would sharpen its applicability

phenomenon: Zipf law in language and city sizes
observation_summary: Rank-frequency distributions follow a power law with exponent near one across unrelated domains and every human language
why_it_resists_explanation: Many generative mechanisms produce power laws, so observing one does not identify the cause, and the near-universal exponent of one is unexplained
leading_hypotheses: Preferential attachment and proportional growth; optimization of communication cost; random typing models producing Zipf trivially; multiplicative noise under constraints
mainstream_view: The pattern is robust and documented; no single explanation has won out and some argue it is statistically shallow
testable_prediction: Mechanistic models should predict tail deviations as well as the bulk, where they often fail
key_evidence_or_cases: Zipf 1935; Heaps law companion; Li critiques using random text; cross-linguistic corpus studies
notable_names: Estoup; Zipf; Mandelbrot; Ferrer i Cancho
implication_if_solved: Would explain a striking regularity spanning language and economics

locus: Sandpiles earthquakes forest fires neural avalanches
observation_summary: Many natural systems sit near a critical point producing power-law event sizes with no tuned control parameter
why_it_resists_explanation: Why systems should self-tune to criticality is not derivable in general, and many claimed examples fail rigorous power-law tests
leading_hypotheses: Dissipative driven systems reach a critical attractor naturally; apparent criticality from mixtures of exponentials; criticality as an evolved optimum in neural tissue
mainstream_view: Influential framework; many specific claimed instances have been challenged on statistical grounds
testable_prediction: Rigorous model selection against alternative heavy-tailed distributions, which often fails to favor power laws
key_evidence_or_cases: Bak-Tang-Wiesenfeld sandpile 1987; Gutenberg-Richter law; neuronal avalanche recordings; Clauset power-law testing critiques
implication_if_solved: Would explain scale-free behavior across many natural systems

observation_summary: Complexity appears to increase over evolutionary and cosmic time in a way no law requires, with no agreed measure of complexity to even test the claim
why_it_resists_explanation: There is no accepted definition of complexity so the phenomenon cannot be measured, and natural selection does not inherently favor complexity
leading_hypotheses: Passive diffusion into available complexity space; energy-flow-driven complexification; constructive neutral evolution; an artifact of a left wall at minimum complexity
mainstream_view: Contested at the level of whether the phenomenon is even real, because the metric is undefined
testable_prediction: A rigorous complexity measure applied to the fossil and genomic record would test the trend
key_evidence_or_cases: Maximum body size trends; genome size distributions; McShea and Brandon zero-force law; assembly theory proposals
implication_if_solved: Would tell us whether complexity is an expected outcome of physics

observation_summary: A proposed measure claims to detect selection and life from molecular complexity alone, with its novelty and validity sharply disputed
why_it_resists_explanation: The claimed independence from existing information theory is contested and the empirical demonstrations are limited
leading_hypotheses: Assembly theory captures a genuinely new physical quantity; it restates existing complexity measures; it is a useful heuristic without new physics
mainstream_view: Highly contested since publication; many complexity scientists argue it reproduces known results
testable_prediction: Blind application to unknown samples should separate biotic from abiotic origin, which is partly demonstrated
key_evidence_or_cases: Marshall et al Nature 2023; mass spectrometry molecular assembly index measurements; published critiques 2023 and 2024
implication_if_solved: Would provide an agnostic biosignature for life detection if valid

observation_summary: Hundreds of proteins perform completely unrelated second functions, which one-gene-one-function logic does not predict
why_it_resists_explanation: Second functions are discovered by accident, so true prevalence is unknown and there is no way to predict which proteins moonlight
leading_hypotheses: Gene sharing under selection for economy; evolutionary accidents retained because harmless; latent surface properties of all folded proteins
mainstream_view: Accepted and catalogued; prevalence and predictability unknown
testable_prediction: Systematic interaction screens should reveal moonlighting functions at a predictable rate
key_evidence_or_cases: Crystallin and enolase dual roles; cytochrome c in apoptosis; MoonProt database
implication_if_solved: Would complicate and enrich functional genome annotation

locus: About a third of the eukaryotic proteome
observation_summary: Many functional proteins have no fixed structure, contradicting the structure-function paradigm that dominated biology for decades
why_it_resists_explanation: Disorder is invisible to crystallography and function emerges from an ensemble rather than a shape, which existing frameworks were not built to describe
leading_hypotheses: Function through binding-induced folding; entropic chains and fuzzy complexes; phase separation into condensates; conformational ensembles as the functional unit
mainstream_view: Fully accepted as real and important; predictive understanding of ensemble function is immature
testable_prediction: Ensemble models should predict binding affinities and condensate behavior from sequence alone
key_evidence_or_cases: p53 transactivation domain; FUS and tau disorder; AlphaFold low-confidence regions mapping onto disorder
implication_if_solved: Would complete the structure-function framework of molecular biology

observation_summary: Membraneless organelles appear to form by liquid-liquid phase separation, and the breadth of this claim is contested
why_it_resists_explanation: In vitro phase separation often occurs at concentrations far from physiological, so in vivo relevance is hard to establish for many claimed condensates
leading_hypotheses: Phase separation organizes much of cell biochemistry; many claimed condensates are artifacts of overexpression and tagging; a smaller genuine set plus artifacts
mainstream_view: Real for structures such as nucleoli and stress granules; the general claim is under significant criticism
testable_prediction: Endogenous-level imaging and quantitative thermodynamics should distinguish real condensates from artifacts
key_evidence_or_cases: P granule phase behavior 2009; nucleolus and stress granules; McSwiggen and Darzacq critiques 2019
implication_if_solved: Would restructure understanding of intracellular organization

observation_summary: Some studies report environmentally induced traits persisting several generations without DNA sequence change, which germline reprogramming should erase
why_it_resists_explanation: The mammalian germline erases most epigenetic marks so a carrier mechanism is required, and many studies lack enough generations or controls for confounds
leading_hypotheses: Small RNA carriers in sperm; retained methylation at specific loci; microbiome and in utero effects mistaken for inheritance; experimental artifacts
mainstream_view: Well established in plants and nematodes; contested and weakly supported in mammals
testable_prediction: Rigorous studies through four or more generations with cross-fostering and microbiome controls
key_evidence_or_cases: Dias and Ressler odor fear studies; Dutch Hunger Winter cohorts; agouti mouse methylation; critiques by Heard and Martienssen
implication_if_solved: Would change inheritance models and public health reasoning about exposures

observation_summary: Cells from a fetus persist in the mother for decades and migrate into her brain heart and other organs, with unclear consequences
why_it_resists_explanation: The cells are rare and hard to track, and outcomes are confounded by many variables over decades
leading_hypotheses: Protective tissue repair contributions; contribution to autoimmune disease risk; immune tolerance effects; mostly inconsequential passengers
mainstream_view: Phenomenon established; functional consequences genuinely unknown
testable_prediction: Longitudinal cohorts tracking microchimeric load against disease outcomes
key_evidence_or_cases: Male DNA found in maternal brain tissue; fetal cells in maternal cardiac repair; autoimmune correlation studies
implication_if_solved: Would illuminate maternal health risks and tissue regeneration

phenomenon: Causal role of the human microbiome
observation_summary: Microbiome composition correlates with conditions from obesity to depression, but causal direction is rarely established
why_it_resists_explanation: Correlational studies dominate, germ-free mouse models translate poorly, and the system has thousands of interacting variables
leading_hypotheses: Specific taxa causally drive host phenotypes; host state shapes the microbiome rather than the reverse; metabolite-level effects independent of taxonomy; confounding by diet
mainstream_view: Associations are robust; causal claims are widely considered overstated outside a few cases such as C difficile
testable_prediction: Randomized interventional transfers in humans with hard outcomes, which are rarely done
key_evidence_or_cases: Fecal microbiota transplant efficacy in C difficile; obesity transfer in mice; replication failures in human cohorts
implication_if_solved: Would open or close an entire therapeutic strategy

observation_summary: Gut state influences mood and cognition through pathways that are only partly mapped, with large claimed effects and weak human evidence
why_it_resists_explanation: Vagal immune endocrine and metabolite pathways operate simultaneously, and human studies cannot isolate them
leading_hypotheses: Vagal afferent signaling; short-chain fatty acids entering circulation; immune mediated effects; serotonin precursor availability; publication bias inflating effect sizes
mainstream_view: Pathways exist and are real; the magnitude of effect on human mood and behavior is contested
testable_prediction: Vagotomy and selective pathway blockade in animals plus rigorous human probiotic trials
key_evidence_or_cases: Germ-free mouse behavioral differences; vagotomy abolishing some effects; mixed probiotic trial results in depression
implication_if_solved: Would legitimize or deflate a large area of health claims

observation_summary: DNA methylation at specific sites predicts chronological and biological age with striking accuracy by an unknown mechanism
why_it_resists_explanation: Clock sites were found by machine learning on correlation, so what they measure causally is unknown and whether they drive aging or record it is open
leading_hypotheses: An epigenetic maintenance program drifting with time; a record of cell division history; a response to accumulated damage; a readout of stochastic methylation noise
mainstream_view: Predictive power accepted and widely used; causal interpretation unresolved
testable_prediction: Interventions that reverse clock age should extend lifespan if the clock is causal, which is being tested
key_evidence_or_cases: Horvath multi-tissue clock 2013; partial reprogramming resetting clocks in mice; clock acceleration in disease
implication_if_solved: Would provide a biomarker endpoint for longevity trials

observation_summary: Naked mole rats almost never develop cancer and live over 30 years, roughly ten times the lifespan predicted for their body size
why_it_resists_explanation: The responsible mechanisms are multiple and species-specific, and no single factor has transferred cleanly to other species
leading_hypotheses: High molecular weight hyaluronan causing early contact inhibition; unusual ribosomal RNA processing with high translational fidelity; cell-cycle arrest mechanisms; altered p53 pathways
mainstream_view: Several mechanisms identified; the full picture and transferability remain open
testable_prediction: Transgenic expression of mole rat hyaluronan synthase in mice should reduce cancer, and a 2023 study reported lifespan extension
key_evidence_or_cases: Gorbunova and Seluanov hyaluronan work; 2023 transgenic mouse lifespan study; Peto paradox context
implication_if_solved: Would identify transferable cancer-resistance mechanisms

observation_summary: Cancer incidence does not scale with body size across species, so whales with thousands of times more cells than humans are not more cancer-prone
why_it_resists_explanation: Testing requires sparse comparative data, and each lineage may have evolved a different solution
leading_hypotheses: Extra tumor suppressor copies such as 20 copies of TP53 in elephants; hypertumor suppression; slower somatic mutation rates in large animals; lower metabolic rate per cell
mainstream_view: The paradox is real and appears to be resolved differently in each lineage
testable_prediction: Somatic mutation rates should scale inversely with lifespan across species, and a 2022 study found exactly that
key_evidence_or_cases: Elephant TP53 copies; bowhead whale genome; Cagan et al 2022 cross-species somatic mutation rates
implication_if_solved: Would reveal evolved anticancer strategies for therapeutic use

observation_summary: Bowhead whales live over 200 years, the longest of any mammal, with mechanisms only partly characterized
why_it_resists_explanation: Studying a 200-year lifespan requires historical specimens or molecular proxies, both limited
leading_hypotheses: Enhanced double-strand break repair; efficient proteostasis; low metabolic rate in cold water; unique cell cycle regulation
mainstream_view: Longevity established by eye lens racemization and recovered 19th century harpoon points; mechanisms partly identified
testable_prediction: Expressing bowhead DNA repair variants in other species should improve repair fidelity, as recent work reports
key_evidence_or_cases: Ancient harpoon tips found in living whales; aspartic acid racemization dating; bowhead genome studies
implication_if_solved: Would identify longevity mechanisms in a mammal

phenomenon: Biological immortality in hydra and Turritopsis
observation_summary: Hydra shows no measurable senescence and Turritopsis dohrnii can revert from adult to polyp stage apparently indefinitely
why_it_resists_explanation: The reversal involves transdifferentiation of fully differentiated cells, a process mammals cannot perform and which is poorly characterized
leading_hypotheses: Continuous stem cell renewal with FoxO activity in hydra; transdifferentiation and cell cycle re-entry in Turritopsis; absence of a segregated germline constraint
mainstream_view: Phenomena fully accepted; mechanisms partly mapped after 2022 comparative genomics
testable_prediction: Comparative genomics with mortal relatives should identify the required gene set, which 2022 work began
key_evidence_or_cases: Martinez 1998 hydra mortality study; Piraino Turritopsis reversal 1996; 2022 Turritopsis genome paper
implication_if_solved: Would reveal whether senescence is avoidable in principle

observation_summary: Tardigrades survive desiccation vacuum radiation doses 1000 times lethal to humans and temperatures near absolute zero
why_it_resists_explanation: Protection involves several simultaneous molecular systems, and DNA protection under extreme radiation is incompletely understood
leading_hypotheses: Intrinsically disordered CAHS proteins forming protective gels; trehalose vitrification; Dsup protein shielding DNA; efficient post-damage DNA repair
mainstream_view: Mechanisms substantially identified over the last decade; details continue to emerge
testable_prediction: Expressing Dsup and CAHS proteins in human cells should confer radiation and desiccation tolerance, which has partly been shown
key_evidence_or_cases: Dsup discovery 2016; CAHS gel formation studies; survival in open space on FOTON-M3 in 2007
implication_if_solved: Would enable radiation protection and dry preservation of biological material

observation_summary: The bacterium survives thousands of times the radiation dose lethal to humans and reassembles a shattered genome within hours
why_it_resists_explanation: Reassembling hundreds of genome fragments into correct order requires a template logic that is only partly understood
leading_hypotheses: Multiple genome copies enabling extended synthesis-dependent strand annealing; manganese scavenging of reactive oxygen species; condensed nucleoid limiting fragment diffusion
mainstream_view: Mechanisms largely identified; the precise reassembly choreography is incompletely described
testable_prediction: Manganese depletion should abolish resistance, and it does
key_evidence_or_cases: Anderson 1956 discovery in irradiated canned meat; Zahradka genome reassembly 2006; Daly manganese model
implication_if_solved: Would inform radioprotection and DNA repair biology

observation_summary: Whole mitochondria move between cells including into cancer cells, restoring respiration in recipients
why_it_resists_explanation: Transfer routes are hard to image in vivo and physiological importance versus culture artifact is still debated
leading_hypotheses: Tunneling nanotubes; extracellular vesicles; gap junction mediated transfer; uptake of free mitochondria; some observations being culture artifacts
mainstream_view: Accepted in vitro with growing in vivo evidence; functional significance contested
testable_prediction: Lineage-labeled mitochondria tracking in vivo should quantify real transfer rates
key_evidence_or_cases: Spees et al 2006; mitochondrial transfer into tumor cells restoring respiration; cell-free mitochondria in blood 2020
implication_if_solved: Would open mitochondrial transplantation as a therapy

observation_summary: A few cancers have become independent transmissible organisms spreading between hosts as clonal cell lineages for thousands of years
why_it_resists_explanation: How a cancer evades allogeneic immune rejection and persists for about 11000 years without genomic collapse is only partly understood
leading_hypotheses: Loss of MHC expression; low host population genetic diversity; millennia of selection for immune evasion; evolution into an effectively parasitic clonal species
mainstream_view: Fully accepted and genomically characterized; immune evasion and long-term genomic stability remain open
testable_prediction: Genome sequencing across the lineage should reveal mutation accumulation and selection signatures, and it does
key_evidence_or_cases: Canine transmissible venereal tumor dated to about 11000 years; devil facial tumor diseases DFT1 and DFT2; bivalve leukemia crossing species
implication_if_solved: Would illuminate immune evasion and the limits of cancer evolution

observation_summary: Everyone accumulates genetically distinct cell clones with age, including cancer driver mutations, most of which never become cancer
why_it_resists_explanation: Why identical driver mutations cause cancer in some contexts and benign expansion in others is unexplained
leading_hypotheses: Additional required mutations; tissue microenvironment constraints; immune surveillance; clonal competition limiting expansion
mainstream_view: Firmly established and now a recognized cardiovascular and cancer risk factor; determinants of progression are open
testable_prediction: Longitudinal single-cell sequencing should identify which clones progress
key_evidence_or_cases: Genovese and Jaiswal 2014 studies; CHIP cardiovascular risk; driver mutations in normal esophagus and skin
implication_if_solved: Would allow prediction and early interception of cancer

observation_summary: Cells compare fitness with their neighbors and eliminate the less fit, with no known universal sensing mechanism
why_it_resists_explanation: Fitness is a relative quantity and how a cell molecularly measures its neighbor state is unresolved
leading_hypotheses: Myc-level comparison; mechanical crowding and compression; the Flower protein code; secreted factor competition; several parallel mechanisms
mainstream_view: Phenomenon accepted and important in development and cancer; the sensing mechanism is open
testable_prediction: Manipulating candidate sensors should abolish competition specifically
key_evidence_or_cases: Minute mutant Drosophila clones 1975; mammalian Myc supercompetition; Flower isoform studies
implication_if_solved: Would explain tissue homeostasis and early tumour suppression

observation_summary: Neurons communicate with spikes, but how information is represented in those spike patterns is not known in general
why_it_resists_explanation: Candidate codes (rate, timing, population geometry, synchrony) all have support in different systems, and no decoding principle generalizes
leading_hypotheses: Rate coding; precise spike-timing codes; population vector and manifold geometry; predictive coding hierarchies; multiplexed codes varying by region
mainstream_view: Recognized as the central unsolved problem of systems neuroscience
testable_prediction: A correct code would permit reading arbitrary percepts from recordings and writing them in
key_evidence_or_cases: Hubel and Wiesel orientation tuning; place cells and grid cells; population decoding in motor cortex; Neuropixels large-scale recordings
implication_if_solved: Would enable high-fidelity brain interfaces and real understanding of cognition

observation_summary: Neurons fire in a perfect hexagonal lattice tiling the environment, a crystalline representation with no obvious developmental origin
why_it_resists_explanation: Why hexagonal rather than another tiling, and how the lattice is generated and anchored, are only partly explained
leading_hypotheses: Continuous attractor network dynamics; oscillatory interference; efficient coding predicting hexagonal optimality; self-organization from place cell input
mainstream_view: Accepted and Nobel-recognized; the generative mechanism is still debated between attractor and interference models
testable_prediction: Optogenetic perturbation should distort the lattice in model-specific ways
key_evidence_or_cases: Hafting et al 2005 discovery; grid cells in humans and bats; modules of discrete grid scales
implication_if_solved: Would reveal how the brain builds abstract coordinate systems

observation_summary: Place cell sequences replay compressed during rest, and sequences for environments not yet visited appear to occur in advance
why_it_resists_explanation: Preplay challenges the idea that sequences are learned from experience, and the statistical tests for preplay are contested
leading_hypotheses: Preexisting network sequences later assigned to experience; statistical artifacts of place field distributions; schema-based scaffolding of new memories
mainstream_view: Replay is firmly established; preplay is genuinely contested on statistical grounds
testable_prediction: Blind reanalysis with matched surrogate distributions should confirm or dissolve preplay
key_evidence_or_cases: Wilson and McNaughton replay 1994; Dragoi and Tonegawa preplay 2011; critiques by Silva and Foster
implication_if_solved: Would determine whether memory uses preexisting scaffolds

phenomenon: Sharp wave ripples and memory consolidation
observation_summary: Brief high-frequency oscillations accompany memory consolidation, and disrupting them impairs learning, but their computational role is unclear
why_it_resists_explanation: The oscillation is a population-level event whose relation to the information being consolidated is correlational
leading_hypotheses: Compressed replay for cortical transfer; synaptic tagging and capture windows; a clock signal coordinating distributed plasticity
mainstream_view: Causal necessity demonstrated; mechanism of action still being worked out
testable_prediction: Selective ripple disruption should impair only the consolidation of concurrently replayed content
key_evidence_or_cases: Buzsaki ripple characterization; closed-loop ripple disruption studies; human intracranial ripple recordings
implication_if_solved: Would allow targeted enhancement of memory consolidation

observation_summary: A specific network is more active at rest than during tasks, consuming large amounts of energy with no agreed function
why_it_resists_explanation: Defining the function of activity that occurs in the absence of a task is methodologically circular, and the network participates in many processes
leading_hypotheses: Self-referential thought and autobiographical simulation; internal model maintenance; a cost of maintaining readiness; mind wandering; integration of memory and prediction
mainstream_view: Existence and importance accepted; function genuinely open
testable_prediction: Targeted disruption should selectively impair the proposed cognitive functions
key_evidence_or_cases: Raichle 2001 default mode identification; task-induced deactivation; alterations in depression and Alzheimer disease
implication_if_solved: Would explain where most of the brain energy budget goes

phenomenon: High metabolic cost of the resting brain
observation_summary: The brain uses about 20 percent of the body energy budget, and task-related changes alter this by only a few percent
why_it_resists_explanation: What the baseline energy is spent on is not accounted for by measured spiking and synaptic activity alone
leading_hypotheses: Maintenance of ion gradients and membrane potential; ongoing synaptic turnover and protein synthesis; spontaneous activity performing computation; glial metabolic demands
mainstream_view: A recognized accounting gap in neuroenergetics
testable_prediction: Detailed energy budgets per cellular process should sum to the measured total, and currently do not
key_evidence_or_cases: Sokoloff deoxyglucose measurements; Attwell and Laughlin energy budget; fMRI small task-related changes
implication_if_solved: Would reveal what the brain is actually doing when apparently idle

observation_summary: The cerebellum contains most of the brain neurons and contributes to language emotion and cognition, not just motor control
why_it_resists_explanation: Its uniform circuit suggests one computation, yet its functional contributions appear highly diverse and are hard to isolate
leading_hypotheses: Universal forward-model prediction applied to any domain; sequence timing computation; internal model learning generalized beyond movement
mainstream_view: Cognitive role now accepted; the unifying computation remains open
testable_prediction: A single computational account should predict deficits across motor and cognitive domains from the same lesions
key_evidence_or_cases: Cerebellar cognitive affective syndrome; cerebellar activation in language tasks; uniform cerebellar microcircuit anatomy
implication_if_solved: Would identify a general-purpose prediction engine in the brain

observation_summary: Whether new neurons are generated in the adult human hippocampus is directly contested, with high-profile papers reaching opposite conclusions
why_it_resists_explanation: The methods depend on markers whose specificity is debated, and postmortem tissue quality strongly affects detection
