leading_hypotheses: Robust lifelong neurogenesis; negligible neurogenesis after childhood; genuine but very low rates obscured by tissue handling differences
mainstream_view: Directly contested since 2018 with leading labs publishing opposite results in the same year
testable_prediction: Standardized tissue processing and single-cell transcriptomics should resolve the marker disputes
key_evidence_or_cases: Eriksson 1998 BrdU study; Sorrells et al 2018 negative; Boldrini et al 2018 positive; Spalding carbon-14 dating
implication_if_solved: Would determine whether adult brain repair is possible in humans

observation_summary: Specific windows exist when experience shapes circuits permanently, after which the same experience has little effect
why_it_resists_explanation: The molecular brakes that close the window are only partly identified, and reopening them has unpredictable effects
leading_hypotheses: Perineuronal net maturation restricting plasticity; inhibitory circuit maturation setting the window; myelin-associated inhibitory signaling; epigenetic state changes
mainstream_view: Well established with partly identified mechanisms; controlled reopening is not yet achievable
testable_prediction: Degrading perineuronal nets should restore juvenile plasticity, which works in animals
key_evidence_or_cases: Hubel and Wiesel monocular deprivation; chondroitinase reopening ocular dominance plasticity; language acquisition windows
implication_if_solved: Would allow treatment of amblyopia and recovery from early deprivation

locus: Patients with primary visual cortex damage
observation_summary: Patients report seeing nothing yet can guess location and motion of stimuli far above chance, and some navigate obstacles
why_it_resists_explanation: Which surviving pathway supports the performance, and why it produces no awareness, are both unresolved
leading_hypotheses: Retino-collicular and pulvinar pathways bypassing V1; spared V1 islands supporting degraded processing; subcortical dorsal stream processing without access to report
mainstream_view: Accepted as real; the pathway and the absence of awareness remain central puzzles for consciousness research
testable_prediction: High-resolution imaging should show intact alternative pathways in blindsight patients and not in others
key_evidence_or_cases: Weiskrantz patient DB; monkey V1 lesion studies; patient TN navigating an obstacle course
implication_if_solved: Would separate visual processing from visual awareness mechanistically

observation_summary: After the hemispheres are disconnected, each can process information independently, yet patients report a single unified self
why_it_resists_explanation: Whether there are two conscious subjects or one is not resolvable by behavioral report, and recent studies challenge the classic picture
leading_hypotheses: Two streams of consciousness with one verbal reporter; a single consciousness with divided access; the classic split interpretation is overstated
mainstream_view: Classic findings established but the interpretation was significantly challenged by 2017 studies showing preserved unified responding
testable_prediction: Careful testing across response modalities should reveal whether integration survives disconnection
key_evidence_or_cases: Sperry and Gazzaniga studies; Pinto et al 2017 unified response findings; interpreter phenomenon
implication_if_solved: Would clarify whether consciousness is divisible

observation_summary: Patients with obvious paralysis sincerely deny any impairment, sometimes confabulating elaborate explanations
why_it_resists_explanation: Denial persists against overwhelming evidence, implying a disrupted self-monitoring system whose architecture is unknown
leading_hypotheses: Damage to a comparator comparing intention with feedback; disrupted interoceptive and body-model updating; impaired belief revision specific to self
mainstream_view: Well documented clinically; mechanism open and informative for self-modeling theories
testable_prediction: Lesion mapping should identify a consistent self-monitoring network
key_evidence_or_cases: Babinski 1914 description; vestibular stimulation temporarily restoring awareness; lesion overlap studies
implication_if_solved: Would reveal how the brain models and monitors itself

observation_summary: Most amputees feel a vivid phantom limb and many experience pain in a limb that does not exist
why_it_resists_explanation: Cortical remapping correlates with phantom experience but recent work shows preserved limb maps, undercutting the standard explanation
leading_hypotheses: Cortical reorganization of somatosensory maps; persistent peripheral nerve activity; preserved limb representation with disrupted input; predictive body model without sensory confirmation
mainstream_view: Phenomenon certain; the cortical remapping explanation has been substantially challenged since 2013
testable_prediction: Imaging should show either reorganization or preserved maps, and recent high-resolution work finds preservation
key_evidence_or_cases: Mirror box therapy effects; Flor remapping studies; Makin preserved hand representation studies
implication_if_solved: Would redirect treatment for a common and severe chronic pain condition

observation_summary: Severe persistent pain often continues with no detectable ongoing tissue injury and no proportional imaging findings
why_it_resists_explanation: Pain is a central construct, so peripheral measures do not track it, and no objective biomarker exists
leading_hypotheses: Central sensitization and altered descending modulation; nociplastic pain as a distinct mechanism; neuroimmune glial activation; predictive processing with miscalibrated priors
mainstream_view: Recognized as nociplastic pain in current classifications; mechanisms partly characterized and no biomarker exists
testable_prediction: An objective central sensitization marker would allow diagnosis independent of report
key_evidence_or_cases: Fibromyalgia functional imaging; quantitative sensory testing profiles; IASP nociplastic pain category 2017
implication_if_solved: Would validate and target a huge burden of disability

observation_summary: Widespread pain fatigue and cognitive difficulty with no detectable inflammation or structural damage
why_it_resists_explanation: No objective marker exists, diagnostic criteria have shifted repeatedly, and the condition was long dismissed as psychogenic
leading_hypotheses: Central sensitization of pain processing; small fiber neuropathy in a subset; autoimmune mechanisms suggested by 2021 antibody transfer experiments in mice; autonomic dysfunction
mainstream_view: Accepted as a real central pain disorder; pathophysiology genuinely unresolved
testable_prediction: The 2021 IgG passive transfer result should replicate if autoimmunity is causal
key_evidence_or_cases: Goebel et al 2021 antibody transfer to mice producing pain behavior; small fiber density studies; functional imaging of pain amplification
implication_if_solved: Would give millions of patients a mechanism and a treatment target

observation_summary: A minor injury triggers disproportionate burning pain with swelling temperature and skin changes, sometimes spreading beyond the original site
why_it_resists_explanation: The trigger is trivial relative to the outcome, and the mechanism spans peripheral nerve, immune and central changes
leading_hypotheses: Neurogenic inflammation with neuropeptide release; autoimmune autoantibodies against autonomic receptors; central sensitization and cortical reorganization; sympathetic dysfunction
mainstream_view: A recognized diagnosis with partly understood mechanisms and no reliable treatment
testable_prediction: Autoantibody detection and passive transfer should reproduce features, as some studies report
key_evidence_or_cases: Mitchell causalgia descriptions; Budapest diagnostic criteria; autoantibody studies; mirror therapy responses
implication_if_solved: Would explain and treat a devastating post-injury syndrome

observation_summary: Cerebrospinal fluid pressure rises enough to threaten vision with no tumor obstruction or identifiable cause
why_it_resists_explanation: The mechanism of CSF homeostasis itself is incompletely understood, so a disorder of it cannot be fully explained
leading_hypotheses: Impaired CSF absorption at the glymphatic or venous interface; venous sinus stenosis as cause or consequence; adipose-driven hormonal effects on CSF secretion; androgen excess
mainstream_view: A defined clinical entity with unknown cause; treatments are empirical
testable_prediction: Venous stenting outcomes should separate cause from consequence of stenosis
key_evidence_or_cases: Papilledema with normal imaging; weight loss reversing the condition; CSF androgen profiling studies
implication_if_solved: Would clarify cerebrospinal fluid regulation generally

observation_summary: Brief lightning-like facial pain attacks triggered by light touch, often with no visible nerve compression
why_it_resists_explanation: Why demyelination produces paroxysmal rather than continuous pain, and why some patients have no compression, remain unexplained
leading_hypotheses: Vascular compression causing focal demyelination and ectopic firing; central generator in the brainstem; ion channel mutations in some familial cases
mainstream_view: Compression explains many cases; the paroxysmal pattern and compression-negative cases are open
testable_prediction: Sodium channel gene sequencing in compression-negative patients should find variants, as some studies report
key_evidence_or_cases: Microvascular decompression success rates; MRI compression findings; Nav1.7 variants in some patients
implication_if_solved: Would improve treatment selection for a severe pain disorder

observation_summary: Attacks of extreme pain recur with striking clock-like and seasonal regularity, often at the same hour nightly
why_it_resists_explanation: Linking a hypothalamic clock to a trigeminal pain circuit requires a pathway that is only partly identified
leading_hypotheses: Hypothalamic circadian pacemaker driving trigeminal autonomic activation; melatonin and orexin signaling abnormalities; genetic circadian variants identified in 2021 studies
mainstream_view: Hypothalamic involvement is established by imaging; the precise mechanism of timing is open
testable_prediction: Circadian gene variants should associate with attack timing, which 2021 and 2023 genome-wide studies support
key_evidence_or_cases: Posterior hypothalamic activation on PET; circadian GWAS findings; response to deep brain stimulation
implication_if_solved: Would connect biological clocks to pain circuits

phenomenon: Migraine aura and cortical spreading depression
observation_summary: A slowly propagating wave of cortical depolarization produces visual aura, but its trigger and relation to headache are unclear
why_it_resists_explanation: The wave is hard to observe in humans and the causal link between aura and pain is contested since many patients have one without the other
leading_hypotheses: Cortical spreading depolarization triggering trigeminal activation; independent brainstem generator for pain; channelopathy-driven hyperexcitability; CGRP release as the common final pathway
mainstream_view: Spreading depolarization is accepted as the aura substrate; its causal role in headache is debated
testable_prediction: CGRP blockade prevents headache without affecting aura, which it largely does
key_evidence_or_cases: Leao 1944 spreading depression; Hadjikhani fMRI of aura 2001; CGRP antibody efficacy; familial hemiplegic migraine channel mutations
implication_if_solved: Would complete the mechanism of the most common neurological disorder

observation_summary: Seizures begin suddenly after long quiescent intervals, and predicting onset remains largely impossible
why_it_resists_explanation: The transition to seizure is a nonlinear network event, and candidate precursors are inconsistent across patients
leading_hypotheses: Critical transition in network excitability; interictal spike cascades; circadian and multidien cycles of excitability discovered recently; stochastic threshold crossing
mainstream_view: Multidien rhythms discovered in 2018 and 2021 improved forecasting; general prediction is still limited
testable_prediction: Chronic intracranial recordings should support forecasting above chance, which recent devices achieve modestly
key_evidence_or_cases: Long-term intracranial recordings revealing multidien cycles; responsive neurostimulation device data; seizure prediction competitions
implication_if_solved: Would allow warning systems and preemptive treatment

observation_summary: Patients die suddenly after seizures with no adequate structural cause found at autopsy
why_it_resists_explanation: The fatal event is rarely monitored, and candidate mechanisms occur within minutes and leave no trace
leading_hypotheses: Postictal central apnea and respiratory arrest; cardiac arrhythmia from autonomic surge; brainstem spreading depolarization; serotonergic dysfunction
mainstream_view: A recognized leading cause of epilepsy-related death with incompletely known mechanism
testable_prediction: Monitored cases in epilepsy units should reveal a consistent sequence, and the MORTEMUS study suggested one
key_evidence_or_cases: MORTEMUS monitored cases showing respiratory then cardiac failure; animal model brainstem spreading depolarization
implication_if_solved: Would enable monitoring and prevention of unexpected deaths

phenomenon: Tourette syndrome tics and premonitory urge
observation_summary: Involuntary movements are preceded by a mounting urge, and suppression is possible but builds tension, a structure with no clear neural account
why_it_resists_explanation: The urge is subjective and the disorder involves distributed cortico-striatal circuits with no single lesion
leading_hypotheses: Dysregulated cortico-striato-thalamo-cortical loops; dopaminergic hyperinnervation; interneuron deficits in striatum; interoceptive prediction error generating urge
mainstream_view: Circuit involvement established; the urge phenomenon and its relation to volition remain open
testable_prediction: Deep brain stimulation targets should relieve tics proportionally to urge suppression
key_evidence_or_cases: Striatal interneuron loss in postmortem tissue; DBS outcomes; habit reversal therapy efficacy
notable_names: Gilles de la Tourette; Leckman; Albin; Worbe
implication_if_solved: Would clarify the boundary between voluntary and involuntary action

observation_summary: Patients have genuine seizures paralysis or movement disorders with normal structural imaging and nerve conduction
why_it_resists_explanation: The symptoms are real and involuntary yet arise from altered function rather than damage, a category standard neurology was not built to handle
leading_hypotheses: Aberrant top-down predictive processing with high precision priors; disrupted sense of agency with intact motor pathways; dissociation from trauma-related mechanisms; attentional modulation of motor control
mainstream_view: Now accepted as a positive diagnosis rather than exclusion; mechanisms are an active research area
testable_prediction: Functional imaging should show normal motor pathways with abnormal agency and attention networks, which it does
key_evidence_or_cases: Charcot hysteria studies; Hoover sign and positive clinical signs; functional imaging of FND motor tasks
implication_if_solved: Would legitimize and treat a very common neurological presentation

observation_summary: Patients become immobile mute and posturing, sometimes for weeks, and often reverse dramatically within minutes of a benzodiazepine dose
why_it_resists_explanation: The dramatic pharmacological reversal implies a specific circuit state, but that state is not identified
leading_hypotheses: GABA-A receptor hypofunction in orbitofrontal and motor circuits; top-down motor inhibition from anterior cingulate; glutamatergic dysfunction in NMDA receptor encephalitis cases
mainstream_view: A recognized syndrome with reliable treatment and unexplained mechanism
testable_prediction: Receptor imaging should show the predicted GABA-A changes, with some supporting evidence
key_evidence_or_cases: Lorazepam challenge test responses; ECT efficacy; GABA-A receptor binding studies; malignant catatonia
implication_if_solved: Would reveal a reversible brain state controlling volition and movement

observation_summary: A syndrome of psychosis and cognitive change with high heritability spread across thousands of genetic variants and no unifying mechanism
why_it_resists_explanation: Hundreds of small-effect loci plus diverse environmental risks combine, and the diagnosis may encompass several distinct conditions
leading_hypotheses: Dopaminergic dysregulation downstream of glutamatergic and interneuron dysfunction; synaptic pruning excess via complement signaling; neurodevelopmental insult plus later stressors; several distinct disorders under one label
mainstream_view: A real and devastating condition with no established pathophysiology; the dopamine hypothesis is a treatment target not a cause
testable_prediction: Complement C4 risk variants should predict synaptic pruning differences, as 2016 work suggested
key_evidence_or_cases: C4 locus finding 2016; ketamine and PCP psychosis models; GWAS with hundreds of loci; migrant and urbanicity risk
implication_if_solved: Would transform treatment of a leading cause of disability

observation_summary: Mood states switch between mania and depression sometimes abruptly, with lithium uniquely effective by unknown means
why_it_resists_explanation: A mechanism must explain bistability and switching, which most neurotransmitter models do not, and lithium hits many targets
leading_hypotheses: Circadian and sleep-wake instability triggering switches; mitochondrial and ion transport dysfunction; GSK-3 and inositol signaling as lithium targets; kindling and allostatic load
mainstream_view: Established disorder; switching mechanism and lithium mechanism both unexplained after 70 years of use
testable_prediction: Identifying the molecular target that mediates lithium response would predict responders
key_evidence_or_cases: Lithium response heritability; circadian gene associations; sleep deprivation triggering mania; patient-derived neuron studies
implication_if_solved: Would explain and predict response to the most effective psychiatric drug

observation_summary: A simple ion has been the most effective mood stabilizer for 75 years and nobody knows which of its many targets matters
why_it_resists_explanation: Lithium affects GSK-3, inositol phosphatases, mitochondrial function and circadian proteins at therapeutic concentrations, with no way to isolate the relevant one
leading_hypotheses: GSK-3 inhibition; inositol monophosphatase inhibition and the inositol depletion hypothesis; circadian period lengthening; neuroprotective and mitochondrial effects
mainstream_view: A standing embarrassment in psychopharmacology; multiple candidate mechanisms with no resolution
testable_prediction: A selective inhibitor of the key target should reproduce lithium efficacy
key_evidence_or_cases: Cade 1949 discovery; GSK-3 inhibitor studies; inositol depletion experiments; patient-derived neuron response differences
implication_if_solved: Would allow design of better-tolerated mood stabilizers

observation_summary: Inducing a seizure is the most effective treatment for severe depression, and the reason is unknown
why_it_resists_explanation: The intervention is massive and nonspecific, affecting neurotransmitters, plasticity, inflammation and connectivity simultaneously
leading_hypotheses: Enhanced neuroplasticity and neurogenesis; normalization of network connectivity; anticonvulsant and GABAergic rebound effects; inflammatory modulation
mainstream_view: Efficacy robustly established; mechanism unexplained after 85 years
testable_prediction: Biomarkers of plasticity should track clinical response across patients
key_evidence_or_cases: Response rates in treatment-resistant depression; hippocampal volume increases on imaging; seizure threshold changes across a course
implication_if_solved: Would allow replication of the benefit without seizures or memory effects

observation_summary: A single subanesthetic dose can lift severe depression within hours, overturning the assumption that antidepressants need weeks
why_it_resists_explanation: The effect outlasts drug clearance by days, so the mechanism must involve induced plasticity rather than receptor occupancy
leading_hypotheses: NMDA receptor blockade on inhibitory interneurons causing glutamate surge and synaptogenesis; hydroxynorketamine metabolite action independent of NMDA; opioid receptor involvement; psychedelic-like effects on expectancy
mainstream_view: Efficacy well established and approved; mechanism actively contested between NMDA, metabolite and opioid accounts
testable_prediction: Naltrexone blockade abolishing the effect would support the opioid pathway, as one controversial study found
key_evidence_or_cases: Berman 2000 trial; Zarate 2006 replication; metabolite studies in mice; naltrexone blockade study 2018
implication_if_solved: Would enable a new class of fast-acting antidepressants

phenomenon: Psychedelic durable effects after single doses
observation_summary: Single doses of psilocybin produce changes in depression anxiety and personality lasting months, far beyond drug exposure
why_it_resists_explanation: Expectancy and blinding are nearly impossible with a drug that produces obvious effects, and the mechanism spans pharmacology and subjective experience
leading_hypotheses: 5-HT2A-driven synaptic plasticity and dendritic growth; relaxation of rigid priors allowing belief updating; mystical experience as a psychological mediator; expectancy and therapeutic context effects
mainstream_view: Clinical results are promising; effect sizes are debated because of severe blinding problems
testable_prediction: Non-hallucinogenic 5-HT2A agonists should work if plasticity alone suffices, which is being tested
key_evidence_or_cases: Griffiths psilocybin trials; non-hallucinogenic analogue studies in mice; active placebo critiques
implication_if_solved: Would separate drug-induced plasticity from subjective experience as the active ingredient

observation_summary: Major depression is diagnosed by symptom clusters with no biomarker, and the serotonin hypothesis has collapsed as an explanation
why_it_resists_explanation: The diagnosis is heterogeneous, likely containing several distinct conditions, and no measure separates them
leading_hypotheses: Multiple distinct disorders under one label; network and connectivity dysfunction; inflammatory subtypes; stress-induced plasticity failure; symptom-level rather than disorder-level biology
mainstream_view: The serotonin deficiency account is now rejected by most researchers; no replacement mechanism is established
testable_prediction: Biologically defined subtypes should predict differential treatment response
key_evidence_or_cases: Moncrieff 2022 serotonin umbrella review; SSRI efficacy despite no serotonin deficit; inflammatory marker subgroups
implication_if_solved: Would allow mechanism-based psychiatry rather than symptom-based

observation_summary: Serotonin levels rise within hours but clinical improvement takes two to six weeks
why_it_resists_explanation: The delay rules out simple neurotransmitter deficiency and implicates slower downstream processes that have not been pinned down
leading_hypotheses: Receptor desensitization and autoreceptor adaptation; neurogenesis and plasticity requiring weeks; gradual emotional reprocessing rather than direct mood change; early improvement masked by measurement
mainstream_view: A classic argument against the simple monoamine hypothesis; the specific slow process remains uncertain
testable_prediction: Blocking hippocampal neurogenesis should abolish efficacy, which it does in rodents
key_evidence_or_cases: Autoreceptor desensitization timelines; neurogenesis-blocking rodent studies; early-onset reanalyses of trial data
implication_if_solved: Would allow design of fast-acting conventional antidepressants

observation_summary: Patients experience intrusive thoughts and compulsions they recognize as irrational yet cannot stop
why_it_resists_explanation: Insight is preserved while behavior is not, which requires a model separating belief from action control
leading_hypotheses: Cortico-striato-thalamo-cortical loop hyperactivity; error signal and habit system dysfunction; glutamatergic abnormalities; immune-mediated subtypes in children
mainstream_view: Circuit involvement well supported by imaging and deep brain stimulation response; full mechanism open
testable_prediction: DBS and capsulotomy at specific loop nodes should relieve symptoms, and they do
key_evidence_or_cases: Orbitofrontal hyperactivity on PET; DBS efficacy; PANDAS immune subtype controversy; glutamate MRS findings
implication_if_solved: Would explain the gap between insight and behavioral control

observation_summary: Patients present with distinct identity states with separate memories and behavior, with the validity and origin of the condition long contested
why_it_resists_explanation: Symptoms are heavily shaped by clinical context and cultural expectation, and prevalence varies enormously across countries and eras
leading_hypotheses: Trauma-driven dissociation of self-states; iatrogenic and sociocognitive construction through suggestion; a mixture in which trauma predisposes and clinical framing shapes presentation
mainstream_view: Included in diagnostic manuals but its etiology is one of the most contested questions in psychiatry
testable_prediction: Prospective studies of trauma cohorts without exposure to dissociative framing would test the trauma model
key_evidence_or_cases: Epidemic rise after Sybil publication; cross-cultural prevalence differences; neuroimaging of identity state switching
implication_if_solved: Would resolve a decades-long dispute about trauma, memory and suggestion

observation_summary: Detailed, confidently held memories of events that never occurred can be created in the laboratory within an hour
why_it_resists_explanation: That memory is reconstructive rather than reproductive runs against strong intuition, and the boundary conditions remain debated
leading_hypotheses: Source monitoring failure; schema-driven reconstruction; imagination inflation; social pressure and authority effects
mainstream_view: Well established experimentally; the implications for eyewitness testimony and recovered memory remain contested in practice
testable_prediction: Suggestive interviewing protocols should produce false memories at predictable rates, and they do
key_evidence_or_cases: Loftus lost in the mall study; Wade doctored photograph studies; DRM word list paradigm; wrongful conviction exonerations
implication_if_solved: Already reshaping legal standards for eyewitness evidence

observation_summary: Highly suggestible individuals show measurable changes including analgesia sufficient for surgery, by a mechanism without consensus
why_it_resists_explanation: Hypnosis effects overlap with expectancy and compliance, and the trait of suggestibility has no identified neural or genetic basis
leading_hypotheses: Altered executive and attentional control with dissociated monitoring; sociocognitive role enactment and expectancy; cold control theory of lost metacognition; a genuine altered state
mainstream_view: Analgesic and perceptual effects accepted as real; whether a distinct state exists is disputed
testable_prediction: Imaging should show state-specific signatures beyond expectancy, with partial support
key_evidence_or_cases: Hypnotic analgesia in surgery; Stroop interference reduction under suggestion; Oakley and Halligan imaging studies
implication_if_solved: Would clarify top-down control of perception and pain

observation_summary: Sham surgical procedures sometimes produce benefits equal to real operations, including for knee arthroscopy and vertebroplasty
why_it_resists_explanation: Surgical placebo trials are rare and ethically difficult, so the extent of the effect across procedures is unknown
leading_hypotheses: Natural history and regression to the mean; strong expectation effects proportional to procedure invasiveness; incidental effects of anesthesia and rest; the targeted mechanism being wrong
mainstream_view: Established for specific procedures; a major and uncomfortable finding in surgical evidence
testable_prediction: Sham-controlled trials of other common procedures, which are rarely performed
key_evidence_or_cases: Moseley knee arthroscopy trial 2002; vertebroplasty sham trials 2009; internal mammary ligation 1959
implication_if_solved: Would prevent large numbers of ineffective operations

phenomenon: Nocebo and symptom contagion in trials
observation_summary: Participants given inert treatment report substantial side effects matching the warned-of profile of the real drug
why_it_resists_explanation: Expectation-generated symptoms are indistinguishable from drug effects by report, making attribution difficult
leading_hypotheses: Expectation and conditioned learning; attentional amplification of normal bodily noise; social transmission of symptom reports; misattribution of unrelated background symptoms
mainstream_view: Well established and quantified, notably in statin and vaccine trials
testable_prediction: Blinded discontinuation studies should show symptoms persisting on placebo, and they do
key_evidence_or_cases: SAMSON statin n-of-1 trial 2020; COVID vaccine placebo arm adverse event rates; informed consent wording experiments
implication_if_solved: Already changing how side effects are communicated to patients

phenomenon: Why general intelligence correlates across tasks
observation_summary: Performance on nearly all cognitive tasks correlates positively, producing a general factor that no mechanism explains
why_it_resists_explanation: The statistical factor could reflect one underlying resource, many overlapping processes, or a developmental artifact, and the data cannot distinguish them
leading_hypotheses: A single limiting neural resource such as processing speed or network efficiency; mutualism in which abilities bootstrap each other during development; sampling overlap of many independent processes; a formative rather than reflective construct
mainstream_view: The positive manifold is one of the most replicated findings in psychology; its cause is genuinely unknown
testable_prediction: Mutualism and sampling models predict different developmental trajectories of correlation, which longitudinal data can test
key_evidence_or_cases: Spearman 1904 positive manifold; network and mutualism models; brain network efficiency correlations; Dickens-Flynn models
notable_names: Spearman; Thomson; van der Maas; Deary
implication_if_solved: Would ground or dissolve the dominant construct in individual differences research

observation_summary: Average IQ scores rose about three points per decade for most of a century, then stalled or reversed in several countries since the 1990s
why_it_resists_explanation: No single environmental factor tracks the gains, and the reversal undercuts explanations based on steady improvement
leading_hypotheses: Improved nutrition and health; increased schooling and test familiarity; reduced lead and infectious disease burden; greater cognitive complexity of environments; heterosis from reduced inbreeding
mainstream_view: The effect is firmly documented and the reversal is increasingly accepted; causes remain contested
testable_prediction: Cohort studies with measured environmental exposures should track score changes
key_evidence_or_cases: Flynn cross-national analyses; Norwegian conscript data reversal 2018; lead exposure decline correlations
implication_if_solved: Would identify modifiable determinants of population cognitive ability

observation_summary: Distributing practice over time produces far better retention than massed practice, robustly and across species, with no settled mechanism
why_it_resists_explanation: Several mechanisms predict the same behavioral pattern, and separating them requires measures of memory trace state that do not exist
leading_hypotheses: Study-phase retrieval requiring effortful reactivation; encoding variability across contexts; deficient processing of massed repetitions; consolidation windows between sessions
mainstream_view: One of the most reliable findings in psychology; mechanism still debated after 140 years
testable_prediction: Neural measures of trace reactivation should predict the spacing benefit
key_evidence_or_cases: Ebbinghaus 1885; Cepeda meta-analysis 2006; optimal spacing interval studies; animal conditioning parallels
implication_if_solved: Would allow optimal scheduling of education and training

observation_summary: Retrieving information strengthens memory more than restudying it, even without feedback, which contradicts intuition and most study habits
why_it_resists_explanation: Why effortful retrieval modifies the trace more than exposure does is not mechanistically explained
leading_hypotheses: Elaborative retrieval creating additional retrieval routes; episodic context updating during retrieval; consolidation triggered by retrieval; desirable difficulty increasing processing depth
mainstream_view: Extremely well replicated; the mechanism is debated
testable_prediction: Neural reactivation during retrieval should predict later retention benefits
key_evidence_or_cases: Roediger and Karpicke 2006; Gates 1917; classroom replications; transfer-appropriate processing studies
implication_if_solved: Would reshape educational practice at scale

observation_summary: Sleeping between exposure and testing increases the rate of sudden insight into hidden rules
why_it_resists_explanation: Insight is a discrete event that is hard to schedule or measure, and sleep stages involved are debated
leading_hypotheses: Replay-driven abstraction of common structure; synaptic downscaling improving signal to noise; hippocampal to neocortical transfer enabling generalization; targeted memory reactivation effects
mainstream_view: Reported repeatedly with moderate effect sizes; mechanism open and some replications weak
testable_prediction: Targeted memory reactivation during specific sleep stages should modulate insight rates
key_evidence_or_cases: Wagner et al 2004 number reduction task; targeted memory reactivation studies; N1 sleep creativity findings 2021
implication_if_solved: Would allow deliberate engineering of insight and creativity

observation_summary: Yawns spread between individuals, across species in some pairings, and correlate with social closeness
why_it_resists_explanation: Attributing contagion to empathy is hard to test, and the effect is sensitive to attention and arousal confounds
leading_hypotheses: Perception-action coupling without empathy; empathy and emotional contagion; shared arousal state synchronization; attentional capture by face stimuli
mainstream_view: Phenomenon well documented; the empathy interpretation is contested
testable_prediction: Contagion should scale with social bond strength independent of attention, with mixed results
key_evidence_or_cases: Human familiarity gradient studies; dog-human cross-species contagion; chimpanzee in-group bias in contagion
implication_if_solved: Would clarify the mechanics of behavioral synchronization

observation_summary: Patients recognize a loved one face but believe the person is an impostor, sometimes only in person and not by phone
why_it_resists_explanation: A model must explain intact recognition with absent familiarity and the failure to reject an absurd conclusion
leading_hypotheses: Disconnection between face recognition and affective familiarity pathways; impaired belief evaluation in right frontal cortex; two-factor model combining anomalous experience with reasoning deficit
mainstream_view: The two-factor account is widely accepted in outline; details unresolved
testable_prediction: Autonomic responses to familiar faces should be absent in these patients, and they are
key_evidence_or_cases: Capgras 1923 case; absent skin conductance to familiar faces; right hemisphere lesion associations
implication_if_solved: Would show how experience and belief jointly construct recognition

observation_summary: Patients sincerely believe they are dead or do not exist, sometimes alongside preserved reasoning in other domains
why_it_resists_explanation: The belief is maximally implausible yet held with conviction, requiring an account of how global affective change becomes a specific proposition
leading_hypotheses: Global loss of affective responsiveness attributed to being dead; two-factor model with belief evaluation deficit; depersonalization taken to its conclusion
mainstream_view: Accepted as a real rare syndrome; mechanism inferred from related conditions
testable_prediction: Metabolic imaging should show widespread cortical hypometabolism, as case studies report
key_evidence_or_cases: Cotard 1880 description; PET hypometabolism case study 2013; overlap with severe depression and depersonalization
implication_if_solved: Would illuminate the construction of the sense of existing

locus: Patients after callosal or frontal damage
observation_summary: A patient hand performs complex purposeful actions the patient disowns and sometimes fights with the other hand
why_it_resists_explanation: Purposeful behavior without the sense of agency separates action generation from ownership in a way standard models do not predict
leading_hypotheses: Loss of interhemispheric inhibition releasing contralateral motor programs; disruption of the agency comparator; medial frontal damage releasing environmentally driven behavior
mainstream_view: Accepted and localized to specific lesion sites; the agency mechanism remains open
testable_prediction: Lesion mapping should consistently implicate callosal and medial frontal structures, and it does
key_evidence_or_cases: Goldstein 1908 case; post-callosotomy cases; corticobasal degeneration cases
implication_if_solved: Would separate motor control from the sense of agency

observation_summary: Stimuli in one modality reliably and involuntarily evoke experiences in another, consistent within an individual for life
why_it_resists_explanation: The neural basis differs across synesthesia types, and whether it reflects extra connectivity or disinhibited feedback is unresolved
leading_hypotheses: Increased structural cross-modal connectivity; disinhibited feedback from multisensory areas; learned associations reinforced in childhood; genetic variation in pruning
mainstream_view: Accepted as genuine and measurable since behavioral and imaging confirmation
testable_prediction: Diffusion imaging should show increased connectivity in the relevant pathways, with partial support
key_evidence_or_cases: Grapheme-color consistency tests; Ramachandran pop-out tests; family aggregation studies; imaging of V4 activation by letters
implication_if_solved: Would reveal how sensory modalities are normally segregated

observation_summary: Some women carry four distinct cone photopigments and a few show enhanced color discrimination, but most functional tetrachromats are not detected
why_it_resists_explanation: Having four pigments does not guarantee four-dimensional perception, since downstream processing may not exploit the extra channel
leading_hypotheses: Functional tetrachromacy requiring postreceptoral adaptation; most carriers remaining behaviorally trichromatic; detection methods too insensitive to find true cases
mainstream_view: Genetic carriers are common; confirmed functional tetrachromats are extremely rare and the phenomenon is contested
testable_prediction: Rigorous color-matching tests should identify four-dimensional discrimination in carriers, which has succeeded in at most a few cases
key_evidence_or_cases: Jordan and Mollon studies; cDa29 identified functional tetrachromat 2010; X-linked opsin polymorphism frequency
implication_if_solved: Would show whether perception can expand with receptor variation

observation_summary: Some studies report human brain responses to rotating magnetic fields, implying an unrecognized sense without conscious perception
why_it_resists_explanation: The effect is small, requires shielded facilities, and earlier behavioral claims failed replication
leading_hypotheses: Cryptochrome-based radical pair sensing in the human retina; magnetite particles in the brain; artifacts from induced currents in recording equipment
mainstream_view: Not accepted; the 2019 alpha-band finding is intriguing but awaits independent replication
testable_prediction: Independent replication in a different shielded facility with blinded analysis
key_evidence_or_cases: Wang et al 2019 eLife alpha power responses; failed earlier behavioral studies by Baker and others; magnetite in human brain tissue
implication_if_solved: Would add an unrecognized human sensory modality

observation_summary: Bodily signals contribute to emotional experience, but whether emotions are discrete biological kinds or constructed categories is unresolved
why_it_resists_explanation: Physiological patterns do not map cleanly onto emotion categories, yet people reliably report discrete emotions
leading_hypotheses: Basic emotions with distinct physiological signatures; constructed emotion from interoceptive prediction plus conceptual categorization; appraisal theories; dimensional affect plus labeling
mainstream_view: A central and unresolved debate in affective science, with meta-analyses favoring constructionist readings
testable_prediction: Physiological pattern classification should distinguish emotion categories, which it does only weakly
key_evidence_or_cases: James-Lange theory; Schachter-Singer experiments; Barrett meta-analyses of emotion specificity; insula interoception studies
implication_if_solved: Would determine whether emotions are natural kinds

locus: About one to two percent of people
observation_summary: A highly heritable developmental condition with hundreds of contributing genes and enormous variation in presentation
why_it_resists_explanation: Hundreds of rare variants and common polygenic risk converge on no single pathway, and the diagnostic category may span many distinct conditions
leading_hypotheses: Convergence on synaptic and chromatin regulation pathways; excitation-inhibition imbalance; altered developmental timing; many etiologically distinct conditions sharing a behavioral profile
mainstream_view: Genetic architecture increasingly mapped; mechanism and category validity remain open
testable_prediction: Gene-specific subgroups should show distinct biology and trajectories, which emerging cohorts support
key_evidence_or_cases: Kanner 1943; twin heritability studies; SFARI gene lists; de novo variant exome studies; prevalence rise analyses
implication_if_solved: Would allow mechanism-based support and intervention

observation_summary: A highly heritable attention and self-regulation condition treated effectively by stimulants, with diagnosis based entirely on behavior
why_it_resists_explanation: No biomarker exists, symptoms are continuous with normal variation, and prevalence varies enormously by country and school policy
leading_hypotheses: Dopaminergic and noradrenergic signaling differences in frontostriatal circuits; delay aversion and reward discounting; maturational delay in cortical development; partly a mismatch between trait distribution and institutional demands
mainstream_view: Established as a valid and heritable condition; mechanism unresolved and the diagnostic boundary is contested
testable_prediction: Neurobiological subtypes should predict differential medication response
key_evidence_or_cases: Twin heritability near 0.7; cortical maturation delay imaging; relative age effects in diagnosis rates; stimulant efficacy trials
implication_if_solved: Would sharpen diagnosis and personalize treatment

locus: Five to ten percent of readers
observation_summary: Specific reading difficulty despite normal intelligence and instruction, with competing causal accounts after 140 years
why_it_resists_explanation: Reading is a recent cultural invention with no dedicated evolved system, so the deficit must be in co-opted machinery that is hard to isolate
leading_hypotheses: Phonological processing deficit; visual attention span and crowding deficits; magnocellular pathway dysfunction; cerebellar automatization deficit; noise exclusion deficits
mainstream_view: The phonological account is dominant but incomplete; competing accounts persist
testable_prediction: Interventions targeting each proposed deficit should improve reading if that deficit is causal
key_evidence_or_cases: Left temporoparietal activation differences; phonological awareness training efficacy; cross-linguistic prevalence variation
implication_if_solved: Would allow targeted remediation for a very common learning difficulty

observation_summary: Involuntary disruption of fluent speech that vanishes during singing, choral reading and private speech
why_it_resists_explanation: The variability across contexts implies intact motor capability, so the deficit must lie in timing or monitoring systems that have not been isolated
leading_hypotheses: Basal ganglia timing circuit dysfunction; impaired auditory-motor integration; white matter differences in left arcuate fasciculus; genetic variants in lysosomal enzyme genes
mainstream_view: Neurobiological basis increasingly supported; the context dependence remains unexplained
testable_prediction: Altered auditory feedback should reduce stuttering, and it reliably does
key_evidence_or_cases: GNPTAB and NAGPA gene variants; delayed auditory feedback effects; dopamine antagonist effects; arcuate fasciculus imaging
implication_if_solved: Would explain the paradox of situation-dependent motor failure

locus: Ten to fifteen percent of adults
observation_summary: People hear persistent sound with no acoustic source, often after hearing loss, and sometimes without measurable hearing damage
why_it_resists_explanation: The percept is generated centrally and cannot be objectively measured, so mechanism and treatment effect are both hard to evaluate
leading_hypotheses: Central gain increase compensating for reduced peripheral input; thalamocortical dysrhythmia; aberrant neural synchrony in auditory cortex; attention and limbic amplification of a normally ignored signal
mainstream_view: Central origin broadly accepted; no objective measure and no reliably effective treatment
testable_prediction: Objective measures such as specific cortical oscillation patterns should track percept loudness
key_evidence_or_cases: Residual inhibition phenomena; somatic modulation of tinnitus; animal models with gap-detection deficits; bimodal stimulation trials
implication_if_solved: Would allow objective measurement and targeted treatment

observation_summary: Specific repetitive sounds such as chewing provoke intense disproportionate anger or distress in otherwise typical hearing
why_it_resists_explanation: The condition was only recently defined, prevalence estimates vary widely, and it fits no existing diagnostic category
leading_hypotheses: Hyperconnectivity between auditory cortex and orofacial motor representation (mirror neuron account); limbic hyperresponsivity to specific triggers; conditioned aversive learning; an attention and salience disorder
mainstream_view: Increasingly accepted as a real condition; mechanism and classification unsettled
testable_prediction: Motor mimicry interventions should reduce distress if the motor account is correct, with preliminary support
key_evidence_or_cases: Kumar 2017 and 2021 imaging studies; consensus definition 2022; trigger specificity studies
implication_if_solved: Would validate and treat a newly recognized condition

phenomenon: Highly sensitive persons and sensory processing sensitivity
observation_summary: A subset of people show heightened reactivity to sensory and emotional input, measurable in brain responses and behavior
why_it_resists_explanation: The construct overlaps heavily with neuroticism and introversion, so its independent status is contested
leading_hypotheses: A distinct temperament trait with a genetic basis; a repackaging of neuroticism and introversion; a differential susceptibility phenotype amplifying both good and bad environments
mainstream_view: A real measurable dimension; whether it is a distinct trait or a relabeling is actively debated
testable_prediction: Incremental validity tests should show prediction beyond established personality factors
key_evidence_or_cases: Aron sensitivity scale studies; differential susceptibility findings; imaging of heightened response to emotional stimuli
implication_if_solved: Would clarify whether environmental sensitivity is a distinct trait

phenomenon: Why humans show pervasive cognitive biases
observation_summary: People violate normative probability and logic in systematic, predictable ways across cultures
why_it_resists_explanation: Whether biases reflect bounded resources, adaptive heuristics, or researchers using the wrong normative standard is disputed
leading_hypotheses: Heuristics and biases from limited computation; ecologically rational heuristics mismatched to artificial tasks; resource-rational adaptation to computational cost; error management under asymmetric payoffs
mainstream_view: The empirical phenomena are robust; interpretation is one of the sharpest debates in the field
testable_prediction: Resource-rational models predict when biases should appear and disappear, with growing support
key_evidence_or_cases: Kahneman and Tversky experiments; Gigerenzer frequency format critiques; Lieder and Griffiths resource rationality
implication_if_solved: Would determine whether human reasoning is flawed or well adapted

observation_summary: Progressive scarring destroys the lungs with no identified trigger and a survival worse than many cancers
why_it_resists_explanation: The initiating injury is invisible by the time of diagnosis, and the fibrotic cascade is self-sustaining
leading_hypotheses: Repeated alveolar epithelial microinjury with aberrant repair; telomere shortening and surfactant gene variants; MUC5B promoter variant altering mucociliary clearance; senescent cell accumulation
mainstream_view: A defined disease with partly identified genetic risk and unknown initiating cause
testable_prediction: Early detection in MUC5B carriers should reveal the initiating lesion
key_evidence_or_cases: MUC5B promoter variant with large effect; telomerase mutations in familial cases; antifibrotic drugs slowing but not stopping decline
implication_if_solved: Would allow prevention rather than slowing of a fatal disease

observation_summary: Granulomas form in lungs and other organs with no identified infectious agent, sometimes resolving spontaneously
why_it_resists_explanation: No causative antigen has ever been isolated despite 150 years of searching, and presentations vary enormously
leading_hypotheses: Immune response to an unidentified environmental or microbial antigen such as Cutibacterium acnes or mycobacterial proteins; autoimmune reaction to vimentin; genetic susceptibility plus multiple triggers
mainstream_view: Recognized disease with unknown cause; a classic idiopathic granulomatous disorder
testable_prediction: Isolation of a consistent antigen from granulomas would resolve it, which has repeatedly failed
key_evidence_or_cases: ACCESS study environmental associations; World Trade Center dust exposure clusters; HLA associations; spontaneous remission rates
implication_if_solved: Would identify a trigger for a multisystem inflammatory disease

observation_summary: A multisystem inflammatory disease with oral and genital ulcers and vascular involvement, concentrated geographically
why_it_resists_explanation: It fits neither autoimmune nor autoinflammatory categories cleanly, and the geographic clustering is unexplained by genetics alone
leading_hypotheses: HLA-B51 associated autoinflammation; microbial trigger in genetically susceptible populations; neutrophil hyperfunction; an intermediate between autoimmune and autoinflammatory disease
mainstream_view: Recognized entity with strong HLA association and unknown trigger
testable_prediction: Microbiome and infectious exposure studies in high and low prevalence regions
key_evidence_or_cases: HLA-B51 association; Silk Road prevalence gradient; oral microbiome studies; pathergy reaction
implication_if_solved: Would clarify the boundary between autoimmunity and autoinflammation

observation_summary: Acute vasculitis with coronary artery aneurysms, epidemic clustering, striking seasonality and no identified pathogen
why_it_resists_explanation: Epidemic waves and wind-borne clustering suggest an environmental agent, but no organism has been isolated in 55 years
leading_hypotheses: A wind-borne environmental agent possibly fungal; an unidentified viral trigger in susceptible children; superantigen-mediated immune activation; a toxin rather than an infection
mainstream_view: A defined disease with unknown cause; tropospheric wind correlations are taken seriously
testable_prediction: Air sampling along implicated wind trajectories should identify a candidate agent
key_evidence_or_cases: Kawasaki 1967 description; Japanese epidemic waves 1979 1982 1986; tropospheric wind trajectory analyses; MIS-C similarity after COVID
implication_if_solved: Would prevent the leading cause of acquired pediatric heart disease

observation_summary: Immune attack on central nervous system myelin with a strong latitude gradient and now strong evidence of Epstein-Barr virus involvement
why_it_resists_explanation: EBV infects almost everyone yet only a few develop MS, so additional necessary factors must exist and are not identified
leading_hypotheses: EBV infection as a necessary but insufficient trigger via molecular mimicry; vitamin D and sunlight exposure; genetic susceptibility in HLA-DRB1; gut microbiome contributions; smoking and adolescent obesity
mainstream_view: The 2022 military cohort study established EBV as a probable necessary cause; the sufficient conditions remain unknown
testable_prediction: EBV vaccination should reduce MS incidence, a test now becoming feasible
key_evidence_or_cases: Bjornevik et al 2022 Science military cohort; GlialCAM molecular mimicry 2022; latitude gradient; HLA-DRB1 association
implication_if_solved: Would make a major neurological disease preventable

observation_summary: Autoimmune destruction of insulin-producing beta cells with rising incidence that genetics alone cannot explain
why_it_resists_explanation: Concordance in identical twins is well below one, so environmental triggers are required and have not been pinned down
leading_hypotheses: Enteroviral infection of beta cells; hygiene hypothesis and reduced microbial exposure; early cow milk protein exposure; vitamin D deficiency; accelerated growth increasing beta cell stress
mainstream_view: Autoimmune mechanism established and now treatable preclinically with teplizumab; triggers remain unidentified
testable_prediction: Antiviral or vaccine intervention trials in at-risk children should reduce incidence if enterovirus is causal
key_evidence_or_cases: TEDDY birth cohort; rising incidence of three to four percent per year; enterovirus serology associations; teplizumab delaying onset
implication_if_solved: Would allow primary prevention in genetically at-risk children

phenomenon: Rising incidence of allergy and asthma
observation_summary: Allergic disease rose dramatically through the late 20th century in developed countries, far too fast for genetic change
why_it_resists_explanation: Many candidate exposures changed simultaneously with industrialization, and intervention trials give mixed results
leading_hypotheses: Hygiene and old friends hypothesis of reduced microbial exposure; dual allergen exposure through skin versus gut; vitamin D changes; dietary fat composition shifts; air pollution and diesel particulates
mainstream_view: The microbial exposure framework is widely accepted in outline; specifics and the recent plateau remain open
testable_prediction: Early oral allergen introduction should prevent allergy, which the LEAP trial confirmed for peanut
key_evidence_or_cases: ISAAC international prevalence study; LEAP trial 2015; farm-childhood protective effects; Amish versus Hutterite comparison
implication_if_solved: Would guide prevention of a mass chronic disease burden

observation_summary: Chronic intestinal inflammation with over 200 genetic risk loci, rising global incidence and no identified cause
why_it_resists_explanation: Genetics explains only a fraction of risk, the microbiome is altered but causality is unclear, and the diagnosis spans distinct conditions
leading_hypotheses: Dysregulated mucosal immunity to commensal bacteria in genetically susceptible hosts; barrier dysfunction; specific organisms such as adherent-invasive E coli; dietary emulsifiers and processed food exposure
mainstream_view: Multifactorial consensus; no single cause identified despite extensive genetics
testable_prediction: Dietary elimination trials and microbiome manipulation should alter disease course predictably
key_evidence_or_cases: NOD2 and ATG16L1 risk variants; rising incidence in newly industrialized countries; emulsifier studies in mice; exclusive enteral nutrition efficacy
implication_if_solved: Would allow prevention and mechanism-based therapy

observation_summary: A well-understood autoimmune reaction to gluten in HLA-DQ2 or DQ8 carriers, yet onset can occur at any age after decades of tolerance
why_it_resists_explanation: The trigger for loss of tolerance in a long-exposed individual is unknown, and introduction timing trials were negative
leading_hypotheses: Viral infection such as reovirus breaking tolerance; microbiome shifts; quantity and timing of early gluten exposure; stochastic loss of regulatory T cell control
mainstream_view: Mechanism of the autoimmune reaction is well characterized; the trigger for onset is not
testable_prediction: Reovirus infection should precede onset in prospective cohorts, which some studies support
key_evidence_or_cases: Reovirus tolerance-breaking in mice 2017; negative gluten introduction timing trials; HLA-DQ2 requirement
implication_if_solved: Would allow prevention in genetically susceptible people

observation_summary: Autoantibodies appear years before joint symptoms, implying the disease starts elsewhere in the body
why_it_resists_explanation: The preclinical phase is asymptomatic so the initiating site and event are inferred rather than observed
leading_hypotheses: Mucosal origin in gum disease via Porphyromonas gingivalis citrullination; lung mucosa origin from smoking; gut microbiome origin; stochastic breach of tolerance to citrullinated proteins
mainstream_view: Preclinical autoimmunity established; the mucosal origin hypothesis is prominent but unproven
testable_prediction: Treating periodontal disease or lung inflammation in antibody-positive people should reduce progression
key_evidence_or_cases: Anti-CCP antibodies years before onset; P gingivalis citrullinating enzyme; smoking as the strongest environmental risk
implication_if_solved: Would allow interception before joint damage begins

observation_summary: A systemic autoimmune disease with extremely variable presentation, flare unpredictability and strong sex bias
why_it_resists_explanation: The disease involves many immune pathways at once, flares have no reliable trigger, and the sex bias has multiple candidate causes
leading_hypotheses: Impaired clearance of nuclear debris driving interferon responses; X chromosome dosage effects including a 2024 Xist ribonucleoprotein finding; hormonal modulation; EBV and UV triggers
mainstream_view: Established disease with partly characterized interferon pathway involvement; cause and flare triggers unknown
testable_prediction: X-linked dosage mechanisms should explain sex bias, which recent Xist work supports
key_evidence_or_cases: Interferon signature in most patients; Klinefelter syndrome increasing male risk; 2024 Xist autoantibody study; UV-triggered flares
implication_if_solved: Would explain the strongest sex bias in autoimmune disease

observation_summary: About eighty percent of autoimmune disease occurs in women, a bias no single mechanism fully explains
why_it_resists_explanation: Sex hormones, X chromosome dosage, pregnancy-related tolerance and microbiome differences all contribute and cannot be isolated in humans
leading_hypotheses: X chromosome gene dosage and incomplete X inactivation; Xist ribonucleoprotein complexes as autoantigens; estrogen effects on B cells; fetal microchimerism; microbiome and hormone interaction
mainstream_view: Robustly documented; mechanisms partly identified with substantial recent progress
testable_prediction: Klinefelter and Turner syndrome risk patterns should track X dosage, and they do
key_evidence_or_cases: Klinefelter XXY male lupus risk; Turner syndrome patterns; 2024 Xist mouse model study; hormone therapy effects
implication_if_solved: Would explain the largest demographic pattern in immune disease

observation_summary: Encephalopathy responsive to steroids occurs alongside thyroid antibodies that appear not to be pathogenic themselves
why_it_resists_explanation: The antibodies are probably bystanders, so the actual autoimmune target is unidentified, and the diagnosis is one of exclusion and treatment response
leading_hypotheses: An unidentified neuronal autoantibody with thyroid antibodies as markers; cerebral vasculitis; a heterogeneous group of autoimmune encephalitides misclassified together
mainstream_view: A contested diagnostic category increasingly reclassified as other autoimmune encephalitides
testable_prediction: Comprehensive neuronal autoantibody panels should reveal the true target
key_evidence_or_cases: Steroid-responsive cases; absence of correlation between antibody titer and severity; reclassification into NMDA receptor encephalitis in some cases
implication_if_solved: Would correctly reclassify a treatable neurological syndrome

observation_summary: Narcolepsy incidence rose sharply in children given one specific H1N1 vaccine, an association later supported by molecular mimicry evidence
why_it_resists_explanation: The effect was vaccine-brand specific and population specific, making the mechanism hard to isolate from confounds
leading_hypotheses: Molecular mimicry between H1N1 nucleoprotein and hypocretin receptor driving T cell attack on orexin neurons; adjuvant-specific immune activation; surveillance and diagnostic bias amplifying a real but smaller effect
mainstream_view: The association is accepted for Pandemrix; the immunological mechanism is partly supported
testable_prediction: T cell cross-reactivity between viral and hypocretin epitopes, which 2015 and 2019 studies reported
key_evidence_or_cases: Finnish and Swedish epidemiology; Pandemrix-specific signal; Ahmed et al molecular mimicry 2015; H1N1 infection also raising risk in China
implication_if_solved: Would clarify how infection and vaccination can trigger autoimmunity

observation_summary: Abrupt onset of obsessive-compulsive symptoms and tics reportedly following strep infection, with validity sharply contested
why_it_resists_explanation: Prospective studies have not reliably linked infection to onset, and the diagnostic criteria are broad and symptom-based
leading_hypotheses: Post-streptococcal autoimmune attack on basal ganglia; coincidental timing in a population with high strep exposure; an iatrogenic diagnostic construct; a real but much rarer entity than claimed
mainstream_view: Remains controversial; major professional bodies differ on whether the entity is valid
testable_prediction: Prospective cohorts with documented infections and blinded symptom assessment, which have been largely negative
key_evidence_or_cases: Swedo 1998 case series; Sydenham chorea as a precedent; negative prospective studies; antibasal ganglia antibody findings
implication_if_solved: Would determine whether a common infection causes psychiatric illness

observation_summary: An acute immune attack on peripheral nerves follows diverse infections and occasionally vaccines, affecting only a tiny fraction of those exposed
why_it_resists_explanation: Molecular mimicry is established for Campylobacter but most cases have no identified trigger, and host susceptibility factors are unknown
leading_hypotheses: Molecular mimicry between Campylobacter lipooligosaccharides and nerve gangliosides; Zika and other viral triggers; host HLA and ganglioside expression susceptibility
mainstream_view: Mimicry mechanism established for specific triggers; susceptibility and most cases remain unexplained
testable_prediction: Ganglioside antibody specificity should predict clinical subtype, and it largely does
key_evidence_or_cases: Campylobacter ganglioside mimicry; Zika outbreak associated cases in 2015 and 2016; anti-GQ1b in Miller Fisher variant
implication_if_solved: Would explain why only a few exposed people develop autoimmunity

observation_summary: Life-threatening allergic reactions occur repeatedly with no identifiable trigger after extensive testing
why_it_resists_explanation: Testing covers only known allergens, and mast cell activation can occur through non-IgE pathways that are hard to assay
leading_hypotheses: Undetected allergens including alpha-gal from tick bites; mast cell clonal disorders with KIT mutations; MRGPRX2-mediated non-IgE activation; cofactor-dependent reactions requiring exercise or NSAIDs
mainstream_view: A shrinking category as new causes such as alpha-gal syndrome and clonal mast cell disease are identified
testable_prediction: Tryptase and KIT D816V testing should reclassify many idiopathic cases, and it does
key_evidence_or_cases: Alpha-gal syndrome discovery 2009; hereditary alpha tryptasemia 2016; clonal mast cell activation syndromes
implication_if_solved: Would convert a frightening unexplained condition into treatable diagnoses

observation_summary: Multisystem symptoms attributed to mast cell mediator release, with diagnostic criteria and prevalence sharply disputed
why_it_resists_explanation: Objective criteria such as tryptase elevation are met by only a minority of those diagnosed, and symptoms overlap with many conditions
leading_hypotheses: Clonal and nonclonal mast cell activation with genuine mediator release; hereditary alpha tryptasemia explaining a subset; overdiagnosis of a nonspecific symptom cluster
mainstream_view: A narrow consensus-criteria entity is accepted; broad diagnosis is widely criticized as unsupported
testable_prediction: Strict mediator criteria applied prospectively would establish true prevalence
key_evidence_or_cases: Consensus criteria debates 2011 to 2021; hereditary alpha tryptasemia gene duplications; tryptase measurement studies
implication_if_solved: Would separate a real disorder from a diagnostic fashion

observation_summary: Heart rate rises excessively on standing with disabling symptoms and no consistent structural abnormality
why_it_resists_explanation: The syndrome is probably several conditions, autonomic testing is variable, and the post-infectious subset grew enormously after COVID
leading_hypotheses: Autoimmune autoantibodies against adrenergic and muscarinic receptors; small fiber neuropathy; hypovolemia and deconditioning; central autonomic dysregulation; hypermobility-associated connective tissue differences
mainstream_view: Recognized as real with multiple likely subtypes; pathophysiology unresolved
testable_prediction: Autoantibody detection and passive transfer should reproduce features in animals, with preliminary reports
key_evidence_or_cases: Autoantibody studies; post-COVID incidence rise; norepinephrine transporter deficiency in one family; hypermobility overlap
implication_if_solved: Would give a mechanism to a rapidly growing patient population

observation_summary: The most common form of Ehlers-Danlos syndrome has no identified genetic cause, unlike every other subtype
why_it_resists_explanation: Diagnosis is clinical, the phenotype is continuous with normal variation, and no candidate gene has replicated
leading_hypotheses: Multiple genes with small effects; variants in untested regulatory regions; a polygenic connective tissue trait rather than a Mendelian disease; several distinct conditions grouped together
mainstream_view: A recognized clinical diagnosis with no molecular marker, unusual among named genetic syndromes
testable_prediction: Large-scale sequencing of well-phenotyped cohorts should identify causal variants, so far unsuccessful
key_evidence_or_cases: 2017 international classification; negative candidate gene studies; tenascin-X deficiency in a rare related form
implication_if_solved: Would provide a diagnostic test for a common and disabling condition

observation_summary: Motor neurons die progressively and selectively, with about ninety percent of cases having no family history or identified cause
why_it_resists_explanation: The disease is diagnosed late after substantial neuron loss, and the initiating event is invisible by then
leading_hypotheses: TDP-43 proteinopathy with prion-like spread; C9orf72 repeat expansions in a subset; glutamate excitotoxicity; RNA metabolism failure; environmental exposures including cyanobacterial BMAA
mainstream_view: Pathology well characterized; sporadic cause unknown and treatments marginally effective
testable_prediction: Identifying a presymptomatic biomarker would reveal the initiating phase
key_evidence_or_cases: TDP-43 inclusions in nearly all cases; C9orf72 discovery 2011; Guam ALS-parkinsonism cluster; military service risk association
implication_if_solved: Would allow early intervention in a uniformly fatal disease

phenomenon: Parkinson disease initiation and Braak staging
observation_summary: Alpha-synuclein pathology appears to begin in the gut or olfactory bulb and ascend to the brain years before motor symptoms
why_it_resists_explanation: The staging is inferred from postmortem cross-sections rather than observed progression, and not all cases follow the pattern
leading_hypotheses: Gut-first origin with vagal spread of misfolded alpha-synuclein; brain-first subtype; environmental toxicant exposure such as paraquat and trichloroethylene; prion-like templating of aggregation
mainstream_view: The dual-hit and body-first models are increasingly supported; initiation remains unestablished
testable_prediction: Vagotomy should reduce risk if the gut-first route is causal, and Danish registry data suggest it does
key_evidence_or_cases: Braak staging studies; vagotomy registry studies; appendectomy associations; REM sleep behavior disorder as a prodrome
implication_if_solved: Would allow prevention before neuron loss begins

observation_summary: A protein alone transmits disease and encodes distinct strains with different incubation times and tissue targets, without nucleic acid
why_it_resists_explanation: How conformational information alone specifies heritable strain properties is only partly understood
leading_hypotheses: Distinct stable misfolded conformations acting as templates; differing aggregate quaternary structures; cofactor involvement such as lipids or RNA in strain determination
mainstream_view: Protein-only transmission accepted and Nobel-recognized; strain encoding remains incompletely explained
testable_prediction: Cryo-EM structures of distinct strains should show conformational differences, which recent structures do
key_evidence_or_cases: Prusiner protein-only hypothesis; kuru and BSE epidemics; synthetic prion generation; 2021 and 2022 cryo-EM fibril structures
implication_if_solved: Would illuminate conformational information transfer in all neurodegeneration

observation_summary: A prion disease spreads efficiently among wild deer through the environment, with prions persisting in soil for years
why_it_resists_explanation: Environmental transmission routes are hard to quantify, and whether it can cross to humans is unresolved
leading_hypotheses: Shedding in saliva urine and feces with soil binding to clay minerals preserving infectivity; plant uptake of prions; carcass-mediated transmission
mainstream_view: Environmental transmission accepted; the species barrier to humans is a genuine open risk question
testable_prediction: Macaque and humanized mouse transmission studies, which give mixed results
key_evidence_or_cases: Soil clay prion binding studies; CWD spread maps; macaque oral transmission experiments; absence of confirmed human cases
implication_if_solved: Would determine a potential zoonotic risk from wild game

phenomenon: Hepatitis of unknown origin in children 2022
observation_summary: A cluster of about 1000 cases of severe acute hepatitis appeared in children with no usual viral cause
why_it_resists_explanation: The outbreak ended before definitive causal proof, and the leading candidate requires an unusual co-infection
leading_hypotheses: Adeno-associated virus 2 co-infection with adenovirus or herpesvirus in HLA-susceptible children; post-pandemic immunity gap increasing susceptibility; adenovirus 41F alone
mainstream_view: Three 2023 Nature papers converged on AAV2 co-infection with an HLA-DRB1 association; considered largely explained but not definitively proven
testable_prediction: Prospective surveillance should show the same AAV2 and HLA pattern in any recurrence
key_evidence_or_cases: WHO outbreak investigation 2022; three independent AAV2 studies in Nature 2023; HLA-DRB1 04:01 enrichment
implication_if_solved: Already a model of rapid outbreak causal investigation

observation_summary: Polio-like paralysis appeared in children in alternating-year peaks strongly associated with enterovirus D68
why_it_resists_explanation: The virus is rarely found in spinal fluid, so causal proof is indirect, and the biennial pattern stopped after 2018
leading_hypotheses: Enterovirus D68 neuroinvasion with rapid clearance from CSF; antibody evidence of recent infection; other enteroviruses in some cases; immune-mediated damage after infection
mainstream_view: EV-D68 is the accepted probable cause; direct detection in CNS remains rare
testable_prediction: CSF antibody and intrathecal synthesis studies should show EV-D68 specificity, and they do
key_evidence_or_cases: CDC surveillance 2014 2016 2018 peaks; EV-D68 CSF antibody studies; mouse model paralysis; absence of 2020 wave during pandemic measures
implication_if_solved: Would enable vaccine development against a paralytic childhood disease

observation_summary: A flesh-destroying mycobacterial infection whose route of transmission remains unknown after 75 years
why_it_resists_explanation: The organism is found in aquatic environments but no transmission route has been demonstrated, and clustering is highly focal
leading_hypotheses: Mosquito or aquatic insect vector transmission; possum reservoir with mosquito vector in Australia; direct environmental inoculation through skin trauma; aerosol exposure near water
mainstream_view: A WHO neglected tropical disease with genuinely unknown transmission
testable_prediction: Vector control interventions should reduce incidence if mosquitoes transmit it, which Australian trials are testing
key_evidence_or_cases: Mycobacterium ulcerans in aquatic environments; Australian possum feces studies; Beating Buruli mosquito control trial
implication_if_solved: Would allow prevention of a disabling neglected disease

observation_summary: Children develop head-nodding seizures with cognitive decline, epidemiologically linked to onchocerciasis but with no parasite in the brain
why_it_resists_explanation: The parasite is not found in the CNS, so an indirect mechanism is required, and affected regions are remote with limited research capacity
leading_hypotheses: Autoimmune reaction to Onchocerca volvulus leiomodin-1 cross-reacting with neuronal proteins; nutritional deficiency interacting with infection; an unidentified toxin; vitamin B6 deficiency
mainstream_view: Onchocerciasis association is strong and the leiomodin-1 autoantibody finding is promising but not confirmed
testable_prediction: Ivermectin mass treatment should reduce incidence, and it appears to have done so
key_evidence_or_cases: Johnson et al leiomodin-1 autoantibody study 2017; epidemiological association with blackfly exposure; decline after ivermectin programs
implication_if_solved: Would explain and prevent a devastating childhood epilepsy

observation_summary: Sudden irreversible spastic paralysis appears in epidemics associated with bitter cassava and protein deficiency
why_it_resists_explanation: The precise neurotoxic mechanism of cyanogenic compounds on upper motor neurons is unclear, and only some exposed people are affected
leading_hypotheses: Cyanide and thiocyanate toxicity to motor neurons under sulfur amino acid deficiency; linamarin metabolite toxicity; interaction with malnutrition and drought
mainstream_view: Cassava-cyanide association is accepted; the selective motor neuron toxicity mechanism remains open
testable_prediction: Cassava processing interventions should prevent outbreaks, and they do
key_evidence_or_cases: Mozambique and DRC epidemics; wetting method processing trials; urinary thiocyanate correlations
implication_if_solved: Would complete prevention of a preventable paralysis

observation_summary: Methylmercury damages specific brain regions such as the calcarine cortex and cerebellum while sparing others
why_it_resists_explanation: Why a diffusely distributed toxin produces highly selective regional damage is not fully explained
leading_hypotheses: Regional differences in antioxidant capacity and selenium availability; transport via the large neutral amino acid carrier concentrating in specific cells; selective vulnerability of granule cells
mainstream_view: Toxicity fully established; regional selectivity incompletely explained
testable_prediction: Regional selenoprotein expression should predict vulnerability patterns
key_evidence_or_cases: Minamata disease pathology; Iraqi grain poisoning 1971; selenium interaction studies
implication_if_solved: Would explain selective vulnerability in neurotoxicology generally

observation_summary: About a quarter of veterans developed persistent multisystem symptoms, with a 2022 study implicating a gene-environment interaction with sarin
why_it_resists_explanation: The exposures were poorly documented, symptoms are nonspecific, and the condition went unexplained for three decades
leading_hypotheses: Low-level sarin exposure interacting with PON1 genotype; pyridostigmine bromide prophylaxis; organophosphate pesticide exposure; depleted uranium or oil fire smoke; combined neurotoxic and stress effects
mainstream_view: Increasingly accepted as a real condition with a 2022 PON1 gene-environment finding providing the strongest mechanistic evidence
testable_prediction: PON1 genotype should interact with documented sarin alarm exposure, as the 2022 study reported
key_evidence_or_cases: Haley and Kramer PON1 study 2022; sarin plume modeling after Khamisiyah demolition; RAC-GWVI reports
implication_if_solved: Would validate and guide treatment for a large veteran population

phenomenon: Agent Orange and dioxin long-term effects
observation_summary: Dioxin exposure is associated with diverse cancers and birth defects decades later by mechanisms that remain partly unclear
