why_it_resists_explanation: Exposure reconstruction is poor, confounders are numerous, and the latency spans decades
leading_hypotheses: Aryl hydrocarbon receptor mediated transcriptional disruption; epigenetic changes persisting across generations; immune and endocrine disruption; confounded epidemiology for some outcomes
mainstream_view: Several associations accepted by health authorities; mechanisms and the transgenerational claims remain contested
testable_prediction: AhR pathway studies and multi-generation cohort follow-up
key_evidence_or_cases: Institute of Medicine periodic reviews; Seveso accident cohort; Vietnamese birth defect studies
implication_if_solved: Would settle long-running compensation and public health disputes

observation_summary: Zika virus causes microcephaly but the severe cluster concentrated in one region while Zika spread far more widely
why_it_resists_explanation: Regional concentration suggests cofactors, and retrospective exposure reconstruction is difficult
leading_hypotheses: Prior dengue immunity enhancing Zika pathogenicity; viral strain differences; cofactors such as malnutrition or pesticide exposure; differential surveillance intensity creating apparent clustering
mainstream_view: Zika causation is established; the geographic concentration remains incompletely explained
testable_prediction: Serological surveys should show whether dengue immunity patterns track microcephaly rates
key_evidence_or_cases: Brazilian 2015 and 2016 outbreak data; experimental confirmation of Zika neurotropism; antibody-dependent enhancement studies
implication_if_solved: Would clarify how flavivirus immunity interacts across serotypes

phenomenon: Why some pandemics are mild and others severe
observation_summary: The 1918 pandemic killed tens of millions with a W-shaped age mortality curve while 1957 1968 and 2009 pandemics were far milder
why_it_resists_explanation: Virulence depends on viral genetics, host immunity history and secondary infections simultaneously, and historical data is limited
leading_hypotheses: Specific viral polymerase and hemagglutinin virulence determinants; bacterial co-infection in the pre-antibiotic era; immune imprinting from prior exposures; cytokine dysregulation in young adults
mainstream_view: Partly explained by reconstructed 1918 virus studies and bacterial co-infection evidence; the full basis of the age pattern is open
testable_prediction: Reconstructed virus studies should identify virulence determinants, and they have in part
key_evidence_or_cases: 1918 virus reconstruction from preserved tissue; bacterial pneumonia autopsy data; antigenic recycling hypothesis for the age curve
implication_if_solved: Would guide pandemic severity forecasting

phenomenon: Why SARS-CoV-2 severity varies so widely
observation_summary: Outcomes ranged from asymptomatic to fatal across a thousandfold range, only partly explained by age and comorbidity
why_it_resists_explanation: Host genetics, immune history and viral dose interact, and prospective measurement of exposure dose is nearly impossible
leading_hypotheses: Interferon pathway autoantibodies and genetic deficiencies in severe cases; OAS1 and 3p21.31 risk loci; prior coronavirus cross-immunity; inoculum dose; immune aging
mainstream_view: Substantially advanced by COVID Human Genetic Effort findings; much residual variance unexplained
testable_prediction: Screening for interferon autoantibodies should identify a high-risk group, and it does
key_evidence_or_cases: Type I interferon autoantibodies in about 15 percent of critical cases; GWAS loci; Neanderthal-derived risk haplotype
implication_if_solved: Would allow risk stratification for future respiratory pandemics

observation_summary: The pandemic virus has no confirmed intermediate host or documented laboratory precursor, and the proximal origin remains contested
why_it_resists_explanation: Early samples and records are unavailable, the market was cleaned before sampling, and both hypotheses remain consistent with the available evidence
leading_hypotheses: Zoonotic spillover via an intermediate host at the Huanan market; laboratory-associated incident; a spillover elsewhere with amplification in Wuhan
mainstream_view: Genuinely unresolved; scientific bodies and intelligence agencies differ, and the dispute is heavily politicized
testable_prediction: Discovery of an infected intermediate animal population or of relevant laboratory records would resolve it
key_evidence_or_cases: Huanan market spatial clustering analyses; raccoon dog genetic material in market swabs; absence of identified intermediate host; early lineage A and B diversity
implication_if_solved: Would determine pandemic prevention priorities for a generation

observation_summary: Hearing disappears in one ear over hours to days with no identified cause in most cases
why_it_resists_explanation: The inner ear cannot be biopsied, imaging rarely shows anything, and recovery is variable and spontaneous
leading_hypotheses: Viral cochleitis; cochlear microvascular occlusion; autoimmune inner ear disease; intracochlear membrane rupture
mainstream_view: A common emergency with unknown cause; steroids are used with modest evidence
testable_prediction: Inner ear imaging advances or biomarkers should distinguish subtypes
key_evidence_or_cases: Spontaneous recovery in a third to two thirds of cases; steroid trial results; temporal bone histopathology studies
implication_if_solved: Would allow targeted treatment of sudden deafness

observation_summary: Episodic vertigo hearing loss and tinnitus associated with inner ear fluid buildup whose cause is unknown
why_it_resists_explanation: Endolymphatic hydrops is found in many patients but also in asymptomatic people, so it may be a consequence rather than a cause
leading_hypotheses: Endolymphatic hydrops from impaired fluid absorption; autoimmune or allergic inflammation; vascular and migraine-related mechanisms; genetic variants in a subset
mainstream_view: A defined syndrome with disputed pathophysiology after 160 years
testable_prediction: MRI visualization of hydrops should correlate with symptoms, which it does only partly
key_evidence_or_cases: Endolymphatic hydrops on postmortem and MRI studies; familial clustering; migraine comorbidity; hydrops in asymptomatic temporal bones
implication_if_solved: Would allow mechanism-based treatment of disabling vertigo

observation_summary: Vertigo episodes occur as a migraine manifestation, overlapping heavily with Meniere disease and making both diagnoses uncertain
why_it_resists_explanation: The two conditions share symptoms, triggers and comorbidity, with no test separating them
leading_hypotheses: A shared ion channel or cortical excitability mechanism; migraine causing inner ear ischemia; two distinct conditions frequently co-occurring
mainstream_view: Now a defined diagnosis; its relationship to Meniere disease remains unresolved
testable_prediction: A biomarker separating the two would resolve the overlap
key_evidence_or_cases: Barany Society diagnostic criteria; high comorbidity rates; shared treatment responses
implication_if_solved: Would resolve a major diagnostic ambiguity in dizziness

observation_summary: Chronic dizziness persists long after the triggering vestibular event resolves, with normal vestibular testing
why_it_resists_explanation: The symptom is a perceptual and postural control problem, not detectable by standard vestibular tests
leading_hypotheses: Maladaptive postural control strategy persisting after acute compensation; altered visual dependence; anxiety-driven reweighting of sensory inputs; functional network changes
mainstream_view: A newly defined entity with a plausible maladaptive-control model and emerging imaging support
testable_prediction: Vestibular rehabilitation targeting visual dependence should help, and it does
key_evidence_or_cases: Barany Society criteria 2017; visual dependence measurements; functional imaging studies
implication_if_solved: Would treat a common cause of chronic disability after vertigo

observation_summary: A stereotyped reflex of diaphragm contraction with glottal closure occurs with no identified function and no agreed circuit
why_it_resists_explanation: The reflex arc has never been fully mapped, and persistent hiccups are rare enough to limit study
leading_hypotheses: A vestigial remnant of amphibian gill ventilation; a burping reflex clearing air from the stomach in nursing mammals; a brainstem pattern generator with no current function
mainstream_view: A recognized reflex with genuinely unknown function and incompletely mapped circuitry
testable_prediction: Comparative studies in amphibians and mammals should test the gill ventilation homology
key_evidence_or_cases: Fetal hiccups observed on ultrasound; intractable hiccups after brainstem lesions; chlorpromazine and baclofen efficacy
implication_if_solved: Would explain a universal human reflex

phenomenon: Sneeze reflex triggers including photic sneezing
observation_summary: Bright light triggers sneezing in many people through a trigeminal-optic crossover that is not mapped
why_it_resists_explanation: The reflex is brief and involuntary, and the proposed crossover site has not been directly demonstrated
leading_hypotheses: Trigeminal nerve cross-activation by optic nerve input at the brainstem; parasympathetic generalization; a genetic variant near ZEB2 and NR2F2 identified by association studies
mainstream_view: A real and heritable trait with an unconfirmed mechanism
testable_prediction: Functional imaging during photic sneezing should localize the crossover
key_evidence_or_cases: Family pedigree studies showing autosomal dominant pattern; 23andMe association study; prevalence surveys
implication_if_solved: Would explain cross-modal reflex wiring

observation_summary: Humans are the only animals known to shed tears from emotion, with no established function
why_it_resists_explanation: The behavior is hard to study experimentally and proposed functions are difficult to distinguish
leading_hypotheses: Social signaling of distress and appeasement; stress hormone excretion; blurring vision to signal vulnerability and non-aggression; a byproduct of autonomic activation
mainstream_view: Treated as a real evolutionary puzzle with several plausible and untested accounts
testable_prediction: Tears should elicit measurable helping behavior and reduce aggression, which some studies report
key_evidence_or_cases: Darwin 1872 observations; chemosignal studies of tears reducing testosterone; cross-cultural crying surveys
implication_if_solved: Would explain a uniquely human emotional behavior

observation_summary: Involuntary facial reddening occurs in response to social attention, a display that appears to harm the displayer
why_it_resists_explanation: Why evolution would produce an involuntary signal of embarrassment is unclear, and the autonomic pathway differs from other flushing
leading_hypotheses: Honest signaling of awareness of social transgression promoting trust; appeasement display reducing retaliation; a byproduct of sympathetic activation in facial vasculature
mainstream_view: A genuine and distinctive human puzzle; the signaling account is favored but untested
testable_prediction: Blushers should be trusted more after transgressions, which some experiments support
key_evidence_or_cases: Darwin 1872 analysis; trust game studies with blushing confederates; facial venous anatomy differences
implication_if_solved: Would explain an involuntary human social signal

observation_summary: Modern humans are the only hominin with a projecting bony chin, which has no agreed functional explanation
why_it_resists_explanation: Every mechanical hypothesis has failed quantitative testing, leaving developmental and selective accounts
leading_hypotheses: Mechanical resistance to chewing stresses (largely refuted by modeling); sexual selection display; a byproduct of facial retraction during evolution; developmental consequence of reduced jaw size
mainstream_view: A long-standing anatomical puzzle; the byproduct account is currently favored
testable_prediction: Finite element modeling should show no chewing advantage, and it does
key_evidence_or_cases: Neanderthal absence of chins; finite element stress modeling; developmental growth studies of the symphysis
implication_if_solved: Would explain a diagnostic feature of our own species

observation_summary: Humans are nearly unique among mammals in lacking a dense coat, at the cost of insulation
why_it_resists_explanation: Multiple proposed drivers predict the same outcome, and timing cannot be read directly from fossils
leading_hypotheses: Thermoregulation during endurance running in open habitats; ectoparasite reduction; sexual selection; aquatic phase (largely rejected); neoteny and developmental timing shifts
mainstream_view: Thermoregulation and parasite hypotheses dominate; no consensus
testable_prediction: Louse genetic divergence dating constrains when clothing and hair loss occurred, and it does to around 170000 years ago
key_evidence_or_cases: Body louse divergence dating; sweat gland density compared with other primates; MC1R pigmentation timing
implication_if_solved: Would date and explain a defining human trait

locus: Human and a few whale species
observation_summary: Human females live decades past reproductive capacity, which direct selection should not favor
why_it_resists_explanation: Testing requires multigenerational demographic data, and the few other species with menopause are hard to study
leading_hypotheses: Grandmother hypothesis of inclusive fitness through helping grandchildren; reproductive conflict between generations; a byproduct of extended lifespan without ovarian extension; patriarch hypothesis
mainstream_view: The grandmother hypothesis has substantial demographic support; the byproduct account persists as an alternative
testable_prediction: Historical demographic records should show grandmother presence improving grandchild survival, and they do
key_evidence_or_cases: Hadza foraging studies; Finnish and Canadian historical demography; killer whale and short-finned pilot whale menopause
implication_if_solved: Would explain the evolution of the human life history

observation_summary: Post-reproductive female killer whales lead groups and their presence improves grandcalf survival, a pattern shared with humans and few others
why_it_resists_explanation: Long-term individual tracking over decades is required, limiting studies to a handful of populations
leading_hypotheses: Inclusive fitness through ecological knowledge transfer such as salmon foraging locations; reproductive conflict favoring menopause; leadership benefits in variable environments
mainstream_view: Well supported in the southern and northern resident populations; generality across species unknown
testable_prediction: Grandmother loss should reduce grandcalf survival, and it measurably does
key_evidence_or_cases: Center for Whale Research multi-decade census; Nattrass et al 2019 grandmother effect study; salmon abundance interactions
implication_if_solved: Would explain convergent evolution of menopause

phenomenon: Whale and dolphin self-awareness and culture
observation_summary: Cetaceans show vocal dialects, named signature whistles, teaching, and possible mirror self-recognition
why_it_resists_explanation: Cognitive testing is extremely difficult with large aquatic animals, and cultural interpretation is contested
leading_hypotheses: Genuine cultural transmission with dialect lineages; associative learning without cultural content; convergent cognitive evolution with primates
mainstream_view: Vocal culture in sperm and killer whales is widely accepted; the depth of cognition remains contested
testable_prediction: Playback and long-term lineage tracking should show stable socially transmitted traditions, and they do
key_evidence_or_cases: Sperm whale coda clans; killer whale dialects by matriline; bottlenose signature whistles; humpback song revolutions
implication_if_solved: Would extend the known range of nonhuman culture

observation_summary: All males in an ocean basin sing the same complex song, which changes progressively each year and occasionally undergoes rapid revolutions spreading across basins
why_it_resists_explanation: Why a display converges on a shared changing standard and why revolutions sweep so fast are both unexplained
leading_hypotheses: Cultural transmission with a preference for novelty; female choice for current song versions; conformity as a social signal; song as a sonar or coordination tool rather than display
mainstream_view: The pattern is firmly documented; the function and transmission dynamics remain open
testable_prediction: Song revolutions should propagate along known migratory contact zones, and they do
key_evidence_or_cases: Payne and McVay 1971 song analysis; Pacific song revolutions spreading west to east; multi-decade recordings
implication_if_solved: Would illuminate cultural evolution in a nonhuman species

phenomenon: Bowhead and blue whale song function
observation_summary: Enormous low-frequency vocalizations carry hundreds of kilometers, and blue whale song frequency has declined worldwide since the 1960s
why_it_resists_explanation: The function of the calls is uncertain and the global frequency decline has no agreed cause
leading_hypotheses: Population recovery allowing quieter calling; ocean noise masking driving adaptation; body size changes; a cultural drift in call conventions
mainstream_view: The frequency decline is well documented across all populations; the cause is unresolved
testable_prediction: Correlating the decline with population recovery and noise data should discriminate
key_evidence_or_cases: Blue whale call frequency decline measured across all ocean basins; bowhead song diversity recordings; SOSUS archives
implication_if_solved: Would explain a synchronized global change in animal behavior

observation_summary: A spiral tooth up to three meters long grows through the lip of males, with no settled function
why_it_resists_explanation: Observation in the wild is extremely difficult, and the tusk has sensory, display and tool-use features simultaneously
leading_hypotheses: Sexual display and male-male assessment; sensory organ detecting salinity and prey via millions of nerve endings; hunting tool for stunning fish (filmed in 2017); thermoregulation
mainstream_view: Multiple functions now documented; the primary selective driver remains open
testable_prediction: Drone observation should quantify tusk use in feeding versus display contexts
key_evidence_or_cases: Nweeia nerve ending studies; 2017 drone footage of tusk striking fish; tusk size and asymmetry data; sexual dimorphism
implication_if_solved: Would explain one of the strangest mammalian structures

observation_summary: Beaked whales dive nearly three kilometers deep for over three hours, surviving pressures and oxygen deprivation that should be lethal
why_it_resists_explanation: Instrumenting free-diving whales at depth is extremely difficult, and physiological measurement at depth is nearly impossible
leading_hypotheses: Myoglobin with electrostatic repulsion preventing aggregation; lung collapse and nitrogen management; extreme bradycardia and selective perfusion; elevated buffering capacity
mainstream_view: Mechanisms substantially identified; the limits and gas management under sonar disturbance are open
testable_prediction: Tagging studies should show predicted heart rate and gas dynamics, which recent tags confirm
key_evidence_or_cases: Cuvier beaked whale 3.7 hour dive record; myoglobin surface charge studies; dive-tag heart rate recordings
implication_if_solved: Would inform decompression physiology and sonar impact mitigation

observation_summary: Birds displaced thousands of kilometers to unfamiliar territory can still correct course to their original destination
why_it_resists_explanation: True navigation requires a map sense as well as a compass, and the map component has never been identified
leading_hypotheses: Magnetic intensity and inclination gradient maps; olfactory gradient maps; infrasound landscape cues; stellar and polarized light cues combined with an unidentified map
mainstream_view: The map sense is one of the long-standing unsolved problems in animal behavior
testable_prediction: Displacement experiments with specific sensory ablations should identify the map modality
key_evidence_or_cases: Perdeck starling displacement experiments 1958; adult versus juvenile correction differences; magnetic displacement simulations
implication_if_solved: Would reveal an unidentified animal sensory map

observation_summary: Birds weighing about 100 grams fly roughly 70000 km annually between polar regions, returning to the same nest site
why_it_resists_explanation: How such precision is maintained over oceanic routes with no landmarks is unexplained beyond general compass mechanisms
leading_hypotheses: Combined sun, star and magnetic compasses with an unidentified map sense; wind and ocean current route optimization; innate route templates refined by experience
mainstream_view: Routes now mapped by geolocators; the navigational mechanism remains unexplained
testable_prediction: Geolocator data combined with magnetic manipulation should reveal cue reliance
key_evidence_or_cases: Egevang et al 2010 geolocator tracking; record-length migration measurements; nest site fidelity data
implication_if_solved: Would explain the most extreme navigation feat known

observation_summary: Birds fly over 13000 km nonstop for up to eleven days without food water or sleep
why_it_resists_explanation: Sustaining flight for eleven days exceeds known metabolic and sleep requirements, and the physiology cannot be measured in flight
leading_hypotheses: Extreme pre-migratory hyperphagia with organ atrophy and rebuilding; unihemispheric or microsleep during flight; fat oxidation efficiency with water recovery from metabolism; wind selection reducing energetic cost
mainstream_view: Flights confirmed by satellite tracking; the sleep and water balance questions remain open
testable_prediction: In-flight physiological telemetry would test sleep and metabolic hypotheses
key_evidence_or_cases: 2007 satellite tracking of bird E7; 2022 record 13560 km flight; organ mass changes before departure
implication_if_solved: Would reveal the limits of vertebrate endurance physiology

observation_summary: Swifts remain airborne for up to ten months continuously, including sleeping on the wing
why_it_resists_explanation: Direct observation of sleep in flight is nearly impossible, and the metabolic sustainability is poorly understood
leading_hypotheses: Unihemispheric slow-wave sleep during gliding; very brief microsleeps; reduced sleep need; sleep during high-altitude ascents at dusk
mainstream_view: Continuous flight is confirmed by accelerometry; sleep in flight is inferred not measured
testable_prediction: EEG telemetry in flight would confirm sleep states
key_evidence_or_cases: Hedenstrom et al 2016 accelerometer study; frigatebird EEG in-flight sleep recordings 2016 as an analogue
implication_if_solved: Would show how sleep requirements can be bypassed

observation_summary: Birds sleep with one or both hemispheres while soaring over the ocean, sleeping less than an hour a day in flight
why_it_resists_explanation: How such minimal sleep is tolerated without the deficits seen in other animals is unexplained
leading_hypotheses: Unihemispheric sleep allowing navigation; reduced sleep requirement during flight phases; sleep debt repaid on land; qualitatively different sleep function in flight
mainstream_view: Directly measured with EEG telemetry; the tolerance of sleep restriction remains unexplained
testable_prediction: Sleep deprivation markers should accumulate during long flights, which they appear not to
key_evidence_or_cases: Rattenborg et al 2016 EEG recordings in flight; comparison with land-based sleep in the same birds
implication_if_solved: Would reveal flexibility in the function of sleep

observation_summary: Monarchs cluster in a dozen tiny mountain sites with specific temperature and humidity, located by butterflies that have never been there
why_it_resists_explanation: The sites are a minuscule fraction of apparently suitable habitat, implying either very precise genetic targeting or local cues
leading_hypotheses: Genetically encoded heading plus local microclimate cue following; magnetic and topographic funneling; conspecific attraction once in the region
mainstream_view: Sites and migration are well documented; the final targeting mechanism is unresolved
testable_prediction: Translocation experiments should reveal whether butterflies find sites de novo
key_evidence_or_cases: Urquhart and Brugger site discovery 1975; microclimate measurements at colonies; tagging recovery data
implication_if_solved: Would complete the explanation of a famous migration

observation_summary: Solitary locusts transform behaviorally morphologically and physiologically into gregarious swarming forms within hours of crowding
why_it_resists_explanation: The trigger is now identified as tactile and chemical, but the full transcriptional and neurochemical cascade is complex and incompletely mapped
leading_hypotheses: Serotonin surge driving behavioral gregarization; tactile stimulation of hind femurs; aggregation pheromone 4-vinylanisole identified in 2020; epigenetic switching of phase states
mainstream_view: Substantially explained over the last 15 years; phase transition details and swarm initiation forecasting remain open
testable_prediction: Blocking serotonin or the pheromone receptor should prevent gregarization, and it does
key_evidence_or_cases: Uvarov phase theory 1921; Anstey serotonin study 2009; Guo et al 4-vinylanisole 2020; FAO swarm forecasting
implication_if_solved: Would allow targeted prevention of devastating locust plagues

observation_summary: Cicada broods emerge synchronously after exactly 13 or 17 years, both prime numbers, with almost perfect timing
why_it_resists_explanation: How an insect counts years underground and why prime intervals evolved are both incompletely explained
leading_hypotheses: Prime cycles minimizing overlap with predator and competitor cycles; satiation of predators requiring synchrony; glacial-cycle origin of long life cycles; tree fluid cues for year counting
mainstream_view: Patterns fully documented; the prime number explanation is plausible but hard to test and the counting mechanism is unknown
testable_prediction: Transplanted nymphs with manipulated host tree cycles should shift emergence timing, which some experiments show
key_evidence_or_cases: Brood emergence records since 1700s; four-year accelerated emergence experiments; brood maps and genetic studies
implication_if_solved: Would explain an extreme adaptation in biological timing

observation_summary: Colonies make accurate collective choices about nest sites and foraging with no individual having global information
why_it_resists_explanation: Mapping individual interaction rules to colony-level outcomes requires tracking all individuals, now newly feasible
leading_hypotheses: Quorum sensing with threshold responses; pheromone trail reinforcement with evaporation; interaction-rate-based task allocation; stigmergy through environmental modification
mainstream_view: Substantially explained for specific decisions; a general theory of colony cognition is incomplete
testable_prediction: Individual-level tracking should let models predict colony decisions, which it increasingly does
key_evidence_or_cases: Temnothorax nest choice experiments; honeybee swarm decision studies; automated individual tracking with tags
implication_if_solved: Would provide design principles for decentralized systems

observation_summary: Bees encode direction and distance to resources in a dance, and recruits fly to the location, a symbolic communication system in an insect
why_it_resists_explanation: How the dance is read and converted into a flight vector by the follower is only partly understood
leading_hypotheses: Vector integration from dance angle and duration with vibration cues; odor cues supplementing the dance; reading via antennal and substrate vibration detection
mainstream_view: Dance language established and Nobel-recognized; the decoding mechanism in followers remains partly open
testable_prediction: Robotic dancers should recruit bees to predicted locations, and they partly do
key_evidence_or_cases: von Frisch dance decoding; robot bee experiments; harmonic radar tracking of recruits; 2023 dance learning study
implication_if_solved: Would explain symbolic communication without a large brain

phenomenon: Insect flight aerodynamics at low Reynolds number
observation_summary: Insects generate far more lift than steady-state aerodynamics allows, a gap once summarized as bumblebees cannot fly
why_it_resists_explanation: Unsteady flow mechanisms are hard to measure on millimeter-scale flapping wings at hundreds of beats per second
leading_hypotheses: Leading edge vortex lift augmentation; clap and fling mechanism; wake capture and rotational circulation; wing flexibility contributions
mainstream_view: Largely solved over the past three decades; fine details and control remain active research
testable_prediction: Robotic flapping wings should reproduce measured forces, and they do
key_evidence_or_cases: Weis-Fogh clap and fling 1973; Ellington leading edge vortex 1996; robotic fly force measurements
implication_if_solved: Already enabling micro air vehicle design

observation_summary: Mantis shrimp have up to sixteen photoreceptor classes and detect circular polarization, yet discriminate colors worse than humans
why_it_resists_explanation: Having more receptor types does not translate into better discrimination, overturning the expected relationship between receptors and perception
leading_hypotheses: Receptor classes used for rapid scanning-based recognition rather than fine discrimination; circular polarization for private signaling; temporal rather than comparative color coding
mainstream_view: The paradox is documented and partly resolved by the scanning hypothesis
testable_prediction: Behavioral discrimination tests should show coarse color categorization, and they do
key_evidence_or_cases: Thoen et al 2014 color discrimination study; circular polarization detection 2008; eye scanning movements
implication_if_solved: Would reveal an alternative architecture for color vision

observation_summary: Cephalopods have a single photoreceptor type yet produce and match complex colors for camouflage and signaling
why_it_resists_explanation: Monochromatic vision should preclude color matching, yet behavior suggests color information is available
leading_hypotheses: Chromatic aberration plus pupil shape allowing spectral discrimination by focus (2016 proposal); dermal opsins in skin sensing light; achromatic brightness matching sufficing for camouflage
mainstream_view: A genuine puzzle; the chromatic aberration hypothesis is intriguing but not confirmed
testable_prediction: Behavioral tests should show spectral discrimination dependent on pupil shape and accommodation
key_evidence_or_cases: Stubbs and Stubbs 2016 chromatic aberration model; dermal opsin expression studies; color-blind electroretinography
implication_if_solved: Would reveal a novel mechanism of color perception

phenomenon: Octopus cognition and distributed nervous system
observation_summary: Two thirds of octopus neurons are in the arms, which show autonomous behavior, and the animals solve problems and show apparent play
why_it_resists_explanation: Studying a soft-bodied solitary animal with a radically different nervous system is methodologically difficult and interpretation is contested
leading_hypotheses: Distributed cognition with arm-level autonomy under central modulation; convergent evolution of complex cognition from a different architecture; overinterpretation of flexible but simple behaviors
mainstream_view: Cognitive abilities widely accepted; the architecture of octopus cognition is a genuine open problem
testable_prediction: Arm-level recording during behavior should reveal autonomous decision making, which recent work supports
key_evidence_or_cases: Tool use with coconut shells; maze and jar opening; arm proprioception studies; RNA editing prevalence in cephalopods
implication_if_solved: Would show how intelligence can be built on a different plan

observation_summary: Octopuses and squid recode a large fraction of their RNA transcripts, trading genomic evolution for transcriptomic flexibility
why_it_resists_explanation: Why this lineage uniquely relies on extensive editing, and what it buys, are not established
leading_hypotheses: Temperature acclimation through editing of ion channels; neural plasticity requiring proteome diversity; a constraint from conserved editing sites slowing genome evolution
mainstream_view: The phenomenon is firmly established; its adaptive logic is partly supported
testable_prediction: Temperature shifts should change editing patterns predictably, and they do
key_evidence_or_cases: Garrett and Rosenthal 2012 temperature editing; Liscovitch-Brauer 2017 genome-wide editing survey
implication_if_solved: Would reveal an alternative route to phenotypic flexibility

observation_summary: Some vertebrates regrow limbs hearts and spinal cord while mammals cannot, despite sharing most genes
why_it_resists_explanation: The capacity appears to have been lost repeatedly, so identifying what blocks it in mammals requires comparing complex programs
leading_hypotheses: Fibrotic scarring response replacing regeneration in mammals; loss of blastema-forming progenitor states; immune system differences especially macrophage phenotypes; positional memory signaling differences
mainstream_view: Mechanisms partly identified; why mammals lost the capacity remains open
testable_prediction: Suppressing fibrosis and restoring blastema signals should enable mammalian regeneration, which partly works in mice
key_evidence_or_cases: Axolotl limb regeneration; spiny mouse scarless healing; zebrafish heart regeneration; neonatal mouse heart window
implication_if_solved: Would unlock regenerative medicine for humans

observation_summary: Axolotls remain aquatic larvae for life, regenerate most tissues, and carry a genome ten times larger than the human genome
why_it_resists_explanation: The giant repetitive genome made assembly extremely difficult until recently, obscuring the genetic basis of neoteny and regeneration
leading_hypotheses: Thyroid hormone signaling failure producing neoteny; transposon expansion explaining genome size; large genome potentially slowing development and enabling regeneration
mainstream_view: Genome assembled in 2018 and 2021; the link between genome size, neoteny and regeneration remains open
testable_prediction: Thyroid hormone treatment induces metamorphosis, and it does
key_evidence_or_cases: 32 gigabase genome assembly 2018; thyroid hormone metamorphosis induction; limb regeneration blastema transcriptomics
implication_if_solved: Would connect genome architecture to regenerative capacity

observation_summary: A fragment of a planarian regenerates a complete worm with correct head-tail polarity, and polarity can be stably reversed by brief treatments
why_it_resists_explanation: Positional information must be stored somewhere that survives extensive tissue loss, and the storage medium is contested
leading_hypotheses: Wnt and BMP gradient reestablishment; bioelectric gradient storage of positional memory (Levin); chromatin-encoded positional identity in muscle cells
mainstream_view: Molecular gradients substantially explain polarity; the stable two-headed phenotype from transient treatment is a genuine puzzle
testable_prediction: Bioelectric manipulation should produce stable heritable anatomical changes without genetic change, which Levin reports
key_evidence_or_cases: Morgan 1898 experiments; beta-catenin RNAi producing two heads; octanol-induced stable two-headed lineages; muscle positional gene expression
implication_if_solved: Would reveal how anatomical layout is encoded and stored

observation_summary: A small tissue region induces head formation and the whole animal continuously replaces its cells while maintaining form
why_it_resists_explanation: Form is maintained through complete cell turnover, requiring a stable pattern memory independent of specific cells
leading_hypotheses: Wnt-based organizer activity with reaction-diffusion dynamics; mechanical and bioelectric feedback stabilizing form; continuous self-organization rather than stored pattern
mainstream_view: Organizer and Wnt signaling established; the full self-organizing mechanism is still being modeled
testable_prediction: Reaction-diffusion models should predict head regeneration dynamics, which they partly do
key_evidence_or_cases: Browne 1909 transplantation experiments; Wnt3 organizer studies; aggregate reformation experiments
implication_if_solved: Would validate reaction-diffusion patterning in a living animal

phenomenon: Immortal strand hypothesis and stem cell asymmetry
observation_summary: Some stem cells may retain the same DNA strands through divisions to protect against mutation, a claim with inconsistent evidence
why_it_resists_explanation: Label retention experiments are confounded by cell cycle and label dilution, and results vary by tissue and method
leading_hypotheses: Nonrandom sister chromatid segregation protecting the stem genome; label retention artifacts; tissue-specific occurrence rather than a general rule
mainstream_view: Reported in some systems and refuted in others; remains unresolved
testable_prediction: Single-cell strand-specific sequencing should directly test segregation bias
key_evidence_or_cases: Cairns 1975 hypothesis; muscle satellite cell label retention; contradicting results in intestinal crypts
implication_if_solved: Would explain how stem cells avoid mutation accumulation

observation_summary: A subpopulation may drive tumor growth and relapse, but whether it is a fixed lineage or a plastic state is disputed
why_it_resists_explanation: Markers are inconsistent across tumors and assays, and plasticity means any cell may acquire the phenotype under stress
leading_hypotheses: A hierarchical stem-like population driving tumors; a plastic state induced by microenvironment and therapy; an artifact of transplantation assay conditions
mainstream_view: The hierarchical model has been substantially replaced by plasticity models in many cancers
testable_prediction: Lineage tracing in situ rather than transplantation should reveal whether hierarchy exists, and results vary by tumor
key_evidence_or_cases: Bonnet and Dick leukemia 1994; melanoma plasticity studies; in vivo lineage tracing in gut tumors
implication_if_solved: Would determine whether therapies must target a specific cell population

observation_summary: Disseminated cancer cells can remain dormant for decades then relapse, sometimes 20 years after apparently successful treatment
why_it_resists_explanation: Dormant cells are rare and hard to find in patients, and the awakening trigger occurs long after monitoring ends
leading_hypotheses: Immune equilibrium holding micrometastases in check; cell-intrinsic quiescence programs; niche-dependent dormancy in bone marrow; angiogenic dormancy limiting growth
mainstream_view: A well-documented clinical phenomenon with partly characterized mechanisms and no clinical test
testable_prediction: Detection of dormant disseminated cells should predict relapse risk
key_evidence_or_cases: Breast cancer relapse 20 years out; melanoma relapse decades later; organ transplant transmitted dormant melanoma cases
implication_if_solved: Would allow prevention of late cancer recurrence

phenomenon: Field cancerization and normal tissue mutation burden
observation_summary: Normal skin esophagus and other tissues carry large clones with cancer driver mutations yet do not become cancer
why_it_resists_explanation: If driver mutations are ubiquitous, drivers alone cannot explain cancer, and the additional requirements are unidentified
leading_hypotheses: Tissue architecture and competition constraining expansion; need for specific mutation combinations and order; microenvironment and inflammation as rate-limiting; immune surveillance
mainstream_view: A major conceptual challenge established by deep sequencing of normal tissue
testable_prediction: Mutation burden alone should not predict cancer risk, and it does not
key_evidence_or_cases: Martincorena normal skin and esophagus sequencing; NOTCH1 clones larger in normal than tumor tissue; aging clone dynamics
implication_if_solved: Would redefine what makes a cell cancerous

observation_summary: Different cancers metastasize to characteristic organs in patterns not explained by blood flow alone
why_it_resists_explanation: Separating mechanical lodging from molecular compatibility requires tracking rare cells over time in vivo
leading_hypotheses: Seed and soil molecular compatibility with specific niches; mechanical trapping by circulatory anatomy; exosome-mediated premetastatic niche priming; organ-specific immune permissiveness
mainstream_view: Both mechanical and molecular factors accepted; the determinants of specificity are incompletely mapped
testable_prediction: Exosome integrin profiles should predict target organs, as 2015 work reported
key_evidence_or_cases: Paget seed and soil 1889; Ewing mechanical hypothesis; Hoshino exosome integrin study 2015; organotropic gene signatures
implication_if_solved: Would allow prediction and blockade of metastatic spread

observation_summary: Tumors sometimes regress following severe infection or fever, the observation that launched immunotherapy
why_it_resists_explanation: The cases are anecdotal and rare, and the triggering immune events cannot be reconstructed retrospectively
leading_hypotheses: Infection-triggered innate immune activation exposing tumor antigens; fever-enhanced immune trafficking; pathogen molecular mimicry of tumor antigens; coincidence in some reported cases
mainstream_view: Historically important and now partly explained by immunotherapy mechanisms; individual cases remain unexplained
testable_prediction: Deliberate immune activation should reproduce regressions, which modern immunotherapy partly achieves
key_evidence_or_cases: Coley toxins case series; erysipelas-associated sarcoma regressions; modern checkpoint inhibitor responses
implication_if_solved: Already the historical foundation of cancer immunotherapy

phenomenon: Why checkpoint immunotherapy works in only some patients
observation_summary: Checkpoint inhibitors produce durable cures in a minority and nothing in the majority, with no reliable predictor
why_it_resists_explanation: Response depends on tumor antigenicity, immune infiltration, microbiome and host genetics simultaneously
leading_hypotheses: Tumor mutational burden and neoantigen quality; T cell exclusion phenotypes; gut microbiome composition modulating response; interferon pathway states
mainstream_view: Several partial biomarkers exist; prediction remains poor
testable_prediction: Composite biomarkers should predict response, which they do only moderately
key_evidence_or_cases: Melanoma long-term survival curves; TMB and MSI biomarkers; microbiome transplant trials improving response
implication_if_solved: Would let oncologists target immunotherapy precisely

observation_summary: Gut bacteria metabolize and modify many drugs, altering efficacy and toxicity in ways not captured in drug development
why_it_resists_explanation: The microbiome is highly variable between individuals, and metabolism occurs in a compartment that pharmacokinetic models treat simplistically
leading_hypotheses: Direct bacterial drug metabolism; bile acid and immune modulation altering host metabolism; competition for drug uptake; interindividual variation determining response
mainstream_view: Established for specific drugs such as digoxin and levodopa; general scope unmapped
testable_prediction: Germ-free and defined-community models should predict drug metabolism differences, and they do
key_evidence_or_cases: Eggerthella lenta digoxin inactivation; bacterial levodopa decarboxylation; Zimmermann drug metabolism screen 2019
implication_if_solved: Would improve dosing and explain unexplained drug failures

observation_summary: A small number of patients are conscious and sometimes in pain during surgery despite standard drug dosing and monitoring
why_it_resists_explanation: Depth of anesthesia cannot be measured directly, and processed EEG monitors do not reliably prevent awareness
leading_hypotheses: Individual pharmacodynamic variation; inadequate dosing in specific scenarios such as trauma and cardiac surgery; monitor insensitivity to the relevant brain state; dissociation between movement suppression and awareness
mainstream_view: A recognized complication with incidence around one in twenty thousand; no monitor reliably prevents it
testable_prediction: A consciousness monitor validated against the isolated forearm technique should eliminate awareness
key_evidence_or_cases: NAP5 national audit; isolated forearm technique studies showing responsiveness; BIS monitor trial results
implication_if_solved: Would eliminate a feared surgical complication

observation_summary: Cognitive decline persists for weeks to years after surgery in some older patients, with anesthesia versus surgery contributions disputed
why_it_resists_explanation: Separating anesthetic effects from surgical inflammation, hospitalization and baseline trajectory is extremely hard
leading_hypotheses: Neuroinflammation from surgical trauma crossing the blood-brain barrier; anesthetic neurotoxicity; unmasking of preexisting neurodegeneration; hospitalization and delirium effects
mainstream_view: Real as a phenomenon; the causal role of anesthesia specifically is contested after regional versus general anesthesia trials showed little difference
testable_prediction: Regional versus general anesthesia trials should separate the contributions, and they largely have
key_evidence_or_cases: ISPOCD studies; regional versus general anesthesia randomized trials; delirium as a risk factor
implication_if_solved: Would guide surgical decisions in older patients

observation_summary: Acute global confusion is triggered by diverse insults and predicts long-term cognitive decline, with no unifying mechanism
why_it_resists_explanation: It is a final common pathway for many insults, so a single mechanism may not exist and the state is transient
leading_hypotheses: Neuroinflammation and cytokine effects on neurotransmission; cholinergic deficiency with dopaminergic excess; network disconnection and reduced functional integration; impaired cerebral energy metabolism
mainstream_view: A recognized syndrome with major prognostic weight and no established mechanism or effective drug treatment
testable_prediction: EEG measures of network integration should track delirium severity, and they do
key_evidence_or_cases: Confusion Assessment Method validation; EEG slowing and connectivity studies; antipsychotic trial failures
implication_if_solved: Would prevent a major driver of hospital mortality and dementia

observation_summary: Many patients report persistent cognitive difficulties after chemotherapy, with inconsistent objective findings
why_it_resists_explanation: Self-report and objective testing often diverge, and fatigue depression and the cancer itself are confounds
leading_hypotheses: Direct neurotoxicity to white matter and progenitor cells; neuroinflammation and cytokine effects; oxidative stress; psychological and fatigue contributions; hormonal changes
mainstream_view: Increasingly accepted as having a biological component; mechanisms and magnitude contested
testable_prediction: Imaging and biomarker studies should show changes tracking objective deficits, with partial support
key_evidence_or_cases: White matter changes on diffusion imaging; pre-treatment baseline studies showing deficits before chemotherapy; animal model neurogenesis effects
implication_if_solved: Would validate and treat a common survivorship complaint

phenomenon: Why some people never get infected during outbreaks
observation_summary: Some individuals resist infection despite heavy repeated exposure, demonstrated in human challenge studies
why_it_resists_explanation: Genetic resistance is identified for only a few pathogens, and quantifying exposure in natural settings is nearly impossible
leading_hypotheses: Specific genetic resistance such as CCR5 delta32 for HIV and FUT2 for norovirus; pre-existing cross-reactive T cell immunity; superior mucosal innate responses; chance in exposure dose
mainstream_view: Established for several pathogens; most resistance remains unexplained
testable_prediction: Human challenge studies with full immune profiling should identify resistance correlates, and recent COVID challenge work did in part
key_evidence_or_cases: CCR5 delta32 HIV resistance; FUT2 nonsecretor norovirus resistance; 2022 and 2023 SARS-CoV-2 challenge studies
implication_if_solved: Would reveal targets for universal protective interventions

locus: A small fraction of HIV-positive people
observation_summary: A tiny minority control HIV without treatment for decades, maintaining undetectable viral loads
why_it_resists_explanation: The mechanism involves specific HLA alleles plus T cell qualities that cannot be induced by current vaccines
leading_hypotheses: HLA-B57 and B27 restricted CD8 T cell responses targeting conserved epitopes; integration of provirus into transcriptionally silent genome regions; superior CD8 metabolic fitness
mainstream_view: Well characterized immunologically; reproducing the state therapeutically has failed so far
testable_prediction: Therapeutic vaccination should reproduce elite controller T cell profiles, which it has not yet
key_evidence_or_cases: HLA-B57 enrichment in controllers; Jiang et al 2020 provirus integration site study; the Berlin and London patients as separate cures
implication_if_solved: Would guide a functional cure strategy for HIV

phenomenon: Long-term nonprogression and spontaneous clearance of hepatitis C
observation_summary: About a quarter of people clear hepatitis C spontaneously while the rest become chronically infected
why_it_resists_explanation: Clearance happens early and asymptomatically, so the immune events are usually unobserved
leading_hypotheses: IL28B interferon lambda genotype determining response; strong early CD4 helper responses; HLA class II associations; viral kinetics and inoculum effects
mainstream_view: IL28B explains a substantial part of the variance; full determinants remain unclear
testable_prediction: Genotype should predict clearance, and it does strongly
key_evidence_or_cases: IL28B genome-wide association 2009; acute infection cohort studies; HLA-B57 association
implication_if_solved: Would inform vaccine design for a virus with no vaccine

phenomenon: Why BCG vaccine efficacy varies by latitude
observation_summary: BCG protection against pulmonary tuberculosis ranges from zero to eighty percent, with efficacy declining toward the equator
why_it_resists_explanation: Trial populations differ in prior mycobacterial exposure, strain and climate simultaneously, and the trials span 70 years
leading_hypotheses: Prior exposure to environmental mycobacteria masking or blocking vaccine effect; BCG strain differences across manufacturers; vitamin D and helminth coinfection effects; genetic population differences
mainstream_view: The latitude gradient is well documented; the masking hypothesis is favored but unproven
testable_prediction: Trials stratified by prior mycobacterial sensitization should show differential efficacy, and some do
key_evidence_or_cases: Meta-analyses of BCG trials by latitude; Chingleput trial null result; UK trial 77 percent efficacy; strain genomic differences
implication_if_solved: Would guide replacement of a century-old vaccine

phenomenon: BCG and other vaccine nonspecific effects
observation_summary: Live vaccines appear to reduce all-cause mortality beyond their target disease, by mechanisms of innate immune reprogramming
why_it_resists_explanation: Observational studies are vulnerable to confounding by health-seeking behavior, and randomized trials are limited
leading_hypotheses: Trained innate immunity through epigenetic reprogramming of monocytes; heterologous T cell cross-reactivity; healthy vaccinee bias explaining part of the effect
mainstream_view: Trained immunity is an accepted biological mechanism; the magnitude of mortality benefit is contested
testable_prediction: Randomized trials of BCG for nonspecific protection, which have given mixed results
key_evidence_or_cases: Guinea-Bissau cohort studies; Netea trained immunity experiments; BCG COVID randomized trials largely null
implication_if_solved: Would change vaccination strategy in high-mortality settings

phenomenon: Allergy to alpha-gal from tick bites
observation_summary: Tick bites induce IgE to a mammalian sugar, causing delayed anaphylaxis to red meat hours after eating
why_it_resists_explanation: A delayed reaction to a carbohydrate contradicted established allergy doctrine, and the sensitizing mechanism is still being worked out
leading_hypotheses: Tick saliva introducing alpha-gal and adjuvanting an IgE response; delayed absorption of glycolipid-bound allergen explaining the time lag; genetic predisposition in blood group A and B individuals
mainstream_view: Fully accepted since discovery; the immunological mechanism of sensitization and delay is partly explained
testable_prediction: Tick bite should produce measurable alpha-gal IgE rises, and it does
key_evidence_or_cases: Commins and Platts-Mills 2009 discovery; cetuximab reaction clustering in the southeast US; lone star tick distribution mapping
implication_if_solved: Already reclassified thousands of idiopathic anaphylaxis cases

observation_summary: Microbes live kilometers deep in rock and sediment with extraordinarily slow metabolism and possible generation times of thousands of years
why_it_resists_explanation: Sampling without contamination is extremely difficult, and metabolic rates are near the detection limit of any method
leading_hypotheses: Hydrogen from water-rock radiolysis supporting chemolithotrophy; extremely slow maintenance metabolism; dormancy with rare division; subsurface ecosystems isolated for millions of years
mainstream_view: Existence firmly established and quantified as a large fraction of Earth biomass; physiology still poorly understood
testable_prediction: Isotope labeling in situ should measure the extremely slow turnover rates
key_evidence_or_cases: Deep Carbon Observatory estimates; 2.7 km deep South African mine isolates; Candidatus Desulforudis audaxviator single-species ecosystem
implication_if_solved: Would define the limits of life and inform the search for subsurface life elsewhere

phenomenon: Microbial dormancy and the great plate count anomaly
observation_summary: Fewer than one percent of environmental microbes grow on standard media, and most cells in nature are dormant or very slow growing
why_it_resists_explanation: Dormancy is defined by failure to grow, which is not a positive measurement, and resuscitation signals are largely unknown
leading_hypotheses: Interspecies resuscitation-promoting factors required for growth; scout cell models with stochastic awakening; slow growth below detection thresholds; unknown nutrient requirements
mainstream_view: Accepted and partly addressed by culturomics and single-cell methods; most taxa remain uncultured
testable_prediction: Adding specific resuscitation factors should enable growth, which works for some taxa
key_evidence_or_cases: Great plate count anomaly measurements; resuscitation-promoting factor discovery; Candidate phyla radiation genomes; iChip in situ cultivation
implication_if_solved: Would open most of Earth biodiversity to study

phenomenon: Bacterial persister cells and antibiotic tolerance
observation_summary: A small fraction of genetically identical bacteria survive antibiotics without resistance mutations, causing relapsing infections
why_it_resists_explanation: Persisters are rare, transient and defined by survival, making prospective identification difficult
leading_hypotheses: Stochastic entry into a dormant low-metabolism state; toxin-antitoxin module activation; ATP depletion; stringent response activation; heterogeneous drug uptake
mainstream_view: Phenomenon firmly established; mechanisms partly identified with substantial methodological disputes
testable_prediction: Single-cell imaging should identify persisters before antibiotic exposure, which it increasingly does
key_evidence_or_cases: Bigger 1944 penicillin observations; hipA mutants; single-cell microfluidic studies; retracted and contested toxin-antitoxin findings
implication_if_solved: Would solve relapsing chronic bacterial infections

observation_summary: Bacteria enter a state where they are metabolically active and infectious but will not grow on media
why_it_resists_explanation: The state is defined negatively, and whether it differs fundamentally from persistence and dormancy is disputed
leading_hypotheses: A distinct physiological program with specific resuscitation requirements; a continuum with dormancy and persistence; injured cells with repairable damage
mainstream_view: Widely reported in environmental and food microbiology; the conceptual distinctness is debated
testable_prediction: Resuscitation under defined conditions should restore culturability reliably, which it does inconsistently
key_evidence_or_cases: Vibrio cholerae VBNC studies; Legionella in water systems; amoeba coculture resuscitation
implication_if_solved: Would affect water safety standards and infection surveillance

phenomenon: Quorum sensing and bacterial collective behavior
observation_summary: Bacteria coordinate gene expression by density-dependent chemical signaling, behaving as a collective
why_it_resists_explanation: Whether signaling communicates density, diffusion conditions, or something else is disputed, and lab conditions differ from natural biofilms
leading_hypotheses: Density sensing to coordinate group behaviors; diffusion sensing to assess local confinement; a combination plus cheating dynamics; efficiency sensing
mainstream_view: Mechanism molecularly established; the information content of the signal is debated
testable_prediction: Manipulating diffusion independently of density should separate the hypotheses
key_evidence_or_cases: Vibrio fischeri bioluminescence; AI-2 universal signal; Redfield diffusion sensing critique; biofilm spatial structure studies
implication_if_solved: Would enable antivirulence therapies targeting communication

observation_summary: Bacteria in biofilms survive antibiotic concentrations thousands of times above the minimum inhibitory concentration
why_it_resists_explanation: Multiple mechanisms operate simultaneously and biofilms are heterogeneous, so no single explanation suffices
leading_hypotheses: Limited drug penetration through matrix; metabolic gradients producing dormant interiors; persister enrichment; matrix sequestration of drugs; altered gene expression in biofilm state
mainstream_view: Well established clinically and mechanistically multifactorial; no clinical solution
testable_prediction: Dispersal agents combined with antibiotics should clear biofilms, with mixed clinical results
key_evidence_or_cases: Costerton biofilm concept; cystic fibrosis Pseudomonas biofilms; device-related infection studies; dispersal compound trials
implication_if_solved: Would solve device infections and chronic wound treatment

observation_summary: Resistance appears within years of each new drug, far faster than expected given the fitness costs of resistance
why_it_resists_explanation: Horizontal gene transfer and enormous population sizes make evolution extremely fast, and compensatory mutations erase expected costs
leading_hypotheses: Horizontal transfer of preexisting environmental resistance genes; large population size and short generations; compensatory evolution eliminating fitness costs; subtherapeutic exposure selecting stepwise resistance
mainstream_view: Mechanistically well understood; prediction of which resistances will emerge remains difficult
testable_prediction: Resistome surveillance should predict clinical resistance emergence, which it partly does
key_evidence_or_cases: Resistance to every antibiotic class within years; environmental resistome surveys; MEGA plate evolution experiments
implication_if_solved: Would enable preemptive drug stewardship and design

observation_summary: Bacteria and phages coevolve continuously with CRISPR and anti-CRISPR systems, producing unending arms races
why_it_resists_explanation: The diversity of defense and counter-defense systems is enormous and most newly discovered systems have unknown mechanisms
leading_hypotheses: Red Queen arms race dynamics; fluctuating selection maintaining diversity; kill the winner dynamics; a largely uncharacterized pan-immune system shared across bacteria
mainstream_view: Framework accepted; most individual defense systems remain mechanistically uncharacterized
testable_prediction: Newly predicted defense systems should confer phage resistance when transferred, and many do
key_evidence_or_cases: CRISPR-Cas discovery as adaptive immunity 2007; anti-CRISPR proteins; retron and cyclic nucleotide defense systems; defense island bioinformatics
implication_if_solved: Would yield new molecular tools and phage therapy strategies

observation_summary: Giant viruses build cytoplasmic virion factories and encode translation components, blurring the virus-cell distinction
why_it_resists_explanation: Their replication machinery includes genes thought exclusive to cells, and most of their genes have no known homologs
leading_hypotheses: Reductive evolution from a cellular ancestor; progressive gene accretion from hosts; a combination with extensive horizontal transfer
mainstream_view: Biology increasingly characterized; evolutionary origin genuinely contested
testable_prediction: Discovery of intermediate forms should settle the direction of evolution
key_evidence_or_cases: Mimivirus 2003; Pandoravirus with 2.5 Mb genome; virophages parasitizing giant viruses; Medusavirus histones
implication_if_solved: Would affect the definition of life and viral origins

observation_summary: Viruses that parasitize other viruses exist, forming a nested parasitic hierarchy with their own evolutionary dynamics
why_it_resists_explanation: The system involves three interacting genomes and was discovered recently, so ecological importance is unquantified
leading_hypotheses: Genuine hyperparasitism providing host protection; mobile genetic element lineage; a route for gene transfer between giant viruses
mainstream_view: Existence firmly established; ecological role and evolutionary origin open
testable_prediction: Field surveys should quantify virophage prevalence and host protection effects
key_evidence_or_cases: Sputnik virophage 2008; Mavirus; Organic Lake virophage metagenomics; protection of amoeba populations
implication_if_solved: Would reveal a new layer of microbial ecology

phenomenon: Electric fish electroreception and signal evolution
observation_summary: Fish generate and detect electric fields for navigation and communication, with species-specific signals evolving rapidly
why_it_resists_explanation: How the brain computes precise object location from electric field distortions is only partly modeled
leading_hypotheses: Electric image computation in the electrosensory lobe; jamming avoidance circuits as a model of neural computation; sexual selection driving rapid signal divergence
mainstream_view: One of the best-understood sensory systems in outline; the computational details remain active research
testable_prediction: Modeling should predict discrimination performance from field geometry, and it partly does
key_evidence_or_cases: Lissmann 1951 discovery; jamming avoidance response circuit mapping; species-specific electric organ discharge catalogs
implication_if_solved: Would provide a complete model of a sensory computation

observation_summary: Bees detect floral electric fields and spiders use atmospheric electric fields to launch silk for ballooning flight
why_it_resists_explanation: Electric field sensing in terrestrial invertebrates was unexpected, and the receptors are only partly identified
leading_hypotheses: Mechanosensory hairs deflected by electrostatic force; charge accumulation during flight creating detectable gradients; electrostatic lift assisting spider ballooning
mainstream_view: Accepted after careful experiments; receptor mechanisms and ecological scope are open
testable_prediction: Shielding or removing hairs should abolish responses, and it does
key_evidence_or_cases: Clarke et al 2013 bumblebee floral field detection; Morley and Robert 2018 spider ballooning experiments
implication_if_solved: Would reveal an unrecognized sensory channel in invertebrates

observation_summary: Spider dragline silk exceeds steel in strength-to-weight and has toughness no synthetic fiber matches
why_it_resists_explanation: The properties depend on a spinning process involving pH gradients, shear and water removal that cannot yet be replicated industrially
leading_hypotheses: Hierarchical beta-sheet nanocrystal structure in an amorphous matrix; spinning duct processing producing molecular alignment; supercontraction providing tunable mechanics
mainstream_view: Structure and genetics largely characterized; industrial replication of the spinning process remains unsolved
testable_prediction: Artificial spinning replicating the pH and shear gradient should match natural properties, which it approaches
key_evidence_or_cases: Silk gene sequencing; artificial spinning with recombinant spidroins; supercontraction measurements
implication_if_solved: Would yield a sustainable ultra-high-performance fiber

observation_summary: Geckos climb smooth vertical surfaces using billions of nanoscale hairs, detaching instantly without residue
why_it_resists_explanation: Van der Waals adhesion explains the attachment, but the rapid controlled detachment and self-cleaning are harder to account for
leading_hypotheses: Van der Waals forces across setae contact; angle-dependent peeling for release; self-cleaning by energetic contact mechanics; contributions from capillary forces in humid air
mainstream_view: Largely solved and biomimetically replicated; humidity contributions and wear remain debated
testable_prediction: Adhesion should persist in vacuum if van der Waals dominates, and it does
key_evidence_or_cases: Autumn single-seta force measurements 2000; gecko-inspired adhesive tapes; adhesion in vacuum tests
implication_if_solved: Already produced reversible dry adhesives

observation_summary: Insects walk on water and basilisk lizards run across its surface without sinking
why_it_resists_explanation: Explaining the force balance required careful accounting of surface tension and unsteady hydrodynamics
leading_hypotheses: Surface tension support with hydrophobic leg hairs and curvature-generated lift for water striders; slapping and stroking phases generating impulse for basilisks
mainstream_view: Well explained after careful measurement and modeling
testable_prediction: Force plate and high-speed video measurements should match model predictions, and they do
key_evidence_or_cases: Hu Chan and Bush 2003 water strider study; Glasheen and McMahon basilisk mechanics 1996
implication_if_solved: Already informs small robot design

observation_summary: A claw closes fast enough to create a cavitation bubble whose collapse stuns prey and emits light and extreme heat
why_it_resists_explanation: Generating the required speed with muscle alone is impossible, requiring a latch mechanism, and the light emission is poorly characterized
leading_hypotheses: Spring-latch energy storage and rapid release; cavitation bubble collapse producing the shock and shrimpoluminescence; plasma formation in the collapsing bubble
mainstream_view: Mechanism substantially understood; the luminescence physics remains tied to sonoluminescence questions
testable_prediction: High-speed imaging and spectroscopy should characterize the collapse, and partly has
key_evidence_or_cases: Versluis et al 2000 high-speed imaging; shrimpoluminescence report 2001; ocean noise contributions from shrimp beds
implication_if_solved: Would connect biological mechanics to extreme cavitation physics

observation_summary: A limb accelerates faster than a bullet underwater, producing cavitation and breaking aquarium glass
why_it_resists_explanation: The acceleration far exceeds muscle capability and the appendage survives thousands of impacts without failure
leading_hypotheses: Saddle-shaped spring latch storing elastic energy; bouligand-structured composite club resisting fracture; cavitation contributing secondary damage
mainstream_view: Mechanism well characterized and biomimetically copied
testable_prediction: Mechanical testing of the club microstructure should show crack deflection, and it does
key_evidence_or_cases: Patek strike kinematics 2004; dactyl club helicoidal structure studies; impact-resistant composite designs
implication_if_solved: Already inspiring impact-resistant materials

phenomenon: Pistol and archer fish ballistic prey capture
observation_summary: Archerfish spit water jets to knock insects off vegetation, correcting for refraction and learning from observing others
why_it_resists_explanation: Compensating for light refraction and target motion requires computation that a small fish brain performs rapidly
leading_hypotheses: Learned refraction compensation through experience; innate ballistic adjustment with rapid learning; observational learning from conspecifics
mainstream_view: Behavior and learning demonstrated experimentally; the neural computation is unmapped
testable_prediction: Naive fish should improve with experience, and they do
key_evidence_or_cases: Schuster learning experiments; observational learning studies; jet dynamics measurements
implication_if_solved: Would reveal rapid sensorimotor learning in a small brain

observation_summary: Snakes form thermal images using pit organs sensitive to temperature changes of thousandths of a degree
why_it_resists_explanation: The sensitivity exceeds what simple thermoreceptors should achieve, and spatial resolution requires neural processing of a crude optical arrangement
leading_hypotheses: TRPA1 channel heat sensing with extreme sensitivity; pinhole optics plus neural sharpening; vascular cooling improving signal to noise
mainstream_view: Molecular receptor identified in 2010; image formation and neural processing partly explained
testable_prediction: TRPA1 knockdown should abolish infrared sensing, and it does in vitro
key_evidence_or_cases: Gracheva et al 2010 TRPA1 identification; behavioral strike accuracy in darkness; pit organ anatomy studies
implication_if_solved: Would complete the account of a non-visual imaging sense

observation_summary: Platypuses hunt with eyes ears and nostrils closed, using bill electroreceptors and mechanoreceptors to locate prey
why_it_resists_explanation: Electroreception in a mammal was unexpected, and how electrical and mechanical signals are combined for ranging is only partly explained
leading_hypotheses: Electro-mechanical time difference computation for distance; dense cortical representation of the bill; push-rod mechanoreceptors paired with mucous gland electroreceptors
mainstream_view: Established and partly mapped; the ranging computation remains a hypothesis
testable_prediction: Behavioral tests with controlled electrical and mechanical cues should confirm time-difference ranging
key_evidence_or_cases: Scheich et al 1986 discovery; bill cortical mapping; prey-capture behavioral experiments
implication_if_solved: Would document a convergently evolved mammalian sense

observation_summary: Bats resolve target distance to under a millimeter and detect insects amid dense clutter using returning echoes
why_it_resists_explanation: Clutter rejection and the resolution achieved exceed straightforward sonar models, and the neural computation is not fully mapped
leading_hypotheses: Delay-tuned neurons computing precise echo delay; spectral interference cues for texture; dynamic call adjustment and jamming avoidance; cocktail party processing in groups
mainstream_view: Well studied and partly solved; the resolution limits and clutter handling are active research
testable_prediction: Neural recordings should show delay-tuned responses at the behavioral resolution, and they largely do
key_evidence_or_cases: Griffin and Galambos 1938 discovery; Doppler-shift compensation in horseshoe bats; jamming avoidance in groups; nanosecond delay discrimination claims
implication_if_solved: Would complete a model sensory computation and improve sonar design

observation_summary: Bats host many lethal viruses including rabies and coronaviruses with little apparent disease
why_it_resists_explanation: The immune features involved are unusual, and the number of bat species makes generalization risky
leading_hypotheses: Dampened inflammatory response with constitutive interferon expression; enhanced DNA damage repair linked to flight metabolism; reduced inflammasome activity; longevity-associated immune features
mainstream_view: Several mechanisms identified; the general picture and its relation to spillover risk remain open
testable_prediction: Bat cell lines should show reduced inflammatory responses to viral challenge, and they do
key_evidence_or_cases: Constitutive IFN-alpha in Pteropus; NLRP3 dampening studies; bat genome comparisons 2020
implication_if_solved: Would inform treatments that suppress harmful inflammation in humans

phenomenon: Why bats live so long for their size
observation_summary: Some bats live over 40 years despite tiny bodies and high metabolic rates, defying the usual size-lifespan relationship
why_it_resists_explanation: Flight metabolism should accelerate damage, so the longevity requires compensating mechanisms that are only partly known
leading_hypotheses: Enhanced DNA repair and antioxidant defenses; telomere maintenance without cancer in Myotis; hibernation reducing cumulative damage; mitochondrial efficiency adaptations
mainstream_view: Phenomenon documented; mechanisms partly identified
testable_prediction: Comparative genomics should reveal repair pathway adaptations, and it does
key_evidence_or_cases: Brandt bat 41-year record; Myotis telomere studies 2018; bat genome consortium analyses
implication_if_solved: Would identify longevity mechanisms in small mammals

observation_summary: Animals drop body temperature near freezing and reduce metabolism by 99 percent, then rewarm without tissue damage
why_it_resists_explanation: Surviving near-freezing brain temperature and preventing clotting, atrophy and reperfusion injury involve mechanisms not fully identified
leading_hypotheses: Metabolic suppression via adenosine and hydrogen sulfide signaling; cold-tolerant tau and cytoskeletal regulation; periodic arousals serving an unknown function; platelet sequestration preventing clots
mainstream_view: Substantially characterized; the periodic arousal function and translation to humans remain open
testable_prediction: Inducing torpor-like states in non-hibernators should reproduce protection, which partial results support
key_evidence_or_cases: Ground squirrel hibernation studies; synthetic torpor induction in rats; tau phosphorylation reversibility in hibernators
implication_if_solved: Would enable medical stasis for trauma and spaceflight

phenomenon: Wood frog and insect freeze tolerance
observation_summary: Animals survive freezing of two thirds of their body water and thaw with full function
why_it_resists_explanation: Ice formation inside tissue normally destroys cells, so protection requires coordinated control of where ice forms
leading_hypotheses: Glucose and urea cryoprotectants; ice-nucleating proteins controlling extracellular ice formation; antifreeze proteins limiting recrystallization; metabolic shutdown during freezing
mainstream_view: Mechanisms substantially identified; full organ cryopreservation in mammals remains unsolved
testable_prediction: Applying the same cryoprotectant strategy to mammalian organs should improve preservation, which partial work pursues
key_evidence_or_cases: Wood frog freeze survival studies; antifreeze glycoprotein discovery in fish; vitrification research in organ banking
implication_if_solved: Would enable organ banking and transform transplantation

phenomenon: Antarctic fish antifreeze and loss of hemoglobin
observation_summary: Antarctic fish survive subzero water using antifreeze glycoproteins, and icefish have lost hemoglobin entirely
why_it_resists_explanation: Living without hemoglobin at all should be lethal, requiring compensations that reduce performance margins to near zero
leading_hypotheses: Antifreeze glycoproteins from a digestive enzyme gene co-opted by evolution; oxygen dissolution sufficient in cold water with large hearts and blood volume; cold-stable microtubules
mainstream_view: Well characterized and a textbook case of molecular evolution; limits under warming are open
testable_prediction: Warming experiments should reveal narrow thermal tolerance, and they do
key_evidence_or_cases: DeVries antifreeze discovery; icefish hemoglobin gene loss; trypsinogen ancestry of AFGP
implication_if_solved: Would predict polar ecosystem vulnerability to warming

observation_summary: Some deep-sea animals grow far larger than shallow relatives while others are much smaller, with no single explanation
why_it_resists_explanation: The depth gradient covaries with temperature, pressure, oxygen and food supply, which cannot be separated in the field
leading_hypotheses: Cold temperature slowing metabolism and delaying maturity; oxygen availability permitting larger size; food scarcity favoring either large storage or small requirements; reduced predation
mainstream_view: Patterns documented across taxa; explanations differ by group and remain contested
testable_prediction: Common garden rearing under controlled pressure and temperature would separate factors
key_evidence_or_cases: Giant isopods and squid; Kleiber scaling arguments; amphipod size-depth clines; oxygen-limitation studies
implication_if_solved: Would explain a major body size pattern in the ocean

observation_summary: Entire ecosystems thrive without sunlight on chemical energy, discovered unexpectedly in 1977
why_it_resists_explanation: The discovery overturned assumptions about the energy basis of life, and dispersal between isolated vents remains poorly understood
leading_hypotheses: Chemolithoautotrophic symbioses in tubeworms and clams; larval dispersal along ridge systems; vent fields as stepping stones with specific current pathways
mainstream_view: Fully accepted and extensively studied; dispersal and connectivity remain open
testable_prediction: Larval genetic connectivity studies should map dispersal routes, and they increasingly do
key_evidence_or_cases: Alvin Galapagos Rift discovery 1977; Riftia symbiont characterization; vent field biogeographic provinces
implication_if_solved: Already redefined where life can exist, including on other worlds
