observation_summary: Worms with no mouth or gut consume whale bone using symbionts and root-like structures
why_it_resists_explanation: Their reproductive biology includes extreme dwarf males in harems, and how they locate rare whale falls is unknown
leading_hypotheses: Heterotrophic symbionts digesting bone collagen and lipids; acid secretion dissolving bone; chemical detection of bone falls by larvae; extremely long larval duration enabling dispersal
mainstream_view: Well characterized since discovery; dispersal and host-finding remain open
testable_prediction: Larval settlement experiments with bone cues should show attraction
key_evidence_or_cases: Rouse et al 2004 description; symbiont genomics; whale fall colonization experiments
implication_if_solved: Would explain specialized dispersal to rare ephemeral habitats

phenomenon: Immortal and highly regenerative colonial animals
observation_summary: Colonial tunicates regenerate entire bodies from blood vessel fragments and fuse with genetically compatible colonies
why_it_resists_explanation: Whole-body regeneration from circulating cells and the histocompatibility system resemble vertebrate features in an invertebrate
leading_hypotheses: Circulating progenitor cells capable of whole-body regeneration; a single-locus histocompatibility system predating vertebrate immunity; germline parasitism between fused colonies
mainstream_view: Well documented with substantial molecular work; the regeneration mechanism remains open
testable_prediction: Transplanting identified progenitors should regenerate a colony, as recent work indicates
key_evidence_or_cases: Botryllus whole body regeneration studies; BHF histocompatibility gene identification 2013; germ cell parasitism observations
implication_if_solved: Would reveal the origins of immune recognition and regeneration

phenomenon: Coral bleaching variability and thermal tolerance
observation_summary: Corals expel their symbionts under heat stress, but tolerance varies enormously between colonies of the same species on the same reef
why_it_resists_explanation: Tolerance depends on host genotype, symbiont strain, microbiome and thermal history simultaneously
leading_hypotheses: Symbiodiniaceae clade D conferring heat tolerance; host genetic variation in heat shock responses; acclimatization from prior exposure; bacterial microbiome contributions
mainstream_view: Mechanisms partly identified and central to reef conservation; prediction remains poor
testable_prediction: Assisted evolution and symbiont shuffling should increase tolerance, which experiments support
key_evidence_or_cases: Mass bleaching events 1998 2016 2024; symbiont clade studies; assisted gene flow experiments
implication_if_solved: Would determine whether reefs can be saved

locus: Great Barrier Reef and other reefs
observation_summary: Entire reefs release gametes within minutes on specific nights, cued by lunar, solar and temperature signals
why_it_resists_explanation: How multiple cues are integrated to produce minute-scale synchrony across species and kilometers is incompletely explained
leading_hypotheses: Cryptochrome-mediated lunar light detection; temperature setting the month and moonlight setting the night; sunset timing setting the hour; chemical signaling among colonies
mainstream_view: Cues identified; the integration mechanism producing minute precision remains open
testable_prediction: Manipulating moonlight exposure should shift spawning timing, and it does
key_evidence_or_cases: Harrison et al 1984 mass spawning description; cryptochrome expression cycles; artificial light disruption studies
implication_if_solved: Would allow reef restoration timed to natural spawning

observation_summary: Females return to lay eggs on the beach where they hatched decades earlier after transoceanic migrations
why_it_resists_explanation: Imprinting on a geomagnetic signature is the leading explanation, but field magnetic conditions shift over decades
leading_hypotheses: Geomagnetic imprinting on natal beach field signature; olfactory imprinting on coastal chemistry; a combination of magnetic maps and local cues
mainstream_view: Magnetic imprinting is well supported by nesting shifts tracking field drift
testable_prediction: Nesting distributions should shift as geomagnetic isolines drift, and they do
key_evidence_or_cases: Brothers and Lohmann 2015 Florida nesting and field drift correlation; magnetic displacement experiments; satellite tracking
implication_if_solved: Would guide conservation of nesting beaches under field drift

observation_summary: Salmon return from thousands of kilometers at sea to the specific stream of their birth
why_it_resists_explanation: Open-ocean navigation and the final freshwater discrimination use different mechanisms, and the ocean phase is poorly understood
leading_hypotheses: Geomagnetic map imprinting for the ocean phase; olfactory imprinting on stream chemistry for the final approach; sequential imprinting during downstream migration
mainstream_view: Olfactory imprinting established; the ocean navigation component remains incompletely explained
testable_prediction: Magnetic displacement should shift ocean-phase orientation, which experiments support
key_evidence_or_cases: Hasler olfactory imprinting experiments; Putman magnetic map analyses of fishery returns; hatchery straying rates
implication_if_solved: Would improve management of a major fishery

phenomenon: European eel and salmon population collapse
observation_summary: European eel recruitment fell by over ninety five percent since the 1980s, with no single identified cause
why_it_resists_explanation: The species has a complex oceanic life cycle that cannot be observed, so causes may act in an unmonitored phase
leading_hypotheses: Ocean current and climate shifts affecting larval transport; swim bladder parasite Anguillicola crassus impairing migration; barriers and habitat loss in freshwater; overfishing of glass eels; contaminant burdens
mainstream_view: Collapse unambiguous; causation multifactorial and unresolved
testable_prediction: Oceanographic modeling plus parasite load studies should rank the causes
key_evidence_or_cases: ICES recruitment indices; Anguillicola spread records; North Atlantic Oscillation correlations
implication_if_solved: Would guide recovery of a critically endangered species

observation_summary: Multiple studies report large declines in insect biomass and diversity, with methodology and generality contested
why_it_resists_explanation: Long-term standardized insect monitoring is rare, baselines differ, and some datasets show no decline or increases
leading_hypotheses: Habitat loss and agricultural intensification; pesticide especially neonicotinoid effects; light pollution; climate change; publication and site-selection bias inflating the apparent decline
mainstream_view: Declines are real in well-monitored regions; the global magnitude and causes remain contested
testable_prediction: Standardized global monitoring networks should resolve magnitude, which they are being built to do
key_evidence_or_cases: Krefeld 1989 to 2016 biomass data; Puerto Rico arthropod study and critiques; meta-analyses with conflicting results
implication_if_solved: Would determine the scale of an ecosystem-level threat

observation_summary: A fungal pathogen drove the largest documented disease-driven loss of biodiversity, with origin and spread only recently traced
why_it_resists_explanation: The pathogen was identified a decade after declines began, and the origin required global genomic sampling
leading_hypotheses: Batrachochytrium dendrobatidis originating in Korea and spread by trade; a second species Bsal threatening salamanders; climate interactions amplifying impact
mainstream_view: Cause established; origin traced to East Asia by 2018 genomics; management remains unsolved
testable_prediction: Genomic phylogeography should pinpoint origin, and it did
key_evidence_or_cases: Berger and Longcore chytrid identification 1998 and 1999; O Hanlon 2018 origin study; 500 species declines estimate
implication_if_solved: Would prevent further pathogen pollution through wildlife trade

observation_summary: A cold-loving fungus from Europe kills hibernating bats by the millions while European bats tolerate it
why_it_resists_explanation: Why European bats survive and North American bats die required comparative immunology across continents
leading_hypotheses: Pseudogymnoascus destructans introduced from Europe where bats are resistant; arousal from hibernation causing fatal energy depletion; immune reconstitution inflammation on emergence
mainstream_view: Cause and mechanism substantially established; resistance in survivors is emerging and unexplained
testable_prediction: Comparative studies should show European tolerance mechanisms, and they do
key_evidence_or_cases: 2006 New York cave discovery; European genotype matching; population declines over 90 percent in some species
implication_if_solved: Would guide bat conservation and model emerging wildlife disease

observation_summary: Billions of sea stars disintegrated in the largest marine wildlife die-off recorded, with the cause still disputed
why_it_resists_explanation: An initially implicated virus was not confirmed, and the condition may be a syndrome with multiple contributors
leading_hypotheses: Densovirus infection (not supported by later work); bacterial boring and organic matter driven oxygen depletion at the body surface; warm anomaly stress; a multifactorial syndrome
mainstream_view: The 2014 viral attribution has been largely retracted; the 2021 boundary-layer oxygen hypothesis is the current leading candidate
testable_prediction: Experimental manipulation of organic matter and oxygen should reproduce lesions, as 2021 work reported
key_evidence_or_cases: Hewson 2014 densovirus study and later reversal; Aquino et al 2021 oxygen hypothesis; Pycnopodia functional extinction
implication_if_solved: Would explain the largest documented marine die-off

observation_summary: Persistent warm anomalies such as the Blob caused cascading ecosystem effects whose propagation is poorly predicted
why_it_resists_explanation: Coupled ocean-atmosphere feedbacks sustaining the anomaly and the ecological cascade both involve many interacting processes
leading_hypotheses: Atmospheric ridging reducing heat loss and mixing; reduced upwelling of nutrients; harmful algal bloom amplification; trophic cascade through forage fish collapse
mainstream_view: Physical drivers partly explained; ecological consequences poorly predictable
testable_prediction: Coupled models should reproduce heatwave persistence, which they do only partly
key_evidence_or_cases: 2013 to 2016 Pacific Blob; Tasman Sea 2015 and 2016 heatwave; seabird and sea lion mortality events
implication_if_solved: Would allow forecasting of marine ecosystem disruption

observation_summary: Massive jellyfish aggregations appear and vanish unpredictably, with long-term trend direction disputed
why_it_resists_explanation: Baseline data is poor, blooms are patchy and episodic, and jellyfish are undersampled by standard surveys
leading_hypotheses: Overfishing removing competitors and predators; eutrophication favoring gelatinous plankton; warming extending polyp reproduction; natural multidecadal oscillations misread as trends
mainstream_view: Individual blooms are real; a global increasing trend is contested after critical reanalyses
testable_prediction: Standardized long-term monitoring should resolve the trend, which is underway
key_evidence_or_cases: Jellyfish Database Initiative analyses; Nomura jellyfish blooms in the Sea of Japan; Condon et al oscillation analysis
implication_if_solved: Would clarify whether ocean ecosystems are shifting to gelatinous dominance

observation_summary: Studies disagree on whether global phytoplankton biomass has declined substantially over a century
why_it_resists_explanation: Historical measurement methods differ fundamentally from modern ones, making century-scale comparison nearly impossible
leading_hypotheses: A real century-scale decline driven by stratification; methodological incomparability of transparency measurements and chlorophyll; regionally mixed trends averaging to little change
mainstream_view: The 2010 claim of a one percent annual decline is heavily contested; regional trends are better established
testable_prediction: Consistent satellite records over longer periods should resolve trends
key_evidence_or_cases: Boyce et al 2010 Nature study; published critiques; satellite ocean color records since 1997
implication_if_solved: Would establish whether the base of the marine food web is shrinking

observation_summary: The biological pump exports carbon to depth at rates uncertain by a factor of two, limiting climate projections
why_it_resists_explanation: Export flux measurement methods disagree, and the twilight zone processes are undersampled
leading_hypotheses: Particle aggregation and sinking rates varying with ecosystem; zooplankton migration actively transporting carbon; microbial remineralization depth setting sequestration time
mainstream_view: A recognized major uncertainty in carbon cycle science
testable_prediction: Autonomous float and sediment trap networks should converge on export estimates
key_evidence_or_cases: Sediment trap versus thorium-234 method discrepancies; EXPORTS field campaigns; BGC-Argo float deployments
implication_if_solved: Would reduce a major uncertainty in climate projection

phenomenon: Ocean mixing and the energy budget
observation_summary: The ocean requires about two terawatts of mixing energy to maintain its stratification, and the sources are only partly accounted for
why_it_resists_explanation: Mixing occurs in sparse intense patches that are hard to sample, and the energy pathways from tides and wind to turbulence are indirect
leading_hypotheses: Internal tide breaking over rough topography; wind-driven near-inertial waves; lee waves from flow over seafloor features; biologically generated mixing (largely dismissed)
mainstream_view: Substantially advanced since the 1998 Munk and Wunsch budget; closure remains incomplete
testable_prediction: Microstructure measurements over rough topography should account for the budget, and increasingly do
key_evidence_or_cases: Munk and Wunsch 1998 abyssal recipes; Brazil Basin tracer release experiment; internal tide energy flux estimates
implication_if_solved: Would set the accuracy of ocean circulation and climate models

observation_summary: The overturning circulation may have tipping points, with recent studies disagreeing about whether it is weakening toward collapse
why_it_resists_explanation: Direct measurements span only two decades, proxy reconstructions are indirect, and models differ in stability behavior
leading_hypotheses: Freshwater input from Greenland melt weakening overturning toward a tipping point; natural multidecadal variability dominating the record; model bias toward excessive stability
mainstream_view: Weakening over the industrial era is supported by proxies; imminent collapse claims are contested and heavily debated
testable_prediction: Continued RAPID array monitoring plus improved proxies should resolve the trend
key_evidence_or_cases: RAPID array since 2004; Caesar and Rahmstorf proxy reconstructions; Ditlevsen 2023 tipping estimate and critiques
implication_if_solved: Would determine a major climate tipping risk for Europe

observation_summary: Cloud feedbacks remain the largest source of uncertainty in how much the planet warms per doubling of carbon dioxide
why_it_resists_explanation: Clouds operate at scales far below model grid resolution and must be parameterized, and observational constraints are weak
leading_hypotheses: Low cloud cover decreasing with warming producing positive feedback; mixed-phase cloud feedbacks; cloud lifetime and aerosol interactions; convective aggregation effects
mainstream_view: Recognized as the dominant uncertainty; constrained to roughly 2.5 to 4 degrees by multiple lines of evidence
testable_prediction: Kilometer-scale global models should resolve convection and narrow the range, which they are beginning to do
key_evidence_or_cases: CMIP model spread; Sherwood et al 2020 assessment; satellite cloud feedback observations; DYAMOND km-scale simulations
implication_if_solved: Would determine the most consequential number in climate science

observation_summary: Aerosols brighten clouds and alter precipitation, offsetting an uncertain fraction of greenhouse warming
why_it_resists_explanation: Separating aerosol effects from meteorological covariation in observations is extremely difficult, and the effect depends on unresolved cloud microphysics
leading_hypotheses: Twomey brightening from increased droplet number; cloud lifetime effects; semidirect effects from absorbing aerosol; buffered systems reducing net effect
mainstream_view: A major and persistent uncertainty; shipping fuel sulfur regulations in 2020 provide a natural experiment
testable_prediction: Ship track and volcanic eruption natural experiments should constrain the effect, and increasingly do
key_evidence_or_cases: Twomey 1977 theory; ship track studies; 2020 IMO sulfur regulation warming signal; Holuhraun eruption analysis
implication_if_solved: Would resolve how much warming is currently being masked

observation_summary: Nanometer particles nucleate from vapors in the atmosphere, seeding clouds, through pathways only recently identified
why_it_resists_explanation: Nucleation involves clusters of a few molecules that were undetectable until specialized instruments were built
leading_hypotheses: Sulfuric acid with ammonia or amine stabilization; highly oxygenated organic molecules driving pure biogenic nucleation; ion-induced nucleation from cosmic rays contributing modestly
mainstream_view: Substantially advanced by the CLOUD chamber experiments; atmospheric relevance of each pathway is still being quantified
testable_prediction: Chamber experiments should reproduce observed atmospheric nucleation rates, and increasingly do
key_evidence_or_cases: CERN CLOUD experiment results since 2011; highly oxygenated molecule discovery; boreal forest nucleation events
implication_if_solved: Would close a gap in the aerosol-cloud-climate chain

observation_summary: A proposed link between cosmic ray flux and cloud cover would make solar variability a larger climate driver
why_it_resists_explanation: The correlation is weak and sensitive to data processing, and the chamber-measured effect is far too small to matter climatically
leading_hypotheses: Ion-induced nucleation enhancing cloud condensation nuclei; the effect exists but is negligible in magnitude; the original correlations were artifacts of satellite calibration
mainstream_view: The CLOUD experiment found the effect too small to be climatically significant; the hypothesis is largely closed
testable_prediction: Chamber measurements should quantify the nucleation enhancement, and they did at negligible levels
key_evidence_or_cases: Svensmark and Friis-Christensen 1997; CLOUD experiment results; Forbush decrease analyses showing no cloud response
implication_if_solved: Already largely resolved against a significant solar-cloud climate link

phenomenon: Global warming hiatus and heat redistribution
observation_summary: Surface warming slowed between about 1998 and 2013 while the climate system kept accumulating energy
why_it_resists_explanation: Surface temperature is only a small part of the energy budget, and ocean heat measurement coverage was incomplete
leading_hypotheses: Heat redistribution into the deep Pacific during a negative Interdecadal Pacific Oscillation phase; coverage bias in Arctic observations; volcanic and solar forcing contributions; the hiatus being largely a statistical artifact
mainstream_view: Now considered substantially explained by internal variability plus coverage bias; the episode is not viewed as a challenge to warming
testable_prediction: Improved coverage and ocean heat content data should remove the apparent slowdown, and they largely did
key_evidence_or_cases: Karl et al 2015 bias corrections; Cowtan and Way coverage analysis; ocean heat content records from Argo
implication_if_solved: Already resolved a widely publicized apparent contradiction

phenomenon: Plant seed dormancy and germination timing
observation_summary: Seeds can remain viable for decades to millennia then germinate at precisely appropriate times
why_it_resists_explanation: Dormancy involves multiple interacting signals and the longest-lived seeds cannot be studied prospectively
leading_hypotheses: Hormonal balance of abscisic acid and gibberellin; after-ripening in the dry state via protein oxidation; temperature and light sensing through phytochrome; DOG1 gene dosage setting depth of dormancy
mainstream_view: Mechanisms substantially identified; extreme longevity remains unexplained
testable_prediction: Manipulating DOG1 and hormone pathways should set dormancy depth, and it does
key_evidence_or_cases: Judean date palm germination after 2000 years; Silene stenophylla from 32000-year-old permafrost; DOG1 studies
implication_if_solved: Would allow seed bank management and crop germination control

observation_summary: Seeds and tissue from thousands to tens of thousands of years ago have been germinated successfully
why_it_resists_explanation: Surviving millennia of DNA and protein damage without repair activity should be impossible by standard degradation rates
leading_hypotheses: Vitrified cytoplasm halting chemical reactions; low water content preventing hydrolysis; dry-state antioxidant protection; permafrost cold limiting damage accumulation
mainstream_view: Germinations verified by radiocarbon dating; the survival mechanism is genuinely unexplained
testable_prediction: Measuring DNA damage accumulation in ancient seeds should reveal protection mechanisms
key_evidence_or_cases: Judean date palm Methuselah germinated 2005; Silene stenophylla regenerated from 32000-year-old fruit tissue 2012; Nelumbo lotus seeds
implication_if_solved: Would enable very long-term biological preservation

phenomenon: Plant electrical signaling and systemic wound responses
observation_summary: Plants propagate electrical and calcium waves after wounding that trigger defense responses in distant leaves
why_it_resists_explanation: The signal propagates faster than chemical diffusion allows, and the molecular basis was unknown until recently
leading_hypotheses: Glutamate-triggered calcium waves via GLR channels; hydraulic pressure waves; reactive oxygen species relay; electrical action-potential-like depolarization
mainstream_view: Mechanism substantially identified since 2018 calcium imaging work
testable_prediction: Knocking out glutamate receptor-like channels should block the wave, and it does
key_evidence_or_cases: Burdon-Sanderson 1873 recordings; Toyota et al 2018 Science calcium wave imaging; GLR mutant studies
implication_if_solved: Would explain long-distance signaling without a nervous system

phenomenon: Plant root foraging and kin recognition
observation_summary: Roots appear to distinguish self from non-self and kin from stranger, adjusting growth accordingly
why_it_resists_explanation: Results are inconsistent across species and experimental setups, and chemical mediation is only partly identified
leading_hypotheses: Root exudate chemical signatures mediating recognition; physiological coordination within a single plant mistaken for recognition; experimental artifacts of pot size and nutrient distribution
mainstream_view: Reported repeatedly but with replication problems and strong criticism of methodology
testable_prediction: Blinded experiments controlling pot volume and nutrient supply, which have given mixed results
key_evidence_or_cases: Dudley and File 2007 kin recognition; self-nonself discrimination in Ambrosia; replication critiques by Klemens and others
implication_if_solved: Would show social behavior in plants if confirmed

observation_summary: Fungal networks connect trees and transfer carbon and nutrients, with the ecological significance sharply contested
why_it_resists_explanation: Field evidence for directed resource transfer is weak, isotope tracing is ambiguous, and the popular narrative outran the data
leading_hypotheses: Functional shared networks transferring resources between trees; fungal self-interest with incidental transfer; isotope signals reflecting soil pathways rather than direct transfer
mainstream_view: Fungal connections are real; the wood-wide web narrative of cooperative resource sharing is strongly criticized in recent reviews
testable_prediction: Controlled isotope labeling with network severing should show directional transfer, with mixed results
key_evidence_or_cases: Simard 1997 Nature isotope study; Karst Jones and Hoeksema 2023 critical review; mycorrhizal network mapping
implication_if_solved: Would settle a widely publicized claim about forest cooperation

observation_summary: Trees stop growing at a maximum height around 100 to 130 meters, and the limiting factor is debated
why_it_resists_explanation: Several constraints converge at similar heights, making the binding one hard to identify
leading_hypotheses: Hydraulic limitation from water column tension and cavitation risk; leaf turgor and photosynthesis limitation at the top; mechanical buckling; carbon balance of maintaining tall trunks
mainstream_view: Hydraulic limitation is the leading explanation with good support from redwood crown studies
testable_prediction: Measurements at the treetop should show water stress limiting photosynthesis, and they do
key_evidence_or_cases: Koch et al 2004 redwood hydraulic limitation study; tallest tree records around 116 metres; cavitation measurements
implication_if_solved: Would determine maximum forest carbon storage

phenomenon: Phloem transport mechanism in tall trees
observation_summary: Sugar transport through phloem over 100 metres appears to exceed what the standard pressure-flow model predicts
why_it_resists_explanation: Measuring pressures and flows inside living sieve tubes is extremely difficult, so the model has never been fully verified in tall trees
leading_hypotheses: Munch pressure flow with active loading and unloading; relay mechanisms along the pathway; additional active transport contributions
mainstream_view: The Munch hypothesis is standard but remains incompletely verified in tall trees
testable_prediction: Direct in vivo pressure measurements in tall tree phloem would test it
key_evidence_or_cases: Munch 1930 pressure flow hypothesis; aphid stylet sampling; microfluidic phloem models; sieve tube anatomy scaling
implication_if_solved: Would validate or replace a foundational plant physiology model

phenomenon: Hydraulic lift and water redistribution by roots
observation_summary: Plants lift water from deep moist soil and release it into dry surface soil at night, benefiting neighbors
why_it_resists_explanation: Quantifying the amounts and the benefit to the plant itself versus neighbors is methodologically hard
leading_hypotheses: Passive water potential gradient flow through roots; facilitation of nutrient uptake in surface soil; incidental leakage with no adaptive function
mainstream_view: Phenomenon established with isotope tracing; adaptive significance debated
testable_prediction: Isotope labeling should show deep water appearing in shallow soil and neighbors, and it does
key_evidence_or_cases: Richards and Caldwell 1987 Artemisia study; deuterium tracing in savanna trees; sap flow reversal measurements
implication_if_solved: Would explain plant facilitation in water-limited ecosystems

observation_summary: Entire populations across continents produce enormous seed crops in the same year then almost none for several years
why_it_resists_explanation: Synchrony occurs over distances far beyond any plausible signaling, implying shared environmental cues plus resource dynamics
leading_hypotheses: Weather cue synchronization such as temperature differentials between years; resource depletion and accumulation cycles; predator satiation selection; pollen coupling through wind pollination
mainstream_view: Predator satiation and weather cue explanations are both supported; integration remains incomplete
testable_prediction: Weather cue models should predict mast years in advance, which they increasingly do
key_evidence_or_cases: Long-term beech and oak seed records; bamboo masting at 40 to 120 year intervals; Kelly weather cue analyses
implication_if_solved: Would allow forecasting of forest regeneration and wildlife cycles

observation_summary: Some bamboos flower simultaneously across their entire range after 40 to 120 years then die, with clonal cohorts keeping time
why_it_resists_explanation: How a plant counts decades, and how clones planted on different continents flower in the same year, are unexplained
leading_hypotheses: An internal cell-division or epigenetic counter; a flowering gene cascade with a long accumulation threshold; predator satiation selection favoring extreme intervals
mainstream_view: The phenomenon is documented in horticultural and field records; the timing mechanism is genuinely unknown
testable_prediction: Clones separated geographically should flower in the same year, and they do
key_evidence_or_cases: Phyllostachys flowering records; Indian mautam rat famines tied to Melocanna flowering; herbarium flowering chronologies
implication_if_solved: Would reveal a biological timer operating over decades

observation_summary: Plants release compounds that inhibit neighbors, but demonstrating this in the field rather than the lab has proven difficult
why_it_resists_explanation: Soil chemistry, microbes and resource competition confound field tests, and lab concentrations often exceed natural ones
leading_hypotheses: Direct chemical inhibition of competitors; indirect effects through soil microbial communities; resource competition misattributed to chemistry
mainstream_view: Real in specific cases such as black walnut juglone; general importance is contested
testable_prediction: Activated carbon addition should remove allelopathic effects, which works inconsistently
key_evidence_or_cases: Juglone from black walnut; Centaurea invasion catechin claims and failed replications; garlic mustard soil effects
implication_if_solved: Would clarify a mechanism of plant competition and invasion

observation_summary: Only a small fraction of introduced species become invasive, and which ones is largely unpredictable
why_it_resists_explanation: Invasion success depends on species traits, propagule pressure, recipient community and chance interacting nonlinearly
leading_hypotheses: Enemy release from native predators and pathogens; novel weapons such as allelochemicals; empty niche availability; propagule pressure dominating trait effects; evolutionary change after introduction
mainstream_view: Patterns well documented; predictive power remains poor despite decades of work
testable_prediction: Trait-based models should predict invasiveness, which they do only weakly
key_evidence_or_cases: Tens of thousands of introduction records; tens rule estimates; cane toad and zebra mussel case studies
implication_if_solved: Would allow prevention rather than reaction in biosecurity

observation_summary: Species richness increases toward the tropics across nearly all taxa, with over thirty proposed explanations and no consensus
why_it_resists_explanation: The pattern has many correlated candidate drivers including energy, area, time and temperature that cannot be separated observationally
leading_hypotheses: Higher energy supporting more species; longer evolutionary time in tropical regions; faster speciation rates in the tropics; greater tropical area; stability reducing extinction
mainstream_view: The pattern is among the most robust in ecology; the explanation remains genuinely unsettled
testable_prediction: Phylogenetic analyses should show whether tropical speciation rates are higher, with conflicting results
key_evidence_or_cases: Wallace and Humboldt observations; global richness maps; fossil record gradients; speciation rate analyses
implication_if_solved: Would explain the fundamental pattern of life distribution on Earth

observation_summary: Species number scales with area as a power law with an exponent clustering near 0.25 across very different systems
why_it_resists_explanation: No derivation predicts the exponent value from first principles, and multiple mechanisms produce similar curves
leading_hypotheses: Random placement and sampling effects; habitat heterogeneity increasing with area; island equilibrium between colonization and extinction; statistical consequence of abundance distributions
mainstream_view: One of the strongest empirical laws in ecology; the mechanistic basis and universality of the exponent remain unsettled
testable_prediction: Mechanistic models should predict the exponent for specific systems, which they partly do
key_evidence_or_cases: Arrhenius 1921; MacArthur and Wilson island biogeography; global dataset compilations
implication_if_solved: Would ground reserve design and extinction forecasting

phenomenon: Extinction debt and delayed species loss
observation_summary: Species persist for decades after their habitat becomes too small to support them, then disappear
why_it_resists_explanation: Confirming that a population is doomed requires waiting decades, so the debt is inferred from models rather than observed
leading_hypotheses: Deterministic decline with long generation times delaying extinction; metapopulation collapse after connectivity loss; rescue effects masking the debt temporarily
mainstream_view: Widely accepted concept with growing empirical support from long-term datasets
testable_prediction: Historical habitat loss should predict current extinction rates better than current habitat, and it does
key_evidence_or_cases: Tilman et al 1994 model; Finnish butterfly and plant studies; tropical forest fragment long-term censuses
implication_if_solved: Would reveal the true magnitude of committed biodiversity loss

phenomenon: Population cycles in lynx and hares
observation_summary: Hare and lynx populations oscillate with a roughly ten-year period documented for two centuries in fur records
why_it_resists_explanation: Simple predator-prey models produce cycles but not with the observed amplitude and synchrony across a continent
leading_hypotheses: Predator-prey coupling with vegetation quality feedback; three-trophic-level interaction including plant defenses; stress-mediated reproductive suppression in hares; climate and sunspot synchronization across the continent
mainstream_view: Cycles firmly documented; the mechanism is a classic partly resolved problem in ecology
testable_prediction: Experimental predator and food manipulation should alter cycle amplitude, which the Kluane project showed
key_evidence_or_cases: Hudson Bay Company fur records; Kluane Lake experimental manipulation; Krebs food and predator exclusion studies
implication_if_solved: Would validate population cycle theory in a natural system

phenomenon: Lemming population cycles and their collapse
observation_summary: Lemming populations cycled with three to four year periods for centuries, then the cycles weakened or stopped in several regions since the 1990s
why_it_resists_explanation: The cycle mechanism was never settled before the cycles began disappearing, complicating causal attribution
leading_hypotheses: Predator-prey dynamics with specialist predators; winter snow conditions enabling subnivean breeding; food quality cycles; warming reducing snow quality and dampening cycles
mainstream_view: Cycles and their recent dampening are documented; mechanism unresolved
testable_prediction: Snow condition monitoring should correlate with cycle amplitude, and it increasingly does
key_evidence_or_cases: Fennoscandian lemming records; Greenland cycle collapse after 1998; snow property measurements; predator numerical responses
implication_if_solved: Would explain a disappearing pattern in Arctic ecosystems

observation_summary: Far more plankton species coexist on the same few limiting nutrients than competition theory permits
why_it_resists_explanation: Competitive exclusion predicts a handful of species, yet hundreds coexist in apparently uniform water
leading_hypotheses: Non-equilibrium conditions preventing exclusion; chaotic dynamics from multi-species competition; spatial microstructure and patchiness; predation and viral lysis maintaining diversity; niche differences too subtle to measure
mainstream_view: A foundational problem in ecology with multiple partial resolutions and no single answer
testable_prediction: Chaotic competition models should predict sustained coexistence, and they do
key_evidence_or_cases: Hutchinson 1961 statement; Huisman and Weissing chaos models 1999; metagenomic diversity surveys
implication_if_solved: Would resolve a central puzzle in coexistence theory

phenomenon: Great Salinity Anomalies and freshwater pulses
observation_summary: Large low-salinity anomalies propagate around the subpolar gyre for years, affecting fisheries and circulation
why_it_resists_explanation: The origin of individual pulses is hard to attribute, and the propagation involves coupled atmospheric and oceanic processes
leading_hypotheses: Arctic sea ice export through Fram Strait; atmospheric circulation anomalies driving freshwater release; Greenland melt contributions in recent events
mainstream_view: Events documented and partly attributed; prediction remains limited
testable_prediction: Ice export records should precede salinity anomalies, and they do for the 1970s event
key_evidence_or_cases: 1968 to 1982 Great Salinity Anomaly; 1990s and 2010s events; Fram Strait ice flux records
implication_if_solved: Would improve forecasting of North Atlantic climate variability

observation_summary: Waves more than twice the surrounding significant wave height appear without warning and have sunk ships
why_it_resists_explanation: They are rare and transient, so instrumental records were scarce until the 1995 Draupner measurement confirmed them
leading_hypotheses: Linear superposition and focusing by currents and refraction; nonlinear modulational instability producing breather solutions; crossing sea states; a combination dominated by linear focusing in most cases
mainstream_view: Existence established and partly explained; which mechanism dominates in the real ocean is debated
testable_prediction: Wave tank experiments and buoy statistics should identify the dominant generation route
key_evidence_or_cases: Draupner wave 1995 measured at 25.6 metres; Peregrine breather tank experiments; satellite radar statistics; 2020 Ucluelet wave
implication_if_solved: Would improve ship and platform design standards

phenomenon: Internal waves and solitons in the ocean
observation_summary: Enormous internal waves over 100 metres in amplitude travel below the surface, visible only as surface slicks
why_it_resists_explanation: They are invisible from above except by subtle signatures, and their generation and dissipation span many scales
leading_hypotheses: Tidal flow over sills generating internal tides that steepen into solitons; nonlinear steepening and dispersion balance; breaking at shelf breaks driving mixing
mainstream_view: Well documented and modeled; dissipation and global mixing contribution remain uncertain
testable_prediction: Satellite and mooring observations should match soliton theory predictions, and they do
key_evidence_or_cases: Luzon Strait internal solitons; Andaman Sea observations; satellite SAR imagery; South China Sea field campaigns
implication_if_solved: Would improve ocean mixing and submarine operation models

observation_summary: The densest water in the world ocean forms in a few small polynyas, and its production appears to be declining
why_it_resists_explanation: The formation sites are tiny, ice-covered and nearly inaccessible, so measurement is sparse
leading_hypotheses: Reduced sea ice formation lowering brine rejection; increased glacial meltwater freshening shelf water; shifts in polynya activity; multidecadal variability misread as trend
mainstream_view: Freshening and contraction documented; attribution and future trajectory uncertain
testable_prediction: Autonomous under-ice measurements should quantify formation rates
key_evidence_or_cases: Weddell and Ross Sea observations; abyssal warming and contraction measurements; Mertz Glacier tongue calving effects
implication_if_solved: Would determine the fate of global abyssal ocean circulation

observation_summary: A vast ice-free area appeared in the winter sea ice for three years then vanished for four decades before briefly returning
why_it_resists_explanation: Deep convection under ice is almost impossible to observe, and the triggering conditions were not measured during the original event
leading_hypotheses: Deep open-ocean convection bringing warm water up; Maud Rise topographic interaction with circulation; wind and stratification preconditioning; stochastic triggering of a bistable system
mainstream_view: Documented and partly modeled; the trigger and the long absence remain unexplained
testable_prediction: Autonomous float observations during a future event would capture the convection
key_evidence_or_cases: 1974 to 1976 satellite observations; 2016 and 2017 partial reappearance; Argo and seal-borne sensor data
implication_if_solved: Would clarify a major potential switch in Southern Ocean heat release

phenomenon: Rapid climate shifts in the last glacial period
observation_summary: Dansgaard-Oeschger events warmed Greenland by up to 15 degrees within decades, repeatedly, during the last ice age
why_it_resists_explanation: The pace exceeds any orbital forcing and the trigger is unidentified, with ice core resolution limiting causal ordering
leading_hypotheses: Abrupt switches in Atlantic overturning circulation; sea ice extent collapse amplifying warming; ice shelf collapse releasing freshwater; a stochastically triggered bistable system
mainstream_view: Events firmly established in ice and marine records; the trigger and sequencing remain unresolved
testable_prediction: Higher resolution bipolar ice core synchronization should establish causal ordering
key_evidence_or_cases: GRIP and NGRIP ice cores; Heinrich events in marine sediments; bipolar seesaw signals in Antarctic cores
implication_if_solved: Would reveal how fast climate can reorganize

observation_summary: Layers of ice-rafted debris record massive episodic iceberg discharges from the Laurentide ice sheet
why_it_resists_explanation: Whether the ice sheet collapsed internally or responded to ocean warming is not resolved, and the timing relative to climate shifts is debated
leading_hypotheses: Internal binge-purge oscillation of the ice sheet; subsurface ocean warming destabilizing the ice margin; triggered by Dansgaard-Oeschger cooling rather than causing it
mainstream_view: Events firmly established; cause and the direction of causation with climate events are open
testable_prediction: High-resolution dating should establish whether discharge leads or lags cooling
key_evidence_or_cases: Heinrich 1988 identification; detrital carbonate layers; MacAyeal binge-purge model; Hudson Strait sourcing
implication_if_solved: Would clarify ice sheet instability mechanisms relevant to future sea level

phenomenon: Marine isotope stage 11 and interglacial duration
observation_summary: One interglacial about 400000 years ago lasted roughly twice as long as others under weak orbital forcing
why_it_resists_explanation: Orbital forcing was unusually weak during this period, so the long warmth requires amplifying feedbacks that are not identified
leading_hypotheses: Weak eccentricity variation prolonging the interglacial; carbon cycle feedbacks sustaining high CO2; ice sheet hysteresis delaying regrowth
mainstream_view: The anomaly is well documented and used as an analogue for the current interglacial
testable_prediction: Climate models forced with MIS 11 orbital configurations should reproduce the duration, with partial success
key_evidence_or_cases: ODP marine records; EPICA Dome C ice core; sea level highstand evidence from Bahamas
implication_if_solved: Would inform how long the current interglacial could last

observation_summary: Glacial cycles switched from 41000-year to 100000-year periodicity about 900000 years ago with no change in orbital forcing
why_it_resists_explanation: The orbital forcing did not change, so the transition must be internal to the climate system and no mechanism is established
leading_hypotheses: Gradual CO2 decline crossing a threshold; regolith removal exposing bedrock and allowing thicker ice sheets; ice sheet size feedback changing response to forcing
mainstream_view: The transition is firmly documented; the cause remains one of the main open problems in paleoclimate
testable_prediction: Ice core CO2 records extending beyond 800000 years would test the CO2 threshold hypothesis, and drilling is underway
key_evidence_or_cases: Benthic isotope stack showing the shift; Beyond EPICA ice core drilling to 1.2 million years; regolith hypothesis modeling
implication_if_solved: Would explain the structure of ice age cycles

observation_summary: Ice ages follow a 100000-year rhythm although the orbital eccentricity forcing at that period is extremely weak
why_it_resists_explanation: The dominant forcing periods are 41000 and 23000 years, so the strong 100000-year response requires nonlinear amplification that is not identified
leading_hypotheses: Nonlinear phase locking skipping obliquity cycles; eccentricity modulation of precession amplitude; internal ice sheet oscillation entrained by orbital forcing; CO2 feedback amplification
mainstream_view: A recognized major unsolved problem in paleoclimate, often called the 100 kyr problem
testable_prediction: A model reproducing the spectrum with realistic physics and no tuning would resolve it
key_evidence_or_cases: Milankovitch theory; Hays Imbrie Shackleton 1976 spectral analysis; Huybers obliquity-pacing models
implication_if_solved: Would complete the astronomical theory of ice ages

observation_summary: The Sun was about 25 to 30 percent fainter early in Earth history, yet geological evidence shows liquid water and even warm conditions
why_it_resists_explanation: Greenhouse gas concentrations high enough to compensate are constrained by mineral proxies that often exclude them
leading_hypotheses: High CO2 and methane greenhouse; reduced cloud albedo and lower continental area increasing absorbed sunlight; nitrogen pressure broadening of greenhouse absorption; a combination of smaller contributions
mainstream_view: A long-standing problem with several partial solutions and no consensus closure
testable_prediction: Paleo-barometry and proxy constraints on early atmospheric composition should test the candidates
key_evidence_or_cases: Sagan and Mullen 1972 formulation; Archean sediment evidence for liquid water; paleosol CO2 constraints; nitrogen isotope paleo-pressure estimates
implication_if_solved: Would constrain early Earth habitability and exoplanet climate models

observation_summary: Hundreds of millions to over a billion years of rock are missing between Precambrian basement and Cambrian sediments across continents
why_it_resists_explanation: The erosion is global in extent but synchrony and magnitude vary, and the removal mechanism must operate worldwide
leading_hypotheses: Snowball Earth glacial erosion stripping continents; supercontinent uplift and erosion; multiple regional unconformities incorrectly merged into one global event; tectonic exhumation
mainstream_view: The feature is real and striking; whether it represents one global event is actively contested
testable_prediction: Thermochronology across many continents should test synchrony, and recent work suggests it is not synchronous
key_evidence_or_cases: Powell 1869 Grand Canyon description; Peters and Gaines 2012 snowball erosion hypothesis; 2019 and 2020 thermochronology studies
implication_if_solved: Would explain a billion-year gap and its link to the Cambrian explosion

observation_summary: Grand unified theories predict protons must eventually decay, but no decay has ever been observed in 50 years of searching
why_it_resists_explanation: The predicted lifetime exceeds 10 to the 34 years, requiring enormous detectors, and simple unified models are now excluded by the limits
leading_hypotheses: Grand unification at high energy with proton lifetime just beyond current limits; supersymmetric GUTs with different decay modes; protons are absolutely stable and baryon number is exactly conserved
mainstream_view: No detection; the limits have already excluded the simplest unified models
testable_prediction: Hyper-Kamiokande and DUNE should probe another order of magnitude in lifetime
key_evidence_or_cases: Super-Kamiokande limits exceeding 10 to the 34 years; minimal SU(5) excluded; Hyper-Kamiokande under construction
implication_if_solved: Would confirm grand unification and explain matter stability

observation_summary: No neutron electric dipole moment has been found despite 70 years of increasingly precise searches
why_it_resists_explanation: Its absence constrains CP violation far more tightly than the Standard Model requires, deepening the strong CP problem
leading_hypotheses: The axion solution making the dipole moment naturally tiny; new physics just beyond current sensitivity; exact CP conservation in the strong sector for an unknown reason
mainstream_view: A central null result driving axion searches and new physics constraints
testable_prediction: Next-generation experiments should either detect the moment or tighten limits by another order of magnitude
key_evidence_or_cases: nEDM experiments at PSI and ILL; current limit near 10 to the minus 26 e cm; planned n2EDM
implication_if_solved: Would reveal new CP violation or confirm the axion

observation_summary: The matter created in heavy ion collisions behaves as a nearly perfect fluid rather than the expected weakly interacting gas
why_it_resists_explanation: Explaining near-minimal viscosity requires strongly coupled dynamics that perturbative QCD cannot treat
leading_hypotheses: Strongly coupled plasma near the holographic viscosity bound; rapid hydrodynamization through far-from-equilibrium attractors; initial state correlations mimicking collectivity
mainstream_view: Existence and near-perfect fluidity established; the mechanism of rapid equilibration remains open
testable_prediction: Small-system collisions should show whether collectivity requires a medium, with ambiguous results
key_evidence_or_cases: RHIC elliptic flow measurements 2000s; LHC heavy ion results; AdS/CFT viscosity bound; small-system ridge observations
implication_if_solved: Would describe the state of matter microseconds after the Big Bang

phenomenon: Color glass condensate and gluon saturation
observation_summary: At very high energy, gluon densities should saturate, a predicted state of matter not yet unambiguously observed
why_it_resists_explanation: Saturation signatures overlap with other effects, and the relevant kinematic regime is barely accessible to current colliders
leading_hypotheses: Color glass condensate as a universal high-energy state; alternative explanations from standard QCD evolution; saturation occurring only at energies beyond current reach
mainstream_view: Theoretically well developed; experimental confirmation is incomplete
testable_prediction: The Electron-Ion Collider should definitively test saturation predictions
key_evidence_or_cases: Forward particle suppression in proton-nucleus collisions; HERA diffractive data; EIC design studies
implication_if_solved: Would complete the picture of hadrons at high energy

observation_summary: Dozens of particles have been found that do not fit the simple quark-antiquark or three-quark classification
why_it_resists_explanation: Their internal structure cannot be read directly from decay patterns, and different configurations predict similar masses
leading_hypotheses: Tetraquark and pentaquark compact multiquark states; loosely bound hadronic molecules; threshold kinematic effects rather than true states; a mixture across the observed spectrum
mainstream_view: Existence of the states is established; their internal nature is genuinely contested
testable_prediction: Lattice QCD and production rate studies should distinguish compact states from molecules
key_evidence_or_cases: X(3872) discovery 2003; LHCb pentaquark observations 2015 and 2019; Tcc tetraquark 2021
implication_if_solved: Would complete the classification of strongly bound matter

phenomenon: Neutrino mass ordering and CP phase
observation_summary: Whether neutrino masses are normally or inversely ordered, and how much CP violation they exhibit, remain unmeasured
why_it_resists_explanation: The measurements require enormous detectors and long baselines, and matter effects complicate interpretation
leading_hypotheses: Normal ordering with substantial CP violation (favored by current global fits); inverted ordering; no leptonic CP violation
mainstream_view: Global fits mildly favor normal ordering and nonzero CP phase; neither is established
testable_prediction: DUNE and Hyper-Kamiokande should determine both parameters definitively
key_evidence_or_cases: T2K and NOvA CP phase hints; global oscillation fits; JUNO ordering sensitivity
implication_if_solved: Would determine whether leptons can explain the matter asymmetry

observation_summary: Several experiments report anomalous neutrino appearance or disappearance suggesting a fourth neutrino species, inconsistent with each other and with cosmology
why_it_resists_explanation: The anomalies appear in some channels but not others, and a sterile neutrino fitting all data conflicts with cosmological constraints
leading_hypotheses: An eV-scale sterile neutrino; unrecognized backgrounds and cross-section mismodeling; multiple unrelated systematic effects
mainstream_view: Increasingly disfavored: MicroBooNE found no excess consistent with the simplest sterile interpretation
testable_prediction: MicroBooNE and SBN program results have largely excluded the simplest models
key_evidence_or_cases: LSND excess 1995; MiniBooNE excess; reactor antineutrino anomaly; gallium anomaly; MicroBooNE 2021 and 2022 null results
implication_if_solved: Would add a new particle species and affect cosmology

phenomenon: Muon anomalies in B meson decays
observation_summary: Measurements hinted that B mesons decay to muons less often than to electrons, violating lepton universality
why_it_resists_explanation: The anomalies required careful efficiency modeling, and the central values shifted when electron identification was improved
leading_hypotheses: New physics coupling preferentially to muons such as leptoquarks or Z prime bosons; underestimated experimental systematics in electron reconstruction
mainstream_view: The 2022 LHCb reanalysis brought the ratios into agreement with the Standard Model; the anomaly has largely evaporated
testable_prediction: Higher statistics measurements should confirm consistency, and they have
key_evidence_or_cases: LHCb RK and RK star measurements 2014 to 2021; 2022 revised analysis; angular observable tensions remaining
implication_if_solved: A surviving deviation would be clear evidence of new physics

observation_summary: Whether certain multiquark configurations such as the H dibaryon are stable bound states remains unresolved after decades
why_it_resists_explanation: Lattice calculations at physical quark masses are expensive, and experimental searches are sensitive only to particular decay modes
leading_hypotheses: Bound H dibaryon exists at physical quark masses; it is unbound; existence depends sensitively on the strange quark mass
mainstream_view: Lattice results suggest binding at heavy quark masses but not clearly at physical masses
testable_prediction: Lattice calculations at physical masses plus dedicated searches should settle it
key_evidence_or_cases: Jaffe 1977 H dibaryon prediction; lattice studies at heavy quark masses; hypernuclear experiment searches
implication_if_solved: Would determine whether exotic nuclear matter can exist

observation_summary: Theory predicts a region of relatively long-lived superheavy nuclei near element 114 or 120 that has not been reached
why_it_resists_explanation: Synthesis cross sections fall steeply with atomic number and suitable target-projectile combinations are exhausted
leading_hypotheses: Shell closures at Z equal 114 or 120 and N equal 184 producing enhanced stability; the island is shifted or shallower than predicted; limits of nuclear binding reached sooner
mainstream_view: A standard prediction with partial support from measured decay trends; the predicted nuclei remain unsynthesized
testable_prediction: Synthesis of element 119 or 120 and neutron-rich isotopes of 114 would test the prediction
key_evidence_or_cases: Oganesson synthesis 2002; increasing half-lives toward predicted shell closures; new accelerator campaigns at RIKEN and Dubna
implication_if_solved: Would complete the periodic table and nuclear shell theory

observation_summary: Frequent measurement can freeze or accelerate quantum evolution, making decay rates depend on observation
why_it_resists_explanation: Explaining why observation alters dynamics brings in the measurement problem, and the crossover between the effects is subtle
leading_hypotheses: Projective measurement resetting the system state; decoherence-based accounts without collapse; environment coupling producing the same effect without observers
mainstream_view: Experimentally confirmed and calculable; its interpretive significance remains tied to the measurement problem
testable_prediction: Decay rates should depend on measurement frequency in the predicted way, and they do
key_evidence_or_cases: Itano et al 1990 trapped ion demonstration; Fischer anti-Zeno observation 2001; cold atom tunneling experiments
implication_if_solved: Would clarify the physical role of measurement

observation_summary: Classical reality appears to emerge because only certain states leave redundant imprints in the environment, a proposal with partial experimental support
why_it_resists_explanation: The framework explains why we see classical outcomes but not why only one outcome occurs, leaving the core measurement problem open
leading_hypotheses: Environment-induced superselection with redundant encoding; a reformulation of decoherence rather than a solution; a complete account when combined with a branching interpretation
mainstream_view: An influential framework with experimental demonstrations; it does not resolve the measurement problem
testable_prediction: Redundancy of information in environment fragments should follow the predicted plateau, and experiments show it
key_evidence_or_cases: Zurek quantum Darwinism papers; 2019 photonic and NV center experiments measuring redundancy
implication_if_solved: Would explain the emergence of classical reality

observation_summary: Quantum superposition has been demonstrated for progressively larger objects with no observed breakdown, but no experiment reaches macroscopic scale
why_it_resists_explanation: Decoherence from the environment grows with mass and size, making it hard to distinguish fundamental collapse from technical noise
leading_hypotheses: Quantum mechanics holds at all scales with decoherence explaining classicality; objective collapse at a mass threshold; gravitationally induced decoherence
mainstream_view: No breakdown observed so far; collapse models are being progressively constrained
testable_prediction: Levitated nanoparticle interferometry should detect collapse-model heating if present
key_evidence_or_cases: Interference of 2000-atom molecules 2019; levitated optomechanics experiments; LISA Pathfinder constraints on collapse models
implication_if_solved: Would test whether quantum mechanics is universal

observation_summary: Whether gravity can entangle two masses, which would show gravity is quantum, has not been tested
why_it_resists_explanation: The required force sensitivity and isolation are at the edge of feasibility, with decoherence overwhelming the signal
leading_hypotheses: Gravity is quantum and will generate entanglement; gravity is fundamentally classical and will not; semiclassical gravity with measurement-induced collapse
mainstream_view: A major proposed test of quantum gravity, not yet performed
testable_prediction: A successful experiment would show entanglement generated only by gravitational interaction
key_evidence_or_cases: Bose et al and Marletto-Vedral proposals 2017; levitated nanodiamond experiments in development
implication_if_solved: Would determine whether gravity must be quantized

observation_summary: An accelerating observer should perceive a thermal bath of particles in empty space, predicted but never directly observed
why_it_resists_explanation: The required acceleration for a measurable temperature is enormous, about 10 to the 20 metres per second squared for one kelvin
leading_hypotheses: The effect is real and follows from quantum field theory; analogue systems demonstrate the physics; the effect may be unobservable in principle for practical accelerations
mainstream_view: Theoretically accepted as a consequence of quantum field theory; direct detection remains out of reach
testable_prediction: Analogue experiments in Bose-Einstein condensates and electron channeling should show Unruh-like signatures
key_evidence_or_cases: Unruh 1976 derivation; proposed electron accelerator tests; analogue gravity experiments
implication_if_solved: Would confirm the observer dependence of particle content

observation_summary: Black holes should radiate thermally, but the temperature of a stellar black hole is nanokelvin, far below the cosmic microwave background
why_it_resists_explanation: The signal is utterly swamped by background radiation and accretion emission, making astrophysical detection impossible
leading_hypotheses: The radiation exists as predicted; analogue systems reproduce the mechanism; modifications at the horizon could alter the spectrum
mainstream_view: Theoretically central and widely accepted; astrophysical detection is considered infeasible
testable_prediction: Analogue Hawking radiation in Bose-Einstein condensates and water tanks has been observed, supporting the mechanism
key_evidence_or_cases: Hawking 1974 derivation; Steinhauer analogue condensate measurements 2016 and 2019; optical analogue experiments
implication_if_solved: Would confirm quantum field theory in curved spacetime

observation_summary: Analogue black holes reproduce Hawking radiation but whether they reproduce information loss is unclear
why_it_resists_explanation: Analogue systems have known underlying microphysics, so they may not capture the actual gravitational paradox
leading_hypotheses: Analogues capture kinematics but not the dynamics relevant to information loss; the analogy extends further than expected; the comparison is fundamentally limited
mainstream_view: Useful as a probe of kinematics; relevance to the real paradox is debated
testable_prediction: Correlation measurements in analogue systems should show entanglement structure matching predictions
key_evidence_or_cases: Steinhauer condensate entanglement measurements; water tank horizon experiments; optical fiber analogues
implication_if_solved: Would clarify what analogue gravity can and cannot teach us

observation_summary: Quantum field theory predicts a vacuum energy density up to 120 orders of magnitude larger than the observed cosmological constant
why_it_resists_explanation: No known symmetry cancels the vacuum energy to the required precision, and supersymmetry would only reduce the discrepancy
leading_hypotheses: Supersymmetric cancellation (insufficient); anthropic selection in a landscape of vacua; a dynamical mechanism relaxing the constant; gravity not coupling to vacuum energy as assumed
mainstream_view: Described as the worst theoretical prediction in physics; entirely unresolved
testable_prediction: Any mechanism must predict the observed value rather than accommodate it
key_evidence_or_cases: Casimir effect confirming vacuum energy differences are real; measured cosmological constant; failed naturalness arguments
implication_if_solved: Would resolve the largest quantitative failure in theoretical physics

phenomenon: Casimir effect sign and geometry dependence
observation_summary: Vacuum fluctuations produce measurable forces between surfaces, with sign and magnitude depending on geometry in ways that resist general calculation
why_it_resists_explanation: Exact solutions exist only for simple geometries, and material dispersion and roughness complicate comparison with experiment
leading_hypotheses: Standard quantum electrodynamic vacuum fluctuation pressure; equivalent description via retarded van der Waals forces between materials; geometry dependence requiring numerical scattering methods
mainstream_view: The effect is confirmed and calculable in principle; repulsive and nontrivial geometries remain an active research area
testable_prediction: Measured forces for new geometries should match numerical predictions, and they increasingly do
key_evidence_or_cases: Casimir 1948 prediction; Lamoreaux 1997 measurement; repulsive Casimir force in fluids 2009; metamaterial proposals
implication_if_solved: Would matter for nanoscale device design and vacuum energy understanding

observation_summary: Rapidly changing boundary conditions create real photons from vacuum, demonstrated only in superconducting circuit analogues
why_it_resists_explanation: Moving a physical mirror fast enough is impossible, so demonstrations use effective modulated boundaries
leading_hypotheses: Photon creation from vacuum by time-dependent boundary conditions; the circuit demonstrations are faithful realizations; mechanical realization remains infeasible
mainstream_view: Demonstrated in circuit QED and considered established; mechanical realization remains undone
testable_prediction: Modulating boundary conditions should produce correlated photon pairs, and it does
key_evidence_or_cases: Wilson et al 2011 superconducting circuit demonstration; Lahteenmaki 2013 metamaterial array; Moore 1970 prediction
implication_if_solved: Would confirm particle creation from vacuum by motion

phenomenon: Quantum thermodynamics and Maxwell demon limits
observation_summary: Information can be converted to work and erasing it costs energy, with the quantum regime limits still being mapped
why_it_resists_explanation: Fluctuations dominate at small scales, so thermodynamic quantities must be redefined, and quantum coherence contributions are unsettled
leading_hypotheses: Landauer bound as the fundamental erasure cost; quantum coherence providing extractable work; fluctuation theorems generalizing the second law
mainstream_view: Landauer bound experimentally confirmed; quantum extensions actively developed
testable_prediction: Single-molecule and single-electron experiments should match generalized fluctuation theorems, and they do
key_evidence_or_cases: Landauer 1961 principle; Berut et al 2012 erasure energy measurement; Toyabe information-to-energy conversion 2010
implication_if_solved: Would set fundamental limits on computation energy

observation_summary: Systems with bounded energy spectra can have negative absolute temperature, hotter than infinite temperature
why_it_resists_explanation: Negative temperature requires an inverted population and a bounded spectrum, and whether the standard entropy definition applies is disputed
leading_hypotheses: Negative temperature is a legitimate thermodynamic state with the Boltzmann entropy; the Gibbs volume entropy definition eliminates negative temperatures; the dispute is about definitions not physics
mainstream_view: Experimentally realized and accepted; the correct entropy definition is contested in the literature
testable_prediction: Experiments distinguishing Boltzmann and Gibbs entropy predictions, which are hard to design
key_evidence_or_cases: Purcell and Pound 1951 nuclear spin experiment; Braun et al 2013 motional degrees of freedom in cold atoms; Dunkel and Hilbert critique 2014
implication_if_solved: Would settle the foundations of statistical mechanics definitions

observation_summary: Systems can break time translation symmetry, oscillating indefinitely in their lowest-energy or driven steady state
why_it_resists_explanation: Equilibrium time crystals were proven impossible, so realizations use driven or dissipative systems whose status as true time crystals was debated
leading_hypotheses: Discrete time crystals in periodically driven many-body localized systems; dissipative time crystals; continuous time crystals in open systems
mainstream_view: Discrete time crystals are now accepted as realized; the conceptual boundaries remain debated
testable_prediction: Subharmonic response robust to perturbations should persist, and it does
key_evidence_or_cases: Wilczek 2012 proposal; Watanabe-Oshikawa no-go theorem; trapped ion and NV center realizations 2017; Google quantum processor 2021
implication_if_solved: Would establish a new nonequilibrium phase of matter

observation_summary: Strongly disordered interacting systems appear to fail to thermalize, retaining memory of initial conditions indefinitely
why_it_resists_explanation: Whether true localization survives in the thermodynamic limit or is only a long-lived transient is unresolved and numerically hard
leading_hypotheses: True many-body localized phase with emergent integrability; an extremely slow thermalizing regime that eventually relaxes; avalanche instability destroying localization in large systems
mainstream_view: An intensely studied regime; whether the phase is genuinely stable is actively contested
testable_prediction: Larger system simulations and longer-time experiments should show whether thermalization eventually occurs
key_evidence_or_cases: Basko Aleiner Altshuler 2006; cold atom MBL experiments; numerical avalanche instability arguments since 2019
implication_if_solved: Would determine whether quantum systems can permanently evade thermalization

observation_summary: How closed quantum systems reach thermal equilibrium despite unitary reversible evolution is only partly explained
why_it_resists_explanation: Thermalization must emerge from unitary dynamics, requiring assumptions about eigenstate structure that are hard to prove
leading_hypotheses: Eigenstate thermalization hypothesis with random-matrix-like eigenstates; typicality arguments; integrable systems as exceptions requiring generalized ensembles
mainstream_view: The eigenstate thermalization hypothesis is widely supported numerically but not proven
testable_prediction: Numerical tests on larger systems should confirm eigenstate thermalization, and they do
key_evidence_or_cases: Deutsch 1991 and Srednicki 1994 formulations; cold atom quench experiments; numerical ETH verifications
implication_if_solved: Would derive statistical mechanics from quantum mechanics

observation_summary: Claims of computational advantage over classical computers have repeatedly been challenged by improved classical algorithms
why_it_resists_explanation: Verifying that a quantum device solved a problem no classical computer can is itself computationally hard
leading_hypotheses: Genuine advantage for specific sampling problems; classical spoofing algorithms closing the gap; advantage existing but the specific demonstrations being weaker than claimed
mainstream_view: Advantage for sampling tasks is partially accepted; several specific claims were substantially eroded by classical simulations
testable_prediction: Scalable verification protocols and problems with efficiently checkable answers
key_evidence_or_cases: Google Sycamore 2019 claim; tensor network classical spoofing; Jiuzhang photonic sampling; Shor factoring as an eventually checkable task
implication_if_solved: Would establish the practical limits of classical computation

phenomenon: Quantum error correction threshold in practice
observation_summary: Error correction should allow arbitrary scaling below a threshold error rate, but reaching the regime of genuine error suppression took three decades
why_it_resists_explanation: Correlated and leakage errors violate the independent-error assumptions of threshold theorems, and the overhead is enormous
leading_hypotheses: Surface codes achieving exponential suppression with sufficient qubits; correlated errors requiring new codes; cosmic ray and leakage events imposing practical ceilings
mainstream_view: Theory established and below-threshold operation demonstrated in 2023 to 2024; large-scale fault tolerance remains unproven
testable_prediction: Scaling code distance should exponentially suppress logical error, which recent experiments demonstrate
key_evidence_or_cases: Shor and Steane codes; surface code theory; Google 2023 and 2024 below-threshold demonstrations; cosmic ray correlated error observations
implication_if_solved: Would make large-scale quantum computing feasible

observation_summary: Excitations carry fractional charge and obey statistics that are neither bosonic nor fermionic
why_it_resists_explanation: Direct demonstration of braiding statistics is extremely difficult, and non-abelian statistics remained unconfirmed for decades
leading_hypotheses: Fractional quantum Hall states hosting abelian anyons (confirmed); non-abelian anyons at specific filling factors; Majorana zero modes in superconductor-semiconductor devices
mainstream_view: Fractional charge and abelian braiding confirmed; non-abelian statistics evidence is growing but contested
testable_prediction: Interferometry should show the predicted braiding phases, which 2020 experiments reported
key_evidence_or_cases: Laughlin wavefunction 1983; fractional charge shot noise measurements 1997; 2020 anyon braiding interferometry; retracted Majorana papers
implication_if_solved: Would enable topological quantum computing

observation_summary: Signatures claimed as Majorana zero modes have repeatedly turned out to have mundane explanations, including two retracted Nature papers
why_it_resists_explanation: The predicted signature, a zero-bias conductance peak, can be mimicked by disorder and trivial Andreev states
leading_hypotheses: Genuine Majorana bound states in topological superconductors; trivial Andreev bound states from disorder mimicking the signature; quasi-Majorana states in smooth potentials
mainstream_view: Several high-profile claims retracted or reinterpreted; the field now demands much stronger criteria
testable_prediction: Quantized conductance plus braiding demonstration rather than zero-bias peaks alone
key_evidence_or_cases: Mourik et al 2012; 2021 Nature retraction; 2022 topological gap protocol claims and critiques
implication_if_solved: Would enable fault-tolerant topological qubits if genuinely realized

observation_summary: Claims of near-room-temperature superconductivity in hydrides under extreme pressure include both accepted results and retracted fraudulent ones
why_it_resists_explanation: Measurements in diamond anvil cells are extremely difficult, samples are microscopic, and raw data has sometimes been withheld or manipulated
leading_hypotheses: Conventional phonon-mediated superconductivity at high Tc in hydrogen-rich compounds (accepted for H3S and LaH10); data fabrication in specific retracted claims; pressure and composition uncertainties inflating reported Tc
mainstream_view: H3S and LaH10 superconductivity is accepted; the carbonaceous sulfur hydride and Lu-N-H claims were retracted amid misconduct findings
testable_prediction: Independent replication with published raw data, which has failed for the retracted claims
key_evidence_or_cases: Drozdov H3S 2015; LaH10 at 250 K; Dias 2020 and 2023 retractions; Hirsch critiques
implication_if_solved: Would deliver ambient superconductivity if a genuine route exists

observation_summary: Whether superconductivity at ambient temperature and pressure is physically possible is unknown, with no theoretical upper limit established
why_it_resists_explanation: Conventional theory permits high Tc with light elements and strong coupling but the required conditions may be unreachable at ambient pressure
leading_hypotheses: Metallic hydrogen or hydride compounds at ambient pressure; unconventional mechanisms in layered materials; a fundamental obstruction not yet identified
mainstream_view: No theoretical prohibition is known; practical achievement remains elusive
testable_prediction: A material with ambient-pressure Tc above 300 K would settle it
key_evidence_or_cases: Cuprate Tc records; hydride high-pressure results; Eliashberg theory limits; nickelate superconductivity
implication_if_solved: Would transform energy transmission, transport and computing

observation_summary: Resistivity rises linearly with temperature over enormous ranges, violating the standard quasiparticle picture and approaching a universal scattering bound
why_it_resists_explanation: No quasiparticle description applies, so standard transport theory fails, and the Planckian dissipation bound has no derivation
leading_hypotheses: Quantum critical scattering at the Planckian limit; holographic strange metal models; marginal Fermi liquid phenomenology; absence of quasiparticles requiring a new framework
mainstream_view: Universality of Planckian dissipation is well documented and theoretically unexplained
testable_prediction: Scattering rates should saturate at the Planckian bound across material classes, and they do
key_evidence_or_cases: Linear resistivity in cuprates over decades of temperature; Planckian dissipation surveys; twisted bilayer graphene strange metal behavior
implication_if_solved: Would require a new theory of metals without quasiparticles

observation_summary: A partial energy gap opens well above the superconducting transition, and whether it is a distinct phase is unresolved
why_it_resists_explanation: Multiple orders compete in the same region, and experimental probes give conflicting characterizations
leading_hypotheses: Preformed Cooper pairs without phase coherence; a competing order such as charge density wave or nematic order; a distinct quantum phase with its own order parameter; a crossover rather than a phase
mainstream_view: One of the central unresolved questions in correlated electron physics
testable_prediction: Identifying a symmetry-breaking order parameter would establish it as a phase
key_evidence_or_cases: ARPES Fermi arc observations; NMR and specific heat signatures; charge density wave discovery in cuprates 2012
implication_if_solved: Would be a key step toward explaining high-Tc superconductivity

observation_summary: Stacking graphene at a magic angle produces superconductivity, correlated insulators and ferromagnetism in a material with no heavy elements
why_it_resists_explanation: The flat bands host many competing phases and the mechanism of superconductivity is not established
leading_hypotheses: Phonon-mediated superconductivity in flat bands; electronically driven unconventional pairing; nontrivial topology of the flat bands as essential; strain and heterostrain effects
mainstream_view: Phenomena robustly reproduced; mechanism unresolved and under intense study
testable_prediction: Isotope effect and gap symmetry measurements should discriminate mechanisms
