key_evidence_or_cases: Cao et al 2018 discovery; magic angle at 1.1 degrees; twisted trilayer and other moire systems
implication_if_solved: Would provide a tunable platform for understanding correlated superconductivity

observation_summary: A predicted state where spins remain disordered down to zero temperature with fractional excitations has no unambiguous material realization
why_it_resists_explanation: Absence of magnetic order is easy to mimic with disorder, and positive identification requires detecting fractionalized excitations
leading_hypotheses: Kitaev material realizations such as alpha-RuCl3; herbertsmithite as a gapless spin liquid; disorder-driven spin glass states mimicking liquid behavior
mainstream_view: Theoretically well developed; experimental identification in real materials remains contested
testable_prediction: Half-integer quantized thermal Hall conductance would be definitive, and claimed observations are disputed
key_evidence_or_cases: Anderson 1973 resonating valence bond proposal; herbertsmithite neutron scattering; alpha-RuCl3 thermal Hall claims and non-replications
implication_if_solved: Would realize fractionalized excitations and host topological qubits

observation_summary: Hydrogen should become metallic and possibly superconducting at high pressure, with experimental claims repeatedly disputed
why_it_resists_explanation: Pressures above 400 gigapascals are at the limit of diamond anvil capability, samples are tiny, and optical measurements are ambiguous
leading_hypotheses: Solid metallic hydrogen above about 400 gigapascals; liquid metallic hydrogen at high temperature (observed); claimed observations being pressure or diamond artifacts
mainstream_view: Liquid metallic hydrogen is accepted; solid metallic hydrogen claims remain contested
testable_prediction: Reflectivity and conductivity measurements with independent pressure calibration
key_evidence_or_cases: Wigner and Huntington 1935 prediction; Dias and Silvera 2017 claim; Loubeyre 2020 reflectivity; NIF liquid metallization
implication_if_solved: Would confirm the predicted state of the most abundant element

phenomenon: Interior structure of Jupiter and Saturn
observation_summary: Gravity measurements show the giant planets have diffuse rather than sharply defined cores, contradicting formation models
why_it_resists_explanation: Interior structure is inferred from gravity harmonics, which allow many solutions, and hydrogen-helium equations of state are uncertain
leading_hypotheses: Dilute cores formed by giant impacts or gradual mixing; helium rain separation in Saturn; core erosion over time; equation of state uncertainties permitting multiple structures
mainstream_view: Juno and Cassini gravity data established the puzzle; interior models remain degenerate
testable_prediction: Seismology or improved equations of state should narrow the solutions
key_evidence_or_cases: Juno gravity harmonics; Cassini Grand Finale measurements; Saturn ring seismology; high-pressure hydrogen experiments
implication_if_solved: Would constrain how giant planets and their cores form

phenomenon: Uranus and Neptune interior and heat flow
observation_summary: Uranus emits almost no internal heat while Neptune emits substantial heat, despite being nearly twins
why_it_resists_explanation: Only one brief flyby has visited each planet, so interior structure and heat flow are poorly constrained
leading_hypotheses: Giant impact disrupting Uranus interior and stopping convection; compositional layering blocking heat transport; superionic ice layers; different formation histories
mainstream_view: A striking unexplained difference between similar planets; a dedicated mission is a high priority
testable_prediction: An orbiter with gravity and magnetic mapping would resolve interior structure
key_evidence_or_cases: Voyager 2 flybys 1986 and 1989; measured heat flow difference; Uranus extreme axial tilt; superionic water experiments
implication_if_solved: Would explain the diversity of ice giants, the most common exoplanet class

phenomenon: Uranus and Neptune magnetic field geometry
observation_summary: Both planets have strongly tilted and offset multipolar magnetic fields unlike any other planet
why_it_resists_explanation: Dynamo modeling requires knowledge of interior conductivity and convection structure that the single flybys could not provide
leading_hypotheses: Thin-shell dynamo in a conducting ionic water layer; convection confined above a stably stratified interior; multipolar dynamo regime from specific Rayleigh numbers
mainstream_view: Thin-shell dynamo models reproduce the geometry; the interior structure assumption is unverified
testable_prediction: Magnetic mapping from orbit would constrain the dynamo region
key_evidence_or_cases: Voyager 2 magnetometer data; Stanley and Bloxham thin-shell dynamo models 2004; superionic conductivity experiments
implication_if_solved: Would reveal the interior structure of ice giants

observation_summary: Titan has an active methane hydrological cycle, but atmospheric methane should be destroyed by sunlight within tens of millions of years
why_it_resists_explanation: A resupply source is required and no surface reservoir large enough has been identified
leading_hypotheses: Cryovolcanic outgassing from a subsurface reservoir; clathrate destabilization releasing stored methane; episodic release with the current epoch being unusual; a large undetected subsurface ocean source
mainstream_view: The resupply problem is well recognized; no confirmed source identified
testable_prediction: Dragonfly surface measurements should identify methane sources and isotopic signatures
key_evidence_or_cases: Cassini-Huygens methane measurements; lake and sea mapping; isotopic ratios suggesting episodic replenishment; Dragonfly mission planned
implication_if_solved: Would explain an active hydrological cycle on another world

observation_summary: Methane has been detected episodically by Curiosity and from orbit, with amounts and timing inconsistent between instruments
why_it_resists_explanation: Curiosity detects seasonal methane at the surface while the Trace Gas Orbiter finds almost none above, which is hard to reconcile
leading_hypotheses: Subsurface clathrate or fluid release through fractures; serpentinization producing methane abiotically; destruction mechanism faster than known chemistry; microbial production (speculative); instrument-specific artifacts
mainstream_view: Detections are real but the surface-to-orbit discrepancy is unresolved and a major puzzle
testable_prediction: Simultaneous coordinated measurements at multiple altitudes should resolve the discrepancy
key_evidence_or_cases: Curiosity SAM seasonal methane; ExoMars Trace Gas Orbiter upper limits; Mars Express detections; nighttime accumulation hypothesis
implication_if_solved: Would determine whether Mars has active subsurface chemistry or biology

observation_summary: Dark streaks grow and fade seasonally on steep slopes, initially interpreted as flowing brine
why_it_resists_explanation: Liquid water should be unstable at Martian surface conditions, and the features behave in ways both wet and dry models struggle with
leading_hypotheses: Briny water seepage; dry granular flows triggered by sublimation and thermal cycling; a combination with small amounts of water lubricating grain flow
mainstream_view: Dry granular flow explanations have gained ground since 2017; the mechanism remains contested
testable_prediction: High-resolution monitoring plus thermal modeling should distinguish wet from dry flows
key_evidence_or_cases: HiRISE monitoring since 2011; hydrated salt spectral detections and later reinterpretation; slope angle statistics matching dry flows
implication_if_solved: Would determine whether liquid water exists at the Martian surface today

observation_summary: The northern hemisphere is several kilometers lower with much thinner crust than the southern highlands, a difference of unknown origin
why_it_resists_explanation: The boundary has been heavily modified by later processes, obscuring the original structure, and both internal and external causes fit the data
leading_hypotheses: A giant impact creating the northern basin; degree-one mantle convection thinning the northern crust; early plate tectonics; multiple large impacts
mainstream_view: A fundamental unexplained feature of Mars; both impact and convection hypotheses remain viable
testable_prediction: Crustal thickness and magnetic mapping plus seismology should test the impact hypothesis
key_evidence_or_cases: MOLA topography; crustal magnetization patterns; InSight seismic crustal thickness measurements; Borealis basin impact models
implication_if_solved: Would explain the most prominent feature of the Martian surface

phenomenon: Martian water loss and the missing carbonate
observation_summary: Mars clearly had abundant surface water and a thicker atmosphere, but the expected carbonate deposits are largely absent
why_it_resists_explanation: If CO2 was lost to carbonate rocks, those rocks should be widespread and they are not, requiring alternative sinks
leading_hypotheses: Atmospheric escape to space via solar wind stripping (supported by MAVEN); sequestration in the subsurface as carbonate at depth; loss of water into hydrated crustal minerals; CO2 trapped as clathrates
mainstream_view: Atmospheric escape is quantified by MAVEN and explains much of the loss; the full budget remains unclosed
testable_prediction: Isotopic fractionation measurements should constrain escape versus sequestration, and they partly do
key_evidence_or_cases: MAVEN escape rate measurements; argon isotope ratios; limited carbonate detections by orbital spectroscopy; crustal hydration estimates
implication_if_solved: Would explain how a habitable planet became uninhabitable

observation_summary: The Moon has strong localized crustal magnetism and bright swirl patterns with no current global field
why_it_resists_explanation: The magnetizing field strength implied exceeds what a small lunar core dynamo should produce, and the swirls require magnetic shielding of the surface
leading_hypotheses: An early lunar core dynamo stronger than expected; impact-generated plasma magnetization; magnetic shielding deflecting solar wind to create albedo swirls; buried dike intrusions
mainstream_view: Anomalies and swirls are well mapped; the magnetizing field source remains debated
testable_prediction: Sample paleomagnetism plus surface rover measurements should constrain the ancient field strength
key_evidence_or_cases: Apollo sample paleomagnetism; Reiner Gamma swirl; Lunar Prospector magnetic maps; Chang-e observations
implication_if_solved: Would reveal whether small bodies can sustain dynamos

phenomenon: Lunar formation details and isotopic similarity
observation_summary: The Moon is isotopically nearly identical to Earth, which the standard giant impact model struggles to produce
why_it_resists_explanation: An impactor should have a different isotopic composition, so either it was unusually similar or the material mixed more thoroughly than models allow
leading_hypotheses: Giant impact with a nearly identical impactor from the same orbital region; high-energy impact creating a synestia with full mixing; multiple smaller impacts; post-impact equilibration between Earth and disk
mainstream_view: Giant impact origin is consensus; the isotopic similarity remains a genuine problem for specific models
testable_prediction: Precise isotopic measurements of returned samples should constrain mixing models
key_evidence_or_cases: Apollo sample oxygen and titanium isotope ratios; synestia modeling; tungsten isotope constraints
implication_if_solved: Would complete the origin story of the Earth-Moon system

observation_summary: Earth formed in a region too hot for water ice yet has oceans, and the delivery mechanism is debated
why_it_resists_explanation: Isotopic signatures of candidate sources overlap and the relevant events happened over four billion years ago
leading_hypotheses: Carbonaceous chondrite delivery from the outer asteroid belt (favored by deuterium ratios); comet contribution (limited by Rosetta measurements); direct nebular hydrogen incorporation into magma; adsorption onto dust grains
mainstream_view: Asteroidal delivery is favored; the proportions and timing remain debated
testable_prediction: Deuterium to hydrogen ratios across sources should constrain contributions, and they do
key_evidence_or_cases: Rosetta 67P high D/H ratio; chondrite isotopic matches; Theia impact water loss modeling; enstatite chondrite hydrogen studies
implication_if_solved: Would determine how common habitable water-bearing planets are

observation_summary: A spike in impacts about 3.9 billion years ago was inferred from lunar samples, but the evidence is now disputed
why_it_resists_explanation: Apollo samples may be biased toward material from a single large basin, inflating the apparent spike
leading_hypotheses: A dynamical instability from giant planet migration causing a bombardment spike; a smooth declining impact flux with sample bias creating an apparent spike; a less intense but real episode
mainstream_view: The classic cataclysm model has been substantially weakened; a declining-flux model is now widely favored
testable_prediction: Dating of diverse lunar and asteroid samples should show whether impacts cluster in time
key_evidence_or_cases: Apollo impact melt age clustering; Nice model dynamical simulations; sample bias arguments from Imbrium ejecta; asteroid meteorite ages
implication_if_solved: Would reframe the environment in which life originated

phenomenon: Planet Nine and distant solar system structure
observation_summary: Extreme trans-Neptunian objects show clustered orbits that some interpret as evidence of an undiscovered massive planet
why_it_resists_explanation: The sample is small and heavily affected by observational selection, and self-gravity of a disk could produce similar clustering
leading_hypotheses: An undetected super-Earth on a distant eccentric orbit; observational bias creating apparent clustering; collective gravity of a massive trans-Neptunian disk; a primordial black hole (a fringe variant)
mainstream_view: Genuinely contested; surveys have not found the planet and bias analyses challenge the clustering
testable_prediction: The Vera Rubin Observatory should either find the planet or eliminate the clustering signal
key_evidence_or_cases: Batygin and Brown 2016 clustering analysis; Sedna and 2012 VP113 orbits; Shankman bias analyses; negative survey results
implication_if_solved: Would add a planet to the solar system or settle a famous claim

observation_summary: The source region of long-period comets is inferred entirely from comet orbits; no Oort cloud object has been directly observed in place
why_it_resists_explanation: The objects are far too faint and distant to detect, so the entire structure is a dynamical inference
leading_hypotheses: A spherical reservoir of icy bodies at thousands of astronomical units; capture of objects from other stars in the birth cluster; an inner Hills cloud supplying the outer cloud
mainstream_view: Universally accepted as a dynamical inference; never directly observed
testable_prediction: Occultation surveys or interstellar probes could eventually detect members
key_evidence_or_cases: Long-period comet orbital energy distribution; Sedna as a possible inner Oort object; Oort 1950 analysis
implication_if_solved: Would confirm the structure of the outermost solar system

observation_summary: The 11-year sunspot cycle varies in strength unpredictably, and forecasts of each cycle peak have repeatedly failed
why_it_resists_explanation: The dynamo operates in the convection zone which cannot be observed directly, and the relevant seed field is poorly constrained
leading_hypotheses: Flux transport dynamo with polar field as a precursor; stochastic fluctuations in flux emergence limiting predictability; nonlinear dynamo with chaotic modulation
mainstream_view: Precursor methods using polar fields work moderately well; the physical dynamo remains incompletely modeled
testable_prediction: Polar field strength at minimum should predict the next maximum, and it does with moderate skill
key_evidence_or_cases: Schwabe cycle discovery 1843; Maunder Minimum; cycle 24 and 25 forecast spread; helioseismic flow measurements
implication_if_solved: Would enable space weather forecasting years in advance

observation_summary: The Sun occasionally stops producing sunspots for decades, as during the Maunder Minimum, for unexplained reasons
why_it_resists_explanation: The dynamo must have multiple states, and the triggering of transitions cannot be observed or reliably modeled
leading_hypotheses: Stochastic dynamo transitions to a weak branch; nonlinear dynamo with intermittency; long-term modulation by meridional flow changes
mainstream_view: Occurrence established by sunspot records and cosmogenic isotopes; mechanism unexplained
testable_prediction: Cosmogenic isotope records should reveal the statistics of minima, and they do
key_evidence_or_cases: Maunder and Sporer minima; carbon-14 and beryllium-10 records; grand minima recurrence statistics over 10000 years
implication_if_solved: Would allow forecasting of long-term solar variability

observation_summary: Large eruptions release billions of tonnes of plasma with limited ability to forecast onset or Earth impact
why_it_resists_explanation: Magnetic field in the corona cannot be measured directly, and the eruption trigger involves instability thresholds that are hard to observe
leading_hypotheses: Magnetic flux rope instability after sufficient twist accumulation; breakout reconnection models; tether-cutting reconnection; combination depending on configuration
mainstream_view: Mechanisms partly understood; forecasting of onset timing remains poor
testable_prediction: Coronal magnetic field measurements should enable instability prediction, which new instruments are starting to allow
key_evidence_or_cases: Carrington event 1859; 2012 near-miss CME; DSCOVR and ACE upstream monitoring; coronal magnetography development
implication_if_solved: Would protect power grids and satellites from a major geomagnetic storm

observation_summary: Extreme geomagnetic storms occur rarely, and the recurrence statistics and worst-case magnitude are poorly constrained
why_it_resists_explanation: The record is short, historical events are measured by proxies, and extreme value statistics are sensitive to assumptions
leading_hypotheses: Power law tail with recurrence of roughly one per century; a physical upper bound on storm magnitude; cosmogenic isotope spikes indicating much larger extreme events
mainstream_view: Recognized as a major infrastructure risk with large uncertainty in return periods
testable_prediction: Cosmogenic isotope records should reveal the frequency of extreme events, and 774 and 993 CE events suggest larger ones occur
key_evidence_or_cases: Carrington event magnetometer records; 1989 Quebec blackout; Miyake events in tree rings 774 and 993 CE; 2012 CME near-miss
implication_if_solved: Would set the design basis for protecting global infrastructure

phenomenon: Miyake events and extreme particle storms
locus: Tree ring and ice core records
observation_summary: Sharp spikes in cosmogenic isotopes record particle events far larger than any observed in the space age
why_it_resists_explanation: No solar observation covers these events, and their energy exceeds extrapolations from modern solar activity
leading_hypotheses: Extreme solar particle events far larger than modern maxima; a nearby supernova or gamma-ray burst; a magnetar giant flare; an unidentified astrophysical source
mainstream_view: Events firmly established in multiple independent records; their source is genuinely unknown
testable_prediction: Multi-isotope signatures should distinguish solar from galactic sources, and analyses are ongoing
key_evidence_or_cases: Miyake 774 and 993 CE carbon-14 spikes; beryllium-10 confirmation in ice cores; additional events found at 7176 and 5410 BCE
implication_if_solved: Would define the true worst case for space weather risk

observation_summary: The distribution of stellar masses at birth appears nearly identical across very different environments, with no derivation from first principles
why_it_resists_explanation: Star formation involves turbulence, magnetic fields, feedback and gravity interacting across scales that cannot be simulated together
leading_hypotheses: Turbulent fragmentation setting the mass spectrum; feedback-regulated accretion; a statistical consequence of hierarchical collapse; variations exist but are masked by observational bias
mainstream_view: Near-universality is well documented with hints of variation in extreme environments
testable_prediction: Resolved stellar populations in extreme environments should reveal variation if it exists
key_evidence_or_cases: Salpeter 1955 power law; Chabrier and Kroupa parameterizations; possible top-heavy IMF in starbursts; ultra-faint dwarf studies
implication_if_solved: Would underpin all inferences about galaxy masses and evolution

observation_summary: Stars above about 20 solar masses should blow away their own accretion material before reaching final mass
why_it_resists_explanation: Radiation pressure should halt accretion, yet stars up to 200 solar masses exist, requiring a way to circumvent the limit
leading_hypotheses: Disk accretion channeling material past radiation pressure; radiation beaming through low-density cavities; competitive accretion in clusters; stellar mergers in dense clusters
mainstream_view: Disk accretion solutions are supported by simulations and ALMA observations; details remain open
testable_prediction: ALMA should resolve disks around forming massive stars, and it does
key_evidence_or_cases: R136a1 at over 150 solar masses; ALMA disk detections around massive protostars; radiation pressure limit calculations
implication_if_solved: Would explain the origin of the most influential stars in galaxies

observation_summary: The maximum stellar mass appears to be around 150 to 300 solar masses, with the limiting mechanism unsettled
why_it_resists_explanation: Mass estimates depend on uncertain models of winds and multiplicity, and apparent record holders may be unresolved binaries
leading_hypotheses: Eddington limit and pulsational instability capping mass; fragmentation limits during formation; apparent extreme masses resulting from unresolved multiples
mainstream_view: A limit exists observationally; whether it reflects formation or stability is unresolved
testable_prediction: High-resolution imaging should reveal whether record-holders are multiples, and it has for some
key_evidence_or_cases: R136a1 mass revision downward in 2022; eta Carinae; pair instability mass limits; cluster population statistics
implication_if_solved: Would set the upper bound on stellar feedback and black hole seeds

observation_summary: Simulations struggled for decades to make stars actually explode rather than collapse quietly
why_it_resists_explanation: The explosion depends on neutrino transport in three dimensions with general relativity, which only recently became computationally tractable
leading_hypotheses: Neutrino-driven convection with standing accretion shock instability; magnetorotational explosions for rapid rotators; three-dimensional turbulence as the essential ingredient
mainstream_view: Three-dimensional simulations now produce explosions for many progenitors; the systematics are still being worked out
testable_prediction: Neutrino detection from a nearby supernova would test the mechanism directly
key_evidence_or_cases: SN 1987A neutrino detection; 3D simulation successes since 2015; pulsar kicks as explosion asymmetry evidence
implication_if_solved: Would complete the theory of how stars end and elements form

observation_summary: The standard distance indicators for cosmology have an unresolved progenitor channel, single or double degenerate
why_it_resists_explanation: No progenitor system has been directly identified before explosion, and both channels can match observed properties
leading_hypotheses: Single degenerate white dwarf accreting from a companion; double degenerate white dwarf merger; sub-Chandrasekhar double detonation; multiple channels contributing
mainstream_view: A genuine open problem with direct implications for cosmological distance calibration
testable_prediction: Pre-explosion imaging and early light curves should reveal companion interaction signatures
key_evidence_or_cases: SN 2011fe early observations ruling out a red giant companion; absence of surviving companions in remnants; delay time distributions
implication_if_solved: Would secure the calibration of cosmological distance measurements

observation_summary: The most energetic explosions known are powered by an engine whose nature cannot be observed directly
why_it_resists_explanation: The engine is hidden inside a collapsing star or merger remnant, and only the emergent jet is observable
leading_hypotheses: Hyperaccreting black hole with magnetically driven jets; rapidly rotating magnetar central engine; a mixture depending on burst class
mainstream_view: Progenitors identified for both long and short bursts; the engine itself remains inferred
testable_prediction: Gravitational wave plus gamma-ray detections should constrain engine properties, as GW170817 began to
key_evidence_or_cases: Long bursts linked to collapsars; GRB 170817A with gravitational waves; plateau phases suggesting magnetar engines
implication_if_solved: Would reveal the physics of the most extreme explosions

observation_summary: A class of transients rises and fades within days, far faster than supernovae, with no established mechanism
why_it_resists_explanation: They are rare, fast and were only identified by high-cadence surveys, so observational coverage is limited
leading_hypotheses: Failed supernova forming a black hole with an accretion disk; interaction with dense circumstellar material; a magnetar-powered event; tidal disruption by an intermediate mass black hole
mainstream_view: A newly identified class; mechanism genuinely unknown
testable_prediction: Multiwavelength coverage of a nearby event would distinguish the models
key_evidence_or_cases: AT2018cow (the Cow) discovery; subsequent similar events; radio and X-ray variability patterns
implication_if_solved: Would reveal a new channel of stellar death

phenomenon: Luminous red novae and common envelope events
observation_summary: Transients of intermediate brightness appear to mark stellar mergers and common envelope ejections, a critical but poorly observed phase
why_it_resists_explanation: The common envelope phase is brief and dusty, making it hard to observe, and simulations cannot follow the full evolution
leading_hypotheses: Stellar merger with envelope ejection; failed common envelope ejection producing a transient; a continuum of outcomes depending on mass ratio
mainstream_view: Association with mergers is well supported by V1309 Scorpii; the physics remains incompletely modeled
testable_prediction: Pre-merger photometry should show the predicted orbital decay, and it did for V1309 Sco
key_evidence_or_cases: V1309 Scorpii pre-merger light curve; V838 Monocerotis; M31 luminous red nova events
implication_if_solved: Would resolve the dominant uncertainty in binary star evolution

observation_summary: Black holes between about 100 and 100000 solar masses are predicted but very few candidates are confirmed
why_it_resists_explanation: They are too small to produce clear dynamical signatures in crowded clusters and too large to form from single stars
leading_hypotheses: Runaway stellar mergers in dense clusters; direct collapse of primordial gas clouds; growth from stellar remnants; they are rare because formation channels are inefficient
mainstream_view: Few confirmed cases; GW190521 provided the clearest gravitational wave evidence
testable_prediction: Gravitational wave detections and dwarf galaxy dynamics should build a population
key_evidence_or_cases: GW190521 merger producing a 142 solar mass remnant; HLX-1 candidate; omega Centauri dynamics claims
implication_if_solved: Would explain how supermassive black holes get started

observation_summary: Billion-solar-mass black holes existed within 700 million years of the Big Bang, too early for standard growth rates
why_it_resists_explanation: Growing from stellar-mass seeds at the Eddington limit takes longer than the available time, requiring either heavy seeds or super-Eddington accretion
leading_hypotheses: Direct collapse of pristine gas clouds into heavy seeds; super-Eddington accretion episodes; primordial black hole seeds; mergers accelerating growth
mainstream_view: A sharp and increasingly severe problem, worsened by JWST discoveries of early massive black holes
testable_prediction: JWST should find the seed population or constrain accretion rates
key_evidence_or_cases: Quasar J0313-1806 at redshift 7.6; JWST early AGN detections; Eddington growth timescale calculations
implication_if_solved: Would explain the origin of the largest objects in the universe

observation_summary: JWST found galaxies that appear more massive and mature at early times than standard models comfortably predict
why_it_resists_explanation: Masses are inferred from spectral fitting with uncertain assumptions about dust, stellar populations and the initial mass function
leading_hypotheses: More efficient early star formation than assumed; top-heavy initial mass function in early galaxies; contribution of active galactic nuclei to the light; overestimated stellar masses from fitting assumptions
mainstream_view: A real observational surprise; whether it challenges cosmology is contested and masses have been revised downward in several cases
testable_prediction: Spectroscopic confirmation and dynamical masses should settle the stellar mass estimates
key_evidence_or_cases: JWST CEERS and JADES detections; initially reported impossible early galaxies revised after spectroscopy; little red dots population
implication_if_solved: Would test galaxy formation models and possibly cosmology

phenomenon: Little red dots in JWST surveys
observation_summary: A population of compact red sources at high redshift has properties not matching either normal galaxies or standard quasars
why_it_resists_explanation: Their spectra combine features of dust-reddened black hole accretion and compact stellar populations in ways no existing model reproduces
leading_hypotheses: Dust-obscured accreting black holes with unusual geometry; extremely compact dense star-forming regions; a new class of early object; black hole stars with gas envelopes
mainstream_view: A newly identified population under intense study; nature genuinely unknown
testable_prediction: Deep spectroscopy including variability monitoring should determine whether black holes dominate
key_evidence_or_cases: JWST photometric selections 2023 and 2024; broad line detections in some sources; unusual V-shaped spectral energy distributions
implication_if_solved: Would identify a previously unknown phase of galaxy or black hole growth

phenomenon: Missing satellites and the small-scale structure problem
observation_summary: Dark matter simulations predicted many more small satellite galaxies than were observed, along with cusp and too-big-to-fail problems
why_it_resists_explanation: Simulations predict dark matter structure while observations see stars, and the mapping between them depends on baryonic physics that was poorly modeled
leading_hypotheses: Baryonic feedback suppressing star formation in small halos (now favored); warm or self-interacting dark matter suppressing small structure; observational incompleteness that surveys have partly filled
mainstream_view: Substantially alleviated by discovery of ultra-faint dwarfs and improved feedback modeling; not fully closed
testable_prediction: Deeper surveys should find predicted numbers of faint satellites, and they increasingly do
key_evidence_or_cases: Klypin 1999 missing satellites paper; SDSS and DES ultra-faint dwarf discoveries; FIRE simulations with feedback
implication_if_solved: Would test dark matter particle properties on small scales

phenomenon: Cusp-core problem in dark matter halos
locus: Dwarf and low surface brightness galaxies
observation_summary: Simulations predict dense central dark matter cusps while observations often show flatter cores
why_it_resists_explanation: Rotation curve interpretation depends on assumptions about gas dynamics and disk inclination, and feedback modeling is uncertain
leading_hypotheses: Supernova feedback flattening cusps into cores; self-interacting dark matter producing cores naturally; observational systematics in rotation curve derivation; dynamical friction from gas clumps
mainstream_view: A long-standing tension, substantially but not entirely addressed by baryonic feedback models
testable_prediction: Stellar kinematics in ultra-faint dwarfs with little feedback should show cusps if dark matter is cold
key_evidence_or_cases: Moore 1994 core observations; THINGS rotation curve surveys; NIHAO and FIRE core formation simulations
implication_if_solved: Would constrain dark matter self-interaction

observation_summary: Some galaxies appear to contain almost no dark matter while others of similar size are dark matter dominated
why_it_resists_explanation: Distance measurements strongly affect inferred mass, and the claims depend on sparse globular cluster velocity samples
leading_hypotheses: Tidal stripping removing dark matter halos; formation from high-velocity gas collisions; distance measurement errors removing the anomaly; modified gravity implications
mainstream_view: The NGC1052-DF2 and DF4 claims are contested on distance grounds; some galaxies do appear dark matter poor
testable_prediction: Improved distance measurements and larger velocity samples should resolve the mass estimates
key_evidence_or_cases: van Dokkum 2018 DF2 claim; Trujillo distance redetermination; bullet dwarf collision hypothesis 2022
implication_if_solved: Would test whether dark matter can be separated from galaxies

observation_summary: Stellar disks thicken with age by more than known heating mechanisms easily account for
why_it_resists_explanation: Multiple heating processes operate over gigayears and cannot be observed in action
leading_hypotheses: Giant molecular cloud scattering; spiral arm and bar heating; satellite accretion and minor mergers; formation of thick disks hot at birth
mainstream_view: Partly explained; the relative contributions of each mechanism remain unresolved
testable_prediction: Gaia age-velocity dispersion relations should separate the mechanisms, and are beginning to
key_evidence_or_cases: Age-velocity dispersion measurements; Gaia DR3 kinematics; Milky Way thick disk chemical signatures
implication_if_solved: Would explain the structure of spiral galaxies including our own

phenomenon: Galactic bar and spiral arm longevity
observation_summary: Spiral arms should wind up and dissolve within a few rotations, yet spiral structure is ubiquitous
why_it_resists_explanation: Distinguishing transient from long-lived patterns requires either simulations or statistical arguments about galaxy populations
leading_hypotheses: Quasi-stationary density waves maintained by self-gravity; transient recurrent arms continuously regenerated; tidally induced arms in interacting systems; swing amplification
mainstream_view: Density wave theory is standard but the transient recurrent picture has gained support from simulations
testable_prediction: Measuring pattern speeds across radius should distinguish steady waves from transients
key_evidence_or_cases: Lin-Shu density wave theory; winding problem formulation; N-body simulations showing transient arms; pattern speed measurements
implication_if_solved: Would explain the most recognizable structures in the universe

observation_summary: Two enormous gamma-ray lobes extend 25000 light years above and below the galactic center from an unknown past event
why_it_resists_explanation: The event happened millions of years ago, so only the relic structure can be studied, and the energy source cannot be observed directly
leading_hypotheses: A past accretion episode of the central black hole; a nuclear starburst driving a wind; a combination with cosmic ray acceleration at the shock front
mainstream_view: Structures firmly established; the origin event remains unidentified
testable_prediction: X-ray and radio counterpart morphology should distinguish black hole from starburst origin
key_evidence_or_cases: Fermi-LAT discovery 2010; eROSITA X-ray bubbles 2020; radio and microwave haze counterparts
implication_if_solved: Would reveal a major past event in our own galaxy

observation_summary: An excess of gamma rays from the galactic center matches dark matter annihilation predictions but also matches pulsar populations
why_it_resists_explanation: Both explanations fit the spectrum, and the spatial distribution analysis is sensitive to modeling of diffuse emission
leading_hypotheses: Dark matter annihilation producing the excess; an unresolved population of millisecond pulsars; mismodeling of cosmic ray diffuse emission
mainstream_view: Increasingly attributed to millisecond pulsars after photon statistics analyses; dark matter interpretation not excluded
testable_prediction: Radio searches should find the predicted millisecond pulsar population if that is the source
key_evidence_or_cases: Goodenough and Hooper 2009; photon clustering analyses favoring point sources; dwarf galaxy non-detections constraining dark matter
implication_if_solved: Would be the first detection of dark matter annihilation if confirmed

observation_summary: The galaxy produces far more positrons than known sources explain, concentrated in the bulge rather than the disk
why_it_resists_explanation: The bulge-dominated distribution does not match any known source population, and positrons propagate before annihilating
leading_hypotheses: Type Ia supernovae in the bulge; low mass X-ray binaries; dark matter decay or annihilation; positron propagation from disk sources into the bulge
mainstream_view: A long-standing unexplained observation; no source population matches the morphology
testable_prediction: Mapping the emission with better angular resolution should match a source population
key_evidence_or_cases: INTEGRAL SPI mapping; bulge-to-disk ratio measurements; COMPTEL and earlier balloon detections
implication_if_solved: Would identify a major unrecognized Galactic particle source

observation_summary: The positron fraction rises with energy above expectations from secondary production, suggesting a primary source
why_it_resists_explanation: Both astrophysical and dark matter sources can fit the spectrum, and propagation modeling is uncertain
leading_hypotheses: Nearby pulsars such as Geminga injecting positrons; dark matter annihilation; secondary production in supernova remnant shocks
mainstream_view: Pulsar explanations are currently favored; dark matter interpretation remains possible but constrained
testable_prediction: Anisotropy measurements should point toward nearby pulsars if they dominate
key_evidence_or_cases: PAMELA 2008 and AMS-02 measurements; HAWC observations of pulsar halos; antiproton spectrum constraints
implication_if_solved: Would identify a nearby cosmic accelerator or detect dark matter

observation_summary: Giant circular radio structures hundreds of kiloparsecs across were discovered with no clear counterpart or mechanism
why_it_resists_explanation: They were found only with new sensitive radio surveys, and only a handful are known, limiting statistical study
leading_hypotheses: Spherical shock waves from merging supermassive black holes; starburst-driven galactic winds terminating in shocks; termination shocks of outflows from central galaxies
mainstream_view: A newly recognized class of object; origin genuinely unknown
testable_prediction: Optical and X-ray follow-up of the central galaxies should identify the energy source
key_evidence_or_cases: ASKAP EMU survey discovery 2019; ORC spectroscopy of host galaxies; MeerKAT follow-up imaging
implication_if_solved: Would reveal a new class of large-scale energetic events

phenomenon: Radio relics and cluster shock acceleration
observation_summary: Enormous arcs of radio emission mark cluster merger shocks, but the shocks appear too weak to accelerate electrons efficiently enough
why_it_resists_explanation: Standard diffusive shock acceleration from the thermal pool cannot supply the observed luminosity at the measured Mach numbers
leading_hypotheses: Reacceleration of a preexisting population of mildly relativistic electrons; shock drift acceleration in specific geometries; underestimated Mach numbers from X-ray measurements
mainstream_view: A recognized efficiency problem in shock acceleration theory
testable_prediction: Combined radio spectral index and X-ray Mach number measurements should constrain the mechanism
key_evidence_or_cases: Sausage and Toothbrush relics; CIZA J2242 observations; LOFAR relic surveys
implication_if_solved: Would resolve how cosmic rays are accelerated in the largest structures

observation_summary: Hot gas in cluster centers should cool and form stars at enormous rates, but the predicted cooling flows and star formation are not observed
why_it_resists_explanation: The heating must be finely balanced against cooling over billions of years, requiring a feedback loop that is hard to observe directly
leading_hypotheses: Active galactic nucleus jet feedback reheating the gas; conduction from outer regions; sloshing and turbulent mixing; a self-regulating feedback cycle
mainstream_view: AGN feedback is the accepted framework; the detailed coupling of jet energy to gas remains open
testable_prediction: X-ray cavity energetics should match cooling rates, and they approximately do
key_evidence_or_cases: Absence of predicted cool gas in XMM and Chandra spectra; X-ray cavities from jets; Perseus cluster ripples
implication_if_solved: Would explain how galaxy growth is regulated

observation_summary: Galaxy rotation speed correlates with baryonic mass with remarkably small scatter, tighter than dark matter halo models naturally predict
why_it_resists_explanation: Dark matter halos should introduce scatter from formation history, yet the observed relation is nearly scatter-free
leading_hypotheses: Fine-tuned feedback regulating the baryon-halo relation; a fundamental acceleration scale as in modified gravity; selection effects reducing apparent scatter
mainstream_view: The relation is firmly established and is the strongest observational argument raised in favor of modified gravity approaches
testable_prediction: Measuring intrinsic scatter precisely should test whether it is consistent with halo models
key_evidence_or_cases: McGaugh baryonic Tully-Fisher measurements; SPARC database analyses; radial acceleration relation 2016
implication_if_solved: Would challenge or constrain dark matter halo models

observation_summary: The observed acceleration in galaxies is a tight single-valued function of the baryonic acceleration, with little scatter
why_it_resists_explanation: A dark matter explanation requires halos to conspire with baryons across galaxy types, which simulations reproduce only with tuning
leading_hypotheses: Emergent from feedback-regulated galaxy formation; evidence for a fundamental acceleration scale and modified dynamics; partly a consequence of how the relation is constructed
mainstream_view: The empirical relation is accepted; its interpretation is one of the sharpest disputes in galaxy dynamics
testable_prediction: Simulations should reproduce the relation and its scatter without tuning, with partial success
key_evidence_or_cases: McGaugh Lelli Schombert 2016; SPARC rotation curve database; EAGLE and FIRE simulation comparisons
implication_if_solved: Would decide between dark matter and modified dynamics on galaxy scales

phenomenon: Dark matter direct detection null results
observation_summary: Four decades of increasingly sensitive searches have found no dark matter particles, excluding most favored parameter space
why_it_resists_explanation: The experiments probe specific interaction types, so null results constrain models rather than existence, and the neutrino floor limits further progress
leading_hypotheses: WIMPs with much weaker couplings than theoretically favored; dark matter not interacting via the assumed channels; much lighter or heavier mass ranges; non-particle dark matter
mainstream_view: A major null result reshaping the field toward lighter and alternative candidates
testable_prediction: Next-generation detectors approaching the neutrino floor will either detect or close the WIMP window
key_evidence_or_cases: XENONnT and LZ limits; DAMA annual modulation claim unreplicated; axion haloscope progress
implication_if_solved: Would identify most of the matter in the universe or close a 40-year hypothesis

observation_summary: One experiment has reported an annually modulating signal consistent with dark matter for over two decades, unreplicated by any other detector
why_it_resists_explanation: The signal appears only in this experiment with this target material, and independent experiments with the same target have not reproduced it
leading_hypotheses: Dark matter interaction specific to sodium iodide; seasonal systematic effects in the detector or environment; unrecognized background modulation
mainstream_view: Widely regarded as not dark matter; the ANAIS and COSINE experiments with the same target see no modulation
testable_prediction: Same-target experiments should reproduce the modulation, and they do not
key_evidence_or_cases: DAMA/LIBRA modulation data; ANAIS-112 and COSINE-100 null results; muon flux seasonal variation arguments
implication_if_solved: Would resolve a long-running anomaly in dark matter searches

phenomenon: Neutrino floor and coherent scattering background
observation_summary: Solar and atmospheric neutrinos will eventually create an irreducible background limiting dark matter searches
why_it_resists_explanation: Separating dark matter from neutrino scattering requires directional sensitivity that current detectors lack
leading_hypotheses: Directional detection to separate signals; annual modulation discrimination; the floor is a fog rather than a hard limit
mainstream_view: A well-characterized limitation; coherent neutrino scattering was first detected in 2017
testable_prediction: Detectors should observe the neutrino background at the predicted rate, and they are beginning to
key_evidence_or_cases: COHERENT experiment detection 2017; XENONnT solar neutrino observations; directional detector development
implication_if_solved: Would define the ultimate reach of direct detection

observation_summary: A particle predicted to solve the strong CP problem and potentially constitute dark matter has not been detected after 48 years
why_it_resists_explanation: The coupling is extremely weak and the mass is unknown across many orders of magnitude, requiring scanning experiments
leading_hypotheses: QCD axions in the microelectronvolt mass range; axion-like particles with different couplings; axions do not exist and the strong CP problem has another solution
mainstream_view: A leading dark matter candidate with an active global search program and no detection
testable_prediction: Haloscopes scanning the favored mass range should detect or exclude the QCD axion
key_evidence_or_cases: ADMX exclusion limits; CAST solar axion searches; astrophysical bounds from stellar cooling; birefringence searches
implication_if_solved: Would solve the strong CP problem and identify dark matter simultaneously

phenomenon: Primordial black holes as dark matter
observation_summary: Black holes formed before stars could constitute some or all dark matter, with most mass windows now closed by observation
why_it_resists_explanation: Constraints come from many independent observations with different systematics, leaving narrow and contested windows
leading_hypotheses: Asteroid-mass primordial black holes in the remaining open window; a subdominant population explaining some gravitational wave events; they do not exist in cosmologically relevant numbers
mainstream_view: Most mass ranges excluded; the asteroid-mass window remains open and actively debated
testable_prediction: Microlensing, Hawking evaporation signatures and gravitational wave statistics constrain the windows
key_evidence_or_cases: OGLE and Subaru microlensing limits; CMB accretion constraints; LIGO black hole mass distribution; Hawking radiation limits
implication_if_solved: Would explain dark matter without new particles

observation_summary: Passing gravitational waves should leave a permanent displacement, a predicted effect not yet detected
why_it_resists_explanation: The effect is far smaller than the oscillatory signal and requires stacking many events
leading_hypotheses: The nonlinear Christodoulou memory as predicted by general relativity; detection requiring next-generation detectors or stacking hundreds of events
mainstream_view: Theoretically well established; detection remains ahead
testable_prediction: Stacking many binary black hole events should reveal the memory signal
key_evidence_or_cases: Zeldovich and Polnarev 1974; Christodoulou nonlinear memory 1991; LIGO stacking analyses with no detection yet
implication_if_solved: Would test the nonlinear structure of general relativity

phenomenon: Black hole ringdown and no-hair theorem tests
observation_summary: Whether merger remnants are exactly the black holes general relativity predicts is being tested but not settled
why_it_resists_explanation: Extracting multiple ringdown modes requires high signal-to-noise events that are rare
leading_hypotheses: Remnants are Kerr black holes exactly as predicted; deviations exist from quantum gravity effects at the horizon; exotic compact objects producing echoes
mainstream_view: Tests so far are consistent with general relativity; precision is limited
testable_prediction: Detecting multiple quasinormal modes in a loud event would test the no-hair theorem
key_evidence_or_cases: GW150914 ringdown analysis; GW190521 and GW250114 high mass events; claimed and disputed echo detections
implication_if_solved: Would test whether black holes have quantum structure at the horizon

observation_summary: Claimed repeating signals after merger ringdown would indicate structure near the horizon, with the detections statistically disputed
why_it_resists_explanation: The claimed signals are weak and the statistical significance depends strongly on analysis choices and templates
leading_hypotheses: Quantum structure or firewall near the horizon producing echoes; noise fluctuations with flexible template searches producing spurious significance
mainstream_view: Not accepted; independent analyses find no significant evidence
testable_prediction: Blind injection tests and preregistered analyses on new events
key_evidence_or_cases: Abedi Dykaar Afshordi 2016 claim; LIGO collaboration null analyses; Westerweck significance reanalysis
implication_if_solved: Would be the first observational evidence of quantum gravity if real

phenomenon: Neutron star maximum mass and the equation of state
observation_summary: The maximum mass a neutron star can reach is unknown within about half a solar mass because the dense matter equation of state is unmeasured
why_it_resists_explanation: Matter above nuclear density cannot be created in laboratories, so the equation of state must be inferred from astrophysical observations
leading_hypotheses: Hadronic matter with specific stiffness; quark matter cores in the heaviest stars; hyperons softening the equation of state; phase transition at a few times nuclear density
mainstream_view: Actively constrained by gravitational wave and X-ray timing observations; not yet determined
testable_prediction: Combined NICER radii and gravitational wave tidal deformability should pin the equation of state
key_evidence_or_cases: PSR J0740+6620 at 2.08 solar masses; GW170817 tidal deformability; NICER radius measurements
implication_if_solved: Would determine the behavior of the densest matter in the universe

observation_summary: Pulsars have been observed for nearly 60 years without an established theory of how their radio emission is generated
why_it_resists_explanation: The emission region is tiny and the plasma physics involves coherent processes in extreme magnetic fields that cannot be simulated fully
leading_hypotheses: Coherent curvature radiation from charge bunches; plasma instabilities in the polar gap; free electron laser mechanisms; reconnection in the current sheet
mainstream_view: A notorious long-standing gap: pulsars are used as precision tools without understanding their emission
testable_prediction: A correct theory should predict the observed polarization and spectral behavior across the population
key_evidence_or_cases: Hewish and Bell discovery 1967; pulse profile and polarization catalogs; nulling and mode changing behavior
implication_if_solved: Would complete the physics of the most precise natural clocks

observation_summary: Some pulsars abruptly stop emitting for seconds to hours then resume, or switch between stable emission modes
why_it_resists_explanation: The switches are global and fast, implying magnetospheric reconfiguration whose trigger is unknown
leading_hypotheses: Global magnetospheric state switching between stable configurations; changes in the particle acceleration gap; non-axisymmetric current redistribution
mainstream_view: Well documented; mechanism unexplained
testable_prediction: Simultaneous radio and X-ray monitoring should show correlated state changes, and it does for some pulsars
key_evidence_or_cases: PSR B0943+10 radio and X-ray mode correlation; nulling fraction statistics; intermittent pulsars with long off states
implication_if_solved: Would reveal how pulsar magnetospheres are organized

observation_summary: The most magnetic objects known release enormous energy in seconds, bright enough to ionize Earth upper atmosphere from other galaxies
why_it_resists_explanation: The crustal and magnetospheric processes involved occur in fields beyond any laboratory regime
leading_hypotheses: Crustal fracture releasing magnetic stress; magnetic reconnection in a twisted magnetosphere; global magnetic instability
mainstream_view: Framework accepted; the specific trigger and energy release pathway remain open
testable_prediction: Quasi-periodic oscillations in flare tails should match crustal modes, and they appear to
key_evidence_or_cases: SGR 1806-20 giant flare 2004; 1979 March 5 event; quasi-periodic oscillations in flare tails; extragalactic giant flare detections
implication_if_solved: Would reveal physics in the strongest magnetic fields known

observation_summary: Some repeating fast radio bursts show activity windows with periods of 16 days or 157 days with no agreed cause
why_it_resists_explanation: The periodicity is in activity rather than individual bursts, which is hard to reconcile with simple rotation
leading_hypotheses: Orbital modulation in a binary system; precession of a magnetar magnetic axis; ultra-slow rotation of a magnetar; modulation by a stellar wind
mainstream_view: Periodicity well measured; mechanism genuinely unknown
testable_prediction: Long-term monitoring should reveal whether the period changes as expected for precession or orbits
key_evidence_or_cases: FRB 180916 16.35 day period; FRB 121102 157 day cycle; CHIME long-term monitoring
implication_if_solved: Would identify the engine and environment of fast radio bursts

observation_summary: Some quasars turn their broad emission lines on or off within months to years, far faster than accretion disk physics allows
why_it_resists_explanation: Standard accretion disk viscous timescales are thousands of years, so the rapid change requires a different mechanism
leading_hypotheses: Accretion state transitions analogous to X-ray binaries; disk instabilities propagating faster than viscous timescales; tidal disruption events; changing obscuration along the line of sight
mainstream_view: Phenomenon firmly established; the timescale problem is a genuine challenge to accretion theory
testable_prediction: Monitoring should distinguish obscuration from intrinsic accretion changes, and polarization helps
key_evidence_or_cases: LaMassa 2015 first clear case; dozens found in time-domain surveys; 1ES 1927+654 dramatic changes
implication_if_solved: Would revise accretion disk physics

observation_summary: X-ray eruptions recur every few hours in some galactic nuclei, a newly discovered phenomenon
why_it_resists_explanation: Only a handful are known, discovered recently, and the mechanism must explain hour-scale repetition near a massive black hole
leading_hypotheses: A stellar object on an eccentric orbit repeatedly passing through an accretion disk; disk instabilities; Roche lobe overflow from an orbiting white dwarf
mainstream_view: A new class under active study; several models proposed, none established
testable_prediction: Orbital period evolution should distinguish orbiting-body models from instabilities
key_evidence_or_cases: GSN 069 discovery 2019; RX J1301.9+2747; additional sources found 2021 to 2024; period drift measurements
implication_if_solved: Would reveal objects orbiting close to massive black holes

observation_summary: Measurements of diffuse optical and infrared background light exceed the integrated light of known galaxies
why_it_resists_explanation: Zodiacal light and galactic foregrounds dominate and must be subtracted with high precision, leaving contested residuals
leading_hypotheses: A population of faint undetected sources; intra-halo light from stripped stars; residual zodiacal light in the subtraction; decaying particles contributing light
mainstream_view: A persistent discrepancy whose magnitude depends strongly on foreground modeling; New Horizons measurements from the outer solar system reduced it
testable_prediction: Measurements from beyond the zodiacal dust should give a clean background, and New Horizons has
key_evidence_or_cases: CIBER rocket measurements; New Horizons LORRI background measurements 2021 and 2022; gamma-ray opacity constraints
implication_if_solved: Would account for all the light ever emitted in the universe

observation_summary: The ARCADE 2 experiment and later analyses found more diffuse radio emission than known source populations explain
why_it_resists_explanation: Galactic foreground subtraction at low frequencies is extremely difficult, and absolute calibration is hard
leading_hypotheses: An undetected population of faint radio sources; dark matter annihilation contributions; galactic foreground mismodeling; calibration systematics
mainstream_view: A real measurement discrepancy; interpretation contested with foreground errors a leading possibility
testable_prediction: Improved absolute calibration and source counts should resolve it
key_evidence_or_cases: ARCADE 2 measurements 2011; LWA and other low-frequency surveys; proposed relevance to the EDGES 21 cm anomaly
implication_if_solved: Would identify a missing population of radio sources

observation_summary: An absorption feature attributed to the first stars was reported with twice the expected depth, implying colder gas than possible in standard cosmology
why_it_resists_explanation: The signal is buried under foregrounds five orders of magnitude brighter, and the fitting procedure is contested
leading_hypotheses: Excess cooling from dark matter interactions; an unaccounted radio background heating the spin temperature; residual foreground or instrumental systematics producing a spurious feature
mainstream_view: Not confirmed: the SARAS 3 experiment reported non-detection of the claimed profile in 2022
testable_prediction: Independent experiments should detect the same profile, and SARAS 3 did not
key_evidence_or_cases: Bowman et al 2018 Nature report; SARAS 3 2022 rejection; foreground modeling critiques by Hills and others
implication_if_solved: Would either reveal new dark matter physics or close a high-profile anomaly

phenomenon: Lyman alpha forest and the missing baryons
observation_summary: For decades about a third of expected baryons were unaccounted for in the local universe, a gap now largely closed
why_it_resists_explanation: Warm hot intergalactic gas is too diffuse and ionized to detect easily, requiring absorption against bright background sources
leading_hypotheses: Warm hot intergalactic medium containing the missing baryons (now substantially detected); circumgalactic gas reservoirs; dispersion measures of fast radio bursts tracing baryons
mainstream_view: Substantially resolved: FRB dispersion measures and X-ray absorption studies have located most baryons
testable_prediction: FRB dispersion measure statistics should match the cosmic baryon density, and they do
key_evidence_or_cases: Fukugita baryon census; Nicastro 2018 X-ray absorption detection; Macquart 2020 FRB baryon measurement
implication_if_solved: Already an example of a cosmic accounting problem resolved by new methods

locus: Early universe between 400 million and one billion years
observation_summary: The universe was reionized by an unidentified mix of sources, and the timeline is only coarsely constrained
why_it_resists_explanation: The sources are faint and distant, and the ionizing photon escape fraction cannot be measured directly at high redshift
leading_hypotheses: Faint early galaxies with high escape fractions; early quasars contributing a minority; globular cluster progenitors; a combination with galaxies dominating
mainstream_view: Galaxies are favored as the dominant source; the photon budget remains difficult to close
testable_prediction: JWST counts of faint galaxies plus escape fraction measurements should close the budget
key_evidence_or_cases: Gunn-Peterson trough measurements; Planck optical depth; JWST faint galaxy luminosity functions; Lyman continuum escape studies
implication_if_solved: Would complete the history of the universe transition to transparency

phenomenon: First stars and their absence in surveys
observation_summary: Metal-free first-generation stars are predicted but none has been observed, directly or in its unmixed chemical signature
why_it_resists_explanation: They are expected to be short-lived and at very high redshift, and their chemical signatures may be diluted
leading_hypotheses: Very massive first stars exploding as pair-instability supernovae; lower masses making them harder to distinguish; signatures preserved only in rare extremely metal-poor stars
mainstream_view: Theoretically expected; observationally unconfirmed
testable_prediction: Detection of a pair-instability supernova signature or a star with first-generation abundance patterns
key_evidence_or_cases: Extremely metal-poor star surveys; SMSS J0313-6708 with no detected iron; 2023 claimed pair-instability abundance pattern in a distant gas cloud
implication_if_solved: Would confirm the predicted first generation of stars

phenomenon: Cosmological lithium and helium abundance details
observation_summary: Deuterium and helium-4 abundances match Big Bang nucleosynthesis predictions superbly while lithium-7 does not
why_it_resists_explanation: The agreement for other elements makes the lithium failure harder to attribute to nuclear physics errors
leading_hypotheses: Stellar depletion of lithium; an unknown nuclear resonance; new physics during nucleosynthesis; systematic errors in stellar abundance measurements
mainstream_view: A specific and well-defined failure in an otherwise successful theory
testable_prediction: Lithium measurements in interstellar gas of low metallicity should discriminate stellar depletion from primordial values
key_evidence_or_cases: Spite plateau; helium-4 and deuterium agreement; lithium in Small Magellanic Cloud gas measurements
implication_if_solved: Would either validate stellar physics or reveal new early-universe physics

phenomenon: Dark flow and bulk flow measurements
observation_summary: Some analyses find bulk flows of galaxy clusters larger than the standard cosmological model predicts
why_it_resists_explanation: The measurements require subtracting the cosmic microwave background dipole and depend on distance calibration
leading_hypotheses: A genuinely anomalous large-scale flow requiring new physics; measurement systematics in distance indicators; a statistical fluke in a small sample
mainstream_view: The strongest dark flow claims have not been confirmed; moderate bulk flow tensions persist in some analyses
testable_prediction: Larger peculiar velocity surveys should either confirm or eliminate the excess
key_evidence_or_cases: Kashlinsky 2008 kinematic Sunyaev-Zeldovich claim; Planck cluster velocity constraints; CosmicFlows survey analyses
implication_if_solved: Would challenge large-scale homogeneity if confirmed

observation_summary: The dipole in quasar and radio source counts is about twice the amplitude expected from our motion inferred from the microwave background
why_it_resists_explanation: Both measurements are precise enough that the discrepancy is several sigma, and no systematic has been identified
leading_hypotheses: An intrinsic anisotropy in the matter distribution; unaccounted selection effects in source catalogs; a breakdown of the cosmological principle
mainstream_view: A live tension taken seriously; systematic explanations have not been demonstrated
testable_prediction: Independent catalogs with different selection should show the same dipole, and several do
key_evidence_or_cases: Secrest et al 2021 and 2022 quasar dipole; NVSS radio dipole; CatWISE catalog analyses
implication_if_solved: Would challenge the foundational assumption of cosmic isotropy

observation_summary: Weak lensing surveys measure slightly less clustering amplitude than the microwave background predicts, a persistent mild tension
why_it_resists_explanation: Both measurements involve complex systematics including photometric redshifts, intrinsic alignments and baryonic feedback
leading_hypotheses: Suppression of small-scale power by baryonic feedback; new physics reducing structure growth; systematic errors in shear calibration or redshift distributions
mainstream_view: A real and persistent tension of two to three sigma; largely attributed to systematics or baryonic effects
testable_prediction: Improved surveys with better calibration should resolve it; recent DES and KiDS results have narrowed it
key_evidence_or_cases: KiDS and DES cosmic shear results; Planck predictions; hydrodynamic simulation feedback studies
implication_if_solved: Would reveal either new physics or the limits of structure measurement

phenomenon: Cosmic ray knee and ankle features
observation_summary: The cosmic ray spectrum has distinct breaks whose physical origins are debated after 65 years
why_it_resists_explanation: Composition measurement at the relevant energies is indirect, inferred from air shower properties with model-dependent assumptions
leading_hypotheses: Knee from the maximum energy of galactic supernova accelerators; ankle from the transition to extragalactic sources; propagation effects producing the features
mainstream_view: Features firmly measured; interpretation partly settled and still debated
testable_prediction: Mass composition measurements across the features should reveal the transition, and are improving
key_evidence_or_cases: Kulikov and Khristiansen knee discovery 1958; KASCADE composition measurements; Auger and Telescope Array composition data
implication_if_solved: Would identify the sources of galactic and extragalactic cosmic rays

observation_summary: A diffuse flux of high-energy cosmic neutrinos has been detected but most sources remain unidentified
why_it_resists_explanation: Neutrinos are hard to localize, event rates are low, and candidate source classes are numerous
leading_hypotheses: Blazars contributing a fraction; tidal disruption events; star-forming galaxies; choked jets in supernovae; a mixture with no dominant class
mainstream_view: Diffuse flux established; TXS 0506+056 and NGC 1068 identified as probable sources; most of the flux unattributed
testable_prediction: Larger detectors should resolve more point sources
key_evidence_or_cases: IceCube diffuse flux 2013; TXS 0506+056 blazar coincidence 2017; NGC 1068 detection 2022; galactic plane emission 2023
implication_if_solved: Would reveal the sources of the most energetic particles

observation_summary: The nearest observed supernova in centuries should have left a neutron star, which was not detected for 35 years
why_it_resists_explanation: Dense dust in the remnant obscures the center, and a cooling neutron star would be faint
leading_hypotheses: A neutron star hidden behind dust (supported by 2024 JWST detection of ionized argon); a black hole formed by fallback; a very rapidly cooling compact object
mainstream_view: Resolved substantially in 2024 when JWST found evidence of a compact object; direct detection remains indirect
testable_prediction: JWST spectroscopy should reveal ionization consistent with a neutron star, and it did
key_evidence_or_cases: Neutrino burst detection 1987; ALMA blob observation 2019; JWST argon ionization evidence 2024
implication_if_solved: Already closing a 37-year-old puzzle about a famous supernova

observation_summary: The star dimmed dramatically in 2019 and 2020, prompting supernova speculation, and its evolutionary state remains uncertain
why_it_resists_explanation: Red supergiant surfaces are poorly modeled, distance is uncertain, and the dimming cause was initially unclear
leading_hypotheses: A large dust cloud ejected after a surface mass ejection (now favored); large convective cells causing surface brightness changes; a possible unresolved binary companion affecting the period
mainstream_view: The dimming is attributed to dust from a surface mass ejection; the evolutionary stage and companion question remain open
testable_prediction: Continued interferometric imaging and radial velocity monitoring should settle the companion question
key_evidence_or_cases: VLT SPHERE imaging of the dimming; Dupree surface mass ejection analysis; 2024 claims of a companion star
implication_if_solved: Would determine when a nearby star will explode

observation_summary: A star brightened to become the second brightest in the sky in the 1840s, ejected over ten solar masses, and survived
why_it_resists_explanation: No modern star has been observed doing this, and the energy source exceeds normal stellar instability
leading_hypotheses: A merger in a triple system ejecting mass; a failed supernova with partial fallback; pulsational pair instability episode; extreme eruptive mass loss from an unstable supergiant
mainstream_view: The event is historically documented and the remnant studied in detail; the mechanism remains unresolved
testable_prediction: Light echoes from the eruption should reveal the spectrum at the time, and they have partially
key_evidence_or_cases: Historical brightness records; Homunculus nebula; light echo spectroscopy 2012 and 2018; current binary orbit measurements
implication_if_solved: Would explain extreme stellar mass loss relevant to supernova progenitors

observation_summary: The most massive red supergiants are not observed to explode as the expected supernova type, leaving a progenitor gap
why_it_resists_explanation: Progenitor identification requires pre-explosion imaging, which is available for few events, and dust affects mass estimates
leading_hypotheses: Massive red supergiants collapsing directly to black holes without bright supernovae; underestimated masses due to circumstellar dust; small sample statistics
mainstream_view: A recognized gap that has weakened as dust corrections and sample sizes improved
testable_prediction: Failed supernova surveys should find disappearing stars, and one candidate has been reported
key_evidence_or_cases: Smartt progenitor compilation 2009; N6946-BH1 disappearing star candidate; dust correction reanalyses
implication_if_solved: Would reveal which stars form black holes quietly

observation_summary: A predicted star with a neutron star core inside a red supergiant envelope has no confirmed example
why_it_resists_explanation: The predicted chemical signature overlaps with other evolved stars, and candidates have been reinterpreted
leading_hypotheses: They exist but are rare and short-lived; the predicted signatures are not distinctive enough; the configuration is unstable and never forms
mainstream_view: Theoretically predicted; no confirmed example after 48 years
testable_prediction: Unusual element ratios from interrupted rapid proton processes would identify one
key_evidence_or_cases: HV 2112 candidate proposed 2014 and later disputed; HV 827 candidate; predicted lithium and rubidium enrichments
implication_if_solved: Would confirm an exotic predicted stellar configuration

observation_summary: Stars appear bluer and more luminous than the cluster turnoff allows, as if rejuvenated
why_it_resists_explanation: Clusters should have stars of a single age, so these stars require mass gain whose channel differs by environment
leading_hypotheses: Mass transfer in binary systems; direct stellar collisions in dense cores; binary mergers; a mixture dependent on cluster density
mainstream_view: Both channels are now identified observationally; proportions vary by cluster
testable_prediction: Binary fraction and radial distribution should distinguish collision from mass transfer origins, and they do
key_evidence_or_cases: Sandage 1953 discovery in M3; HST surveys of blue straggler populations; two distinct sequences in M30
implication_if_solved: Would explain stellar rejuvenation and cluster dynamics

observation_summary: Clusters once thought to contain single stellar populations show distinct chemical groups, especially in helium and light elements
why_it_resists_explanation: The polluting stars that enriched later generations are not present, and mass budget arguments fail for every proposed source
leading_hypotheses: Asymptotic giant branch star pollution; fast rotating massive stars; supermassive stars in the cluster core; multiple episodes of star formation with gas accretion
mainstream_view: Multiple populations firmly established; no model satisfies the mass budget
testable_prediction: Any model must explain the light element anticorrelations without requiring an implausibly large first generation
key_evidence_or_cases: Sodium-oxygen anticorrelation; HST split main sequences; omega Centauri metallicity spread
implication_if_solved: Would explain how the oldest stellar systems formed

observation_summary: The largest Milky Way globular cluster has a metallicity spread and possible central black hole unlike normal clusters
why_it_resists_explanation: Distinguishing a stripped dwarf galaxy nucleus from an unusual cluster requires detailed dynamics and chemistry
leading_hypotheses: The stripped nucleus of an accreted dwarf galaxy; an extreme globular cluster with self-enrichment; hosting an intermediate mass black hole
mainstream_view: Increasingly interpreted as a stripped dwarf nucleus; the central black hole claim is debated
testable_prediction: Proper motion measurements of central stars should reveal a black hole, as 2024 work claims
key_evidence_or_cases: Metallicity spread measurements; 2024 HST proper motion black hole claim; retrograde orbit in the Galaxy
implication_if_solved: Would identify a surviving fragment of an accreted galaxy

observation_summary: Whether the universe has a small net rotation is observationally constrained but a few analyses report hints of handedness
why_it_resists_explanation: Any rotation would be extremely small and the tests depend on galaxy orientation measurements prone to bias
leading_hypotheses: No rotation consistent with isotropy; an extremely small rotation below current limits; claimed spiral handedness asymmetries being selection artifacts
mainstream_view: Mainstream view is no detectable rotation; claimed asymmetries are generally attributed to observational bias
testable_prediction: Large unbiased galaxy orientation surveys should show no handedness preference
key_evidence_or_cases: Godel rotating universe solutions; galaxy spin handedness claims and rebuttals; CMB isotropy constraints
implication_if_solved: Would overturn the cosmological principle if confirmed

observation_summary: Our galaxy may sit in an underdense region, which could bias local expansion measurements
why_it_resists_explanation: Mapping the local density field requires complete galaxy surveys and distance measurements with controlled systematics
leading_hypotheses: A local void biasing the measured expansion rate upward; the void being too small to explain the Hubble tension; selection effects in the density mapping
mainstream_view: A local underdensity probably exists; whether it is large enough to affect the Hubble tension is debated and generally considered insufficient
testable_prediction: Supernova distance measurements inside and outside the void should differ if the effect is real
key_evidence_or_cases: Keenan Barger Cowie local hole measurement; supernova sample analyses; Hubble tension void explanations and rebuttals
implication_if_solved: Would partly explain the Hubble tension if the void is large enough

observation_summary: Dark energy and matter densities are comparable right now even though their ratio changes by many orders of magnitude over cosmic history
why_it_resists_explanation: Explaining why we observe this particular epoch requires either anthropic reasoning or a dynamical coupling
leading_hypotheses: Anthropic selection since observers require structure; quintessence tracking fields making the coincidence generic; the problem is not a problem because any epoch would be observed by someone
mainstream_view: Widely discussed; many consider it a genuine puzzle and others consider it an anthropic selection non-issue
testable_prediction: Tracking quintessence models predict specific dark energy evolution, testable by DESI and Euclid
key_evidence_or_cases: Measured matter and dark energy densities; tracker field models; anthropic arguments by Weinberg
implication_if_solved: Would explain our place in cosmic history

observation_summary: Time appears as a parameter in quantum mechanics and a dimension in relativity, with no agreed account of its flow or of the present moment
why_it_resists_explanation: The two theories treat time incompatibly, and quantum gravity candidates often make time emergent or eliminate it
leading_hypotheses: Time as emergent from entanglement or thermodynamics; the block universe with flow as an illusion; fundamental time in causal set and some quantum gravity approaches; relational time
mainstream_view: One of the deepest conceptual problems; approaches differ fundamentally
testable_prediction: Quantum gravity theories make different predictions about whether time is fundamental
key_evidence_or_cases: Problem of time in canonical quantum gravity; Wheeler-DeWitt equation timelessness; thermal time hypothesis; page-Wootters mechanism
implication_if_solved: Would resolve the nature of time itself

phenomenon: Problem of time in quantum gravity
observation_summary: The fundamental equation of canonical quantum gravity contains no time variable, so dynamics must be recovered somehow
