why_it_resists_explanation: General relativity makes time a gauge choice while quantum mechanics requires an external time parameter
leading_hypotheses: Relational time from internal clocks; thermal time from the state; Page-Wootters conditional probability mechanism; time as fundamentally emergent
mainstream_view: A central technical and conceptual obstacle in quantum gravity
testable_prediction: Any complete quantum gravity theory must recover standard time evolution in the appropriate limit
key_evidence_or_cases: Wheeler-DeWitt equation; Page and Wootters 1983 mechanism; experimental quantum clock demonstrations of relational time
implication_if_solved: Would be required for any complete theory of quantum gravity

observation_summary: The information in a region appears bounded by its surface area rather than volume, a principle with no general proof
why_it_resists_explanation: The principle is proven in specific anti-de Sitter settings but our universe is not anti-de Sitter, so generalization is unclear
leading_hypotheses: Universal holography with area-bounded information; holography specific to negatively curved spacetimes; de Sitter holography requiring new formulations
mainstream_view: Strongly supported in AdS/CFT; cosmological holography remains unresolved
testable_prediction: A de Sitter holographic duality would extend the principle to our universe
key_evidence_or_cases: Bekenstein bound; t Hooft and Susskind formulations; Maldacena AdS/CFT 1997; covariant entropy bound
implication_if_solved: Would establish the information structure of spacetime

phenomenon: AdS/CFT applicability to the real world
observation_summary: A remarkable duality between gravity and quantum field theory holds exactly in a spacetime unlike ours, with unclear real-world applicability
why_it_resists_explanation: Our universe has positive vacuum energy while the duality requires negative, and no equivalent duality is known for our case
leading_hypotheses: A de Sitter analogue exists and will be found; the duality is a calculational tool without direct physical applicability; the principles generalize even if the specific duality does not
mainstream_view: The duality itself is well established and enormously productive; its physical applicability is a separate open question
testable_prediction: Constructing a controlled de Sitter holographic dual would settle it
key_evidence_or_cases: Maldacena 1997; successful applications to quark-gluon plasma and strange metals; de Sitter holography attempts
implication_if_solved: Would connect string theory to observable physics

observation_summary: String theory appears to permit an enormous number of possible vacua, undermining unique predictions
why_it_resists_explanation: The number of vacua is estimated at 10 to the 500 or more and no principle selects ours, making falsifiable prediction difficult
leading_hypotheses: Anthropic selection among vacua with eternal inflation populating them; a selection principle yet to be discovered; the landscape indicates the framework is not the right one; swampland constraints narrowing possibilities
mainstream_view: An active and contentious issue about whether string theory is predictive
testable_prediction: Swampland conjectures make falsifiable claims about which effective theories are possible
key_evidence_or_cases: Flux compactification counting; KKLT construction 2003; swampland program constraints; de Sitter conjecture debates
implication_if_solved: Would determine whether the leading unification framework is testable

observation_summary: Proposed constraints distinguish effective theories that can arise from quantum gravity from those that cannot, with varying levels of support
why_it_resists_explanation: The conjectures are motivated by examples rather than proven, and some versions conflict with observations such as accelerating expansion
leading_hypotheses: Weak gravity conjecture and distance conjectures as genuine quantum gravity constraints; the de Sitter conjecture ruling out our universe in its strong form; the conjectures being artifacts of limited examples
mainstream_view: An influential research program; individual conjectures range from well supported to contested
testable_prediction: Observational constraints on dark energy evolution test the de Sitter conjecture
key_evidence_or_cases: Weak gravity conjecture evidence; de Sitter conjecture and dark energy tension; distance conjecture in string examples
implication_if_solved: Would make quantum gravity observationally constraining

phenomenon: Cosmological constant sign and de Sitter stability
observation_summary: String theory has difficulty producing stable positive vacuum energy, which our universe appears to have
why_it_resists_explanation: Constructions producing positive vacuum energy involve delicate ingredient balancing whose consistency is debated
leading_hypotheses: Metastable de Sitter vacua as in KKLT; quintessence instead of a constant avoiding the problem; our acceleration being transient; de Sitter is impossible in quantum gravity
mainstream_view: A genuine tension between observation and the best-developed quantum gravity framework
testable_prediction: Dark energy evolution measurements by DESI and Euclid test whether it is a constant
key_evidence_or_cases: KKLT construction and critiques; DESI 2024 and 2025 dark energy evolution hints; quintessence model predictions
implication_if_solved: Would reconcile or falsify string theory against cosmological observation

phenomenon: Why spacetime has three large spatial dimensions
observation_summary: Nothing in known physics requires exactly three large spatial dimensions, and no mechanism explains the number
why_it_resists_explanation: Compactification scenarios permit many choices and no dynamical principle selects three
leading_hypotheses: Anthropic selection because stable orbits and atoms require three; brane gas dynamics favoring three-dimensional expansion; three dimensions being a topological accident of compactification
mainstream_view: An open question with anthropic and dynamical proposals and no established answer
testable_prediction: A dynamical mechanism should predict three uniquely from first principles
key_evidence_or_cases: Ehrenfest stability arguments 1917; Brandenberger-Vafa brane gas cosmology; extra dimension search limits at the LHC
implication_if_solved: Would explain the basic geometry of the world

observation_summary: Large extra dimensions were proposed to explain the hierarchy problem, and experiments have pushed limits to tens of micrometers
why_it_resists_explanation: Testing gravity at short distances is extremely difficult because electromagnetic backgrounds dominate
leading_hypotheses: Extra dimensions at micrometre scales still allowed; extra dimensions at unobservably small scales; no extra dimensions
mainstream_view: Large extra dimension scenarios are strongly constrained by both torsion balance and collider limits
testable_prediction: Torsion balance experiments should see deviations from Newtonian gravity if dimensions are large enough
key_evidence_or_cases: Eot-Wash torsion balance limits; LHC missing energy searches; Casimir force measurements at short range
implication_if_solved: Would solve the hierarchy problem and reveal new geometry

observation_summary: Whether constants such as the fine-structure constant vary in time or space has produced contested claims of detection
why_it_resists_explanation: The claimed variations are at the level of parts per million over billions of years, at the edge of systematic control
leading_hypotheses: Spatial dipole variation in the fine-structure constant as claimed from quasar spectra; no variation with claimed detections being wavelength calibration systematics; variation below current sensitivity
mainstream_view: Claims of variation are not accepted; laboratory clock comparisons and Oklo constrain variation tightly
testable_prediction: Atomic clock comparisons should detect drift if constants vary, and they have not
key_evidence_or_cases: Webb and Murphy quasar absorption claims; wavelength calibration systematics; Oklo reactor constraints; optical clock comparisons
implication_if_solved: Would indicate new physics with a dynamical scalar field

observation_summary: Different materials fall at the same rate to parts in 10 to the 15, with any violation indicating new forces
why_it_resists_explanation: Testing requires eliminating every environmental gradient, and space experiments are expensive and one-off
leading_hypotheses: Exact equivalence as in general relativity; violation from new scalar or vector fields at some level; violation specific to antimatter or dark matter interactions
mainstream_view: Confirmed to extraordinary precision; searches continue because violation would reveal new physics
testable_prediction: MICROSCOPE and successor missions should improve limits by orders of magnitude
key_evidence_or_cases: Eotvos experiments; lunar laser ranging; MICROSCOPE satellite 2017 and 2022 results at 10 to the minus 15
implication_if_solved: Would reveal a fifth force or new fields

observation_summary: Plate tectonics operates only on Earth among known planets, and when and why it started is unresolved
why_it_resists_explanation: Early crustal rocks are almost entirely destroyed by the process itself, leaving only indirect geochemical evidence
leading_hypotheses: Initiation in the Archean around three billion years ago; episodic early tectonics alternating with stagnant lid; initiation requiring water to weaken the lithosphere; gradual onset with no sharp start
mainstream_view: Modern-style tectonics is accepted for at least the last billion years; earlier history is genuinely contested
testable_prediction: Zircon trace element and isotope records should mark the onset of subduction, with conflicting interpretations
key_evidence_or_cases: Jack Hills zircons; eclogite inclusion ages; mantle potential temperature estimates; paleomagnetic plate motion records
implication_if_solved: Would explain why Earth is geologically and biologically unique

phenomenon: Why Earth has plate tectonics and Venus does not
observation_summary: Two similar planets have radically different tectonic regimes, and the decisive difference is uncertain
why_it_resists_explanation: Venus surface conditions prevent direct interior study and only limited radar mapping exists
leading_hypotheses: Water weakening Earth lithosphere and allowing subduction; Venus high surface temperature preventing plate bending; Venus losing water and seizing up; episodic resurfacing instead of plates
mainstream_view: The water hypothesis is favored; the question remains open and motivates upcoming Venus missions
testable_prediction: VERITAS and EnVision missions should map Venus deformation and crustal structure
key_evidence_or_cases: Magellan radar mapping; Venus crater age distribution suggesting global resurfacing; Earth hydrated mantle rheology experiments
implication_if_solved: Would explain planetary habitability divergence

observation_summary: Whether hotspot volcanoes are fed by deep mantle plumes or shallow processes is a decades-long dispute
why_it_resists_explanation: Seismic imaging resolution at mid-mantle depths is limited and geochemical signatures can be produced multiple ways
leading_hypotheses: Deep plumes rising from the core-mantle boundary; shallow upper mantle processes and plate stresses; a mixture with only some hotspots plume-fed
mainstream_view: Plume existence is supported by improved tomography for several hotspots; the generality remains contested
testable_prediction: Seismic tomography should resolve continuous low-velocity conduits, and increasingly does for Hawaii and Iceland
key_evidence_or_cases: Morgan 1971 plume hypothesis; French and Romanowicz 2015 tomography; helium-3 isotope signatures; Anderson and Natland critiques
implication_if_solved: Would determine how Earth loses deep interior heat

locus: Base of the mantle beneath Africa and the Pacific
observation_summary: Two continent-sized regions at the core-mantle boundary have anomalous seismic properties of unknown composition and origin
why_it_resists_explanation: They are 2900 km deep, sampled only indirectly by seismic waves, and composition cannot be determined uniquely
leading_hypotheses: Accumulated subducted oceanic crust; primordial material preserved since accretion; remnants of the Moon-forming impactor; thermochemical piles with distinct composition
mainstream_view: Existence firmly established; composition and origin genuinely unknown
testable_prediction: Seismic anisotropy plus mineral physics experiments should constrain composition
key_evidence_or_cases: Global seismic tomography models; ultralow velocity zones at their edges; 2023 impactor remnant hypothesis
implication_if_solved: Would reveal Earth deep structure and possibly preserved primordial material

observation_summary: Thin patches where seismic velocities drop by tens of percent indicate partial melt or exotic composition
why_it_resists_explanation: They are only tens of kilometers thick at 2900 km depth, at the limit of seismic resolution
leading_hypotheses: Partial melt pockets; iron-enriched post-perovskite; subducted oceanic crust accumulations; reaction products between core and mantle
mainstream_view: Detected in many locations; composition unresolved
testable_prediction: Waveform modeling with dense arrays should constrain their thickness and velocity structure
key_evidence_or_cases: Seismic waveform studies near hotspots; ScS and PKP precursor observations; high-pressure iron-rich mineral experiments
implication_if_solved: Would reveal core-mantle interaction and the source of hotspots

observation_summary: Minerals in the transition zone can hold several oceans worth of water, and how much they actually hold is unknown
why_it_resists_explanation: Direct sampling is impossible and electrical conductivity and seismic proxies are ambiguous
leading_hypotheses: Transition zone holding one to three ocean masses of water in ringwoodite; much drier mantle with localized wet regions; deep water cycle with subduction delivery and ridge return
mainstream_view: Hydrous ringwoodite confirmed in a diamond inclusion; global water content unconstrained
testable_prediction: Electrical conductivity and seismic velocity measurements should constrain water content
key_evidence_or_cases: Pearson et al 2014 hydrous ringwoodite inclusion in diamond; seismic discontinuity sharpness; conductivity profiles
implication_if_solved: Would determine Earth total water budget and the deep water cycle

observation_summary: Primordial helium-3 continues to leak from Earth interior although it should have escaped during accretion and differentiation
why_it_resists_explanation: Helium-3 is primordial and cannot be produced in significant amounts, so a 4.5 billion year old reservoir must survive
leading_hypotheses: An undegassed primordial mantle reservoir; storage in the core leaking into the mantle; deep mantle regions never processed by plate tectonics
mainstream_view: Measurements are robust; the reservoir location is contested
testable_prediction: Helium isotope ratios in hotspot lavas should map reservoir distribution, and they do partially
key_evidence_or_cases: High helium-3 to helium-4 ratios in Iceland and Hawaii; Baffin Island picrites; core helium partitioning experiments
implication_if_solved: Would reveal whether Earth retains primordial material

observation_summary: Heat flow across the boundary is uncertain by a factor of three, limiting understanding of the geodynamo and mantle convection
why_it_resists_explanation: It cannot be measured directly, and estimates depend on thermal conductivity of iron at extreme conditions which was revised sharply upward in 2012
leading_hypotheses: High core thermal conductivity requiring a young inner core and extra energy sources; lower conductivity consistent with traditional models; compositional convection driving the dynamo
mainstream_view: A major uncertainty with the new core paradox following revised conductivity estimates
testable_prediction: Improved conductivity measurements and dynamo modeling should resolve the energy budget
key_evidence_or_cases: Pozzo et al 2012 conductivity calculations; inner core age estimates; geodynamo energy budget analyses
implication_if_solved: Would determine the history of Earth magnetic field

phenomenon: Inner core age and the new core paradox
observation_summary: Revised thermal conductivity estimates imply the inner core is much younger than previously thought, creating an energy budget problem for the ancient magnetic field
why_it_resists_explanation: Paleomagnetic evidence shows a field at least 3.5 billion years old, but the energy source before inner core formation is unclear
leading_hypotheses: Precipitation of magnesium or silicon oxides from the core providing buoyancy; a thermally stratified early core with a different dynamo mode; higher early core-mantle heat flow
mainstream_view: A recognized paradox; several candidate energy sources are proposed
testable_prediction: Experimental core chemistry should show whether oxide precipitation is feasible
key_evidence_or_cases: Revised conductivity calculations; 3.45 billion year old paleomagnetic records; MgO precipitation experiments
implication_if_solved: Would explain the longevity of Earth protective magnetic field

observation_summary: Whether Earth had a strong magnetic field four billion years ago is disputed, with zircon paleomagnetic claims challenged
why_it_resists_explanation: Ancient magnetic signals can be overwritten by later events, and single-crystal measurements are at the sensitivity limit
leading_hypotheses: A strong field from 4.2 billion years ago as claimed from Jack Hills zircons; the zircon signals being secondary magnetizations; a weak or intermittent early field
mainstream_view: The early strong-field claims are contested on grounds of magnetic overprinting
testable_prediction: Rigorous demonstration that zircon magnetization is primary would settle it
key_evidence_or_cases: Tarduno 2015 Jack Hills zircon claims; Borlina and Weiss critiques; Archean dike paleointensity records
implication_if_solved: Would determine whether early Earth was shielded from solar wind

observation_summary: Large earthquakes trigger others thousands of kilometers away, sometimes days later, by mechanisms that are only partly understood
why_it_resists_explanation: Dynamic stress changes from passing waves are transient, so delayed triggering requires additional time-dependent processes
leading_hypotheses: Dynamic stress from passing seismic waves triggering critically stressed faults; fluid pressure changes from wave-induced permeability changes; subcritical crack growth delaying failure
mainstream_view: Remote triggering is firmly established; the delayed mechanism remains open
testable_prediction: Statistical analyses should show elevated rates following large events at specific distances, and they do
key_evidence_or_cases: 1992 Landers triggering of remote seismicity; tremor triggered by teleseismic waves; Sumatra 2004 global triggering
implication_if_solved: Would improve short-term seismic hazard assessment

observation_summary: Faults slip over weeks without generating damaging earthquakes, accompanied by weak tremor, in a mode unrecognized before GPS networks
why_it_resists_explanation: The slip is too slow for seismometers and too small for older geodesy, and the frictional conditions permitting it are unclear
leading_hypotheses: Transitional frictional stability near the base of the seismogenic zone; high fluid pressure enabling slow rupture; dehydration reactions providing fluids
mainstream_view: Firmly established worldwide; mechanism and relationship to large earthquakes remain open
testable_prediction: Monitoring should show whether slow slip loads or relieves the locked zone, and both occur
key_evidence_or_cases: Cascadia episodic tremor and slip; Nankai and Guerrero slow slip events; 2011 Tohoku preceding slow slip
implication_if_solved: Would improve forecasting of great subduction earthquakes

observation_summary: Some ruptures propagate faster than shear wave speed, once thought impossible, producing unusual shaking patterns
why_it_resists_explanation: The conditions permitting supershear are specific and the events are rare, so observations are limited
leading_hypotheses: Rupture transition to supershear on smooth mature faults; energy conditions requiring low fracture energy; damage zone structure enabling the transition
mainstream_view: Confirmed in several events and reproduced in laboratory experiments
testable_prediction: Rupture velocity measurements should exceed shear wave speed on specific fault segments, and they do
key_evidence_or_cases: 1999 Izmit earthquake; 2001 Kokoxili; 2018 Palu Sulawesi; laboratory supershear experiments
implication_if_solved: Would improve ground motion prediction for major faults

locus: Oil and gas and geothermal fields
observation_summary: Wastewater injection has caused earthquakes up to magnitude 5.8, with maximum magnitude unpredictable
why_it_resists_explanation: Whether injection volume limits maximum magnitude or the regional tectonic setting does is disputed
leading_hypotheses: Pore pressure diffusion unclamping faults; poroelastic stress transfer at distance; maximum magnitude limited by injected volume; maximum magnitude limited only by fault size
mainstream_view: Causation established; maximum magnitude prediction remains unresolved and consequential
testable_prediction: Volume-based maximum magnitude models should bound observed events, which they sometimes fail to do
key_evidence_or_cases: Oklahoma seismicity increase after 2009; 2016 Pawnee magnitude 5.8; Basel and Pohang geothermal events
notable_names: Healy; Ellsworth; Keranen; van der Elst
implication_if_solved: Would allow safe regulation of injection and geothermal energy

observation_summary: Thousands of similar-sized earthquakes occur over weeks without a dominant main shock, unlike normal sequences
why_it_resists_explanation: Standard earthquake statistics assume a main shock and aftershocks, which swarms violate, implying a different driving process
leading_hypotheses: Fluid migration driving sequential failure; magmatic intrusion stressing faults; slow slip driving seismicity; heterogeneous fault structure preventing large rupture
mainstream_view: Fluid and magma driving is well supported; the controls on maximum magnitude remain open
testable_prediction: Migration patterns should track fluid diffusion rates, and they often do
key_evidence_or_cases: Matsushiro swarm 1965 to 1967; Reykjanes 2020 to 2024 sequences; Long Valley caldera swarms
implication_if_solved: Would distinguish volcanic unrest from tectonic hazard

observation_summary: Some eruptions are forecast successfully days ahead while others occur with little or no warning
why_it_resists_explanation: Precursor patterns differ between volcanoes and eruption styles, and the relationship between unrest and eruption is probabilistic
leading_hypotheses: Magma ascent producing characteristic seismic and deformation precursors; failure of forecasting when magma ascends rapidly through open conduits; gas-driven eruptions with minimal precursors
mainstream_view: Short-term forecasting works at well-monitored volcanoes; general prediction remains limited
testable_prediction: Multiparameter monitoring should raise forecast skill, and it has at instrumented volcanoes
key_evidence_or_cases: Pinatubo 1991 successful evacuation; Whakaari White Island 2019 with little warning; Nevado del Ruiz 1985 failure
implication_if_solved: Would save lives at the hundreds of populated active volcanoes

observation_summary: What triggers the largest eruptions and how quickly magma bodies mobilize are not established
why_it_resists_explanation: Such eruptions have not occurred in recorded history, so the processes are reconstructed from deposits and crystal records
leading_hypotheses: Rapid remobilization of crystal mush by hot recharge; gradual accumulation reaching a critical overpressure; external triggering by tectonic events; decompression from roof failure
mainstream_view: Crystal zoning records indicate decades to centuries of pre-eruptive mobilization in some cases; triggers remain unresolved
testable_prediction: Crystal diffusion chronometry should reveal pre-eruptive timescales, and it does
key_evidence_or_cases: Yellowstone and Toba deposits; Bishop Tuff crystal zoning; Taupo eruption records; magma mush modeling
implication_if_solved: Would allow preparation for a civilization-scale hazard

observation_summary: A proposal that the Toba supereruption 74000 years ago nearly extinguished humans is now largely contradicted by evidence
why_it_resists_explanation: Genetic bottleneck signals have multiple possible causes and the archaeological record across the ash layer shows continuity
leading_hypotheses: A severe volcanic winter causing a population bottleneck; regional rather than global impact with human populations surviving; the genetic bottleneck predating Toba
mainstream_view: Largely rejected: archaeological sites show continuity across the ash layer and climate models suggest milder effects
testable_prediction: Sites spanning the ash layer should show occupation discontinuity, and they do not
key_evidence_or_cases: Rampino and Self volcanic winter modeling; Jwalapuram India continuity across ash; Lake Malawi sediment record; 2018 Pinnacle Point findings
implication_if_solved: Already a resolved case of an attractive hypothesis failing against evidence

observation_summary: A large caldera under a populated area has undergone meters of ground uplift in episodes since the 1950s without erupting
why_it_resists_explanation: Distinguishing magmatic from hydrothermal causes of uplift is difficult, and the system has not erupted since 1538
leading_hypotheses: Magmatic intrusion at depth driving uplift; hydrothermal fluid pressurization without new magma; progressive crustal weakening approaching failure
mainstream_view: Unrest is well monitored; eruption probability and mechanism are genuinely uncertain
testable_prediction: Gas chemistry and seismicity should distinguish magmatic from hydrothermal drivers
key_evidence_or_cases: 1969 to 1972 and 1982 to 1984 uplift episodes of about 3.5 metres total; ongoing uplift since 2005; 2023 crustal weakening analysis
notable_names: Del Gaudio; Chiodini; Kilburn; De Natale
implication_if_solved: Would protect half a million people living inside a caldera

observation_summary: Seismic imaging shows a large partially molten reservoir, with melt fraction estimates differing enough to change hazard assessment
why_it_resists_explanation: Melt fraction is inferred from seismic velocities which depend on melt geometry as well as amount
leading_hypotheses: Low melt fraction crystal mush unlikely to erupt soon; higher melt fractions in localized bodies; 2022 analysis suggesting higher melt than previously thought
mainstream_view: Reservoir existence established; melt fraction and eruption likelihood actively debated
testable_prediction: Joint seismic and magnetotelluric imaging should constrain melt fraction
key_evidence_or_cases: Seismic tomography models; 2022 melt fraction reanalysis; ground deformation and gas flux monitoring
implication_if_solved: Would quantify the hazard from a major caldera system

observation_summary: Steam explosions occur without magma involvement and with almost no warning, as at Whakaari in 2019
why_it_resists_explanation: The triggering involves rapid pressure changes in shallow hydrothermal systems that are hard to monitor
leading_hypotheses: Sudden depressurization causing flash boiling; seal failure in self-sealed hydrothermal systems; gas slug ascent; rainfall-triggered pressure changes
mainstream_view: A recognized hazard with very limited forecasting capability
testable_prediction: Dense shallow monitoring should detect pressurization before failure
key_evidence_or_cases: Whakaari White Island 2019 eruption killing 22; Yellowstone hydrothermal explosion craters; Mount Ontake 2014
implication_if_solved: Would protect visitors to geothermal tourist sites

observation_summary: Deep lakes can suddenly release enormous volumes of dissolved carbon dioxide, suffocating people and animals
why_it_resists_explanation: The 1986 Nyos event killed 1746 people and the trigger of the overturn was never definitively identified
leading_hypotheses: Landslide or rainfall-triggered overturn of a stratified saturated lake; internal wave triggering; volcanic gas influx causing saturation; spontaneous exsolution at saturation
mainstream_view: Mechanism broadly understood and now mitigated by degassing pipes; the specific trigger remains unidentified
testable_prediction: Monitoring of gas concentration and stratification should predict saturation risk, and degassing has reduced it
key_evidence_or_cases: Lake Monoun 1984 and Lake Nyos 1986 events; degassing pipe installation; Lake Kivu methane and CO2 monitoring
implication_if_solved: Would protect populations near other gas-charged lakes

observation_summary: A mud eruption that began in 2006 continues and has displaced tens of thousands, with the trigger disputed
why_it_resists_explanation: An earthquake and a drilling operation occurred near the same time, making attribution contentious and legally charged
leading_hypotheses: Triggering by a nearby gas drilling blowout; triggering by the Yogyakarta earthquake two days earlier; a natural eruption that would have occurred regardless
mainstream_view: Scientifically contested with significant literature on both sides and legal implications
testable_prediction: Pressure data from the drilling operation and earthquake stress modeling should discriminate
key_evidence_or_cases: Lusi eruption since May 2006; drilling records; seismic triggering analyses; continuing mud discharge
implication_if_solved: Would settle liability and inform drilling safety near mud volcano provinces

observation_summary: Vast methane stores exist in hydrates whose stability under warming is uncertain, affecting climate projections
why_it_resists_explanation: Hydrate deposits are hard to quantify and release mechanisms operate over timescales from decades to millennia
leading_hypotheses: Gradual dissociation with most methane oxidized before reaching the atmosphere; catastrophic release scenarios (largely discounted); Arctic shelf release contributing modestly
mainstream_view: Current consensus rejects catastrophic clathrate gun scenarios; the magnitude of gradual release is uncertain
testable_prediction: Monitoring of seafloor seeps and atmospheric isotopes should quantify release, and so far shows modest contributions
key_evidence_or_cases: Clathrate gun hypothesis; East Siberian Arctic Shelf seep observations; PETM carbon isotope excursion debates
implication_if_solved: Would resolve a major climate feedback uncertainty

observation_summary: A massive carbon release warmed the planet five degrees in a few thousand years from an unidentified source
why_it_resists_explanation: The isotopic signature constrains the source but multiple candidates fit within uncertainty, and the release rate is debated
leading_hypotheses: Volcanic carbon from the North Atlantic Igneous Province; methane hydrate dissociation; permafrost and peat burning; thermogenic methane from sill intrusion into organic sediments
mainstream_view: The event is extremely well documented; the carbon source remains unresolved
testable_prediction: Precise carbon isotope mass balance plus mercury proxies should identify volcanic contributions
key_evidence_or_cases: Carbon isotope excursion in marine and terrestrial records; North Atlantic volcanism timing; mercury anomalies; boron isotope pH records
implication_if_solved: Would calibrate the climate response to rapid carbon release

observation_summary: Antarctica glaciated abruptly, with the relative roles of carbon dioxide decline and ocean gateway opening disputed
why_it_resists_explanation: Both CO2 decline and the opening of Southern Ocean gateways occurred near the same time and cannot be cleanly separated
leading_hypotheses: CO2 decline crossing a glaciation threshold; Drake Passage opening thermally isolating Antarctica; orbital configuration triggering within a CO2 window
mainstream_view: CO2 decline is now generally favored over gateway opening as the primary driver
testable_prediction: Proxy CO2 records and modeling should show the threshold crossing, and increasingly do
key_evidence_or_cases: Oxygen isotope records; alkenone and boron CO2 proxies; Drake Passage opening dating; modeling of glaciation thresholds
implication_if_solved: Would clarify what controls the growth of continental ice sheets

observation_summary: The Mediterranean Sea largely evaporated between 5.9 and 5.3 million years ago, leaving kilometers of salt, then refilled rapidly
why_it_resists_explanation: The mechanism of closure and the speed of refilling through the Zanclean flood are both debated
leading_hypotheses: Tectonic closure of the Gibraltar connection with evaporation; glacio-eustatic sea level fall contributing; refilling via catastrophic Zanclean megaflood; partial rather than complete desiccation
mainstream_view: The crisis is firmly established from drill cores; the degree of desiccation and refill mechanism remain debated
testable_prediction: Seismic imaging of the Gibraltar channel should reveal flood erosion features, and it does
key_evidence_or_cases: DSDP Leg 13 salt cores 1970; Zanclean flood erosion channel evidence; salt thickness estimates up to 2 km
implication_if_solved: Would document the largest flood in Earth history

observation_summary: A proposed flood refilled the Mediterranean in months to a few years with discharge a thousand times the Amazon
why_it_resists_explanation: The erosional evidence is buried under sediment and the timescale estimates vary by orders of magnitude
leading_hypotheses: Catastrophic incision-driven flood refilling in under two years; gradual refilling over thousands of years; multiple partial flooding episodes
mainstream_view: The flood is widely accepted; its speed and magnitude are contested
testable_prediction: Detailed seismic mapping of the erosion channel should constrain discharge
key_evidence_or_cases: Garcia-Castellanos 2009 analysis; 200 km erosion channel identified in seismic data; sediment deposits in the western basin
implication_if_solved: Would characterize the most extreme flood event known

observation_summary: Enormous flood channels were carved by catastrophic glacial lake outbursts, a theory rejected for decades before acceptance
why_it_resists_explanation: Catastrophism conflicted with uniformitarian geology, and the evidence required recognizing landforms at unfamiliar scale
leading_hypotheses: Repeated outburst floods from glacial Lake Missoula; a single catastrophic flood; subglacial outburst sources contributing
mainstream_view: Fully accepted; the number and sources of floods remain under study
testable_prediction: Dating of flood deposits should reveal the number of events, and it indicates dozens
key_evidence_or_cases: Bretz 1923 hypothesis and decades of rejection; giant current ripples; Lake Missoula shoreline evidence; slackwater rhythmites
implication_if_solved: Already a landmark case of a correct theory rejected for decades

observation_summary: Moraine-dammed lakes fail catastrophically with limited warning, killing thousands, and failure timing cannot be predicted
why_it_resists_explanation: Dam internal structure is unknown, triggers include avalanches and earthquakes, and the lakes are remote
leading_hypotheses: Moraine dam piping and overtopping after a trigger wave; ice core melting within the dam; permafrost degradation weakening dams
mainstream_view: Mechanisms understood in outline; prediction of individual failures remains infeasible
testable_prediction: Remote sensing of lake growth plus dam geometry should rank risk, and it does
key_evidence_or_cases: 2013 Kedarnath disaster; 2023 South Lhonak Lake outburst in Sikkim; Peruvian Cordillera Blanca historical events
implication_if_solved: Would protect downstream populations in the Himalaya and Andes

observation_summary: Permafrost holds roughly twice the carbon in the atmosphere, and how much will be released under warming is uncertain by a factor of several
why_it_resists_explanation: Abrupt thaw processes like thermokarst are not represented in most models, and the balance between CO2 and methane release is uncertain
leading_hypotheses: Gradual thaw releasing carbon over centuries; abrupt thaw doubling the release; vegetation uptake offsetting part of the release; microbial processing rates limiting release
mainstream_view: Recognized as a major uncertainty in carbon cycle projections
testable_prediction: Long-term warming experiments and flux monitoring should constrain release rates
key_evidence_or_cases: Permafrost Carbon Network syntheses; thermokarst mapping; Yedoma carbon inventories; flux tower measurements
implication_if_solved: Would determine a major amplifying feedback on climate

observation_summary: The Arctic is warming three to four times faster than the global average, and the contributions of each mechanism are disputed
why_it_resists_explanation: Several feedbacks operate simultaneously in a data-sparse region with strong seasonality
leading_hypotheses: Sea ice albedo feedback; lapse rate feedback from stable Arctic stratification; increased poleward heat and moisture transport; cloud and water vapor feedbacks
mainstream_view: Amplification is firmly measured; attribution among feedbacks is debated
testable_prediction: Feedback decomposition in models and observations should converge, and is beginning to
key_evidence_or_cases: Arctic temperature records; sea ice extent decline since 1979; feedback decomposition studies; 2022 four-times amplification estimate
implication_if_solved: Would improve projections of Arctic change and its global effects

phenomenon: Arctic sea ice loss and midlatitude weather
observation_summary: Whether Arctic sea ice loss causes extreme midlatitude weather through a wavier jet stream is strongly contested
why_it_resists_explanation: The proposed signal is small compared with natural variability, observational records are short, and model experiments disagree with observational studies
leading_hypotheses: Sea ice loss weakening the jet stream and increasing blocking; the effect being too small to detect; apparent correlations arising from a common driver; model underestimation of the response
mainstream_view: A high-profile dispute; model evidence generally shows weaker effects than observational studies claim
testable_prediction: Large coordinated model experiments should quantify the response, and they show small effects
key_evidence_or_cases: Francis and Vavrus 2012 wavy jet hypothesis; PAMIP coordinated model experiments; Blackport and Screen critiques
implication_if_solved: Would determine whether Arctic change drives midlatitude extremes

observation_summary: Sudden stratospheric warmings disrupt the polar vortex and cause severe cold outbreaks weeks later, with limited predictability
why_it_resists_explanation: The triggering wave activity arises from tropospheric variability that is itself only predictable about two weeks ahead
leading_hypotheses: Upward propagating planetary wave forcing from the troposphere; internal stratospheric dynamics; preconditioning by the vortex state
mainstream_view: Mechanism well understood; forecasting lead times are improving but remain limited
testable_prediction: Subseasonal forecast systems should predict warmings a few weeks out, and they increasingly do
key_evidence_or_cases: Scherhag 1952 discovery; February 2021 Texas cold outbreak; 2018 Beast from the East; forecast skill assessments
implication_if_solved: Would extend useful weather forecasts to several weeks

observation_summary: A planetary-scale convective disturbance circles the tropics every 30 to 60 days, and models still simulate it poorly
why_it_resists_explanation: It involves interactions between convection, moisture and large-scale circulation across scales that models struggle to resolve
leading_hypotheses: Moisture mode theory with convection coupled to moisture; wave-driven theories involving Kelvin waves; skin temperature and air-sea coupling contributions
mainstream_view: Moisture mode theory has gained consensus; model simulation remains deficient
testable_prediction: Models with better convective parameterization should reproduce the oscillation, and improvement has followed
key_evidence_or_cases: Madden and Julian 1971 discovery; DYNAMO field campaign; model intercomparison of MJO skill
implication_if_solved: Would extend tropical and global subseasonal forecasting

observation_summary: A highly regular 28-month wind reversal in the stratosphere was unexpectedly disrupted in 2016 and 2019 for the first time on record
why_it_resists_explanation: The oscillation was regarded as the most predictable mode in the atmosphere, so the disruptions were unforecast and remain unexplained
leading_hypotheses: Unusual extratropical wave fluxes into the tropics; a response to anomalous El Nino conditions; a possible manifestation of climate change altering wave forcing
mainstream_view: The disruptions are firmly documented; their cause and whether they will recur are unresolved
testable_prediction: Wave flux diagnostics should identify the disrupting forcing, and partial analyses have
key_evidence_or_cases: Reed and Ebdon discovery 1960s; 2016 and 2019 disruptions; wave flux analyses; model reproduction attempts
implication_if_solved: Would reveal whether a key predictable atmospheric mode is destabilizing

phenomenon: El Nino diversity and prediction limits
observation_summary: El Nino events differ substantially in pattern and impact, and forecasts beyond about six months remain unreliable
why_it_resists_explanation: The spring predictability barrier limits forecast skill, and event diversity means the same index can produce different impacts
leading_hypotheses: Central Pacific versus eastern Pacific event types with different dynamics; stochastic wind bursts limiting predictability; coupled instability with multiple regimes
mainstream_view: Mechanism broadly understood; diversity and the predictability barrier remain open problems
testable_prediction: Improved ocean initialization should extend skill past the spring barrier, with modest progress
key_evidence_or_cases: 1997 and 2015 major events; central Pacific El Nino identification; forecast skill assessments across models
implication_if_solved: Would improve seasonal forecasts affecting billions of people

observation_summary: Monsoon onset timing and seasonal rainfall totals affect billions and remain poorly predictable at useful lead times
why_it_resists_explanation: The monsoon couples ocean, land surface, aerosols and atmospheric dynamics, and models have persistent biases
leading_hypotheses: Land-sea thermal contrast with moisture feedbacks; aerosol effects on heating and rainfall; internal intraseasonal variability limiting seasonal predictability; ENSO and Indian Ocean Dipole modulation
mainstream_view: Dynamics broadly understood; seasonal prediction skill is low and model biases persist
testable_prediction: High-resolution models with better aerosol treatment should improve skill, with incremental progress
key_evidence_or_cases: Halley 1686 monsoon theory; Indian Meteorological Department forecast skill records; aerosol dimming studies
implication_if_solved: Would improve food security forecasting for a quarter of humanity

phenomenon: Tropical cyclone intensification and rapid intensification
observation_summary: Storms sometimes intensify explosively within 24 hours, and these cases are the hardest to forecast
why_it_resists_explanation: Intensification depends on inner core processes at scales below operational model resolution and on unmeasured ocean subsurface structure
leading_hypotheses: Inner core convective bursts and vortex alignment; ocean heat content and shallow warm layers; dry air intrusion suppression; stochastic inner core variability limiting predictability
mainstream_view: Track forecasting has improved greatly; intensity forecasting especially rapid intensification remains much harder
testable_prediction: High-resolution coupled models should improve intensity skill, and recent progress supports this
