mainstream_view: The carvings are documented in detail; interpretations remain speculative
testable_prediction: Statistical analysis of symbol co-occurrence across enclosures might reveal grammar-like structure
key_evidence_or_cases: Pillar 43 the Vulture Stone; animal species distribution across enclosures; Karahan Tepe comparative iconography
implication_if_solved: Would recover the symbolic system of the earliest monumental builders

phenomenon: Karahan Tepe and the Tas Tepeler sites
observation_summary: A dozen related sites with megalithic architecture predate agriculture, revealing a whole unknown cultural horizon
why_it_resists_explanation: Excavation is in early stages, and the relationship between sites and the nature of the society are unknown
leading_hypotheses: A regional ritual and social network among hunter-gatherers; permanent settlements with communal architecture; a cultural phenomenon preceding and enabling agriculture
mainstream_view: Sites are confirmed and under active excavation; interpretation is preliminary
testable_prediction: Continued excavation should reveal settlement versus ritual function
key_evidence_or_cases: Karahan Tepe human head pillars and carved chamber; Tas Tepeler project since 2021; Sayburc reliefs
implication_if_solved: Would transform understanding of the transition to agriculture

phenomenon: Natufian and the origins of sedentism
observation_summary: People settled in permanent villages before domesticating plants or animals, inverting the assumed sequence
why_it_resists_explanation: The drivers of sedentism are inferred from settlement remains, and multiple environmental and social factors coincide
leading_hypotheses: Abundant wild resources permitting sedentism; climate improvement during the Bolling-Allerod; social and ritual aggregation driving settlement; storage technology enabling permanence
mainstream_view: Sequence firmly established; causation debated
testable_prediction: Paleoenvironmental records should correlate with settlement onset, and they partly do
key_evidence_or_cases: Ain Mallaha and Abu Hureyra settlements; wild cereal processing evidence; Younger Dryas impact on Natufian settlement
implication_if_solved: Would explain the origin of settled life

observation_summary: Agriculture arose independently in many places within a few thousand years after 200000 years of foraging
why_it_resists_explanation: The near-simultaneity across unconnected regions suggests a common driver, but each region has distinct local trajectories
leading_hypotheses: Post-glacial climate stabilization making farming viable everywhere at once; rising CO2 improving plant productivity; population pressure; social and ritual drivers; a combination of global enabling conditions and local triggers
mainstream_view: Independence of origins is established genetically and archaeologically; the simultaneity is partly explained by climate
testable_prediction: Climate records should show a threshold crossing at the right time, and the Holocene onset fits
key_evidence_or_cases: Domestication genetics in wheat rice and maize; Holocene climate stabilization; eleven independent centers identified
implication_if_solved: Would explain the foundational transition of human history

observation_summary: Unrelated domesticated animals share traits like floppy ears, piebald coats and reduced brain size, and crops share parallel changes
why_it_resists_explanation: No single selective pressure explains why traits unrelated to the selected ones co-occur across species
leading_hypotheses: Neural crest cell developmental deficits producing linked traits (Wilkins hypothesis); selection on tameness dragging linked traits; the syndrome being partly a post hoc construct from inconsistent trait lists
mainstream_view: The neural crest hypothesis is influential but the syndrome itself has been criticized as inconsistently defined
testable_prediction: Neural crest gene variants should appear in domesticated lineages, with partial support
key_evidence_or_cases: Darwin 1868 observations; Belyaev fox experiment and its reinterpretation; Wilkins neural crest hypothesis 2014; Lord et al critique 2020
implication_if_solved: Would explain parallel evolution under human selection

observation_summary: Dogs were the first domesticated animal but when, where and how many times remains disputed despite extensive ancient DNA work
why_it_resists_explanation: Ancient dog and wolf genomes are limited, dogs moved with humans obscuring geography, and the wolf ancestor population is extinct
leading_hypotheses: A single domestication in Eurasia between 15000 and 30000 years ago; dual domestication in East and West; domestication from an extinct wolf population with contributions from two source populations as 2022 work suggests
mainstream_view: Multiple ancient DNA studies disagree on number and location of origins
testable_prediction: More ancient wolf and dog genomes should resolve the population structure
key_evidence_or_cases: Bonn-Oberkassel dog burial 14200 years old; Frantz 2016 dual origin proposal; Bergstrom 2022 ancient wolf genomes
implication_if_solved: Would date the first human-animal partnership

observation_summary: Cats domesticated themselves through commensalism rather than deliberate breeding, with timing and process unclear
why_it_resists_explanation: Cats remain genetically close to wild ancestors and show few domestication changes, making the transition hard to date
leading_hypotheses: Commensal self-domestication around grain stores in the Near East about 10000 years ago; later Egyptian intensification; limited human selection explaining minimal genetic change
mainstream_view: Near Eastern origin established genetically; the process timeline remains coarse
testable_prediction: Ancient cat genomes across the Mediterranean should trace the spread, and they partly do
key_evidence_or_cases: Cyprus burial with a cat 9500 years old; Ottoni 2017 ancient DNA study; Egyptian cat mummies
implication_if_solved: Would document a distinct pathway to domestication

observation_summary: Horse domestication transformed human mobility but its origin was misattributed for decades before ancient DNA resolved it
why_it_resists_explanation: Early candidate sites such as Botai turned out to represent a different lineage that did not contribute to modern horses
leading_hypotheses: Origin in the Western Eurasian steppe around 2200 BCE as shown by 2021 ancient DNA; Botai horses as a separate domestication that left no modern descendants; multiple failed domestications
mainstream_view: Substantially resolved by the 2021 genomic study identifying the Volga-Don region
testable_prediction: Ancient genomes should show a rapid expansion from one region, and they do
key_evidence_or_cases: Botai site evidence and its reinterpretation; Librado et al 2021 Nature study; chariot and spoked wheel spread
implication_if_solved: Already resolved the origin of a transformative technology

observation_summary: A single language family came to dominate Eurasia, with the homeland and mechanism debated for over two centuries
why_it_resists_explanation: Linguistic, archaeological and genetic evidence point to overlapping but not identical scenarios
leading_hypotheses: Steppe origin with Yamnaya expansion around 3000 BCE; Anatolian farming origin around 7000 BCE; a hybrid model with a Caucasus-Lower Volga homeland as 2025 genomic work suggests
mainstream_view: The steppe hypothesis is dominant and supported by ancient DNA; refinements continue, including 2025 work identifying an earlier source population
testable_prediction: Ancient genomes along proposed migration routes should show the expected ancestry, and they increasingly do
key_evidence_or_cases: Jones 1786 language relationships; Haak and Allentoft 2015 steppe ancestry studies; Renfrew Anatolian hypothesis; 2025 Caucasus-Lower Volga papers
implication_if_solved: Would explain the linguistic map of half the world

observation_summary: Basque is the only surviving pre-Indo-European language in western Europe, with no established relatives
why_it_resists_explanation: Proposed relationships to Caucasian or other families have failed to meet standard comparative criteria
leading_hypotheses: A survival of a pre-Indo-European language family otherwise extinct; a distant relationship to Iberian or Caucasian languages (unproven); a true isolate with all relatives lost
mainstream_view: Accepted as an isolate; its deeper affiliations are unknown and probably unrecoverable
testable_prediction: Decipherment of Iberian or Aquitanian material might reveal relationships
key_evidence_or_cases: Aquitanian inscriptions as an ancestor; Hand of Irulegi inscription 2022; failed Vasconic and Dene-Caucasian proposals
implication_if_solved: Would recover the pre-Indo-European linguistic landscape of Europe

observation_summary: The language of the first writing system has no established relatives among known language families
why_it_resists_explanation: Sumerian died as a spoken language around 2000 BCE and its relatives, if any, were never written
leading_hypotheses: A language isolate whose relatives are extinct; a relationship to Caucasian or Dravidian families (unproven); a substrate language of southern Mesopotamia
mainstream_view: Well understood as a language through bilingual texts; its genetic affiliation is unknown
testable_prediction: Any related language would need to be identified among undeciphered scripts
key_evidence_or_cases: Extensive Sumerian-Akkadian bilingual lexical lists; grammatical descriptions; failed affiliation proposals
implication_if_solved: Would place the first written language in a family

observation_summary: Place names and vocabulary suggest pre-Indo-European languages across Europe that left no direct records
why_it_resists_explanation: Substrate reconstruction from loanwords and toponyms is methodologically contested and allows wide latitude
leading_hypotheses: Multiple pre-Indo-European language families leaving substrate traces; many claimed substrate words having Indo-European etymologies after all; a Vasconic substrate across western Europe (contested)
mainstream_view: Substrates certainly existed; specific reconstructions are highly speculative
testable_prediction: Ancient DNA correlations with linguistic substrate zones might support specific scenarios
key_evidence_or_cases: Non-Indo-European river names in Europe; Vennemann Vasconic hypothesis and critiques; Aegean pre-Greek substrate
implication_if_solved: Would recover the linguistic diversity of pre-Indo-European Europe

observation_summary: A population has maintained total isolation, and their language is completely unknown and unclassifiable
why_it_resists_explanation: All contact attempts have been refused, often violently, and contact would endanger them through disease
leading_hypotheses: Related to other Andamanese languages but divergent; an isolate distinct from Great Andamanese; unclassifiable without contact
mainstream_view: Isolation respected by policy; the language and culture remain undocumented and should remain so
testable_prediction: No ethical research pathway exists; linguistic classification will likely remain unknown
key_evidence_or_cases: Failed contact expeditions; 1991 brief peaceful contact; Indian government no-contact policy since 1996
implication_if_solved: Would document the last fully uncontacted language, though contact would be unethical

observation_summary: Extensive trade between Mesopotamia and the Indus implies a shared commercial language or interpreter system that left no trace
why_it_resists_explanation: Mesopotamian records mention Meluhha and interpreters but preserve no Indus-language material
leading_hypotheses: Akkadian used as a lingua franca with Meluhhan interpreters; a pidgin trade language; the Indus script serving commercial functions across the network
mainstream_view: Trade is firmly documented; the linguistic mechanism is unknown
testable_prediction: Finding an Indus-Akkadian bilingual document would resolve both this and the Indus script
key_evidence_or_cases: Meluhha references in cuneiform; Indus seals found in Mesopotamia; a cylinder seal of a Meluhhan interpreter
implication_if_solved: Would decipher the Indus script and document early globalization

observation_summary: Inca knotted cord records encoded numerical data and possibly narrative content that has never been fully read
why_it_resists_explanation: Only numerical conventions are decoded, most khipu are unprovenanced, and no bilingual key exists
leading_hypotheses: A numerical accounting system with some non-numerical encoding; a full logosyllabic writing system in cord form; a mnemonic aid requiring oral context
mainstream_view: Numerical khipu are substantially decoded; narrative khipu remain unread
testable_prediction: Matching a khipu to a colonial Spanish transcription of its content would provide a key
key_evidence_or_cases: Locke 1923 numerical decipherment; Santa Cruz khipu matched to a Spanish census; Khipu Database Project; 2022 ethnographic khipu studies
implication_if_solved: Would recover the records of the largest pre-Columbian empire

observation_summary: Correlating the Maya calendar with the Gregorian calendar relies on a conventional constant that has small residual uncertainties
why_it_resists_explanation: The correlation depends on colonial-era records and astronomical events recorded in inscriptions, each with interpretive latitude
leading_hypotheses: The GMT correlation constant of 584283 as the standard; small adjustments of a few days supported by some evidence; different correlations for different regions
mainstream_view: The GMT correlation is standard and strongly supported by radiocarbon cross-checks
testable_prediction: Radiocarbon dating of dated monuments should match the correlation, and it does
key_evidence_or_cases: Goodman Martinez Thompson correlation; 2013 radiocarbon test of a dated lintel; Venus table and eclipse records
implication_if_solved: Would allow precise dating of Mesoamerican history

observation_summary: Maya writing is largely deciphered but a fraction of signs remain unread
why_it_resists_explanation: The remaining signs are rare, appear in limited contexts, and lack phonetic complements
leading_hypotheses: Rare logograms for uncommon words; signs from regional or archaic variants; signs whose referents are no longer identifiable
mainstream_view: Decipherment is one of the great successes of epigraphy; residual signs remain
testable_prediction: New inscriptions with phonetic complements should resolve individual signs
key_evidence_or_cases: Knorozov phonetic approach; Proskouriakoff historical readings; current sign catalogs with unread entries
implication_if_solved: Would complete the reading of a major ancient literature

observation_summary: Pre-contact population estimates vary by a factor of five or more, affecting assessment of the demographic collapse
why_it_resists_explanation: Colonial censuses postdate massive mortality, and archaeological methods give wide ranges
leading_hypotheses: High estimates of 50 to 100 million for the Americas; low estimates of 8 to 20 million; regional estimates converging around 40 to 60 million
mainstream_view: A long-standing dispute with substantial consequences for understanding the conquest
testable_prediction: Settlement archaeology and lidar surveys should constrain densities, and lidar has raised estimates
key_evidence_or_cases: Lidar surveys of Maya lowlands revealing dense settlement; colonial tribute records; paleoecological land use indicators
implication_if_solved: Would quantify the largest demographic catastrophe in recorded history

observation_summary: Epidemics killed up to 80 percent of the indigenous population with a disease that Spanish and Aztec accounts describe but which has no clear modern equivalent
why_it_resists_explanation: Descriptions do not match European diseases well, and ancient DNA work has produced only partial answers
leading_hypotheses: Salmonella enterica Paratyphi C as suggested by 2018 ancient DNA; a viral hemorrhagic fever of local origin; multiple pathogens with drought-driven amplification
mainstream_view: A 2018 study identified Salmonella in victims, which is suggestive but not conclusive
testable_prediction: Additional ancient DNA from other cocoliztli cemeteries should confirm the pathogen
key_evidence_or_cases: Vagene et al 2018 Teposcolula-Yucundaa ancient DNA; Sahagun and Spanish accounts; tree ring drought records
implication_if_solved: Would identify the pathogen behind the Americas demographic collapse

phenomenon: Syphilis origin and the Columbian exchange
observation_summary: Whether syphilis came from the Americas or was present in Europe before 1492 has been debated for 500 years
why_it_resists_explanation: Skeletal diagnosis of treponemal disease is ambiguous, and the treponemal subspecies are nearly identical genetically
leading_hypotheses: American origin with introduction to Europe after 1493; pre-Columbian European presence with a change in virulence; a combination with both continents having treponemal diseases that recombined
mainstream_view: The 2024 ancient genome work supports American origins for the venereal form; pre-Columbian European treponemal disease remains debated
testable_prediction: Ancient treponemal genomes from both continents should establish the phylogeny, and recent work supports American origins
key_evidence_or_cases: Pre-Columbian skeletal lesions in both regions; 2020 and 2024 ancient Treponema genomes from Brazil and Mexico; historical outbreak records
implication_if_solved: Would settle a 500-year-old epidemiological dispute

phenomenon: Easter Island rongorongo relationship to contact
observation_summary: Whether rongorongo was invented before European contact or stimulated by seeing Spanish writing in 1770 is disputed
why_it_resists_explanation: All surviving tablets were collected after contact, and the 2024 radiocarbon dates on one tablet are suggestive but limited
leading_hypotheses: Pre-contact independent invention supported by a 2024 radiocarbon date around 1500; post-contact stimulus diffusion after the 1770 Spanish visit; a pre-contact proto-system elaborated after contact
mainstream_view: The 2024 dating of one tablet to before contact supports independent invention but does not settle it
testable_prediction: Radiocarbon dating of more tablets should establish the chronology
key_evidence_or_cases: Ferrara et al 2024 radiocarbon dating of Rome tablets; 1770 Spanish annexation document signing; Jaussen collection history
implication_if_solved: Would establish whether writing was independently invented in Polynesia

observation_summary: Herodotus reports a Phoenician voyage around Africa around 600 BCE, with the account containing a detail that argues for authenticity
why_it_resists_explanation: No archaeological evidence exists, but the sailors reported the sun on their right hand which would only be observed in the southern hemisphere
leading_hypotheses: A genuine circumnavigation under Necho II; a partial voyage with the solar detail added later; a fabrication that coincidentally included a plausible detail
mainstream_view: Historically debated; the solar observation detail is widely considered suggestive of authenticity
testable_prediction: Archaeological evidence of Phoenician presence on the East or West African coast would support it
key_evidence_or_cases: Herodotus Histories 4.42; the sun on the right hand detail; absence of corroborating archaeology; Hanno Periplus as a comparable voyage
implication_if_solved: Would document a navigational achievement 2000 years ahead of its rediscovery

observation_summary: Most claimed pre-Columbian contacts are unsupported, but Polynesian-South American contact is now genetically confirmed
why_it_resists_explanation: Claims proliferated without evidence for a century, and distinguishing genuine from spurious contacts requires genetic or botanical proof
leading_hypotheses: Confirmed Polynesian-South American contact around 1200 CE from genomic admixture; sweet potato dispersal by Polynesian voyaging; Norse contact at L Anse aux Meadows confirmed; most other claims unsupported
mainstream_view: Two contacts are confirmed (Norse and Polynesian); the rest of the claimed contacts lack evidence
testable_prediction: Genomic and botanical evidence should show admixture or crop transfer, and it does for these two cases
key_evidence_or_cases: Ioannidis et al 2020 Polynesian-Native American admixture; L Anse aux Meadows dated to 1021 CE; sweet potato genetics
implication_if_solved: Would map genuine pre-modern transoceanic connections

phenomenon: Norse presence in North America beyond Vinland
observation_summary: Norse presence is confirmed at one site, with evidence of wider Arctic contact but no other confirmed settlement
why_it_resists_explanation: Norse artifacts in Arctic contexts may reflect trade rather than settlement, and site identification is contested
leading_hypotheses: One short-lived settlement with wider trade contact; additional undiscovered sites; claimed sites such as Point Rosee being natural features
mainstream_view: L Anse aux Meadows is confirmed and precisely dated to 1021 CE; other claimed sites are unverified
testable_prediction: Excavation of candidate sites should find Norse material, which has failed at Point Rosee
key_evidence_or_cases: L Anse aux Meadows excavation; 2021 dendrochronological dating to 1021 CE; Norse artifacts at Baffin Island sites; Point Rosee negative results
implication_if_solved: Would map the extent of pre-Columbian European contact

observation_summary: A map claimed to show Norse knowledge of America before Columbus was proven a 20th century forgery in 2021
why_it_resists_explanation: Ink analysis gave conflicting results for decades until comprehensive 2021 analysis resolved it
leading_hypotheses: A modern forgery as established by 2021 titanium-based ink analysis; an authentic 15th century map (now refuted)
mainstream_view: Definitively resolved as a forgery by Yale analysis in 2021
testable_prediction: Ink composition analysis should reveal modern pigments, and it did
key_evidence_or_cases: Yale 1965 publication; decades of anatase titanium dioxide ink disputes; 2021 comprehensive analysis confirming forgery
implication_if_solved: Already resolved; a case study in forgery detection

phenomenon: Kensington Runestone and North American runic claims
observation_summary: A runestone claimed to record a 14th century Norse expedition is regarded by runologists as a 19th century creation
why_it_resists_explanation: The stone was found by a farmer with no archaeological context, and the runes and language contain modern features
leading_hypotheses: A modern creation by Scandinavian immigrants; an authentic medieval inscription (rejected by runologists); a deliberate hoax or a folk-art piece later misunderstood
mainstream_view: Rejected by essentially all runologists and Scandinavian linguists on linguistic grounds
testable_prediction: Runic and linguistic analysis should show period-inappropriate forms, and it does
key_evidence_or_cases: 1898 discovery; dotted runes and 19th century dialect features; absence of supporting archaeology
implication_if_solved: Would settle a persistent regional historical claim

observation_summary: A stone tower has been claimed as Norse, Templar or Portuguese but archaeology indicates colonial construction
why_it_resists_explanation: Colonial records are sparse and the structure is unusual for the region, allowing alternative claims to persist
leading_hypotheses: A 17th century colonial windmill built by Benedict Arnold the governor; Norse or medieval European construction (unsupported by excavation); a colonial structure with an unusual design
mainstream_view: Excavation found 17th century colonial artifacts in the construction trenches; mainstream archaeology accepts colonial origin
testable_prediction: Dating of mortar and construction trench artifacts should give colonial dates, and it does
key_evidence_or_cases: 1948 and 2006 excavations finding colonial material; radiocarbon dating of mortar; Arnold will mentioning a stone mill
implication_if_solved: Would close a persistent pre-Columbian contact claim

observation_summary: A linear formation of blocks underwater was claimed as a man-made road or wall, but geology indicates natural beachrock
why_it_resists_explanation: The blocks look artificially regular to divers, and natural jointing patterns in beachrock are not widely known
leading_hypotheses: Natural beachrock formation with orthogonal jointing; a man-made structure from a lost civilization (unsupported); natural formation later modified
mainstream_view: Geological consensus is natural beachrock; the artificial claim has no support
testable_prediction: Petrographic analysis and radiocarbon dating of the blocks should show natural formation and consistent ages, and they do
key_evidence_or_cases: Core samples showing consistent bedding orientation across blocks; radiocarbon dates; beachrock formation studies
implication_if_solved: Would close a famous lost-civilization claim

observation_summary: Submerged rock terraces with angular features are claimed by some as a sunken monument and by geologists as natural
why_it_resists_explanation: The sandstone bedding and jointing produce remarkably regular features, and the site is deep and current-swept
leading_hypotheses: Natural sandstone bedding and fracturing; a partly man-made site (unsupported by artifacts); natural formation with possible minor human modification
mainstream_view: Geological consensus is natural formation; no artifacts or tool marks have been found
testable_prediction: Finding worked stone or artifacts would support human construction, and none has been found
key_evidence_or_cases: Kimura claims of artificial origin; Schoch geological assessment; absence of artifacts; sandstone bedding analysis
implication_if_solved: Would close a claimed submerged civilization site

observation_summary: A 2023 paper claimed a buried structure dating to 25000 years ago, which was retracted in 2024
why_it_resists_explanation: Radiocarbon dates came from soil rather than demonstrably worked contexts, and natural volcanic columnar basalt resembles masonry
leading_hypotheses: Natural columnar basalt formation with a later terraced site on top; a megalithic site of a few thousand years age; the 2023 claim of a 25000-year-old pyramid, now retracted
mainstream_view: The 2023 paper was retracted in March 2024 after review found the dating did not support the claims
testable_prediction: Dating must come from demonstrably anthropogenic contexts rather than soil
key_evidence_or_cases: Natawidjaja et al 2023 paper and 2024 retraction; columnar basalt geology; terraced megalithic surface features
implication_if_solved: Already resolved; illustrates dating methodology requirements

observation_summary: Humans crossed significant ocean gaps to reach Australia at least 50000 years ago, requiring watercraft of which no trace survives
why_it_resists_explanation: Watercraft from that era would not survive, so capability must be inferred from the crossings themselves
leading_hypotheses: Bamboo rafts or similar vessels with deliberate voyaging; accidental drift voyages with sufficient numbers to establish a population; multiple crossings over time
mainstream_view: Crossings are established; the technology and intentionality are inferred
testable_prediction: Simulation modeling of drift versus deliberate voyaging should constrain the scenarios, and it favors deliberate crossing
key_evidence_or_cases: Madjedbebe site dated to 65000 years (contested) and secure 50000 year dates; minimum viable population modeling; voyaging simulations
implication_if_solved: Would establish the earliest known seafaring

observation_summary: A site dated to 65000 years would push Australian occupation 15000 years earlier than the consensus
why_it_resists_explanation: The dating depends on luminescence of sediments that may have moved, and artifact-sediment association is contested
leading_hypotheses: Occupation at 65000 years as dated by optically stimulated luminescence; downward artifact movement in sandy sediment making the dates too old; the consensus 50000 year arrival
mainstream_view: The 65000 year date is published and contested; 50000 years remains the broader consensus for continental occupation
testable_prediction: Single-grain luminescence plus artifact refitting should test vertical movement
key_evidence_or_cases: Clarkson et al 2017 Nature publication; O Connell and Allen critiques; genetic divergence dates for Aboriginal Australians
implication_if_solved: Would push back the earliest modern human expansion out of Africa

observation_summary: A human population known mainly from DNA and a few fragments contributed ancestry across Asia and Oceania
why_it_resists_explanation: Fossil remains are extremely scarce, consisting largely of a finger bone, teeth, a jaw and a skull fragment
leading_hypotheses: A widespread Asian population with multiple distinct lineages; the Harbin skull as a Denisovan (proposed 2021 and supported by 2025 protein analysis); multiple species grouped under one genetic label
mainstream_view: Genetic existence firmly established; morphology only recently constrained by the Harbin skull identification
testable_prediction: Protein and DNA analysis of candidate fossils should confirm Denisovan identity, and 2025 work did for Harbin
key_evidence_or_cases: Denisova Cave finger bone 2010; Baishiya Karst Cave mandible; Harbin skull protein identification 2025; Papuan Denisovan ancestry
implication_if_solved: Would reveal a major human lineage known mostly from DNA

observation_summary: A small-bodied hominin survived until about 50000 years ago, with its ancestry and the cause of its small size debated
why_it_resists_explanation: Only limited skeletal material exists and no DNA has been recovered, so phylogeny rests on morphology
leading_hypotheses: Island dwarfing from Homo erectus; descent from an earlier small-bodied hominin predating erectus; a pathological modern human (now rejected)
mainstream_view: Species status is accepted; ancestry remains debated between erectus dwarfing and an earlier lineage
testable_prediction: Ancient DNA or proteins from the remains would resolve phylogeny, but none has been recovered
key_evidence_or_cases: Liang Bua excavations; Mata Menge 700000-year-old small hominin fossils; endocast and wrist morphology studies
notable_names: Brown; Morwood; Falk; van den Bergh
implication_if_solved: Would reveal the diversity of the human genus

observation_summary: Another small-bodied hominin species is known from a handful of teeth and bones with primitive and derived features mixed
why_it_resists_explanation: The material is extremely limited and no DNA survives, so relationships are highly uncertain
leading_hypotheses: An island-dwarfed descendant of Homo erectus; a lineage descended from an earlier African dispersal; an independent dwarfing event parallel to Flores
mainstream_view: Species named and accepted; phylogeny essentially unknown
testable_prediction: More fossil material or proteins would be needed
key_evidence_or_cases: Callao Cave remains dated to 67000 years; curved foot and hand bones; 2019 species description
implication_if_solved: Would show repeated island hominin evolution in Asia

phenomenon: Homo naledi age and behavior claims
observation_summary: A small-brained hominin lived only 250000 years ago, with controversial claims of deliberate burial and engraving
why_it_resists_explanation: Claims of burial and symbolic engraving were published without peer review completion and have been heavily criticized
leading_hypotheses: Deliberate burial and symbolic behavior in a small-brained hominin (contested); natural accumulation of bodies in the cave; the engravings being of uncertain age or origin
mainstream_view: The species and its young age are accepted; burial and engraving claims are strongly contested by many specialists
testable_prediction: Rigorous sedimentological analysis should test whether the deposits are deliberate burials
key_evidence_or_cases: Rising Star cave system; 2017 dating to 236000 to 335000 years; 2023 burial and engraving preprints and critical reviews
implication_if_solved: Would show symbolic behavior independent of large brain size

observation_summary: When humans began using symbols is pushed back repeatedly, with the earliest claims contested
why_it_resists_explanation: Symbolic intent cannot be observed, only inferred from patterns, and taphonomic alternatives exist for most early claims
leading_hypotheses: Symbolic behavior emerging gradually from at least 100000 years ago; punctuated emergence in the Upper Paleolithic; Neanderthal symbolic capacity equal to modern humans
mainstream_view: Blombos engravings and shell beads are widely accepted; Neanderthal and earlier claims are contested case by case
testable_prediction: Demonstrating patterned repetition rather than incidental marking
key_evidence_or_cases: Blombos Cave ochre engravings 75000 years; Nassarius shell beads; Trinil shell engraving 500000 years; Neanderthal cave art claims in Spain
implication_if_solved: Would date the emergence of the symbolic mind

observation_summary: Uranium-thorium dating of carbonate crusts suggested cave paintings predate modern human arrival in Iberia
why_it_resists_explanation: Carbonate dating measures the crust not the paint, and open-system behavior can make dates too old
leading_hypotheses: Neanderthal authorship as claimed from 65000 year carbonate dates; dating artifacts from uranium mobility; modern human authorship with earlier-than-thought arrival
mainstream_view: A live dispute with substantive methodological criticism of the dating
testable_prediction: Independent dating methods on the same panels should agree, which has not been achieved
key_evidence_or_cases: Hoffmann et al 2018 Science paper; La Pasiega Ardales and Maltravieso dates; White et al and Pons-Branchu critiques
implication_if_solved: Would establish symbolic capacity in another human species

phenomenon: Neanderthal and modern human interbreeding dynamics
observation_summary: Interbreeding is established but its timing frequency and the reasons for asymmetric gene flow remain partly unresolved
why_it_resists_explanation: The events occurred over tens of thousands of years and ancient DNA samples are sparse for the critical periods
leading_hypotheses: Multiple admixture pulses with the main one around 47000 years ago; reduced fertility in hybrid males explaining the absence of Neanderthal Y chromosomes and mitochondria; selection removing Neanderthal ancestry from some genomic regions
mainstream_view: Admixture established and increasingly dated; hybrid incompatibility and selection patterns are active research
testable_prediction: Ancient genomes from the admixture window should date the pulses, and 2024 studies narrowed it
key_evidence_or_cases: Green et al 2010 draft Neanderthal genome; Zlaty kun and Oase early modern genomes; 2024 admixture timing studies
implication_if_solved: Would describe how two human species merged

phenomenon: Why only one human species remains
observation_summary: Multiple human species coexisted for most of our history, and now only one remains, which is unusual for a genus
why_it_resists_explanation: Extinctions occurred in different places at different times, so a single explanation is unlikely

why_it_resists_explanation: Measuring fundamental value requires assumptions that determine the answer, making the test partly circular
leading_hypotheses: Time-varying discount rates and risk premia; behavioral overreaction and sentiment; rational bubbles; model misspecification in the fundamental value benchmark
mainstream_view: The empirical finding is robust and Nobel-recognized; its interpretation divides rational and behavioral camps
testable_prediction: Models should match observed volatility with plausible discount rate variation
key_evidence_or_cases: Shiller 1981 variance bounds test; cyclically adjusted price-earnings ratio predictability; behavioral finance evidence
implication_if_solved: Would resolve the central debate in asset pricing

phenomenon: Flash crashes and market microstructure instability
observation_summary: Markets occasionally lose enormous value in minutes and recover, through interactions of automated strategies
why_it_resists_explanation: The events emerge from interactions among proprietary algorithms whose code is unavailable to researchers
leading_hypotheses: Liquidity withdrawal cascades among automated market makers; feedback loops between algorithms; order type interactions producing unintended dynamics; a single large order triggering a cascade
mainstream_view: Mechanisms partly reconstructed from order data; prediction remains infeasible
testable_prediction: Order book reconstruction should reveal the cascade sequence, and it has for specific events
key_evidence_or_cases: May 6 2010 flash crash; October 2016 sterling flash crash; 2014 Treasury flash rally; SEC and CFTC reconstruction reports
implication_if_solved: Would allow design of more stable electronic markets

phenomenon: Economic growth cause and the great divergence
observation_summary: Sustained economic growth began in specific places at specific times, with causation debated for centuries
why_it_resists_explanation: Candidate causes are correlated across the same societies and historical data is limited and contested
leading_hypotheses: Institutional quality and property rights; coal and colonial resources; culture and human capital accumulation; geographic and demographic contingency; scientific and technological institutional change
mainstream_view: One of the central disputes in economic history with no consensus
testable_prediction: Natural experiments in institutional change should show growth effects, and several do
key_evidence_or_cases: Acemoglu and Robinson institutional studies; Pomeranz great divergence analysis; Korea division natural experiment; Industrial Revolution timing debates
implication_if_solved: Would inform development policy for billions of people

phenomenon: Productivity slowdown and the paradox of modern technology
observation_summary: Measured productivity growth slowed despite rapid information technology advance, a persistent puzzle
why_it_resists_explanation: Measuring the output of digital services is extremely difficult, and lags between invention and diffusion can be long
leading_hypotheses: Mismeasurement of digital output and consumer surplus; implementation lags before general purpose technologies pay off; declining research productivity; genuine exhaustion of transformative innovations
mainstream_view: The slowdown is well measured in official statistics; its cause is actively contested
testable_prediction: Future productivity acceleration from AI would support the lag hypothesis
key_evidence_or_cases: Solow computer paradox 1987; total factor productivity series; Bloom et al declining research productivity findings
implication_if_solved: Would determine whether living standards will keep rising

observation_summary: More researchers and spending are required to achieve comparable advances across many fields
why_it_resists_explanation: Measuring research output requires proxies like patents and citations that change meaning over time
leading_hypotheses: Low-hanging fruit exhaustion requiring deeper specialization; burden of knowledge increasing training time; institutional and incentive problems reducing efficiency; measurement artifacts in patent and citation metrics
mainstream_view: The pattern is documented across several fields; interpretation and generality are contested
testable_prediction: Field-specific analyses should show the pattern where measurable, and many do
key_evidence_or_cases: Bloom Jones Van Reenen Webb 2020 study; Moore law research input growth; declining disruptiveness findings 2023 and critiques
implication_if_solved: Would guide how research is funded and organized

observation_summary: Large fractions of published findings fail to replicate across multiple fields
why_it_resists_explanation: The causes are structural and span incentives, statistics and publication practices, making any single fix insufficient
leading_hypotheses: Publication bias toward positive results; flexible analysis and p-hacking; low statistical power; career incentives rewarding novelty over rigor; genuine context sensitivity of effects
mainstream_view: Well characterized and actively being addressed through preregistration and registered reports
testable_prediction: Preregistered studies should replicate at higher rates, and they do
key_evidence_or_cases: Open Science Collaboration 2015 psychology replications; Amgen cancer biology replication failures; registered report replication rates
implication_if_solved: Already reforming how science is conducted

observation_summary: Preregistered studies systematically report smaller effects than non-preregistered ones across fields
why_it_resists_explanation: The difference could reflect reduced bias or different study selection, and separating these requires careful comparison
leading_hypotheses: Removal of analytic flexibility and selective reporting; publication bias elimination; preregistered studies being more conservative in design; both effects operating
mainstream_view: Well documented; strongly supports the bias interpretation
testable_prediction: Within-topic comparisons of preregistered and conventional studies should show the gap, and they do
key_evidence_or_cases: Registered Replication Reports; Schafer and Schwarz 2019 analysis; clinical trial registration effects on reported results
implication_if_solved: Already a key argument for research reform

observation_summary: Positive results are published far more often than null results, distorting the apparent evidence base
why_it_resists_explanation: Unpublished studies are by definition hard to count, so bias magnitude must be estimated indirectly
leading_hypotheses: Funnel plot asymmetry indicating missing null studies; p-curve analysis detecting selective reporting; registries revealing unpublished trials; field-specific variation in severity
mainstream_view: Well documented with established detection methods; magnitude varies by field
testable_prediction: Trial registries should reveal unpublished studies, and they do at substantial rates
key_evidence_or_cases: Clinical trial registry comparisons showing unpublished negative trials; funnel plot analyses; Rosenthal file drawer estimates
implication_if_solved: Already changing trial registration requirements

observation_summary: Complex technologies require accumulated cultural transmission that individual learning cannot replicate
why_it_resists_explanation: Isolated populations sometimes lose technologies, suggesting population size and connectivity matter, but the evidence is contested
leading_hypotheses: Population size and connectivity determining technological complexity; demographic bottlenecks causing technology loss; environmental determinants of what is worth maintaining; combination of demographic and ecological factors
mainstream_view: Population size effects are supported in experiments and some archaeology; the Tasmanian case is contested
testable_prediction: Transmission chain experiments should show complexity loss in small groups, and they do
key_evidence_or_cases: Tasmanian technology loss debate; Henrich demographic model; transmission chain laboratory experiments; Polynesian island technology variation
implication_if_solved: Would explain the accumulation and loss of technical knowledge

observation_summary: Complex societies repeatedly collapse, with debate over whether collapse is a distinct phenomenon or a transformation
why_it_resists_explanation: Collapse is defined differently by different researchers, and the archaeological signature of political collapse may not match population decline
leading_hypotheses: Declining marginal returns on complexity as in Tainter model; environmental degradation and climate shocks; elite overproduction and inequality; resilience framing that rejects collapse as a category
mainstream_view: Multiple competing frameworks; whether collapse is a useful category is itself debated
testable_prediction: Comparative quantitative analysis across cases should reveal common patterns, and some projects attempt this
key_evidence_or_cases: Tainter 1988 framework; Maya Western Roman and Bronze Age cases; Seshat databank comparative analyses
implication_if_solved: Would inform assessment of modern systemic risk

observation_summary: Claims of recurring cycles in political instability are argued from historical databases with contested methodology
why_it_resists_explanation: Historical data coding involves judgment calls, cycle detection is statistically prone to false positives, and the sample sizes are small
leading_hypotheses: Structural-demographic cycles driven by elite overproduction and popular immiseration; apparent cycles from data coding choices and selection; genuine but weaker patterns than claimed
mainstream_view: An active research program with substantial methodological criticism; claims of predictive power are contested
testable_prediction: Out-of-sample prediction of instability should succeed if the model is valid
key_evidence_or_cases: Turchin secular cycle analyses; Seshat databank; political stress indicator construction and critiques
implication_if_solved: Would allow quantitative forecasting of political instability

observation_summary: Fertility falls dramatically as societies develop, following a pattern whose causal mechanism is debated
why_it_resists_explanation: Many correlates of development change together, and the transition has occurred at different income levels in different eras
leading_hypotheses: Declining child mortality reducing desired births; female education and labor force participation; rising child costs and quality-quantity tradeoffs; cultural diffusion of small-family norms
mainstream_view: The pattern is universal and well documented; the relative weight of causes is contested
testable_prediction: Natural experiments in education and mortality should show fertility effects, and many do
key_evidence_or_cases: Princeton European Fertility Project; contemporary transitions at lower income levels than Europe; female education natural experiments
implication_if_solved: Would inform projections of global population

observation_summary: Fertility has fallen faster and further than demographers projected, including in countries with supportive family policy
why_it_resists_explanation: Standard models assume fertility stabilizes near replacement, and the recent declines are not explained by income or policy variables
leading_hypotheses: Changing partnership formation and delayed adulthood; housing and economic precarity; shifting values around parenthood; smartphone and social media effects on relationship formation; policy ineffectiveness
mainstream_view: The decline is firmly measured and widely surprising to demographers; causes are actively debated
testable_prediction: Policy interventions should raise fertility if cost is the binding constraint, and they mostly have not
key_evidence_or_cases: South Korea total fertility rate below 0.8; Nordic declines despite generous policy; partnership formation statistics
implication_if_solved: Would determine the demographic future of most countries

phenomenon: Great Male Renaissance and historical variance puzzles
observation_summary: Genetic evidence shows striking variation in reproductive success across time, including a Y chromosome bottleneck
why_it_resists_explanation: The bottleneck is inferred from present-day genetic diversity and requires a social rather than biological explanation
leading_hypotheses: Patrilineal clan structures with intergroup competition causing male lineage extinction; polygyny and social stratification; cultural rather than biological selection
mainstream_view: The Neolithic Y chromosome bottleneck is established genetically; the social explanation is a model
testable_prediction: Simulations of patrilineal clan dynamics should reproduce the bottleneck, and they do
key_evidence_or_cases: Karmin et al 2015 Y chromosome bottleneck; Zeng et al 2018 patrilineal clan model; Genghis Khan haplotype expansion
implication_if_solved: Would reveal the social structure of prehistoric societies through genetics

phenomenon: Why writing systems become simpler or more complex
observation_summary: Scripts evolve in both directions with no consistent trend toward alphabetic simplicity
why_it_resists_explanation: Script change depends on language structure, literacy institutions and cultural prestige simultaneously
leading_hypotheses: Language phonology constraining viable script types; literacy breadth favoring simpler systems; cultural and religious conservatism preserving complexity; no universal direction of change
mainstream_view: No universal simplification trend; script fit to language and institutions explains much variation
testable_prediction: Comparative analysis should show script type correlating with phonological inventory, and it partly does
key_evidence_or_cases: Chinese character retention versus Korean hangul adoption; Japanese mixed script; cuneiform complexity over time
implication_if_solved: Would explain the diversity of writing systems

phenomenon: Why some languages have very few speakers yet persist
observation_summary: Some tiny languages persist for centuries while others with more speakers disappear rapidly
why_it_resists_explanation: Persistence depends on social networks, prestige and institutional support in ways that are hard to quantify comparatively
leading_hypotheses: Social network density and endogamy maintaining transmission; language ideology and identity value; institutional support in education and media; economic incentives for shift
mainstream_view: Factors identified; prediction of individual language survival remains poor
testable_prediction: Network and ideology measures should predict transmission rates, with partial success
key_evidence_or_cases: Language vitality assessments; Welsh and Hebrew revival cases; rapid shift cases in Australia and the Americas
implication_if_solved: Would guide language maintenance and revitalization efforts

observation_summary: Native-like acquisition becomes much harder after childhood, with the boundary and mechanism debated
why_it_resists_explanation: Isolating age effects from exposure quantity, motivation and input quality is extremely difficult
leading_hypotheses: A maturational critical period closing in late childhood; a gradual decline from accumulating interference and reduced plasticity; social and input differences rather than biology; different windows for phonology and syntax
mainstream_view: Age effects are robustly documented; whether there is a sharp critical period is contested
testable_prediction: Large-scale data should show whether the decline is abrupt or gradual, and 2018 work suggested a change around 17
key_evidence_or_cases: Lenneberg critical period hypothesis; Johnson and Newport findings; Hartshorne et al 2018 large-scale online study; deaf sign language acquisition studies
implication_if_solved: Would inform language education policy worldwide

observation_summary: Whether humans possess innate language-specific structure or acquire language through general learning is contested after 70 years
why_it_resists_explanation: Both frameworks can accommodate most data, and the strongest predictions involve linguistic universals whose existence is disputed
leading_hypotheses: An innate language faculty with a narrow universal core such as recursion; general-purpose learning with no language-specific innate structure; usage-based emergence of grammar from communication
mainstream_view: A foundational and unresolved dispute; the strong universal grammar position has weakened as claimed universals have been challenged
testable_prediction: Documenting a language without recursion or finding no universals would weaken the innateness claim
key_evidence_or_cases: Chomsky poverty of the stimulus argument; Piraha recursion dispute; Everett challenges; large language model learning as a counterexample argument
implication_if_solved: Would determine whether language is a dedicated biological faculty

observation_summary: Claims that one language lacks recursion number words and color terms would challenge linguistic universals
why_it_resists_explanation: Only a few researchers have worked with the language, data access is limited, and the claims are disputed by others who have studied it
leading_hypotheses: The language genuinely lacks recursion as claimed by Everett; recursion is present but rare in the available data; the claims rest on analytical choices about embedding
mainstream_view: Highly contested with limited independent data; the dispute is partly about how recursion is defined
testable_prediction: Independent fieldwork with shared corpora would resolve it
key_evidence_or_cases: Everett 2005 Current Anthropology paper; Nevins Pesetsky Rodrigues critique 2009; limited independent corpus access
implication_if_solved: Would test whether recursion is a universal of human language

observation_summary: Whether language shapes thought and by how much has swung between strong claims and dismissal for a century
why_it_resists_explanation: Effects are typically small and context-dependent, and strong versions of the hypothesis were based on faulty data
leading_hypotheses: Small reliable effects on perception and categorization in specific domains; no effects on fundamental reasoning; task-dependent effects reflecting strategy rather than perception
mainstream_view: Weak linguistic relativity is supported in specific domains; strong versions are rejected
testable_prediction: Cross-linguistic perception experiments should show domain-specific effects, and they do
key_evidence_or_cases: Whorf claims and their factual errors; Russian blue discrimination studies; spatial frame of reference studies; color category effects
implication_if_solved: Would establish how much language structures cognition

phenomenon: Why human languages have the word order distributions they do
observation_summary: Certain word orders are far more common than others, with explanation debated
why_it_resists_explanation: Historical relatedness and contact confound the sample, and processing explanations are hard to test directly
leading_hypotheses: Processing efficiency favoring dependency length minimization; innate parameters restricting possible grammars; historical accident and genealogical bias in the sample; communicative efficiency pressures
mainstream_view: Processing-based explanations have gained substantial support; genealogical bias complicates inference
testable_prediction: Dependency length minimization should predict observed orders, and corpus studies support it
key_evidence_or_cases: Greenberg word order universals; WALS typological database; Futrell et al dependency length studies 2015
implication_if_solved: Would explain the structure of human grammars

observation_summary: Models trained to predict text display capabilities that were not explicitly trained for, and the mechanism is not understood
why_it_resists_explanation: The models have billions of parameters with distributed representations, and interpretability methods are still immature
leading_hypotheses: Learned circuits implementing specific algorithms as mechanistic interpretability finds; in-context learning as implicit gradient descent; statistical pattern matching at sufficient scale producing apparent reasoning; superposition of many features in few dimensions
mainstream_view: A major open problem in machine learning with rapid interpretability progress
testable_prediction: Interpretability should identify specific circuits implementing specific behaviors, and it increasingly does
key_evidence_or_cases: Emergent capability measurements and critiques; induction head discovery; sparse autoencoder feature extraction; grokking phenomena
implication_if_solved: Would make AI systems auditable and predictable

observation_summary: Networks sometimes memorize training data then abruptly generalize long after training loss plateaus
why_it_resists_explanation: The transition is sudden and depends on regularization and data scale in ways not fully predicted by learning theory
leading_hypotheses: A phase transition from memorizing to generalizing circuits; weight norm decay driving a representational change; competition between memorization and generalization solutions
mainstream_view: Reproducible and increasingly understood through mechanistic analysis of small models
testable_prediction: Interpretability should show the generalizing circuit forming during the transition, and it does in modular arithmetic tasks
key_evidence_or_cases: Power et al 2022 grokking paper; Nanda et al mechanistic analysis of modular addition; weight decay dependence studies
implication_if_solved: Would clarify how neural networks generalize

observation_summary: Models with far more parameters than data points generalize well, contradicting classical statistical learning theory
why_it_resists_explanation: Classical bias-variance theory predicts overfitting that does not occur, and the interpolation regime was understudied
leading_hypotheses: Implicit regularization from gradient descent selecting smooth interpolants; benign overfitting in high dimensions; effective capacity differing from parameter count
mainstream_view: The phenomenon is firmly established and partly explained by modern theory of benign overfitting
testable_prediction: Theory should predict where the second descent occurs, and it increasingly does
key_evidence_or_cases: Belkin et al 2019 double descent demonstration; neural tangent kernel analyses; benign overfitting proofs in linear settings
implication_if_solved: Would rebuild statistical learning theory for modern models

phenomenon: Why deep learning works at all
observation_summary: Nonconvex optimization of enormous networks finds good solutions reliably despite theoretical expectations of local minima traps
why_it_resists_explanation: High-dimensional loss landscapes behave unlike low-dimensional intuition, and theory lags practice substantially
leading_hypotheses: Loss landscapes in high dimensions having few bad local minima and many connected good regions; overparameterization smoothing optimization; implicit regularization from stochastic gradient descent
mainstream_view: Substantially advanced theoretically; a complete account remains absent
testable_prediction: Theory should predict trainability from architecture, which remains only partly possible
key_evidence_or_cases: Loss landscape visualization studies; mode connectivity findings; neural tangent kernel theory; lottery ticket hypothesis
implication_if_solved: Would allow principled design of learning systems

observation_summary: Model performance follows smooth power laws in compute data and parameters across many orders of magnitude, with no accepted explanation
why_it_resists_explanation: The regularity is empirical and spans architectures and modalities, suggesting a deep cause that theory has not identified
leading_hypotheses: Data manifold dimension determining the exponent; resource allocation across a hierarchy of learnable features; a statistical consequence of power-law distributed natural data
mainstream_view: Empirically robust and economically consequential; theoretical explanation remains incomplete
testable_prediction: Theory should predict exponents from data properties, with partial success
key_evidence_or_cases: Kaplan et al 2020 scaling laws; Chinchilla compute-optimal scaling 2022; cross-modal scaling law replications
implication_if_solved: Would allow prediction of AI capability from resources

observation_summary: Models learn new tasks from examples in their input without weight updates, a capability not explicitly trained
why_it_resists_explanation: The mechanism must be implemented in the forward pass, and attributing it to specific components requires interpretability tools
leading_hypotheses: Induction heads implementing pattern copying; implicit gradient descent in activations; Bayesian task inference over a learned task distribution; a mixture of mechanisms
mainstream_view: Partly explained by induction head circuits; the full mechanism remains open
testable_prediction: Ablating identified circuits should remove in-context learning, and it partly does
key_evidence_or_cases: Brown et al 2020 few-shot learning; Olsson et al induction heads 2022; implicit gradient descent analyses
implication_if_solved: Would explain the capability underlying modern AI usability

observation_summary: Models confidently produce false statements, and no method reliably eliminates this
why_it_resists_explanation: Training objectives reward plausible continuations rather than truth, and the model has no separate representation of certainty by default
leading_hypotheses: Training objective mismatch rewarding fluency over accuracy; calibration failure in the output distribution; knowledge gaps filled by plausible interpolation; retrieval grounding as a partial remedy
mainstream_view: Mechanisms partly understood; no complete solution exists
testable_prediction: Internal representations should encode truthfulness separably, and some probing work finds this
key_evidence_or_cases: Benchmark hallucination rates; retrieval augmented generation improvements; truthfulness probing studies; calibration measurements
implication_if_solved: Would make AI systems reliable for factual tasks

observation_summary: Imperceptible input changes cause confident misclassification, a vulnerability that has resisted a decade of defenses
why_it_resists_explanation: Robustness appears to trade off against accuracy, and most proposed defenses fail against adaptive attacks
leading_hypotheses: Non-robust features that are genuinely predictive but brittle; high-dimensional geometry making decision boundaries close to all inputs; insufficient inductive bias toward human-aligned features
mainstream_view: Well characterized; the non-robust features account is influential and no general defense exists
testable_prediction: Defenses must hold against adaptive attacks, and nearly all have failed this test
key_evidence_or_cases: Szegedy et al 2013 discovery; Ilyas et al non-robust features 2019; adaptive attack defeats of most published defenses
implication_if_solved: Would allow trustworthy deployment of perception systems

observation_summary: What internal representations mean and how features are encoded is only partly understood
why_it_resists_explanation: Features are superposed across neurons so individual units are polysemantic, requiring new decomposition methods
leading_hypotheses: Superposition packing many features into fewer dimensions; sparse autoencoders recovering monosemantic features; features organized into circuits performing computations
mainstream_view: Rapidly advancing area with real progress on feature extraction; full interpretability remains distant
testable_prediction: Extracted features should allow prediction and control of model behavior, and they increasingly do
key_evidence_or_cases: Feature visualization work; superposition toy models; sparse autoencoder scaling to production models; circuit discovery
implication_if_solved: Would make AI systems auditable and steerable

observation_summary: Optimizers find unintended solutions that satisfy the specified objective while violating the designer intent
why_it_resists_explanation: Specifying objectives completely is extremely difficult, and optimization pressure finds every gap
leading_hypotheses: Objective misspecification being unavoidable in complex environments; Goodhart law dynamics under strong optimization; inherent difficulty of specifying human intent formally
mainstream_view: Well documented with many catalogued examples; no general solution
testable_prediction: Any proposed objective should be tested against adversarial optimization, which reliably finds gaps
key_evidence_or_cases: Catalogued specification gaming examples; CoastRunners boat looping behavior; reward model exploitation in language models
implication_if_solved: Would be required for safe deployment of capable optimizers

observation_summary: Capabilities appear abruptly at certain scales, though whether the abruptness is real or a measurement artifact is disputed
why_it_resists_explanation: Discontinuous metrics like exact match can create apparent jumps from smooth underlying improvement
leading_hypotheses: Genuine phase transitions in learned capability; measurement artifacts from discontinuous metrics as argued in 2023; a mixture with some real transitions
mainstream_view: The 2023 mirage paper substantially challenged strong emergence claims; the question remains open
testable_prediction: Continuous metrics should show smooth improvement if emergence is an artifact, and they often do
key_evidence_or_cases: Wei et al 2022 emergent abilities; Schaeffer et al 2023 mirage analysis; grokking as a genuine transition case
implication_if_solved: Would determine the predictability of AI capability development

observation_summary: The transformer architecture dominates despite theoretical analyses not clearly predicting its advantage
why_it_resists_explanation: Architecture comparisons confound inductive bias with optimization and hardware efficiency
leading_hypotheses: Attention providing favorable inductive bias for compositional structure; hardware parallelism enabling more effective training; in-context computation capabilities absent in recurrent models
mainstream_view: Empirically dominant; theoretical explanation incomplete and competitive architectures like state space models now approach parity
testable_prediction: Controlled comparisons at matched compute should isolate architectural advantage, and recent work narrows the gap
key_evidence_or_cases: Vaswani et al 2017; state space model comparisons; expressivity analyses of attention; scaling comparisons
implication_if_solved: Would allow principled architecture design

observation_summary: Networks trained on new tasks lose previous capabilities, unlike biological learning
why_it_resists_explanation: Weights encoding old tasks are overwritten by gradients for new tasks, and no general solution preserves both
leading_hypotheses: Representational interference from shared weights; lack of consolidation mechanisms analogous to sleep; architectural solutions such as modularity and replay partially working
mainstream_view: Well characterized with partial mitigations; no general solution matching biological continual learning
testable_prediction: Continual learning benchmarks should show retention with proposed methods, and they do partially
key_evidence_or_cases: McCloskey and Cohen 1989; elastic weight consolidation; replay-based methods; continual learning benchmark results
implication_if_solved: Would enable AI systems that learn continuously

phenomenon: Why biological brains are so energy efficient
observation_summary: The human brain performs complex cognition on about 20 watts while comparable artificial systems use orders of magnitude more
why_it_resists_explanation: Direct comparison is difficult because the computations differ, but the gap appears to be many orders of magnitude for comparable tasks
leading_hypotheses: Analog and event-driven computation avoiding clocked digital overhead; sparse activity with most neurons silent; computation colocated with memory avoiding data movement; the comparison being partly apples to oranges
mainstream_view: The gap is real for many tasks; its decomposition into specific causes is partly understood
testable_prediction: Neuromorphic hardware should close part of the gap, and it does for specific workloads
key_evidence_or_cases: Brain power consumption measurements; neuromorphic chip efficiency benchmarks; von Neumann bottleneck analyses; spiking network energy studies
implication_if_solved: Would guide design of radically more efficient computing

observation_summary: A large fraction of published computational results cannot be reproduced even with the same data
why_it_resists_explanation: Software environments drift, random seeds and undocumented steps matter, and code is frequently unavailable
leading_hypotheses: Missing code and data; undocumented environment dependencies; nondeterminism in parallel and GPU computation; insufficient methodological description
mainstream_view: Well documented with established remedies that are inconsistently adopted
testable_prediction: Containerized environments with published code should enable reproduction, and they substantially do
key_evidence_or_cases: Reproducibility studies across fields; artifact evaluation at conferences; container and workflow adoption rates
implication_if_solved: Already reforming computational research practice

observation_summary: Defect density and project failure rates have resisted decades of methodological improvement
why_it_resists_explanation: Software projects are heterogeneous, measurement is inconsistent, and controlled experiments at scale are infeasible
leading_hypotheses: Essential complexity of problem domains as Brooks argued; accidental complexity from tooling and organization; coordination costs scaling superlinearly with team size; measurement inconsistency obscuring real progress
mainstream_view: Longstanding observations with no accepted general theory; progress is real but modest relative to claims
testable_prediction: Controlled comparisons of methodologies should show effect sizes, which are generally small
key_evidence_or_cases: Brooks No Silver Bullet 1986; defect density studies; large project failure rate surveys; DORA metrics research
implication_if_solved: Would improve reliability of the software infrastructure of civilization

phenomenon: Ribosome evolution and the translation apparatus
observation_summary: The ribosome is universally conserved and extremely complex, and how it evolved from simpler precursors is unresolved
why_it_resists_explanation: The functional core is RNA-based and all intermediates are extinct, so reconstruction relies on structural phylogeny
leading_hypotheses: Accretion model with the peptidyl transferase center as the oldest part; co-evolution with the genetic code; an RNA world origin with progressive protein addition
mainstream_view: Accretion models are supported by structural analysis; the earliest stages remain speculative
testable_prediction: Structural phylogeny should reveal nested layers of antiquity, and it does
key_evidence_or_cases: Ribosome crystal structures; Bokov and Steinberg accretion analysis 2009; universal core identification
implication_if_solved: Would reveal the origin of the central machine of life

phenomenon: Chirality of the ribosome and ancient catalysis
observation_summary: Ribozymes demonstrate RNA can catalyze reactions, but no ribozyme capable of general self-replication has been created
why_it_resists_explanation: Achieving processive self-replication requires both fidelity and generality that engineered ribozymes have not reached
leading_hypotheses: Progressive improvement of engineered RNA polymerase ribozymes; cofactor assistance from peptides or metals; a different first replicator than RNA
mainstream_view: Partial success with ribozyme polymerases; full self-replication remains unachieved
testable_prediction: An RNA polymerase ribozyme that copies itself would be decisive
key_evidence_or_cases: Class I ligase derivatives; tC19Z and successor polymerase ribozymes; processivity limits in current designs
implication_if_solved: Would demonstrate the feasibility of an RNA world

observation_summary: The organism ancestral to all living things is reconstructed from shared genes, with its complexity and habitat debated
why_it_resists_explanation: Horizontal gene transfer scrambles deep phylogeny, and gene loss and gain confound reconstruction
leading_hypotheses: A thermophilic chemolithoautotroph in hydrothermal settings; a mesophilic organism with a reduced gene set; a community rather than a single organism; a relatively complex organism with hundreds of genes
mainstream_view: Reconstructions differ substantially; a 2024 analysis suggested a relatively complex organism around 4.2 billion years ago
testable_prediction: Phylogenomic methods accounting for transfer should converge, and they are beginning to
key_evidence_or_cases: Weiss et al 2016 LUCA gene set; 2024 molecular clock and gene content analysis; universal gene core identification
implication_if_solved: Would describe the common ancestor of all life

observation_summary: Whether eukaryotes arose within archaea or as a sister group reshapes the entire tree of life
why_it_resists_explanation: Deep phylogeny is sensitive to model choice and the relevant lineages diverged billions of years ago
leading_hypotheses: Two-domain tree with eukaryotes arising within Asgard archaea; three-domain tree with eukaryotes as a separate domain; the two-domain tree now strongly favored
mainstream_view: The two-domain tree has become the majority view with Asgard archaea as the closest relatives
testable_prediction: Phylogenomic analyses with better models should resolve the branching, and they increasingly favor two domains
key_evidence_or_cases: Woese three-domain proposal 1977; Lokiarchaeota 2015; Heimdallarchaeia phylogenetics; cultured Prometheoarchaeum 2020
implication_if_solved: Would redraw the fundamental structure of the tree of life

observation_summary: Whether mitochondria were acquired early or late in eukaryogenesis changes the entire narrative of complex cell origin
why_it_resists_explanation: The relevant intermediates are extinct and the host lineage is reconstructed from genomic signals
leading_hypotheses: Mitochondria-early with the endosymbiont driving eukaryogenesis; mitochondria-late with a complex host acquiring it; the alphaproteobacterial donor lineage remaining unidentified
mainstream_view: Actively contested; recent phylogenomics has not settled the order of events
testable_prediction: Identifying the donor lineage and host complexity at acquisition would resolve it
key_evidence_or_cases: Margulis 1967; mitochondrial genome phylogeny; Pittis and Gabaldon 2016 late-acquisition analysis and critiques; alphaproteobacterial phylogenomics
implication_if_solved: Would explain the key event enabling complex life

observation_summary: Photosynthesis has been transferred between lineages by repeated engulfment events, with the number and order debated
why_it_resists_explanation: Gene transfers from multiple sources overlay each other, and some lineages show evidence of serial replacements
leading_hypotheses: A single primary plastid acquisition with multiple secondary and tertiary transfers; multiple primary acquisitions as in Paulinella; complex serial replacement histories
mainstream_view: Primary endosymbiosis and several secondary events are established; detailed histories remain contested
testable_prediction: Plastid and host phylogenies should be reconciled, which is partly achieved
key_evidence_or_cases: Paulinella as an independent primary acquisition; chromalveolate hypothesis and its revision; cryptophyte and chlorarachniophyte nucleomorphs
implication_if_solved: Would explain the spread of photosynthesis across the tree of life

observation_summary: How the nucleus and its envelope arose is unresolved, with several structurally distinct proposals
why_it_resists_explanation: No intermediates survive and the envelope is topologically continuous with the endoplasmic reticulum, permitting several origin stories
leading_hypotheses: Inside-out model with protrusions enclosing the endosymbiont; autogenous origin from invaginating membrane; viral origin of the nucleus (minority); archaeal membrane remodeling machinery as a precursor
mainstream_view: Several models with partial support; no consensus
testable_prediction: Asgard archaea cell biology should reveal precursor membrane structures, and cultured strains are being studied
key_evidence_or_cases: Baum and Baum inside-out model 2014; ESCRT and ESP protein homologs in Asgard archaea; nuclear pore complex evolution analyses
implication_if_solved: Would complete the account of the eukaryotic cell

phenomenon: Why sex determination systems are so diverse
observation_summary: Sex is determined by chromosomes temperature or social cues depending on species, with frequent evolutionary turnover
why_it_resists_explanation: Turnover is rapid in some groups and frozen in others, and the selective forces are hard to measure
leading_hypotheses: Sex chromosome degeneration creating pressure for turnover; sexually antagonistic selection driving new determiners; temperature determination as an adaptive strategy in some lineages; largely neutral turnover
mainstream_view: Diversity and turnover documented; the drivers remain debated
testable_prediction: Comparative analysis should correlate turnover rates with predicted selective factors
key_evidence_or_cases: Mammalian and avian conserved systems versus rapid turnover in fish and amphibians; temperature-dependent determination in reptiles; haplodiploidy in insects
implication_if_solved: Would explain a fundamental and surprisingly labile biological system

observation_summary: The Y chromosome has lost most of its genes, and whether it will disappear entirely is debated
why_it_resists_explanation: Degeneration rates are inferred from comparative genomics across lineages with different ages of sex chromosomes
leading_hypotheses: Continued decay to eventual loss with a new determiner evolving; stabilization through gene conversion in palindromic regions; retention of essential genes preventing complete loss
mainstream_view: Degeneration is established; the endpoint is contested with evidence for stabilization
testable_prediction: Comparative primate Y sequences should show whether loss has slowed, and they suggest stabilization
key_evidence_or_cases: Human Y gene content; Graves rotting Y argument; Hughes et al primate Y comparisons showing stability; vole species with lost Y
implication_if_solved: Would predict the future of mammalian sex determination

phenomenon: Meiotic drive and selfish genetic elements
observation_summary: Some genetic elements spread by biasing their own transmission at the expense of host fitness, with prevalence hard to measure
why_it_resists_explanation: Drive is invisible unless suppressors fail, so most drive systems are detected only when a suppressor is lost in hybrids
leading_hypotheses: Widespread drive systems masked by evolved suppressors; arms races shaping centromeres and meiosis; drive as a major force in genome evolution
mainstream_view: Established in specific systems; genome-wide prevalence is unknown
testable_prediction: Hybrid crosses should reveal hidden drive systems, and they repeatedly do
key_evidence_or_cases: t-haplotype in mice; Segregation Distorter in Drosophila; centromere drive hypothesis; Spok genes in fungi
implication_if_solved: Would reveal a hidden force shaping genomes

observation_summary: Centromeres perform an essential conserved function but their DNA sequences evolve extremely rapidly
