why_it_resists_explanation: The function is epigenetically specified by a histone variant rather than sequence, which permits sequence turnover
leading_hypotheses: Epigenetic specification by CENP-A allowing sequence divergence; centromere drive arms races driving rapid change; satellite DNA expansion through replication slippage
mainstream_view: The epigenetic specification resolves much of the paradox; drive dynamics remain under study
testable_prediction: Neocentromere formation should be possible at non-centromeric sequences, and it is
key_evidence_or_cases: Rapid satellite sequence divergence between species; CENP-A epigenetic marking; human neocentromeres; centromere drive model
implication_if_solved: Would explain how essential functions tolerate rapid sequence change

observation_summary: What fraction of the human genome is functional is contested, with estimates ranging from a few percent to most of it
why_it_resists_explanation: Function is defined differently by biochemical activity versus evolutionary conservation versus phenotypic consequence
leading_hypotheses: Most of the genome being non-functional with transcription being biochemical noise; widespread regulatory function as ENCODE claimed; function depending entirely on the definition used
mainstream_view: The ENCODE 80 percent functional claim was heavily criticized; conservation-based estimates of under 15 percent are widely favored
testable_prediction: Conservation and deletion experiments should identify function, and large deletions are often tolerated
key_evidence_or_cases: ENCODE 2012 claims and Graur critiques; mouse megabase deletion experiments; conserved fraction estimates; C-value paradox
implication_if_solved: Would determine how much of our genome matters

phenomenon: Genome size variation and the C-value paradox
observation_summary: Genome size varies 60000-fold across eukaryotes with no correlation to organismal complexity
why_it_resists_explanation: Genome size is affected by transposon activity, polyploidy and deletion rates that vary independently of complexity
leading_hypotheses: Transposable element proliferation balanced by deletion; effective population size determining tolerance of junk DNA; nucleotype effects where genome size affects cell size and development; selection on cell size in some lineages
mainstream_view: The paradox is resolved in principle by distinguishing gene number from genome size; the determinants of size remain partly open
testable_prediction: Population genetic models should predict genome size from effective population size, and they partly do
key_evidence_or_cases: Lungfish and salamander genomes exceeding 100 gigabases; Utricularia compact genomes; Lynch mutational hazard hypothesis
implication_if_solved: Would explain why genomes are the sizes they are

observation_summary: Mobile elements make up large fractions of genomes and are suppressed by systems whose evolutionary arms races are ongoing
why_it_resists_explanation: Elements and suppressors coevolve rapidly, and most elements in a genome are inactive remnants
leading_hypotheses: piRNA and small RNA silencing systems; DNA methylation and heterochromatin suppression; domestication of elements for host functions; an ongoing arms race with periodic bursts
mainstream_view: Mechanisms well characterized; the dynamics of bursts and the triggers remain open
testable_prediction: Disabling silencing should cause element mobilization, and it does
key_evidence_or_cases: McClintock discovery of transposition; piRNA pathway characterization; LINE-1 activity in humans; element domestication examples such as RAG1
implication_if_solved: Would explain a major force in genome evolution and disease

observation_summary: Hundreds of regions evolved rapidly in humans after separating from chimpanzees, mostly non-coding, with functions largely unknown
why_it_resists_explanation: They are regulatory rather than protein coding, so effects require developmental assays rather than sequence comparison
leading_hypotheses: Regulatory changes affecting brain development; a mixture of positive selection and biased gene conversion creating false signals; enhancer changes with subtle developmental effects
mainstream_view: Regions identified; functions established for only a handful
testable_prediction: Enhancer reporter assays and organoid models should reveal functions, and they are beginning to
key_evidence_or_cases: HAR1 and HACNS1 characterization; Pollard et al 2006 identification; organoid functional testing; GC-biased gene conversion critiques
implication_if_solved: Would identify the genetic changes that made humans human

observation_summary: Brain size tripled in under three million years at enormous metabolic cost, with the selective driver and genetic basis incompletely known
why_it_resists_explanation: The selective environment cannot be reconstructed directly, and brain size involves many genes with small effects
leading_hypotheses: Social brain hypothesis with group size driving cognition; ecological intelligence for foraging and tool use; cooking and dietary quality permitting metabolic cost; cultural accumulation creating selection for learning ability
mainstream_view: The increase is firmly documented; the driver remains contested among several hypotheses
testable_prediction: Comparative analyses should correlate brain size with predicted ecological or social variables
key_evidence_or_cases: Endocranial volume series; ARHGAP11B and NOTCH2NL human-specific genes; expensive tissue hypothesis; cooking hypothesis
implication_if_solved: Would explain the defining feature of human evolution

phenomenon: Human brain size decrease in the Holocene
observation_summary: Human brain size appears to have decreased somewhat over the last 10000 to 30000 years, a claim recently disputed
why_it_resists_explanation: Sample sizes are small, body size changed too, and a 2021 claim of a very recent decrease was rebutted
leading_hypotheses: Reduction accompanying body size decrease; increased neural efficiency with no cognitive loss; externalization of information storage in culture; the decrease being a sampling artifact as 2022 critiques argue
mainstream_view: A modest decrease since the Pleistocene is reported by several studies; the 2021 claim of a 3000-year-ago decrease was rebutted in 2022
testable_prediction: Larger well-dated cranial samples controlling for body size would settle it
key_evidence_or_cases: Henneberg analyses; DeSilva et al 2021 claim; Villmoare and Grabowski 2022 rebuttal; body size scaling corrections
implication_if_solved: Would reveal whether human cognition is still evolving

phenomenon: Great ape and human cognitive differences
observation_summary: Which cognitive capacities are uniquely human is repeatedly revised as ape abilities are better tested
why_it_resists_explanation: Testing requires methods valid across species, and apes underperform on tasks designed around human communication conventions
leading_hypotheses: Shared cognition with differences in social learning and cumulative culture; uniquely human capacities in shared intentionality and language; methodological artifacts underestimating ape abilities
mainstream_view: Many claimed human-unique capacities have been found in apes; cumulative culture and shared intentionality remain candidate differences
testable_prediction: Matched-methods testing across species should identify genuine differences, and it narrows the list
key_evidence_or_cases: Theory of mind task results in chimpanzees; Tomasello shared intentionality studies; ape numerical and memory abilities exceeding humans in some tasks
implication_if_solved: Would define what is actually distinctive about human cognition

observation_summary: Which animals have subjective experience cannot be determined by any agreed test, with enormous ethical implications
why_it_resists_explanation: Consciousness is private, and behavioral and neural markers are proxies whose validity across very different nervous systems is unknown
leading_hypotheses: Consciousness requiring specific cortical structures limiting it to vertebrates; widespread sentience including invertebrates with centralized nervous systems; graded consciousness across taxa; no reliable test currently exists
mainstream_view: An active and consequential question; the 2024 New York Declaration asserted a realistic possibility of consciousness in all vertebrates and many invertebrates
testable_prediction: Behavioral markers such as trace conditioning and flexible goal-directed behavior should correlate with neural complexity
key_evidence_or_cases: Cambridge Declaration 2012; New York Declaration on Animal Consciousness 2024; cephalopod and insect pain behavior studies; fish nociception research
implication_if_solved: Would determine the moral status of most animals

observation_summary: Whether insects experience pain rather than merely detecting damage is unresolved and increasingly consequential given insect farming
why_it_resists_explanation: Behavioral criteria developed for vertebrates may not transfer, and insect nervous systems are organized very differently
leading_hypotheses: Nociception without subjective pain; genuine pain experience supported by motivational tradeoffs and wound tending in some species; graded sentience varying across insect orders
mainstream_view: Increasingly taken seriously; evidence of nociceptive sensitization in flies and tradeoff behavior in bees
testable_prediction: Motivational tradeoff experiments should show pain-like weighting of damage against reward, and bee studies report this
key_evidence_or_cases: Drosophila nociceptive sensitization studies; bumblebee tradeoff experiments 2022; Gibbons et al 2022 evidence review across insect orders
implication_if_solved: Would determine welfare obligations for trillions of farmed insects

observation_summary: Whether fish feel pain has been debated for two decades with substantial evidence on both sides
why_it_resists_explanation: Fish lack a neocortex which some argue is necessary, while behavioral evidence of pain-like responses is substantial
leading_hypotheses: Nociception with pain-like behavioral responses indicating experience; absence of the neural substrate thought necessary for conscious pain; alternative neural architectures supporting experience
mainstream_view: The majority position has shifted toward fish feeling pain; a vocal minority disputes this on neuroanatomical grounds
testable_prediction: Analgesic administration should change motivated behavior, and it does in several species
key_evidence_or_cases: Sneddon trout nociceptor studies; Rose neuroanatomical critiques; analgesic effects on behavior; zebrafish place preference studies
implication_if_solved: Would affect welfare standards for trillions of fish

observation_summary: Plants respond to anesthetics by losing responsiveness, an unexpected parallel with animals
why_it_resists_explanation: The mechanism of anesthetic action is itself unresolved in animals, so the parallel is suggestive rather than explanatory
leading_hypotheses: Common membrane or ion channel targets of anesthetics across kingdoms; disruption of electrical signaling in plants; coincidental effects on unrelated systems
mainstream_view: The phenomenon is reproducible; its significance is contested and does not imply plant sentience
testable_prediction: Identifying shared molecular targets would explain the parallel
key_evidence_or_cases: Yokawa et al 2018 anesthetic effects on Venus flytrap and Mimosa; electrical signaling suppression measurements
implication_if_solved: Would illuminate the general mechanism of anesthesia

observation_summary: General anesthetics affect organisms without nervous systems including plants and protozoa
why_it_resists_explanation: If anesthetics act on consciousness-generating networks, their effects on cells without networks require another explanation
leading_hypotheses: Conserved membrane or protein targets present across kingdoms; nonspecific membrane effects at high concentrations; different mechanisms producing superficially similar immobility
mainstream_view: A real cross-kingdom phenomenon that complicates network-level theories of anesthesia
testable_prediction: Identifying conserved molecular targets would unify the observations
key_evidence_or_cases: Protozoan and plant anesthetic responses; mitochondrial effects of anesthetics; lipid raft and membrane ordering studies
implication_if_solved: Would clarify what anesthetics actually do

phenomenon: Mechanism of lithium and other old drugs
observation_summary: Several widely used drugs including lithium metformin aspirin and paracetamol have incompletely understood mechanisms
why_it_resists_explanation: These drugs have many molecular targets, and identifying which mediates the therapeutic effect requires selective tools that do not exist
leading_hypotheses: Multiple targets contributing jointly; a single unidentified primary target; the therapeutic effect emerging from network-level changes rather than one interaction
mainstream_view: A recognized and somewhat embarrassing feature of pharmacology for several blockbuster drugs
testable_prediction: Selective agents for each candidate target should reproduce or fail to reproduce the effect
key_evidence_or_cases: Paracetamol mechanism still debated after 130 years; metformin AMPK-independent effects; lithium multiple targets; aspirin beyond COX inhibition
implication_if_solved: Would allow improvement of widely used medicines

observation_summary: One of the most used drugs in the world has no settled mechanism after 130 years
why_it_resists_explanation: It is a weak COX inhibitor peripherally yet effective centrally, and several candidate pathways are hard to isolate in humans
leading_hypotheses: Central COX inhibition especially COX-2 in the brain; AM404 metabolite acting on cannabinoid and TRPV1 systems; serotonergic descending pathway modulation; multiple mechanisms combined
mainstream_view: A standing puzzle in pharmacology; the AM404 metabolite pathway has gained support
testable_prediction: Blocking the AM404 pathway should abolish analgesia, which animal studies support
key_evidence_or_cases: Weak peripheral COX inhibition; AM404 metabolite identification; TRPV1 knockout mouse studies; cannabinoid antagonist blockade experiments
implication_if_solved: Would allow safer analgesics with the same efficacy

phenomenon: Why metformin has broad health effects
observation_summary: A cheap diabetes drug is associated with reduced cancer and mortality risk through mechanisms not established
why_it_resists_explanation: Observational associations may reflect confounding, and the drug has multiple molecular targets
leading_hypotheses: AMPK activation and mitochondrial complex I inhibition; gut microbiome mediated effects; growth signaling suppression reducing cancer risk; confounding by indication in observational studies
mainstream_view: Diabetes efficacy established; broader benefits are promising but confounded in observational data
testable_prediction: The TAME randomized trial of metformin for aging outcomes would test the broader claims
key_evidence_or_cases: UK Prospective Diabetes Study outcomes; observational cancer incidence associations; AMPK mechanism studies; planned TAME trial
implication_if_solved: Would establish or refute the first anti-aging drug

observation_summary: Statins reduce cardiovascular events somewhat more than their cholesterol lowering alone appears to explain
why_it_resists_explanation: Separating lipid-lowering from other effects requires comparing drugs with the same lipid effect and different mechanisms
leading_hypotheses: Anti-inflammatory effects independent of cholesterol lowering; endothelial function improvement; plaque stabilization; the effects being fully explained by LDL lowering after all
mainstream_view: Mostly attributed to LDL lowering; residual pleiotropic contributions remain debated
testable_prediction: Drugs achieving identical LDL reduction by other mechanisms should have identical outcomes, which PCSK9 trials largely support
key_evidence_or_cases: JUPITER trial with CRP reduction; PCSK9 inhibitor outcome trials; Mendelian randomization of LDL variants
implication_if_solved: Would clarify whether cholesterol lowering is the whole story

observation_summary: Long-term aspirin use is associated with reduced colorectal cancer incidence through an incompletely understood mechanism
why_it_resists_explanation: Effects appear after years of use, requiring very long trials, and bleeding risk complicates net benefit assessment
leading_hypotheses: COX-2 inhibition reducing tumor-promoting inflammation; platelet-mediated effects on circulating tumor cells; effects on specific tumor genotypes such as PIK3CA mutants
mainstream_view: The effect is established in trial follow-up; mechanism and patient selection remain open
testable_prediction: Genotype-stratified trials should show effects in specific tumor subtypes, and observational data supports this
key_evidence_or_cases: Pooled trial follow-up showing reduced colorectal cancer; CAPP2 trial in Lynch syndrome; PIK3CA mutation interaction studies
implication_if_solved: Would enable targeted chemoprevention

observation_summary: Exercise reduces risk of almost every chronic disease through mechanisms that are only partly identified
why_it_resists_explanation: The effects are systemic and involve many tissues and signaling molecules simultaneously
leading_hypotheses: Myokine signaling from muscle to other organs; mitochondrial biogenesis and metabolic flexibility; anti-inflammatory effects; improved vascular function; combination of many mechanisms
mainstream_view: Benefits firmly established; the full mechanistic account remains incomplete
testable_prediction: Identified myokines should reproduce some benefits when administered, with partial success
key_evidence_or_cases: Morris bus driver studies 1953; irisin and other myokine discoveries and controversies; exercise mimetic drug research
implication_if_solved: Would allow pharmacological capture of exercise benefits

phenomenon: Why caloric restriction extends lifespan in some species
observation_summary: Reducing calories extends lifespan in many organisms but the effect varies by species and genotype
why_it_resists_explanation: Primate studies take decades and the two major studies gave different results due to differing control diets
leading_hypotheses: Nutrient sensing pathways including mTOR and sirtuins mediating the effect; reduced growth signaling; a response to perceived scarcity that is not universal; dietary composition mattering more than calories
mainstream_view: Robust in rodents and invertebrates; primate results are mixed and human effects are unestablished
testable_prediction: Intervention testing programs should show consistent effects across strains, and they show genotype dependence
key_evidence_or_cases: McCay 1935 rat studies; Wisconsin and NIA primate studies with different outcomes; ITP mouse strain variation; CALERIE human trial
implication_if_solved: Would identify intervention targets for human healthspan

locus: Specific regions claimed to have exceptional longevity
observation_summary: Claims of extreme longevity clusters have been substantially undermined by analysis of record-keeping errors
why_it_resists_explanation: Age records in these regions are often unreliable, and pension fraud and clerical error inflate apparent longevity
leading_hypotheses: Genuine moderate longevity advantages from diet and social factors; age record errors and pension fraud inflating the claims; selective reporting of favorable cases
mainstream_view: Substantially challenged: a 2024 analysis showed strong correlation between claimed longevity and poor record keeping
testable_prediction: Document verification should confirm ages, and it frequently fails to
key_evidence_or_cases: Newman 2024 analysis of age record reliability; Okinawa and Sardinia data; pension fraud investigations in Italy and Japan
implication_if_solved: Would correct widely promoted health advice based on faulty data

observation_summary: A large fraction of claimed extreme ages fail documentary verification, distorting longevity research
why_it_resists_explanation: Birth records from the 19th century are often missing or inconsistent, and incentives exist to overstate age
leading_hypotheses: Age exaggeration and record errors explaining most unvalidated claims; a small number of genuine supercentenarians; systematic bias in regions with poor record keeping
mainstream_view: Well recognized in demography; validated cases are far fewer than claimed ones
testable_prediction: Independent document verification should confirm ages, and it eliminates most claims
key_evidence_or_cases: Gerontology Research Group validation standards; rejected claims from several regions; Calment case verification and challenges
implication_if_solved: Would place longevity research on reliable data

phenomenon: Why height increased then stalled in developed countries
observation_summary: Average height rose dramatically for a century then plateaued, with the plateau mechanism uncertain
why_it_resists_explanation: Height depends on nutrition, disease burden and genetics interacting during growth, and the plateau could reflect a genetic ceiling or saturated environment
leading_hypotheses: Environmental saturation with nutrition and disease no longer limiting; approach to a genetic potential ceiling; changing population composition through migration; obesity and dietary quality effects
mainstream_view: The trend and plateau are well documented; the mechanism of the plateau is debated
testable_prediction: Continued improvement in developing countries should continue until saturation, and it does
key_evidence_or_cases: NCD Risk Factor Collaboration height data; Dutch and Scandinavian plateaus; height heritability estimates around 0.8
implication_if_solved: Would indicate whether environmental limits to growth have been reached

observation_summary: Puberty is starting earlier, especially in girls, by about three months per decade with no agreed cause
why_it_resists_explanation: Multiple candidate exposures changed together, and puberty assessment methods have changed over time
leading_hypotheses: Rising childhood obesity advancing puberty; endocrine disrupting chemical exposure; improved nutrition and reduced infection burden; psychosocial stress effects; measurement changes contributing
mainstream_view: The trend is well documented including a further acceleration after 2020; causes remain contested
testable_prediction: Cohort studies with measured exposures should identify the drivers
key_evidence_or_cases: Breast development onset data across cohorts; 2020 meta-analysis of trends; post-pandemic acceleration reports; obesity correlation studies
implication_if_solved: Would address a change with health and social consequences for children

observation_summary: Short-sightedness has risen to affect 80 to 90 percent of young adults in parts of East Asia within two generations
why_it_resists_explanation: Candidate causes including near work and outdoor time are correlated, and the mechanism linking light exposure to eye growth is partly known
leading_hypotheses: Insufficient outdoor light exposure failing to inhibit axial elongation; intensive near work and education; genetic susceptibility interacting with environment; dopamine-mediated growth signaling
mainstream_view: Outdoor time is established as protective in trials; the dopaminergic mechanism is supported in animals
testable_prediction: Outdoor time interventions should reduce incidence, and randomized trials show they do
key_evidence_or_cases: Taiwan and Singapore prevalence data; outdoor time randomized trials in China; animal form deprivation myopia models; atropine trials
implication_if_solved: Would prevent a major global cause of visual impairment

observation_summary: Obesity rates tripled since 1975 faster than genetics can explain, with the dominant driver contested
why_it_resists_explanation: Many dietary and lifestyle factors changed simultaneously, and food intake measurement in free-living people is unreliable
leading_hypotheses: Ultraprocessed food availability increasing energy intake; carbohydrate and insulin driven fat storage; reduced physical activity; food environment and portion sizes; microbiome and environmental chemical contributions
mainstream_view: Energy surplus is established; which environmental changes drive it and the role of food processing are actively debated
testable_prediction: Controlled feeding trials should show which food properties drive overconsumption, and ultraprocessed food trials do
key_evidence_or_cases: NHANES prevalence trends; Hall et al 2019 ultraprocessed food controlled feeding trial; carbohydrate-insulin model debates
implication_if_solved: Would guide policy affecting a billion people

observation_summary: People eat about 500 more calories per day on ultraprocessed diets matched for macronutrients, by unclear mechanisms
why_it_resists_explanation: The category is defined by processing rather than composition, and many properties covary including texture, energy density and palatability
leading_hypotheses: Energy density and eating rate allowing more intake before satiety; hyperpalatability overriding satiety signals; reduced protein density triggering compensatory eating; additives affecting the microbiome or appetite signaling
mainstream_view: The intake effect is established by controlled trials; the mechanism is genuinely open
testable_prediction: Isolating individual properties in controlled trials should identify the driver, and studies are underway
key_evidence_or_cases: Hall et al 2019 NIH inpatient crossover trial; eating rate measurements; protein leverage hypothesis tests; NOVA classification debates
implication_if_solved: Would allow reformulation of the food supply

phenomenon: Set point and body weight regulation
observation_summary: Body weight is defended against change by powerful mechanisms, and why the defended level drifts upward is unclear
why_it_resists_explanation: Weight regulation involves many redundant signals, and the defended level appears to be settable upward but not easily downward
leading_hypotheses: Leptin resistance raising the defended level; hypothalamic inflammation from diet; a settling point determined by environment rather than a fixed set point; adipose tissue expansion changing signaling
mainstream_view: Defense of weight is firmly established; the asymmetry and upward drift remain open
testable_prediction: GLP-1 agonists lower the defended weight, which they appear to do
key_evidence_or_cases: Leptin discovery and resistance; metabolic adaptation after weight loss; GLP-1 receptor agonist efficacy; Biggest Loser follow-up studies
implication_if_solved: Would explain why weight loss is usually temporary without medication

phenomenon: Why GLP-1 agonists have broad effects
observation_summary: Drugs developed for diabetes reduce weight cardiovascular events kidney disease and possibly addiction behaviors
why_it_resists_explanation: The receptors are widely distributed including in the brain, and central and peripheral effects are hard to separate in humans
leading_hypotheses: Central appetite and reward signaling through brainstem and hypothalamic receptors; direct cardiovascular and renal effects; weight loss mediating most benefits; anti-inflammatory effects
mainstream_view: Clinical effects well established; mechanistic attribution across pathways is incomplete
testable_prediction: Trials in non-obese patients should separate weight-mediated from direct effects, and some do
key_evidence_or_cases: SELECT cardiovascular outcome trial; FLOW kidney trial; addiction behavior observational signals; central receptor mapping
implication_if_solved: Would guide use of a transformative drug class

observation_summary: Dozens of hormones and neural signals regulate appetite, and how they are integrated into eating decisions is incompletely mapped
why_it_resists_explanation: The system is highly redundant so blocking single signals has little effect, which obscures their individual roles
leading_hypotheses: Hypothalamic and brainstem circuits integrating peripheral signals; redundancy ensuring robustness and complicating study; cortical and reward override of homeostatic signals
mainstream_view: Many signals identified; the integration architecture remains partly unknown
testable_prediction: Circuit-level manipulation should change feeding predictably, and it does in rodents
key_evidence_or_cases: Leptin ghrelin and PYY discoveries; AgRP and POMC neuron circuit mapping; vagal afferent studies; redundancy demonstrated by single knockouts
implication_if_solved: Would enable rational design of appetite therapeutics

phenomenon: Circadian clock entrainment in constant conditions
observation_summary: Internal clocks run near 24 hours in complete darkness, and how the period is set so precisely is only partly explained
why_it_resists_explanation: The clock is a molecular feedback loop whose period depends on many rate constants, yet it is temperature compensated
leading_hypotheses: Transcription-translation feedback loops with delayed negative feedback; temperature compensation through balanced opposing reactions; post-translational mechanisms setting period
mainstream_view: Mechanism substantially identified and Nobel-recognized; temperature compensation remains incompletely explained
testable_prediction: Mutating clock genes should change period predictably, and it does
key_evidence_or_cases: de Mairan plant experiments 1729; period and timeless gene discovery; cyanobacterial KaiABC in vitro oscillator; temperature compensation measurements
notable_names: de Mairan; Konopka; Hall; Rosbash; Young
implication_if_solved: Would allow precise manipulation of biological timing

observation_summary: Some organisms time annual cycles without detectable seasonal cues, implying an endogenous circannual clock
why_it_resists_explanation: Circannual rhythms require years of observation per cycle, making experiments extremely slow
leading_hypotheses: An endogenous circannual timer distinct from the circadian clock; histogenesis-based timing in the pituitary; subtle unidentified environmental cues
mainstream_view: Circannual rhythms are documented in several species; the molecular mechanism is unknown
testable_prediction: Long-term constant-condition experiments should show persistent annual rhythms, and they do in sheep and squirrels
key_evidence_or_cases: Soay sheep circannual rhythms in constant conditions; ground squirrel hibernation timing; pituitary histogenesis model
implication_if_solved: Would reveal a biological timer operating over a year

observation_summary: Several mammals appear to align their bodies with the geomagnetic field when resting or hunting
why_it_resists_explanation: The effects are statistical across many observations and some high-profile claims failed replication
leading_hypotheses: Genuine magnetic alignment serving an unknown function; wind and sun orientation confounds; publication of positive results with failed replications unpublished
mainstream_view: Reported repeatedly with at least one notable failed replication; status genuinely uncertain
testable_prediction: Blinded observation with controlled confounds should confirm alignment, with mixed results
key_evidence_or_cases: Begall et al 2008 cattle alignment from satellite images; Hert et al replication failure 2011; dog defecation alignment study 2013; fox mousing study
implication_if_solved: Would reveal a widespread and unexplained sensory capacity

phenomenon: Homing in domestic animals over long distances
observation_summary: Anecdotal reports of animals traveling long distances to find owners or homes are numerous but poorly documented
why_it_resists_explanation: Most cases are retrospective anecdotes without verification, and selection bias favors reporting successes
leading_hypotheses: Verified pigeon homing using magnetic and olfactory maps; most mammal cases being unverified anecdotes or misidentification; some genuine navigation within familiar range
mainstream_view: Pigeon homing is well established scientifically; long-distance mammal homing anecdotes lack verification
testable_prediction: Controlled displacement experiments with marked animals would test the claim, and few exist
key_evidence_or_cases: Pigeon homing research; Psychical Research anecdote collections; occasional documented cat return cases; absence of controlled studies
implication_if_solved: Would establish whether mammals have navigational maps

phenomenon: Seasonal brain size changes in shrews
observation_summary: Shrew skulls and brains shrink by up to 20 percent in winter and partly regrow in spring
why_it_resists_explanation: Reversible loss of brain tissue contradicts expectations about neural tissue permanence, and the mechanism is unclear
leading_hypotheses: Dehoyos phenomenon from energy saving in a high-metabolism animal; bone and tissue resorption with regrowth; selective loss of specific brain regions with functional consequences
mainstream_view: The phenomenon is firmly documented by repeated measurement of individuals; mechanism and functional costs are open
testable_prediction: Longitudinal imaging of individuals should quantify regrowth, and it has
key_evidence_or_cases: Dehnel 1949 observations; Lazaro et al 2017 longitudinal study of individual shrews; cognitive performance measurements across seasons
implication_if_solved: Would reveal reversible neural plasticity at a gross anatomical scale

observation_summary: Antlers are the fastest growing and only fully regenerating mammalian appendage, regrown annually from a stump
why_it_resists_explanation: Mammals generally cannot regenerate appendages, so the mechanism is of exceptional interest and is only partly characterized
leading_hypotheses: Antler stem cells in the pedicle periosteum driving blastema-like regeneration; hormonal control through testosterone and photoperiod; rapid vascularization and nerve regrowth
mainstream_view: Substantially characterized with stem cell populations identified by 2023 single-cell work
testable_prediction: Transplanting identified stem cells should produce ectopic antler tissue, and it does
key_evidence_or_cases: Growth rates up to 2 cm per day; pedicle periosteum transplantation experiments; 2023 single-cell atlas of antler regeneration
implication_if_solved: Would inform mammalian regenerative medicine

observation_summary: A mammal regenerates skin hair follicles cartilage and kidney tissue without scarring, unlike other mammals
why_it_resists_explanation: Most mammals scar, so the difference must involve specific immune and extracellular matrix differences that are only partly identified
leading_hypotheses: Altered macrophage response reducing fibrosis; different extracellular matrix composition permitting regeneration; conserved regeneration programs reactivated in this lineage
mainstream_view: Phenomenon established; mechanism partly identified with immune differences central
testable_prediction: Transferring the immune phenotype should enable regeneration in mice, with partial success
key_evidence_or_cases: Seifert et al 2012 skin autotomy and regeneration; kidney and heart regeneration reports; macrophage profiling studies
implication_if_solved: Would identify the barrier to mammalian regeneration

observation_summary: Zebrafish fully regenerate 20 percent of their heart within two months, while mammals scar
why_it_resists_explanation: Mammals lose this capacity shortly after birth, so the relevant block is developmental and only partly mapped
leading_hypotheses: Cardiomyocyte dedifferentiation and proliferation; epicardial and endocardial signaling; metabolic state permitting proliferation; immune response differences
mainstream_view: Well characterized in fish; translating to mammals remains unsolved
testable_prediction: Reactivating the proliferative program in mammalian hearts should restore regeneration, with partial success in neonatal mice
key_evidence_or_cases: Poss et al 2002 demonstration; neonatal mouse regeneration window; cardiomyocyte proliferation markers; hypoxia and metabolic manipulation studies
implication_if_solved: Would allow cardiac repair after heart attacks

observation_summary: Mammals scar rather than regenerate, apparently having lost an ancestral capacity
why_it_resists_explanation: Explaining loss requires identifying what mammals gained in exchange, and candidate tradeoffs are hard to test
leading_hypotheses: Tradeoff with cancer suppression since proliferative capacity carries risk; tradeoff with rapid wound closure and infection control in endotherms; tradeoff with homeothermy and metabolic constraints
mainstream_view: Several plausible tradeoff hypotheses; none established
testable_prediction: Species comparisons should show regeneration capacity trading off against cancer rates, with suggestive patterns
key_evidence_or_cases: Comparative regeneration across vertebrates; cancer incidence comparisons; spiny mouse and bat exceptions; neonatal regeneration windows
implication_if_solved: Would identify what must be overcome for human regeneration

observation_summary: Highly regenerative animals might be expected to have high cancer rates but often do not
why_it_resists_explanation: Measuring cancer incidence in wild and non-model animals is difficult, and regeneration and tumor suppression may use shared pathways
leading_hypotheses: Shared control mechanisms allowing both regeneration and tumor suppression; genuinely higher cancer rates in regenerative species that go undetected; no tradeoff with the two being independently evolved
mainstream_view: A plausible but weakly tested hypothesis; data on cancer in regenerative species is sparse
testable_prediction: Systematic cancer surveys in axolotls and planarians should test the tradeoff
key_evidence_or_cases: Low reported cancer rates in axolotls; planarian tumor resistance; zoo animal cancer registries; shared Wnt and Hippo pathway roles
implication_if_solved: Would clarify whether regeneration and cancer control conflict

phenomenon: Hydra and planarian apparent absence of aging
observation_summary: Some animals show no measurable increase in mortality with age over years of observation
why_it_resists_explanation: Demonstrating negligible senescence requires very long cohort studies, and apparent immortality may reflect short observation relative to lifespan
leading_hypotheses: Continuous stem cell renewal replacing all somatic cells; absence of a segregated germline limiting soma disposability; FoxO signaling maintaining stem cell pools
mainstream_view: Negligible senescence is well documented in hydra over multi-year cohorts
testable_prediction: Long-term cohort mortality tracking should show flat mortality rates, and it does
key_evidence_or_cases: Martinez 1998 four-year hydra cohorts; Schaible 2015 eight-year study; FoxO knockdown experiments; planarian asexual lineage age
implication_if_solved: Would show that senescence is not a necessary feature of animal life

observation_summary: Several vertebrates show little or no increase in mortality with age over decades
why_it_resists_explanation: Long-lived species require decades of mark-recapture data, and historical records are often incomplete
leading_hypotheses: Continuous growth and indeterminate maturity reducing senescence; efficient repair and low metabolic damage; protective morphology reducing extrinsic mortality and relaxing selection against longevity
mainstream_view: Established in 2022 for several turtle and tortoise species using long-term datasets
testable_prediction: Mark-recapture mortality analysis should show flat age-specific mortality, and it does for several species
key_evidence_or_cases: Reinke et al 2022 Science study of 77 species; da Silva et al 2022 zoo tortoise analysis; Greenland shark age estimates of 270 to 400 years
implication_if_solved: Would show that vertebrate aging is evolutionarily optional

observation_summary: Greenland sharks live an estimated 270 to 400 years, the longest-lived vertebrates known
why_it_resists_explanation: Ages come from eye lens radiocarbon dating with substantial uncertainty, and the species cannot be studied in captivity
leading_hypotheses: Extremely slow metabolism in cold water extending lifespan; efficient DNA repair; late maturity around 150 years; dating uncertainty inflating estimates
mainstream_view: Extreme longevity accepted with wide confidence intervals; physiology largely unstudied
testable_prediction: Genomic analysis should reveal longevity adaptations, and a 2024 genome assembly began this
key_evidence_or_cases: Nielsen et al 2016 eye lens radiocarbon dating; 2024 genome assembly; growth rate estimates
implication_if_solved: Would identify extreme longevity mechanisms in a vertebrate

phenomenon: Rougheye rockfish and long-lived fish physiology
observation_summary: Several rockfish species live over 200 years with no apparent reproductive senescence
why_it_resists_explanation: Ages come from otolith annuli requiring validation, and the species are deep-dwelling and hard to study
leading_hypotheses: Cold deep water slowing metabolism; genomic adaptations in DNA repair and immune genes identified in 2021; indeterminate growth without senescence
mainstream_view: Longevity validated by otolith and radiometric methods; mechanisms partly identified by comparative genomics
testable_prediction: Comparative genomics across rockfish lifespans should identify longevity genes, and 2021 work did
key_evidence_or_cases: Otolith annuli validation with lead-radium dating; Kolora et al 2021 Science rockfish genomes; butyrophilin immune gene expansion
implication_if_solved: Would identify longevity genes through natural variation

phenomenon: Why some species have no detectable senescence while close relatives do
observation_summary: Lifespan varies enormously between close relatives, allowing comparative identification of longevity mechanisms
why_it_resists_explanation: The comparisons require accurate lifespan data for many species, which is rare outside captivity
leading_hypotheses: Specific genomic adaptations in repair and proteostasis pathways; life history tradeoffs with reproduction; extrinsic mortality shaping selection on maintenance
mainstream_view: A productive comparative approach; mechanisms are being identified lineage by lineage
testable_prediction: Comparative genomics across lifespan-divergent pairs should identify convergent changes, and it increasingly does
key_evidence_or_cases: Bat versus mouse lifespan comparison; naked mole rat versus mouse; rockfish species comparisons; AnAge longevity database
implication_if_solved: Would identify the genetic levers of lifespan

phenomenon: Reproductive senescence absence in some organisms
observation_summary: Some organisms show increasing rather than decreasing fertility with age
why_it_resists_explanation: Documenting this requires lifelong fertility records, and the pattern conflicts with standard life history theory
leading_hypotheses: Indeterminate growth increasing reproductive output with size; negative senescence from size-dependent fitness; selection favoring continued investment in reproduction
mainstream_view: Documented in several taxa; theoretical integration with life history theory is incomplete
testable_prediction: Lifelong fertility tracking should show increasing output with age, and it does in several species
key_evidence_or_cases: Vaupel negative senescence theory; turtle and tortoise fertility records; bristlecone pine seed viability with age
implication_if_solved: Would extend life history theory beyond standard senescence models

phenomenon: Bristlecone pine and extreme plant longevity
observation_summary: Individual trees live over 4800 years with apparently undiminished seed viability and growth
why_it_resists_explanation: Measuring senescence in trees requires comparing young and ancient individuals, and sampling the oldest trees is restricted
leading_hypotheses: Modular growth replacing tissues continuously; absence of a mandatory senescence program in plants; protective growth form and arid environment reducing damage; meristem genetic integrity maintained over millennia
mainstream_view: Longevity established by ring counting; absence of senescence supported by 2001 study of pollen and seed viability
testable_prediction: Comparing physiological performance across tree ages should show no decline, and studies find little
key_evidence_or_cases: Methuselah tree over 4800 years; Lanner and Connor 2001 study finding no senescence; clonal Pando aspen and Old Tjikko
implication_if_solved: Would show indefinite somatic maintenance is possible in multicellular life

observation_summary: Clonal organisms may be thousands of years old and cover square kilometres, raising questions about what counts as an individual
why_it_resists_explanation: Determining clonal identity and age requires genetic mapping and growth rate estimates with wide uncertainty
leading_hypotheses: Genetically identical ramets forming a single individual by some definitions; somatic mutation accumulation creating genetic mosaics; individuality being definition-dependent rather than a natural fact
mainstream_view: Clonal extent is measurable; age estimates are uncertain and individuality is partly definitional
testable_prediction: Genetic mapping should reveal clone boundaries and mutation accumulation, and it does
key_evidence_or_cases: Pando aspen clone of about 43 hectares; Posidonia seagrass clone estimated at 100000 years; Armillaria fungal clones over 9 square kilometres
implication_if_solved: Would clarify what constitutes a biological individual

phenomenon: Somatic mutation accumulation in long-lived organisms
observation_summary: Long-lived organisms accumulate fewer somatic mutations per year than expected, or tolerate them better
why_it_resists_explanation: Measuring somatic mutations requires single-cell or deep sequencing that was only recently feasible
leading_hypotheses: Lower per-year mutation rates in long-lived species as 2022 work found; efficient repair reducing accumulation; tolerance through redundancy and cell replacement; low mutation rates in plant meristems
mainstream_view: Established across mammals in 2022; plant findings suggest very low meristem mutation rates
testable_prediction: Somatic mutation rates should scale inversely with lifespan, and they do
key_evidence_or_cases: Cagan et al 2022 cross-species somatic mutation study; oak and poplar somatic mutation measurements; crypt and skin sequencing
implication_if_solved: Would link mutation accumulation to lifespan determination

phenomenon: Polyploidy and whole genome duplication consequences
observation_summary: Whole genome duplications occur repeatedly and are associated with evolutionary innovation, with mechanisms partly understood
why_it_resists_explanation: Duplications are followed by extensive gene loss over millions of years, obscuring immediate consequences
leading_hypotheses: Gene duplication providing raw material for functional innovation; buffering against deleterious mutations; immediate dosage and meiotic problems requiring resolution; most duplications being evolutionary dead ends
mainstream_view: Well documented in plants and at the base of vertebrates; the link to innovation is correlational
testable_prediction: Comparative genomics should show innovation following duplications, and it does for specific gene families
key_evidence_or_cases: Two rounds of vertebrate genome duplication; teleost fish duplication; angiosperm duplication events; Hox cluster duplications
notable_names: Ohno; Wolfe; Van de Peer; Soltis
implication_if_solved: Would explain a major source of evolutionary novelty

phenomenon: Horizontal gene transfer scale in prokaryotes
observation_summary: Gene transfer between unrelated organisms is so extensive that the concept of a bacterial species is contested
why_it_resists_explanation: Transfer rates vary enormously by gene and environment, and reconstructing history requires separating transfer from inheritance
leading_hypotheses: Pervasive transfer making tree-like phylogeny inappropriate for prokaryotes; a conserved core genome with a fluid accessory genome; species-like clusters maintained by ecological differentiation despite transfer
mainstream_view: Extensive transfer is established; the implications for species concepts remain debated
testable_prediction: Pangenome analyses should show the core-accessory structure, and they do
key_evidence_or_cases: Pangenome analyses across bacterial species; antibiotic resistance gene spread; Doolittle web of life proposals; ecological species cluster evidence
implication_if_solved: Would redefine the species concept for most of life

observation_summary: Whether bacteria form discrete species is contested given pervasive gene transfer and continuous genetic variation
why_it_resists_explanation: Species definitions developed for sexual eukaryotes do not transfer, and operational thresholds are arbitrary
leading_hypotheses: Ecologically differentiated clusters functioning as species; a continuum with arbitrary cutoffs; recombination barriers creating genuine species boundaries in some groups
mainstream_view: An unresolved conceptual problem with practical consequences for taxonomy and medicine
testable_prediction: Population genomic structure should show discrete clusters if species exist, and results vary by group
key_evidence_or_cases: 16S rRNA and average nucleotide identity thresholds; Vibrio ecological population studies; recombination rate analyses across genera
implication_if_solved: Would ground microbial taxonomy and epidemiology

observation_summary: The most abundant photosynthetic organism on Earth was unknown until 1988 and contains enormous cryptic diversity
why_it_resists_explanation: It is extremely small and was missed by conventional microscopy, and its ecotypes are genetically distinct but morphologically identical
leading_hypotheses: Ecotype differentiation along light and nutrient gradients; extreme genome streamlining under nutrient limitation; a vast pangenome distributed across the population
mainstream_view: Well characterized since discovery; the extent of diversity and its ecological structuring remain under study
testable_prediction: Single-cell genomics should reveal ecotype diversity, and it reveals enormous variation
key_evidence_or_cases: Chisholm 1988 discovery by flow cytometry; ecotype depth distributions; single-cell genomic diversity surveys; 10 to the 27 estimated cells globally
implication_if_solved: Would characterize the organism producing much of Earth oxygen

phenomenon: Marine viral abundance and ecological role
observation_summary: Viruses are the most abundant biological entities on Earth and kill a large fraction of marine microbes daily
why_it_resists_explanation: Most marine viruses are uncultured and their hosts unknown, so their ecological effects are estimated indirectly
leading_hypotheses: Viral shunt redirecting carbon from higher trophic levels to dissolved organic matter; kill the winner dynamics maintaining diversity; auxiliary metabolic genes altering host metabolism during infection
mainstream_view: Abundance and importance established; specific host-virus pairings and quantitative effects remain largely unknown
testable_prediction: Metagenomic host prediction plus field measurements should quantify mortality, and they increasingly do
key_evidence_or_cases: Bergh et al 1989 abundance measurements; 10 to the 31 estimated viruses globally; viral shunt carbon flux estimates; Tara Oceans virome data
implication_if_solved: Would quantify a major driver of ocean biogeochemistry

phenomenon: CPR and candidate phyla radiation biology
observation_summary: An enormous group of bacteria with tiny genomes and no cultured representatives was discovered by metagenomics
why_it_resists_explanation: They lack many essential biosynthetic pathways, implying obligate dependence on hosts that have not been identified for most
leading_hypotheses: Obligate episymbiotic lifestyles dependent on other microbes; extreme genome reduction under host dependence; a vast unexplored branch of bacterial diversity
mainstream_view: Existence and genomic characteristics established; biology almost entirely unknown
testable_prediction: Co-culture with candidate hosts should enable growth, which has worked for a few lineages such as Saccharibacteria
key_evidence_or_cases: Brown et al 2015 genomic description; Saccharibacteria episymbiosis with Actinobacteria; CPR representing a large fraction of bacterial diversity
implication_if_solved: Would open a major unexplored branch of life

observation_summary: Archaea with eukaryote-like genes were discovered by metagenomics, and the first cultured representatives have unusual morphology
why_it_resists_explanation: Growth is extremely slow with doubling times of weeks, making experimental work very difficult
leading_hypotheses: Cell biological complexity intermediate between prokaryotes and eukaryotes; eukaryotic signature proteins performing membrane remodeling; protrusion-based engulfment as a eukaryogenesis mechanism
mainstream_view: Cultured in 2020 after 12 years of effort; cell biology now being characterized
testable_prediction: Imaging cultured cells should reveal cytoskeletal and membrane structures, and it has
key_evidence_or_cases: Spang et al 2015 Lokiarchaeota; Imachi et al 2020 Prometheoarchaeum culture; actin and tubulin homolog characterization
implication_if_solved: Would reveal the cellular precursor of eukaryotes

phenomenon: Nitrogen fixation energy cost and evolution
observation_summary: Biological nitrogen fixation is extraordinarily energetically expensive and the enzyme has not been improved by evolution
why_it_resists_explanation: Nitrogenase requires 16 ATP per nitrogen molecule and is oxygen sensitive, constraints that appear not to have been overcome in 2 billion years
leading_hypotheses: Fundamental chemical constraints on breaking the nitrogen triple bond; an evolutionary local optimum that cannot be escaped; oxygen sensitivity as an unavoidable consequence of the active site chemistry
mainstream_view: The cost and oxygen sensitivity are well characterized; whether they are fundamental or contingent is open
testable_prediction: Engineering an oxygen-tolerant or cheaper nitrogenase would show the constraint is contingent, and attempts continue
key_evidence_or_cases: Nitrogenase structure and mechanism; FeMo cofactor chemistry; failed attempts to engineer improved variants; synthetic nitrogen fixation requiring high temperature and pressure
implication_if_solved: Would transform agriculture by enabling cheap biological nitrogen fixation

observation_summary: The most abundant enzyme on Earth is slow and confuses carbon dioxide with oxygen, wasting a large fraction of photosynthetic output
why_it_resists_explanation: Despite enormous selective pressure the enzyme has not been improved, suggesting a fundamental tradeoff
leading_hypotheses: A catalytic tradeoff between specificity and speed that cannot be escaped; an evolutionary local optimum; compensating mechanisms like C4 and CAM photosynthesis evolving instead
mainstream_view: The tradeoff is well characterized; whether it is absolute is debated and engineering efforts continue
testable_prediction: Engineering a faster specific Rubisco would show the tradeoff is not absolute, and attempts have had limited success
key_evidence_or_cases: Photorespiration costs of 20 to 50 percent; C4 evolution over 60 times independently; carboxysome and pyrenoid concentrating mechanisms; engineering attempts
implication_if_solved: Would increase crop yields substantially if overcome

observation_summary: A complex multi-step photosynthetic pathway evolved independently over 60 times, which seems improbable for a complex trait
why_it_resists_explanation: Each evolution required anatomical and biochemical changes together, yet it happened repeatedly, implying an accessible evolutionary path
leading_hypotheses: A stepwise path through intermediate states each individually beneficial; pre-existing anatomical features in some lineages lowering the barrier; declining atmospheric CO2 creating strong selective pressure
mainstream_view: The repeated evolution is firmly documented and the stepwise path is partly reconstructed
testable_prediction: Intermediate C3-C4 species should show viable intermediate states, and they do
key_evidence_or_cases: Over 60 independent origins identified phylogenetically; C3-C4 intermediate species; Oligocene CO2 decline correlation; Flaveria genus intermediates
implication_if_solved: Would guide engineering of C4 traits into rice and wheat

observation_summary: Crassulacean acid metabolism allows nocturnal carbon fixation with high water use efficiency, evolved many times independently
why_it_resists_explanation: The pathway requires coordinated temporal separation of processes, and its repeated evolution and plasticity are only partly explained
leading_hypotheses: Circadian regulation enabling temporal separation; stepwise evolution through facultative CAM; repeated evolution from pre-existing metabolic capacity
mainstream_view: Mechanism well characterized; the repeated evolution and regulatory control are partly explained
testable_prediction: Facultative CAM species should show inducible switching, and they do
key_evidence_or_cases: Nocturnal acidity cycles described in the 1800s; over 30 independent origins; facultative CAM in Mesembryanthemum; engineering efforts in crops
implication_if_solved: Would enable drought-resistant crop engineering

phenomenon: Why photosynthesis uses only visible light
observation_summary: Oxygenic photosynthesis uses a narrow band of the solar spectrum and ignores most infrared energy
why_it_resists_explanation: Longer wavelengths carry insufficient energy per photon to split water, setting a hard physical limit
leading_hypotheses: Photon energy requirement for water oxidation setting a red limit around 700 nanometres; far-red adapted cyanobacteria extending the limit slightly; chlorophyll f and d enabling use beyond 700 nm in some organisms
mainstream_view: Substantially explained by energetics; the discovery of far-red photosynthesis shows the limit is softer than thought
testable_prediction: Organisms using light beyond 750 nanometres for oxygenic photosynthesis should exist, and some do
key_evidence_or_cases: Chlorophyll d in Acaryochloris; chlorophyll f discovery 2010; far-red light photoacclimation; quantum requirement measurements
implication_if_solved: Would set the limits for engineered and extraterrestrial photosynthesis

observation_summary: The manganese cluster that splits water operates through a cycle whose intermediate states are still being resolved
why_it_resists_explanation: The reaction is extremely fast, the cluster is damaged by X-rays during crystallography, and intermediate states are short-lived
leading_hypotheses: A Mn4CaO5 cluster cycling through five S states; specific oxygen-oxygen bond formation mechanism still debated between two proposals; proton-coupled electron transfer coordination
mainstream_view: Structure resolved by X-ray free electron lasers; the oxygen bond formation step remains contested
testable_prediction: Time-resolved serial femtosecond crystallography should capture the intermediates, and it increasingly does
key_evidence_or_cases: Kok cycle S states; 2011 and 2014 XFEL structures; 2023 time-resolved intermediate structures; artificial water splitting catalyst design
implication_if_solved: Would enable efficient artificial photosynthesis

phenomenon: Why life uses only 20 amino acids
observation_summary: Life uses 20 standard amino acids out of hundreds available, with the selection only partly explained
why_it_resists_explanation: The choice may reflect prebiotic availability, functional requirements or historical contingency, which are hard to disentangle
leading_hypotheses: Prebiotic availability determining the early set; functional sufficiency with diminishing returns beyond 20; frozen accident with the code becoming unchangeable; error minimization constraints
mainstream_view: A recognized question with several partial explanations; expanded genetic codes show more are possible
testable_prediction: Engineered organisms with expanded codes should function, and they do
key_evidence_or_cases: Miller-Urey amino acid yields; Murchison meteorite amino acids; synthetic organisms with 21 amino acids; unnatural amino acid incorporation
implication_if_solved: Would explain the chemical composition of all proteins

phenomenon: Why DNA rather than RNA stores genetic information
observation_summary: DNA replaced RNA as the genetic material, with the transition partly explained by stability but details unresolved
why_it_resists_explanation: The transition occurred before the last common ancestor, and the enzymes involved differ between bacteria and archaea
leading_hypotheses: Greater chemical stability of deoxyribose and thymine for long-term storage; separate origins of DNA replication machinery in bacteria and archaea; viral origin of DNA as a modification escaping host defenses
mainstream_view: The stability advantage is clear; the timing and mechanism of transition remain open
testable_prediction: The non-homology of bacterial and archaeal replication machinery should indicate independent origins, and it does
key_evidence_or_cases: Ribonucleotide reductase phylogeny; non-homologous replisomes across domains; RNA degradation rate measurements; viral DNA hypotheses
implication_if_solved: Would illuminate a key transition in early evolution

observation_summary: Cells process information at energy costs that approach but do not reach thermodynamic limits, with the gap unexplained
why_it_resists_explanation: Identifying the relevant computation and its minimum cost requires defining the biological task precisely
leading_hypotheses: Proofreading and error correction costs explaining much of the gap; speed-accuracy-energy tradeoffs; biological systems operating far from the Landauer limit for robustness reasons
mainstream_view: Theoretical framework developing rapidly; biological measurements are limited
testable_prediction: Measuring energy cost per bit in specific biological processes should approach predicted bounds
key_evidence_or_cases: Kinetic proofreading energy costs; Landauer bound comparisons; sensory adaptation energy measurements; ribosome fidelity energetics
implication_if_solved: Would establish the physical limits on biological information processing

observation_summary: Cells achieve accuracy beyond equilibrium thermodynamic limits by expending energy, a general principle whose scope is still being mapped
why_it_resists_explanation: Identifying proofreading in a given system requires measuring energy expenditure and error rates together, which is difficult
leading_hypotheses: Kinetic proofreading operating across replication translation and immune recognition; multiple proofreading stages compounding accuracy; the principle being more general than originally conceived
mainstream_view: A well-established principle with expanding scope
testable_prediction: Energy-dependent accuracy improvement should be measurable in candidate systems, and it is
key_evidence_or_cases: Hopfield and Ninio 1974 and 1975 formulations; DNA polymerase proofreading; T cell receptor discrimination; ribosome fidelity
implication_if_solved: Would explain how biology achieves precision

observation_summary: Binding at one site changes activity at a distant site through mechanisms that resist general prediction
why_it_resists_explanation: Allosteric pathways involve subtle dynamic changes distributed across the structure that static structures do not reveal
leading_hypotheses: Conformational selection among preexisting states as in the MWC model; induced conformational change; dynamic allostery through entropy changes without structural change; combinations varying by protein
mainstream_view: Classical models explain many cases; dynamic allostery and prediction from structure remain open
testable_prediction: Predicting allosteric sites from structure should succeed, which machine learning is beginning to achieve
key_evidence_or_cases: Monod Wyman Changeux model 1965; hemoglobin cooperativity; dynamic allostery in catabolite activator protein; allosteric drug discovery
implication_if_solved: Would enable rational design of allosteric drugs

phenomenon: Protein design and de novo function
observation_summary: Designing proteins with new structures now works well while designing new catalytic functions remains far harder
why_it_resists_explanation: Structure prediction and design became tractable with machine learning, but catalysis requires precise transition state stabilization that design methods capture poorly
leading_hypotheses: Structure design being a simpler problem than function design; catalysis requiring dynamic and electrostatic precision beyond current methods; directed evolution still needed to reach natural rates
mainstream_view: Structure design is substantially solved and Nobel-recognized; functional design lags by orders of magnitude
testable_prediction: Designed enzymes should approach natural catalytic rates, which they currently do not
key_evidence_or_cases: Rosetta and RFdiffusion design successes; designed enzymes orders of magnitude slower than natural; 2024 Nobel Prize for protein design
implication_if_solved: Would enable designed catalysts for arbitrary reactions

observation_summary: Molecular machines convert chemical energy to directed motion with high efficiency through partly understood mechanisms
why_it_resists_explanation: Single-molecule measurements are at the limit of resolution, and the chemomechanical coupling involves sub-nanometre steps
leading_hypotheses: Brownian ratchet mechanisms rectifying thermal motion; power stroke mechanisms with conformational changes; hand-over-hand stepping confirmed for kinesin; dynein mechanism still less clear
mainstream_view: Kinesin and ATP synthase substantially explained; dynein and some others less so
testable_prediction: Single-molecule tracking should resolve the stepping pattern, and it has for kinesin
key_evidence_or_cases: Optical trap measurements; kinesin hand-over-hand demonstration; ATP synthase rotation visualization; cryo-EM dynein structures
implication_if_solved: Would enable design of synthetic molecular machines

phenomenon: Bacterial flagellar motor assembly and switching
observation_summary: The flagellar motor rotates at up to 100000 rpm and switches direction within milliseconds through a mechanism not fully mapped
why_it_resists_explanation: The motor has dozens of components in a membrane-embedded assembly that is difficult to image in action
leading_hypotheses: Conformational switching of the C ring upon CheY binding; stator remodeling under load; torque generation by ion flux through stator units
mainstream_view: Structure increasingly resolved by cryo-EM; switching dynamics partly explained
testable_prediction: Cryo-EM structures in both rotational states should reveal the switch, and recent work approaches this
key_evidence_or_cases: Berg motor characterization; cryo-EM structures of the motor; stator remodeling under load measurements; CheY binding studies
implication_if_solved: Would complete the description of a remarkable biological machine

observation_summary: Bacteria detect concentration gradients of a few percent across their body length, approaching physical limits of detection
why_it_resists_explanation: The measurement is limited by molecular counting noise, and the signaling network must integrate over time optimally
leading_hypotheses: Temporal integration with adaptation implementing near-optimal gradient estimation; receptor clustering amplifying signals; the system operating near the physical limit set by diffusion
mainstream_view: Substantially explained and a model system for biophysical limits
testable_prediction: Measured sensitivity should approach the Berg-Purcell limit, and it does
key_evidence_or_cases: Berg and Purcell 1977 physical limits analysis; receptor cluster cooperativity measurements; single-cell FRET signaling studies
implication_if_solved: Would establish how close biology operates to physical limits

phenomenon: Quorum of transcription factors and gene expression noise
observation_summary: Genetically identical cells in identical conditions express genes at widely varying levels, with functional consequences
why_it_resists_explanation: Noise arises from small molecule numbers and bursty transcription, and distinguishing functional from incidental noise is difficult
leading_hypotheses: Intrinsic noise from stochastic biochemical events in low copy numbers; extrinsic noise from cell-to-cell differences in machinery; noise exploited functionally for bet hedging and differentiation
mainstream_view: Noise sources are well characterized; which noise is functional remains partly open
testable_prediction: Noise reduction should impair bet hedging in variable environments, with supporting evidence
key_evidence_or_cases: Elowitz et al 2002 noise decomposition; transcriptional bursting measurements; bacterial persistence as noise-driven bet hedging
implication_if_solved: Would explain the role of randomness in cellular decisions

phenomenon: Embryonic stem cell state and pluripotency
observation_summary: Pluripotency is maintained by a self-reinforcing network whose stability and exit mechanisms are partly understood
why_it_resists_explanation: The state is metastable and culture conditions strongly affect it, complicating comparisons between studies and species
leading_hypotheses: A core transcription factor network with Oct4 Sox2 and Nanog; chromatin state maintaining competence; metabolic state contributing to pluripotency; distinct naive and primed states
mainstream_view: The core network is established and reprogramming is routine; state transitions and species differences remain open
testable_prediction: Defined conditions should produce uniform states, which they increasingly do
key_evidence_or_cases: Mouse ES cell derivation 1981; Yamanaka reprogramming 2006; naive and primed state characterization; human and mouse state differences
implication_if_solved: Would enable controlled differentiation for therapy

observation_summary: Converting adult cells to pluripotent cells works but with low efficiency and unclear rate-limiting barriers
why_it_resists_explanation: Only a small fraction of cells reprogram, and identifying why most fail requires single-cell trajectory analysis
leading_hypotheses: Stochastic barrier crossing with chromatin state as the limiting factor; deterministic privileged subpopulations; epigenetic memory resisting reprogramming; senescence and p53 barriers
mainstream_view: Reprogramming is routine; the efficiency barrier is partly characterized
testable_prediction: Single-cell trajectory analysis should identify committed and failing paths, and it does
key_evidence_or_cases: Takahashi and Yamanaka 2006; single-cell reprogramming trajectory studies; chemical reprogramming improvements; p53 barrier identification
implication_if_solved: Would make cell therapy scalable

observation_summary: Stem cells self-organize into structures resembling organs but stall at an immature stage with incomplete architecture
why_it_resists_explanation: Vascularization and the full cell type complement are missing, and the signals required are only partly known
leading_hypotheses: Missing vascular supply limiting growth and maturation; absent mechanical and signaling cues from surrounding tissue; incomplete cell type recruitment; intrinsic limits of self-organization without a body plan
mainstream_view: Organoids are powerful and widely used; maturation and vascularization remain the key barriers
testable_prediction: Adding vascular and immune components should improve maturation, and assembloid work supports this
key_evidence_or_cases: Sato and Clevers intestinal organoids; Lancaster cerebral organoids; vascularized organoid and assembloid advances; maturation state comparisons
implication_if_solved: Would enable organ replacement and better disease models

observation_summary: Human development is slowed relative to other primates in ways that may underlie brain expansion
why_it_resists_explanation: Comparing development across species requires matched cell types and timepoints, which is methodologically hard
leading_hypotheses: Species-specific developmental clocks set by biochemical rates; neoteny extending plasticity; metabolic rate differences; segmentation clock period differences measured in vitro
mainstream_view: Species differences in developmental rate are now measurable in vitro; mechanisms are being identified
testable_prediction: Matched in vitro systems should show species-specific rates, and they do
key_evidence_or_cases: Human and mouse segmentation clock period comparisons 2020; neural differentiation rate comparisons; protein degradation rate differences
implication_if_solved: Would explain how developmental timing shapes species differences

observation_summary: Hox genes are arranged on the chromosome in the same order as the body regions they specify, a correspondence with no agreed cause
why_it_resists_explanation: Colinearity is conserved across animals, suggesting a functional requirement, but the mechanism is only partly identified
leading_hypotheses: Sequential chromatin opening across the cluster during development; shared regulatory elements requiring physical arrangement; a frozen ancestral arrangement maintained by regulatory interdependence
mainstream_view: The phenomenon is firmly documented; the mechanistic requirement is partly explained by chromatin dynamics
testable_prediction: Disrupting cluster organization should disrupt patterning, and it does
key_evidence_or_cases: Lewis bithorax studies; Hox cluster organization across phyla; chromatin topology studies during limb development; cluster splitting in some lineages
implication_if_solved: Would explain a striking genome-development correspondence

observation_summary: Embryos reliably break left-right symmetry in a specific direction, through mechanisms that differ across species
why_it_resists_explanation: The initial symmetry breaking happens at a tiny scale and the chirality source must connect molecular handedness to body axis
leading_hypotheses: Nodal cilia creating leftward flow in the node; ion flux and bioelectric asymmetry earlier than cilia; chiral cytoskeletal arrangement providing the initial handedness; species-specific mechanisms
mainstream_view: Cilia-driven flow is established in mice and fish; earlier steps and other species differ
testable_prediction: Disrupting cilia should randomize asymmetry, and it does in relevant species
key_evidence_or_cases: Kartagener syndrome situs inversus; nodal flow imaging; Levin bioelectric asymmetry findings; chiral cell behavior in Drosophila
implication_if_solved: Would explain how molecular chirality becomes anatomical asymmetry

observation_summary: Cells in a regenerating limb know their position along the axis, allowing correct structures to form
why_it_resists_explanation: Positional information must be stored stably in differentiated cells and read during regeneration, and the storage medium is contested
leading_hypotheses: Hox gene expression encoding position; cell surface molecule gradients enabling position comparison; bioelectric gradients; retinoic acid responsive positional memory
mainstream_view: Positional memory is demonstrated experimentally; its molecular basis is partly identified
testable_prediction: Grafting experiments should produce predictable intercalation, and they do
key_evidence_or_cases: Axolotl limb grafting intercalation experiments; retinoic acid proximalization; Hox expression mapping; 2022 single-cell positional studies
implication_if_solved: Would be required for engineered limb regeneration

phenomenon: Why some wounds heal without scars in fetuses
observation_summary: Fetal mammals heal skin wounds without scarring, a capacity lost before birth
why_it_resists_explanation: The transition happens during gestation and the responsible changes involve immune and fibroblast differences that are partly identified
leading_hypotheses: Immature immune response with reduced inflammation; distinct fetal fibroblast populations; extracellular matrix composition differences; specific fibroblast lineages identified as scar-forming in 2021
mainstream_view: Phenomenon well established; mechanisms increasingly identified with specific fibroblast lineages implicated
testable_prediction: Blocking the scar-forming fibroblast program should reduce scarring, and 2021 work reported this
key_evidence_or_cases: Fetal lamb and mouse wound healing studies; Engrailed-1 fibroblast lineage identification; YAP inhibition reducing scarring 2021
implication_if_solved: Would eliminate surgical and burn scarring

observation_summary: Reduced early microbial exposure appears to miscalibrate immune development, though the specific exposures matter
why_it_resists_explanation: Many exposures changed simultaneously with industrialization, and intervention trials are long and difficult
leading_hypotheses: Reduced exposure to specific regulatory microbes and helminths; altered microbiome colonization in infancy; the old friends hypothesis emphasizing coevolved organisms; antibiotic effects in early life
mainstream_view: The general framework is widely accepted; the specific protective exposures remain unidentified
testable_prediction: Defined microbial exposure interventions should reduce allergic disease, with mixed results so far
key_evidence_or_cases: Strachan 1989 family size observations; Amish versus Hutterite farm dust studies; helminth therapy trials; antibiotic exposure cohort studies
implication_if_solved: Would allow deliberate immune calibration in childhood

observation_summary: Alum has been used for a century as an adjuvant without a settled mechanism of action
why_it_resists_explanation: Adjuvants act through multiple innate pathways and their effects are hard to isolate in vivo
leading_hypotheses: NLRP3 inflammasome activation; DNA release from dying cells acting as an adjuvant signal; depot effect prolonging antigen exposure (largely discounted); multiple mechanisms acting together
mainstream_view: A recognized gap; several mechanisms identified without consensus on which dominates
testable_prediction: Knockout models should identify the required pathway, with inconsistent results across studies
key_evidence_or_cases: Glenny alum discovery 1926; NLRP3 knockout studies with conflicting results; host DNA release findings; newer adjuvants with defined receptor targets
implication_if_solved: Would enable rational adjuvant design for difficult vaccines

phenomenon: Why some vaccines confer lifelong immunity and others do not
observation_summary: Measles vaccine protects for life while pertussis and influenza protection wanes within years, for reasons only partly known
why_it_resists_explanation: Durability depends on antigen properties, memory cell programming and pathogen evolution simultaneously
