leading_hypotheses: Live attenuated vaccines generating durable memory through prolonged antigen exposure; bone marrow plasma cell niche occupancy determining durability; pathogen antigenic evolution outpacing memory; tissue-resident immunity requirements for mucosal pathogens
mainstream_view: Patterns well documented; the determinants of durability are an active research question
testable_prediction: Measuring long-lived plasma cell establishment should predict durability, and it partly does
key_evidence_or_cases: Measles lifelong protection; acellular pertussis waning; influenza annual revaccination; smallpox antibody persistence studies
implication_if_solved: Would allow design of durable vaccines against difficult pathogens

phenomenon: Correlates of protection for difficult vaccines
observation_summary: For several pathogens including HIV tuberculosis and malaria no immune measurement predicts protection, blocking vaccine development
why_it_resists_explanation: Without a correlate, trials must measure clinical endpoints, which requires enormous expensive studies
leading_hypotheses: Protection requiring tissue-resident or cellular immunity that is not measured in blood; antibody quality rather than quantity determining protection; multiple correlates needed in combination
mainstream_view: A central practical obstacle in vaccinology for the hardest pathogens
testable_prediction: Controlled human infection studies should identify correlates, and they have for some pathogens
key_evidence_or_cases: RTS,S malaria vaccine modest efficacy; BCG variable efficacy; HIV vaccine trial failures; controlled human malaria infection studies
implication_if_solved: Would unlock vaccines against the three largest infectious killers

phenomenon: Original antigenic sin and immune imprinting
observation_summary: First exposure to a pathogen shapes lifetime immune responses in ways that can impair responses to later variants
why_it_resists_explanation: Lifetime exposure histories are rarely known, and imprinting effects are confounded with age
leading_hypotheses: Memory B cell dominance suppressing new responses; germinal center competition favoring memory recall; birth year cohort effects in influenza susceptibility
mainstream_view: Well established for influenza with clear cohort effects; mechanisms partly identified
testable_prediction: Birth cohort should predict susceptibility to specific influenza subtypes, and it does
key_evidence_or_cases: Francis original antigenic sin 1960; H5N1 and H7N9 age-specific susceptibility patterns; SARS-CoV-2 imprinting studies
implication_if_solved: Would guide vaccine strain selection and pandemic risk assessment

observation_summary: Prior immunity sometimes worsens rather than protects against subsequent infection, a mechanism that complicates vaccine design
why_it_resists_explanation: Predicting which antibody profiles enhance rather than protect requires detailed serology and large cohorts
leading_hypotheses: Suboptimal antibodies facilitating viral entry into Fc receptor bearing cells; antibody titer windows determining enhancement; T cell contributions to severity
mainstream_view: Well established for dengue with a defined antibody titer window identified in 2017
testable_prediction: Pre-existing antibody titers should predict severe disease risk in a specific range, and they do
key_evidence_or_cases: Dengue secondary infection severity; Katzelnick et al 2017 titer window study; Dengvaxia vaccine safety issues in seronegative recipients
implication_if_solved: Would allow safe vaccine deployment against dengue and related viruses

phenomenon: Why HIV has no vaccine after 40 years
observation_summary: Despite enormous investment no HIV vaccine has shown meaningful efficacy
why_it_resists_explanation: The virus mutates rapidly, integrates into the host genome, has a heavily glycosylated envelope and no natural immunity precedent exists
leading_hypotheses: Extreme antigenic diversity requiring broadly neutralizing antibodies that are hard to elicit; glycan shielding of conserved epitopes; absence of natural clearance providing no template; germline targeting approaches now in trials
mainstream_view: A recognized extraordinary challenge; germline-targeting immunogen approaches show promise in early trials
testable_prediction: Germline-targeting immunogens should initiate broadly neutralizing antibody lineages, and early trials show this
key_evidence_or_cases: RV144 modest partial efficacy; broadly neutralizing antibody isolation; germline targeting trial results 2022 and 2024; antibody mediated prevention trials
implication_if_solved: Would prevent millions of infections

phenomenon: Why tuberculosis latency and reactivation occur
observation_summary: Mycobacterium tuberculosis persists for decades without symptoms then reactivates in a minority for unclear reasons
why_it_resists_explanation: Latency is defined by the absence of disease, the bacteria are hard to find in latent infection, and the spectrum from infection to disease is continuous
leading_hypotheses: Granuloma containment with bacterial dormancy; a spectrum of infection states rather than binary latency; immune senescence and comorbidity triggering reactivation; some apparent latency being cleared infection
mainstream_view: The binary latency model has been substantially revised toward a spectrum; reactivation triggers remain unclear
testable_prediction: Biomarkers should distinguish infection states and predict progression, and incipient tuberculosis signatures do partly
key_evidence_or_cases: Latent infection prevalence estimates; incipient tuberculosis RNA signatures; HIV coinfection reactivation risk; granuloma imaging studies
implication_if_solved: Would allow targeted prevention of the leading infectious killer

phenomenon: Why leprosy transmission is so inefficient
observation_summary: Leprosy spreads poorly despite long exposure, with over 95 percent of exposed people never developing disease
why_it_resists_explanation: The bacterium cannot be cultured, the incubation period is years to decades, and transmission routes are unconfirmed
leading_hypotheses: Strong genetic resistance in most people with specific susceptibility variants; nasal droplet transmission requiring prolonged exposure; armadillo and red squirrel zoonotic reservoirs contributing
mainstream_view: Host genetic susceptibility is partly identified; transmission remains incompletely characterized
testable_prediction: Genetic susceptibility variants should predict disease risk among exposed, and they do
key_evidence_or_cases: PARK2 and NOD2 susceptibility variants; armadillo zoonotic transmission in the southern US; red squirrel reservoir in Britain; nine-banded armadillo genotyping
implication_if_solved: Would allow targeted prevention in endemic areas

observation_summary: Prions transmit efficiently within species and poorly across species, with the barrier determined by factors only partly known
why_it_resists_explanation: Testing requires long incubation animal experiments, and strain and sequence effects interact
leading_hypotheses: Sequence compatibility between host and donor prion protein; conformational compatibility of strain and host protein; the barrier being strain-specific rather than species-specific
mainstream_view: Partly explained by sequence and conformational compatibility; prediction of barriers remains imperfect
testable_prediction: Transgenic mice expressing specific prion proteins should show predicted susceptibility, and they do
key_evidence_or_cases: BSE transmission to humans as variant CJD; transgenic mouse susceptibility studies; chronic wasting disease barrier experiments
implication_if_solved: Would allow assessment of zoonotic prion risks

phenomenon: Multiple system atrophy and synucleinopathy diversity
observation_summary: The same protein aggregates cause distinct diseases depending on which cells and conformations are involved
why_it_resists_explanation: Distinguishing conformational strains requires structural methods only recently applied to patient material
leading_hypotheses: Distinct alpha-synuclein conformational strains determining disease type as cryo-EM now shows; cell-type-specific vulnerability; different seeding and spreading patterns
mainstream_view: Strain differences are now structurally demonstrated; the determinants of cell targeting remain open
testable_prediction: Cryo-EM of patient-derived aggregates should show distinct structures, and 2023 work did
key_evidence_or_cases: Multiple system atrophy versus Parkinson disease pathology; 2023 cryo-EM structures showing distinct fibril folds; seeding assay differences
implication_if_solved: Would enable strain-specific diagnosis and treatment

observation_summary: Different tau aggregate structures correspond to distinct diseases, a correspondence only recently demonstrated structurally
why_it_resists_explanation: Tau aggregates were long considered generic, and structural methods were not applicable to patient tissue until recently
leading_hypotheses: Disease-specific fibril folds as cryo-EM shows; different isoform composition driving distinct structures; conformational templating determining spread patterns
mainstream_view: Established structurally since 2017; the origins of fold specificity remain open
testable_prediction: Cryo-EM of aggregates from each disease should show distinct reproducible folds, and it does
key_evidence_or_cases: Fitzpatrick et al 2017 Alzheimer tau structure; distinct folds in progressive supranuclear palsy and corticobasal degeneration; tau PET tracer selectivity
implication_if_solved: Would enable precise diagnosis of tauopathies

phenomenon: Brain clearance and the glymphatic system
observation_summary: A proposed waste clearance system using cerebrospinal fluid flow is influential but its mechanism and magnitude are disputed
why_it_resists_explanation: Measuring fluid flow in living brain tissue is extremely difficult, and anesthesia and tracer methods affect the results
leading_hypotheses: Convective glymphatic flow driven by arterial pulsation and aquaporin channels; diffusion-dominated clearance with convection playing a minor role; perivascular transport without the proposed glial involvement
mainstream_view: Influential but contested; several groups argue the convective component is much smaller than claimed
testable_prediction: Independent measurement methods should agree on flow rates, and they currently do not
key_evidence_or_cases: Iliff et al 2012 glymphatic description; Smith and Verkman critiques; sleep-dependent clearance measurements; 2024 contradictory findings
implication_if_solved: Would clarify brain waste clearance and its link to dementia

observation_summary: Classical models of cerebrospinal fluid production and circulation have been substantially challenged without a settled replacement
why_it_resists_explanation: Measuring production and flow in humans is difficult, and the classical model was based on limited early experiments
leading_hypotheses: Choroid plexus secretion with bulk flow as in the classical model; substantial production and absorption across capillary walls throughout the brain; a combination with the classical model being incomplete
mainstream_view: The classical model is increasingly questioned; no replacement consensus exists
testable_prediction: Direct flow measurements with modern imaging should resolve production and absorption sites
key_evidence_or_cases: Dandy early experiments; Oreskovic and Klarica critiques of the classical model; MRI flow measurements; idiopathic intracranial hypertension as a test case
implication_if_solved: Would ground understanding of hydrocephalus and intracranial pressure disorders

observation_summary: The barrier excludes most drugs while permitting specific molecules through mechanisms that resist general prediction
why_it_resists_explanation: Transport involves dozens of specific transporters plus passive permeability properties that interact unpredictably
leading_hypotheses: Specific transporter-mediated uptake and efflux; passive diffusion for small lipophilic molecules; receptor-mediated transcytosis for large molecules; active efflux by P-glycoprotein limiting drug entry
mainstream_view: Mechanisms substantially identified; predicting brain penetration from structure remains unreliable
testable_prediction: Computational models should predict brain penetration, which they do only moderately
key_evidence_or_cases: P-glycoprotein efflux characterization; focused ultrasound barrier opening; transferrin receptor shuttle antibodies; brain penetration prediction model performance
implication_if_solved: Would unlock drug delivery for neurological disease

observation_summary: Most drugs that work in animal models fail in humans, with translation rates below 15 percent in many areas
why_it_resists_explanation: Animal models differ in metabolism, immune function and disease mechanism, and publication bias inflates apparent preclinical efficacy
leading_hypotheses: Species differences in target biology and metabolism; animal models not reproducing human disease mechanisms; poor preclinical study design and publication bias; human genetic diversity absent in inbred models
mainstream_view: Well documented translation failure rates; the relative contributions of biology and methodology are debated
testable_prediction: Improved preclinical rigor should raise translation rates, with some evidence it does
key_evidence_or_cases: Phase II and III attrition rates; mouse sepsis model failures; preclinical reproducibility studies; human organoid and organ-on-chip alternatives
implication_if_solved: Would reduce an enormous waste of research resources and patient risk

observation_summary: Drugs often have different efficacy and toxicity in women and men, historically understudied because of male-dominated trials
why_it_resists_explanation: Women were excluded from many early trials, and sex differences involve body composition hormones and gene expression simultaneously
leading_hypotheses: Pharmacokinetic differences from body composition and metabolism; sex-specific gene expression affecting drug targets; hormonal cycling affecting response; historical data gaps obscuring the differences
mainstream_view: Well documented for specific drugs; systematic understanding remains incomplete because of historical exclusion
testable_prediction: Sex-stratified trial analysis should reveal differences, and it increasingly does
key_evidence_or_cases: Zolpidem dose revision for women 2013; sex differences in adverse event rates; NIH sex as a biological variable policy 2016
implication_if_solved: Would improve prescribing safety for half the population

observation_summary: Genetic variation causes large differences in drug metabolism, but pharmacogenomic testing has limited clinical uptake
why_it_resists_explanation: Many drugs have multiple metabolic pathways and genotype explains only part of the variation in response
leading_hypotheses: Cytochrome P450 variants explaining much variation for specific drugs; polygenic and environmental contributions for most drugs; limited clinical utility for drugs with wide therapeutic windows
mainstream_view: Established for specific drug-gene pairs; broad clinical utility is debated
testable_prediction: Preemptive genotyping should reduce adverse events, and the 2023 PREPARE trial reported this
key_evidence_or_cases: CYP2D6 and codeine; CYP2C19 and clopidogrel; HLA-B*57:01 and abacavir; PREPARE trial 2023 showing 30 percent adverse event reduction
implication_if_solved: Would reduce preventable adverse drug reactions

phenomenon: Antidepressant and placebo response rates in trials
observation_summary: Placebo response rates in antidepressant trials have risen over decades, shrinking measurable drug-placebo differences
why_it_resists_explanation: Trial populations, expectations and rating practices have all changed, and the drivers cannot be isolated retrospectively
leading_hypotheses: Increasing placebo response from trial design and patient expectation changes; declining severity of enrolled patients; rating scale inflation by investigators; more trial sites with less experienced raters
mainstream_view: The trend is well documented; causes are partly identified and partly structural
testable_prediction: Trial design changes such as placebo lead-in should reduce placebo response, with mixed success
key_evidence_or_cases: Meta-analyses of placebo response trends; FDA trial database analyses; severity-dependent efficacy findings; rater training interventions
implication_if_solved: Would make psychiatric drug trials able to detect real effects

phenomenon: Why most cancer drugs show small survival benefits
observation_summary: Many approved cancer drugs extend survival by weeks to months despite strong preclinical results
why_it_resists_explanation: Tumor heterogeneity and resistance evolution limit durable responses, and surrogate endpoints overestimate benefit
leading_hypotheses: Intratumoral heterogeneity enabling rapid resistance; surrogate endpoints like progression-free survival overestimating real benefit; patient selection without biomarkers diluting effect; genuine biology of resistance
mainstream_view: Well documented in regulatory analyses; resistance evolution is the central mechanism
testable_prediction: Biomarker-selected trials should show larger benefits, and they often do
key_evidence_or_cases: European Medicines Agency approval benefit analyses; progression-free survival surrogate validity studies; resistance mutation sequencing
implication_if_solved: Would redirect drug development toward durable benefit

observation_summary: Resistance to targeted therapy arises predictably in some cancers and unpredictably in others
why_it_resists_explanation: Resistance arises from rare pre-existing clones that are below detection limits before treatment
leading_hypotheses: Pre-existing resistant subclones selected by treatment; de novo mutation during treatment; non-genetic plasticity producing resistant states; combination of mechanisms varying by cancer
mainstream_view: Mechanisms substantially characterized; prediction for individual patients remains limited
testable_prediction: Deep sequencing before treatment should detect resistant clones, and it increasingly does
key_evidence_or_cases: EGFR T790M resistance in lung cancer; circulating tumor DNA monitoring; TRACERx evolution study; adaptive therapy trials
implication_if_solved: Would enable treatment sequencing that anticipates resistance

phenomenon: Why immune checkpoint inhibitors cause autoimmune toxicity
observation_summary: Removing immune brakes causes autoimmune damage in unpredictable organs in a substantial minority of patients
why_it_resists_explanation: Toxicity targets different organs in different patients with no predictive marker, implying individual immune repertoire effects
leading_hypotheses: Pre-existing autoreactive T cell clones released by checkpoint blockade; shared antigens between tumors and normal tissue; microbiome influences on toxicity; HLA type determining target organs
mainstream_view: Toxicity is well documented; prediction and prevention remain unsolved
testable_prediction: Pre-treatment autoantibody and repertoire profiling should predict toxicity, with early supporting evidence
key_evidence_or_cases: Myocarditis and colitis incidence rates; pre-existing autoantibody associations; HLA associations with specific toxicities
implication_if_solved: Would allow safer use of transformative cancer drugs

phenomenon: Why some tumors are immunologically cold
observation_summary: Some tumors exclude immune cells entirely, making immunotherapy ineffective, through mechanisms only partly understood
why_it_resists_explanation: Tumor immune exclusion involves stromal, vascular and signaling barriers that interact and vary between tumors
leading_hypotheses: Stromal and TGF-beta mediated T cell exclusion; low mutational burden reducing antigenicity; WNT signaling excluding dendritic cells; metabolic suppression in the tumor microenvironment
mainstream_view: Several exclusion mechanisms identified; converting cold to hot tumors remains largely unsuccessful clinically
testable_prediction: Blocking identified exclusion pathways should permit immune infiltration, with partial success
key_evidence_or_cases: Immune-excluded tumor phenotypes; TGF-beta blockade studies; WNT pathway and dendritic cell exclusion; oncolytic virus approaches
implication_if_solved: Would extend immunotherapy to the majority of cancer patients

phenomenon: Why metastasis is rate-limiting and inefficient
observation_summary: Millions of cells enter circulation daily from tumors yet metastases are rare, making the process extremely inefficient
why_it_resists_explanation: Tracking rare cells through the full metastatic cascade in vivo is technically very difficult
leading_hypotheses: Most circulating cells dying from shear stress and immune clearance; the need for a permissive niche at the destination; dormancy requirements before colonization; specific genetic and epigenetic requirements for each step
mainstream_view: Inefficiency is well quantified; the rate-limiting steps are partly identified
testable_prediction: Lineage tracing through the cascade should identify the bottleneck, and it increasingly does
key_evidence_or_cases: Circulating tumor cell counts versus metastasis rates; experimental metastasis assays; dormancy models; barcoded lineage tracing studies
implication_if_solved: Would allow blockade of the process that causes most cancer deaths

phenomenon: Why cancer incidence rises with age then plateaus
observation_summary: Cancer incidence rises steeply with age then levels off or declines in the very old, which multi-hit models do not predict
why_it_resists_explanation: Competing mortality and diagnostic intensity confound incidence measurement at extreme ages
leading_hypotheses: Declining cell proliferation and immune surveillance changes in the very old; selection of robust survivors; reduced diagnostic intensity in the very old; tissue microenvironment changes limiting tumor growth
mainstream_view: The plateau is observed in registry data; its cause is debated including artifactual explanations
testable_prediction: Autopsy studies should reveal whether undiagnosed cancers explain the plateau, with suggestive evidence
key_evidence_or_cases: SEER age-specific incidence curves; Armitage-Doll multistage model predictions; autopsy prevalence studies in the very old
implication_if_solved: Would clarify the relationship between aging and cancer

phenomenon: Why humans have such variable pain sensitivity
observation_summary: Pain sensitivity varies several-fold between individuals, with genetic and psychological contributions only partly mapped
why_it_resists_explanation: Pain is subjective, measurement depends on report, and many genes each contribute small effects
leading_hypotheses: Variation in sodium channel genes including SCN9A; catechol-O-methyltransferase variants; descending modulation differences; psychological and expectation factors
mainstream_view: Rare monogenic insensitivity and severe pain syndromes are well characterized; common variation is polygenic and partly explained
testable_prediction: Rare variant studies should identify pain pathway genes, and they have
key_evidence_or_cases: Congenital insensitivity to pain from SCN9A loss; paroxysmal extreme pain disorder from gain-of-function variants; FAAH-OUT variant case; COMT association studies
implication_if_solved: Would enable personalized pain treatment

phenomenon: Why opioid tolerance and hyperalgesia develop
observation_summary: Chronic opioid use reduces efficacy and can paradoxically increase pain sensitivity through partly understood mechanisms
why_it_resists_explanation: Tolerance and hyperalgesia develop over weeks, involve multiple systems, and are hard to separate clinically
leading_hypotheses: Receptor desensitization and downstream signaling adaptation; glial activation and neuroinflammation; NMDA receptor mediated central sensitization; descending facilitation changes
mainstream_view: Mechanisms partly identified; clinical prediction and prevention remain limited
testable_prediction: Blocking identified pathways should prevent tolerance, with partial success for NMDA antagonists
key_evidence_or_cases: Opioid-induced hyperalgesia measurements; ketamine coadministration studies; glial inhibitor experiments; biased agonist development
implication_if_solved: Would allow sustained analgesia without escalating doses

phenomenon: Why addiction develops in only some users
observation_summary: Most people who use addictive substances do not become addicted, and predicting who will remains difficult
why_it_resists_explanation: Addiction involves genetic, developmental, social and pharmacological factors interacting over years
leading_hypotheses: Polygenic genetic risk interacting with environment; adverse childhood experiences and stress; developmental timing of first use; social context and availability determining escalation
mainstream_view: Risk factors are well documented; individual prediction remains poor
testable_prediction: Polygenic risk scores plus environmental measures should predict risk, with modest accuracy so far
key_evidence_or_cases: Heritability estimates around 0.5; Vietnam veteran heroin use cessation data; Rat Park and environmental enrichment studies; polygenic score performance
implication_if_solved: Would allow targeted prevention for those at highest risk

phenomenon: Why psychiatric diagnoses do not map onto biology
observation_summary: Diagnostic categories defined by symptoms show extensive genetic and neural overlap rather than distinct biological signatures
why_it_resists_explanation: Categories were defined by expert consensus on symptoms before any biology was known, and the biology appears dimensional rather than categorical
leading_hypotheses: Current categories not corresponding to biological kinds; shared genetic risk across diagnoses as cross-disorder studies show; a dimensional structure requiring new classification such as HiTOP or RDoC
mainstream_view: Widely accepted as a serious problem; replacement frameworks exist but none has displaced symptom-based diagnosis in practice
testable_prediction: Genetic and neural data should cluster by diagnosis if categories are valid, and they largely do not
key_evidence_or_cases: Cross-Disorder Group genetic correlation findings; p factor analyses; RDoC and HiTOP frameworks; limited biomarker validity for any diagnosis
implication_if_solved: Would allow psychiatry to be organized around mechanisms

phenomenon: Why consciousness has the specific contents it does
observation_summary: Why experience has its particular structure, with this sensory richness and this temporal flow, has no explanatory account even granting a solution to the hard problem
why_it_resists_explanation: Explaining specific contents requires bridging from neural organization to experiential structure, and no principle maps one onto the other
leading_hypotheses: Integrated information structure determining experiential structure as IIT proposes; representational content determined by functional role; neural geometry mapping to quality space; the question may be unanswerable in principle
mainstream_view: An extension of the hard problem that is less discussed and arguably even less tractable
testable_prediction: Theories mapping neural to experiential structure make testable predictions about perceptual similarity spaces
key_evidence_or_cases: Perceptual similarity space measurements; IIT cause-effect structure proposals; qualia space formalizations; binocular rivalry and bistable perception studies
implication_if_solved: Would complete the explanation of mind from matter
